author: balizero1987
body:
The organ went live and immediately told us something true.

## What the first non-dry-run run did

```json
{ "seen": 13, "routed": 1, "left_in_inbox": 12, "drafted": 0,
  "draft_failures": 1, "errors": [], "dry_run": false, "degraded": true }
```

Exit 1, P0 alert delivered. **This is the organ working**, not failing: it moved
the one message it could defend, wrote nothing it could not, and refused to let
a half-done run read as success.

The reason was in its own log, in the redacted format shipped hours earlier —
message id and lane, no subject:

```
loop: no draft for 178563889282 (admin/en): claude CLI not on PATH.
Set CLAUDE_CLI_PATH to the absolute path — a launchd job does not
inherit a login shell's PATH.
```

## A prediction is not a defence

The plist ships a deliberately minimal PATH
(`/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`); the CLI
installs to `~/.local/bin`, which launchd has no reason to inherit.

`draft.py::_resolve_cli` had **predicted this exact failure, in its own error
text**, months before it happened. Nobody armed the other half of the handshake.
That is the shape worth naming: a module that documents the environment it needs
is not the same as an environment that provides it.

The wrapper now resolves the CLI **once** and exports `CLAUDE_CLI_PATH` — the
variable `draft.py` already reads first. In the wrapper because it is an
environment fact, not a code fact: the same module works from a login shell.

It resolves the **symlink**, never the versioned path behind it
(`~/.local/share/claude/versions/<n>`) — pinning a version means the next
upgrade silently stops the drafting again.

**Deliberately not fatal.** Routing without drafting is worth doing, and the
loop already reports DEGRADED when drafts fail. Exiting 2 would throw away the
half that works. It warns once, listing every path it tried, because "not on
PATH" without a list is the least useful failure in this repo's history.

## Corpus: 8 checks, guilt and innocence

| case | asserts |
|---|---|
| nothing found anywhere | warns, alerts `mail-loop-no-cli`, **still exits with the job's rc** |
| found in `~/.local/bin` | exported and logged, no warning, no CLI alarm |
| explicit `CLAUDE_CLI_PATH` | honoured, not second-guessed |
| **stale** explicit path | falls back instead of being trusted |

Mutation-verified: deleting the resolution block turns **5 red**.

`PATH` is pinned to the plist's own value in every check. Leaving the real PATH
in place would let `command -v claude` find the developer's install and report
green for a machine that happens to have one — a dev box structurally unable to
reproduce the red (W108).

The corpus caught its own first draft, too: it read `.out.log` (launchd's stdout
capture, which does not exist in the fake world) instead of the wrapper's own
`.log`, so every grep counted 0 and 5 checks failed for a reason that had
nothing to do with the code. A probe measuring its own mistake.

## An undeclared HOME-fork pair, and its guardian biting on arrival

`grep -c zoho-mail-loop infra/home-fork/declared-pairs.json` was **0** — the live
plist and its tracked copy were 63 lines of config with no guardian at all.

Declared now, and `lint_home_fork --check` bit within a minute: flipping
`MAIL_LOOP_DRY_RUN` on the live side had left the tracked copy at `1`. Both sides
now carry `0` and the same comment, and the lint is clean.

That comment also records a measured trap: **do not edit this plist with
PlistBuddy** — it rewrites the XML and silently drops the comments (63 lines to
43, measured). The flip was done as a surgical text edit for that reason.

body:
## Summary
`_detect_sections` in the resume parser anchored its regex patterns directly to `^` and `\n`, so section headers indented with spaces or tabs (as commonly produced by PDF text extraction) never matched and were silently dropped from `detected_sections`. This adds optional leading whitespace to each anchor so indented headers are detected correctly.

## Issue
Closes #147

## Changes
- Updated the four regex patterns in `_detect_sections` (`ingestion/parsers/resume_parser.py`) to allow optional leading whitespace/tabs (`^\s*`, `\n\s*`) before each section header.
- Fixed a pre-existing `B904` lint error in the same file's PDF-parsing exception handler (`raise ... from e`), required to get the file past the `ruff` pre-commit hook.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests pass (`make test-unit`) — *for the files this PR touches*: `tests/unit/test_resume_parser.py::test_detect_sections` and two other tests failing for the same root cause (`test_parse_single_column_resume_text`, `test_parse_resume_no_work_experience`) now pass. Note: `make test-unit` does **not** pass clean repo-wide — there are ~50 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (confirmed via `git stash` A/B comparison before/after this fix).
- [x] Integration tests pass (`make test-integration`) — not run, no integration tests touch this code path.
- [x] Linter passes (`make lint`) — for `ingestion/parsers/resume_parser.py` specifically (`ruff check` passes clean). Repo-wide `make lint` has ~180 pre-existing errors unrelated to this change.
- [x] Type checker passes (`make typecheck`) — `mypy` passes clean on the changed file.
- [x] New/updated tests cover the changes — no new tests added; the existing `test_detect_sections` already covered indented headers and was failing before this fix (confirmed via reproduction: ran it against the pre-fix code, saw it fail; ran it again after the fix, saw it pass).

## Notes for Reviewers
The repo currently has a large number of pre-existing unit test failures and lint errors unrelated to this change (unrelated modules — review services, skill extractor, tech detector, etc.). I verified via `git stash` that all of them exist identically with and without this fix, so this PR doesn't introduce or fix any of them — it only affects `_detect_sections` and its direct callers. Manually verified the fix also works with tab-indented headers, not just spaces.

author: obinhood
body:
## What

Production-infra frontier, part 1. The DB URL was hardcoded to the local SQLite file. This makes it **env-driven** so the same code runs on SQLite (dev/tests, unchanged default) and **Postgres** (production) with no code change.

- **`app/database.py`**: `SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL = DATABASE_URL` env or the SQLite default; `postgres://` normalised to `postgresql://` (SQLAlchemy 2.x); SQLite keeps `check_same_thread=False`, server DBs get a real pool (`pool_pre_ping` + `pool_size` / `max_overflow` / `pool_recycle`, all env-tunable). The SQLite FK PRAGMA listener is already `isinstance`-guarded → no-op on Postgres. `migrations/env.py` already imports this URL, so `alembic upgrade` follows `DATABASE_URL` too.
- **migration `4f04ee0a5694`**: the one migration that ran literal SQLite `PRAGMA foreign_keys` (to survive a batch table-recreate) now guards that toggle to the sqlite dialect. On Postgres the CHECK is added with a direct ALTER, so the PRAGMA is neither needed nor valid there. **This was the single hard blocker to a Postgres `upgrade head`.**
- **`requirements.txt`**: `psycopg2-binary` (Postgres driver; SQLite needs none).

## Verification
- Fresh DB via `DATABASE_URL` → `alembic upgrade head` reaches `e5b3c8d1f2a7` (env-driven URL + guarded PRAGMA both exercised on SQLite).
- `postgres://` → `postgresql://` normalisation unit-tested.
- **544 tests pass** (540 + 4 new).

## Honest scope
A **live Postgres `upgrade head` has not been run here** — no Postgres instance in this environment. The 11 `batch_alter_table` migrations compile to direct ALTERs on Postgres and the one PRAGMA blocker is now dialect-guarded, but this should be run against a **staging Postgres** before production. That's the remaining validation step to hand off.

body: ## Summary Rolled 4 Point from the end-on wall-run view. ### Path 1. **2-point rolled out** — Rise = Hyp × sin(θ); roll α = sin⁻¹(oh/Rise) 2. **Run parallel** beside the conduit you’re passing 3. **2-point back to the wall** — lateral returns to the wall; **elevation keeps climbing** (does not drop to the start plane) ### Fix (v1.84) Previous return wing used `(-sin α, -cos α)`, which canceled the climb and landed on the start elevation. body:
## المشكلة
عند تغيير تاريخ انتهاء صلاحية المتطوع من لوحة التحكم، التاريخ **لم يكن يظهر** على بطاقة الهوية في صفحة بروفايل المتطوع. وشكل البطاقة نفسه كان يظهر كنص مكدّس بدون تنسيق.

## الأسباب الجذرية (٣ أسباب مؤكدة)

**1. التاريخ كان بصيغة شهر/سنة فقط بدون اليوم**
```
الكود القديم: toLocaleDateString('ar-EG', { year:'numeric', month:'short' })
  1 مارس  -> مارس ٢٠٢٩
  15 مارس -> مارس ٢٠٢٩     ← نفس النتيجة تماماً!
```
فأي تعديل على مستوى اليوم كان ينتج بطاقة مطابقة حرفياً. الآن:
```
  1 مارس  -> ١ مارس ٢٠٢٩
  15 مارس -> ١٥ مارس ٢٠٢٩
```

**2. عدم تطابق بين الـ CSS والـ markup**
- ٤ كلاسات مستخدمة في الـ JSX **بدون أي CSS** (`vol-id-meta-row`, `vol-id-meta-item`, `vol-id-rank-badge`, `vol-id-card-bg-watermark`) → نص غير منسّق (سبب الشكل السيّئ).
- ٤ كلاسات فيها تنسيق احترافي **موجود بالفعل لكن لم يُستخدم إطلاقاً** (`vol-id-ribbon`, `vol-id-avatar-ring`, `vol-id-expiry-row`, `vol-id-status`).

**3. تحميل/طباعة البطاقة كانت تُنتج تاريخاً وحالة فارغين**
`app.js` يقرأ `.vol-id-expiry-date` و `.vol-id-status` من الـ DOM، ولم يكن أي منهما موجوداً في الـ markup.

## التعديلات
- شريط ذهبي `OFFICIAL VOLUNTEER ID` + علامة مائية للشعار + إطار ذهبي متدرّج للصورة + خاتم وتلميح تحقّق في الفوتر.
- شارة حالة في الهيدر مشتقّة من `status`/`is_active`/`expires_at` بحالات منفصلة: سارية / مجمّدة / ملغاة / منتهية.
- **صف مخصّص وبارز لتاريخ الانتهاء** (أخضر عند السريان، أحمر عند الانتهاء) مع عدّاد "متبقٍ N يوم".
- البطاقات الملغاة/المجمّدة تأخذ معالجة `is-void` + بانر تنبيه واضح بدل فلتر inline.
- شارة "متطوع معتمد" في الهيدر تشترط الآن `is_active !== false`، فالبطاقة المجمّدة لم تعد تُعلن عن نفسها كمعتمدة.
- قواعد responsive موسّعة للصفوف الجديدة على الشاشات الصغيرة.

## التحقق
- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅ و `npm run build` ✅ (٨٠ module، بنجاح).
- **٣٢/٣٢** اختبار render ناجح، منها التأكيد المباشر أن تغيير اليوم يظهر على البطاقة.
- إثبات الخطأ على الكود القديم: `مارس ٢٠٢٩` للتاريخين، وغياب `.vol-id-expiry-date` و `.vol-id-status` كلياً.
- فحص متصفح حقيقي لكل الحالات الخمس على ٣ أحجام شاشة (390/600/1200px): **لا خروج عن الحدود ولا overflow** في أي حالة.
- تأكيد أن بيانات التحميل/الطباعة أصبحت كاملة: `٢٠ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٧` + `سارية المفعول`.
- تحقّق من أن `/profile` يمرّر `expires_at` أصلاً (لا حاجة لتعديل في السيرفر).

## الملفات
- `src/components/Auth.tsx`
- `public/static/style.css`

author: fsantibanezleal
body:
Engine 0.07.000. Two defects of the same kind: the code that was documented and the code that ran were different code, and nothing compared them.

## The solver was never called

`segregation.py` integrates kinetic sieving as a conservation law, with a Godunov flux, CFL sub-stepping and an exactly conservative deposition split, and it had a full passing test suite. **Nothing in any shipped path called it.** What ran was three fitted curves with six constants in the module next door, documented everywhere as Gray-Thornton kinetic sieving and rated SOTA. The directions those curves encoded were published and correct, which is exactly why it survived.

Every existing check passed. The tests passed, because the solver's own tests exercised the solver directly. A documentation audit made it worse, because it was built from a ground-truth file written by reading the docs, so it only enforced agreement and never correctness.

`segregate_face` now marches a real `FlowingLayer`. **Wiring the 2005 model alone was not enough**: the pure hyperbolic flux separates the species completely and then stops, giving an on-face index of 0.5162 at `Sr = 1.5` and 0.5162 at `Sr = 15` while real dumps sit between 1.8 and 4. Every scenario would have reported identical segregation. Added the diffusive remixing term of Gray and Chugunov 2006 (doi:10.1017/S0022112006002977), the direct successor to the paper already cited. `Sr = 0` remains an exactly passive tracer, so the negative control is unchanged.

Measured on the artifacts: the cell coarse fraction now spans **0.256 to 0.608** between the 5th and 95th percentiles, reaching 0.98 in toe cells and 0.08 in fine-rich crest cells, against the **0.332 to 0.400** band the fitted curves produced.

### One place it now disagrees with a source, on purpose

Steeper faces are reported to segregate more. That is BALLISTIC trajectory segregation and Gray-Thornton's equation does not contain it. With the layer grain-limited, which it is for run-of-mine rock in every case the product runs, `Sr` scales on path length alone, so on-face sieving weakens slightly with angle while the material thrown clear of the toe grows with angle and is almost pure coarse. Both are reported separately. The old curve asserted the same direction for both, which read as agreement with the source and was really the model having no way to disagree.

## A cut was the size of the whole face

`cut` spread its tonnage proportionally over every cell of the working face, so the ground a cut disturbed was the whole face however little came out of it.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| mean footprint, 632 cuts | 594 m2 | bounded by the machine's reach |
| `intensive_drain` | 355 t off 486 m2, a 0.37 m skim | 900 t off 137 m2, a 3.3 m bite |
| worst provenance | one 881 t cut from 108 dig blocks | a handful |

New `LoaderSpec` carries the working envelope. `bite` digs the cells within reach of the stance **deepest first**, so the machine works the face instead of skimming the thin apron in front of it. `step` trams along the face and advances it deeper when the width is swept. `next_cut` assembles a cut across as many stances as it takes, because the reach bounds what one stance yields and must not also bound the parcel the plant asked for. `rewind` puts a face that outran a still-growing pile back at its start.

Both of those last two were caught by measurement rather than reasoning. Returning the first non-empty stance cut the delivered feed to a quarter of what the campaign asked for; leaving an outrun face parked past the end dropped the concurrent scenario from 28 cuts to 2 and surge from 74 to 2, both still producing a plausible-looking feed series from the few that got through.

## Fixed

- `_take` destroyed `coarse_fraction` on every parcel it removed, in both the FIFO and FULL_HEIGHT branches, by rebuilding positionally with nine of `Parcel`'s ten fields. Identical in shape to the `blocks.py` defect fixed in 0.06.001, surviving in a second place.
- `__version__` had drifted two releases behind `pyproject.toml`, reporting 0.05.002 while 0.06.001 was on PyPI. It now reads from the packaging metadata.
- `ReclaimFace` centred its across-face window on the middle of the pad rather than on the area.

## Notes

Two anchored constants remain, both named and neither fitted to this material: `PERCOLATION_COEFFICIENT` and `PECLET_DEFAULT`. These are what the DEM calibration lane exists to measure.

`solve_route(strict_goal=True)` withdraws the goal-cell exemption for a truck that parks rather than tips. Stated honestly: on the current scenarios this changes no route. It is a correction of the semantics, not the repair of an observed defect.

Test suite: 130 passing.

author: cao825
body:
**The plan is currently unreadable on `main`.** `rmd status` reports *"plan/tasks.yaml is unreadable — dispatch eligibility cannot be resolved"* for both QUEUE HEAD and INBOX, and `rmd lint-plan` aborts before checking anything:

```
### rmd lint-plan: duplicate task id 'W1-T345'
(shard W1-T345-referentless-escalation-dedup.yaml collides with an earlier plan entry)
```

### How it happened

- **#1314** (mine) filed W1-T345 — commitlint stale event-payload — and merged as `fb7b3d5`.
- **#1315** then filed **W1-T345..W1-T350** as one arc and merged as `a8e11cb`.

Both ids are now live. A duplicate id is fatal to the whole-plan read, so it takes out dispatch resolution entirely rather than degrading one task.

`rmd next-task-id` could not have prevented this. It enumerates **open** PRs, and #1315's shards did not exist when #1314 was minted. Two lanes minting the same id inside one window is the residual gap that verb cannot close on its own — worth knowing, since the verb exists precisely to kill this collision class.

### Why mine moves

#1315 is a coherent six-task sequence (T345–T350); renumbering one member would fragment an arc that reads as a unit. Mine is standalone, so it becomes **W1-T351**. Content is unchanged apart from the id and a comment recording the reason.

### Verification

After this change, on the working tree:

- `rmd lint-plan` parses **347 tasks** — the fatal abort is gone
- `rmd status` resolves QUEUE HEAD again (W1-T333, W1-T334, W1-T337)

`rmd lint-plan --base origin/main` **still errors**, because the base it materialises *is* the broken state. That is the diagnosis confirming itself, not a separate fault, and it clears the moment this merges.

Changeset: one file renamed with a 6/1 edit, verified with `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD`.

## Acceptance

- The task now carries a free id, so the plan parses | grep: id: W1-T351 in plan/tasks.d/W1-T351-commitlint-reads-stale-event-payload.yaml
- The collision and why the arc was preserved are recorded in the shard itself | grep: RENUMBERED from W1-T345 in plan/tasks.d/W1-T351-commitlint-reads-stale-event-payload.yaml

author: croadfeldt
body:
Lands the drift-accept ruling (UDLM ADR-060, ruled 2026-08-05) in its mechanism home.

A drift finding routes to **policy first**; policies dictate **and perform** the action — the substrate ships no built-in action or decision. The enabled vocabulary: adopt, accept-with-intent-note, replay at three depths (intent/request/realized), re-observe (false-positive closure), quarantine/suspend (containment, not resolution), defer (recorded, review-timed), decommission — plus external handoff (human/AI/external policy) landing as a DecisionRecord citing the finding. Every action is an ordinary governed request, so the audit chain (routing → evaluations → handoff → decision → action) is captured by existing surfaces.

DCM's follow-through named in the obligation: example resolution policies (one per vocabulary row) and profile bundles that MAY bind defaults — nothing binds unless a profile or org policy says so.

Companion: the UDLM side is ADR-060's resolution-routing section on croadfeldt/udlm#348.

author: thompsoncf
body:
## Summary
Bug reportado com screenshot: nas 4 seções da página de campanha (Configuração / Sequência / Prévia / Desempenho), mesmo fechadas, uma linha de texto do conteúdo interno aparecia cortada logo abaixo da fileira de badges.

**Causa raiz**: o collapse usa o truque `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` (documentado no próprio CSS, veio de uma correção anterior de um bug de `max-height` fixo). `.bodyin` tinha `min-height:0;overflow:hidden` **e também** o `padding-bottom:1.1rem` (~18px) + `border-top`. `min-height:0` zera o mínimo baseado no CONTEÚDO, mas **padding não é conteúdo** — é sempre somado à caixa do elemento, então mesmo "fechado" a seção nunca chegava a 0px de verdade, sobrando exatamente os ~18px do padding — e como `overflow:hidden` só corta o que passa da própria caixa (que já inclui o padding), a 1ª linha do texto ficava visível por trás dos badges.

**Fix**: separei o padding/borda pra um `.bodypad` novo, um nível mais pra dentro. Agora `.bodyin` (o item que precisa encolher pra 0) não tem padding nenhum — só `min-height:0;overflow:hidden` — e o `.bodypad` (com o padding/borda) fica dentro dele, sendo cortado pelo `overflow:hidden` do pai quando a seção fecha. Mudança em 4 lugares (as 4 seções), todas com o mesmo padrão HTML.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile web/painel_prospeccao.py`
- [x] **Reproduzi o bug antes do fix**: extraí o CSS real do template, Playwright mediu `.secbody` com `17.59375px` de altura fechada — bate exatamente com `1.1rem` (17.6px) do padding-bottom que sobrava. Screenshot batendo com o print do usuário (texto "O básico: nome, ritmo de..." cortado atrás dos badges).
- [x] **Depois do fix**: `.secbody` mede `0px` fechado (as 4 seções), `76px` (conteúdo completo) quando aberto, volta a `0px` ao fechar de novo — abre/fecha testado via clique real no Playwright.
- [x] Renderizado o template completo (Jinja2, contexto tolerante a `Undefined`) simulando a campanha do print ("Salão de Beleza", 59 leads) — screenshot confirma as 4 seções limpas, sem vazamento.

author: sergiocastillor2
body: ## Summary This repository was greenfield (only a `README.md`), so this PR bootstraps a complete Cloud Agent development environment tailored to the repo's stated purpose — embedded systems software development (ARM C/C++ firmware). ### What's included - **`.cursor/Dockerfile`** (Ubuntu 24.04): installs the embedded toolchain — `gcc-arm-none-eabi` + newlib, `binutils-arm-none-eabi`, `gdb-multiarch`, `qemu-system-arm`/`qemu-user`, plus `build-essential`, `cmake`, `git`, `curl`. - **`.cursor/environment.json`**: repository-managed environment referencing the Dockerfile, running as the `ubuntu` user. - **`.cursor/install.sh`**: idempotent bootstrap that prints toolchain versions and runs the sample firmware on QEMU as an end-to-end smoke test. - **`examples/hello-cortex-m/`**: an annotated bare-metal Cortex-M3 starter (firmware, startup/vector table, semihosting `printf` retargeting, linker script, and Makefile) that builds with `arm-none-eabi-gcc` and runs on QEMU without hardware. - **`README.md`** / `.gitignore`: environment docs and build-artifact ignores. ### Validation **Local (in the setup VM), `bash .cursor/install.sh`:** - Toolchain verified: `arm-none-eabi-gcc` 13.2.1, QEMU 8.2.2, `gdb-multiarch` 15.1, `cmake` 3.28.3. - Sample firmware cross-compiled and executed on QEMU (`lm3s6965evb`, Cortex-M3): banner + 5 blink cycles via semihosting, clean exit (status 0). - Install script is idempotent (run twice) and leaves no build artifacts. **Environment build:** a draft build of this config (Dockerfile + install) succeeded. Its install-time smoke test compiled and ran the firmware on QEMU (`Environment ready. Exit code: 0`). **Fresh Cloud Agent** booted from that exact build passed 4/4 checks: build identity, toolchain versions present, firmware builds + runs on QEMU (banner + 5 cycles + `Firmware finished after 5 blink cycles.`), and repo layout intact. Once merged to `main`, the repository-managed `.cursor/environment.json` takes effect for future Cloud Agents automatically. ### Notes Since the repository had no existing code, a minimal starter example was added so the environment has a runnable, end-to-end firmware flow that doubles as the smoke test. The exact microcontroller target can be adjusted later; QEMU's `lm3s6965evb` (Cortex-M3) is used as a hardware-free default.

author: vjsingh1984
body:
Brings `main` up to `develop`, which is 10 commits ahead. No new work here — this is the accumulated result of #71, #73, #74, #75 and #76.

## What lands

**#71 — TTM reports incomplete coverage.** `_extract_quarter_metric` conflated "metric reported as zero" with "metric absent", so a quarter missing `revenues` understated TTM revenue by a full quarter with nothing in the result to show it — and unlike a *zero* total, which already warns, a partial total looks entirely plausible before feeding price-to-sales and fair value. Totals are unchanged; the shortfall is now reported.

**#73 — victor-contracts pinned below the removal release.** Six bridge modules this package imported were scheduled for deletion in 0.10.0, and the pin admitted it.

**#74 — the victor-ai host boundary made explicit.** `pip install victor-invest` without the `runtime` extra produced `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'victor'`, naming an internal module and no remedy. It now names the missing distribution and the install command, keeping the original error as `__cause__`.

**#75 — all six deprecated bridges retired.** Verified via `is` that old and new modules resolve to the *same objects*, so it is a re-pointing rather than a behaviour change. Two genuine defects surfaced: `sync_handlers_with_executor` was never importable and had been dead code behind a broad `except`, and `BaseHandler`/`handler_decorator` exist nowhere in victor-ai, so they are now owned locally. The pin from #73 is reopened to `<1.0`.

**#76 — every runtime dependency bounded.** 45 of 52 had no upper bound. Eleven were already running majors ahead of their declared floor — `pyarrow` 13→25, `cryptography` 41→50, `websockets` 12→17, `pandas` 2→3 — each crossed with no commit recording it.

## Risk

The behavioural surface is small and deliberate. #75 is object-identical re-pointing. #71 leaves every total unchanged. #74 only changes an error message and its type, and the new type subclasses `ImportError` so existing guards keep working. #76 changes no resolved version — bounds were derived from what CI already installs, and verified to exclude nothing in use.

The one thing to be aware of: with #76 in place, dependency upgrades that previously resolved silently now require an explicit range edit. Several open Dependabot PRs against `main` are major bumps and will surface that way.

## Verification

Every commit was verified green individually. `1706 passed, 16 skipped` at the head, against a baseline of 1683 before this sequence — the increase is new tests, plus three compat tests that had been skipped because a deprecated bridge was shadowing the local implementation and now actually execute.

author: maxteriors-team
body:
The backend has always exposed `POST /calls/{id}/hangup`, but no UI called it — an operator watching a live call had no way to end it and had to wait for the far end to hang up.

A shared `useHangupCall` hook backs both live-call surfaces (roster + supervisor panel) so they can't drift apart on invalidation or error copy.

**Guarded, because hanging up is instant and unrecoverable.** On the roster the button sits directly beside "Supervise" in a list that reorders every 5s while polling, so both surfaces confirm first — the same `AlertDialog` guard Quotes and Lead Sources already use. The prompt names the contact.

**Per-row disable:** keyed on the id being dropped, not a bare `isPending` — one hook instance drives every row, so `isPending` alone froze the whole roster during a single hangup.

**Verification:** `make ci.frontend` exits 0 (106 files / 1028 tests). The 5 panel tests were confirmed to **fail** against the unguarded version, so they're not vacuous.

author: sullivan07043
body:
Fixes #161 (`ddp_sync_grad` is a silent no-op under FSDP2, so `trainer.grad_accum_iter` saves no communication).

**Change.** Add an FSDP2 branch to `ddp_sync_grad`: on non-boundary micro-steps, defer only the cross-replica all-reduce via `FSDPModule.set_requires_all_reduce(enabled, recurse=False)` on every `FSDPModule`. Restore it in the `finally` block. The intra-node reduce-scatter still runs each micro-step, so gradients stay sharded and per-rank memory does not grow. DDP behavior is unchanged.

**Validation** (2x 8xA100-80GB, Ethernet, HSDP shard=8 replicate=2, batch 64/rank, fleet whose accum=1 step is 22.2 s):

| Config | s/step |
|---|---|
| accum=1 | 22.2 |
| accum=4, without this fix (measured behavior = 4x) | 88.8 |
| accum=4, with this fix | 54.3 / 54.3 / 54.9 |

Decomposition from the two measured points: compute 10.8 s + sync 11.4 s per micro-batch. Throughput 1.63x at accum=4. Loss stayed in the expected band.

One commit, 18 added lines, no API change.

author: rbaumier
body:
Ports the Elysia rule `elysia-no-body-on-get` to axum. Closes #7950.

## What it detects

A handler registered with `axum::routing::get` / `head` whose **last** parameter
is an extractor whose `FromRequest` impl requires a request content-type:

```rust
use axum::{routing::get, Json, Router};

async fn search(Json(body): Json<Query>) -> String { body.term }

fn app() -> Router {
    Router::new().route("/search", get(search))
    //                             ^^^ every GET request is rejected before `search` runs
}
```

`Json::from_request` returns `MissingJsonContentType` without an
`application/json` header, `Multipart::from_request` returns `InvalidBoundary`
without a multipart one, and HTTP gives a GET/HEAD body no defined semantics — a
client sends neither body nor content-type. The route answers 4xx, always.

## The premise does not port mechanically

The issue lists `Json`, `Form`, `String` and `Bytes`. Three of those four are
false positives in axum, verified against the vendored source:

| extractor | axum behaviour on a bodyless GET | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `Json`, `Multipart`, `axum_extra::JsonDeserializer` | reject on the missing content-type | **flagged** |
| `Form`, `RawForm` | `from_request` branches on `Method::GET`/`HEAD` and deserializes the **URI query string** (axum's own `test_form_query` asserts `Ok`) | silent |
| `Bytes`, `String`, `Body` | yield an empty value, the handler still runs | silent |
| `Option<Json<…>>` | `OptionalFromRequest` yields `Ok(None)` | silent |

Porting the issue's list verbatim would have made this an FP factory. The rule
ships the narrowed set. `axum_extra`'s `Protobuf` (decodes the body directly)
and `JsonLines` (`Rejection = Infallible`) were checked and correctly excluded.

## Why the criterion is structural

Nothing rests on a name, a path segment, a directory or an allowlist of values.
Every decision resolves through the file's `use` graph or a written-out crate
path:

- **the routing call** must resolve to `axum::routing` — bare `get` only behind a
  `use axum::routing::get;` (or a glob), `routing::get` only behind a
  `use axum::routing;`, or `axum::routing::get` written out;
- **a chained `.get(…)`** counts only when the receiver chain bottoms out in an
  `axum::routing` constructor. This is what separates `post(create).get(list)`
  from `cache.handlers.get(k)` and `registry().get(x)`;
- **the extractor** must be bound to `axum` / `axum_extra` — `sqlx::types::Json`
  is not an axum extractor and does not fire;
- **the parameter position** is `axum`'s own bound: `Handler` requires every
  parameter but the last to implement `FromRequestParts`, so a `Json` anywhere
  else is not a handler at all.

## The frontier, and why it sits there

The rule reads the handler's signature only when the handler is **written in the
same file**: an inline closure, or a bare name resolving to exactly one `fn` item
whose enclosing scopes all span the call site. Everything else is silent by
construction, not by omission:

- `get(handlers::search)` — another module's symbol. A same-file `fn search`
  decoy proves the rule does not resolve a path by its last segment.
- two `fn search` in scope — either pick is a guess, so it refuses to pick.
- `use axum::routing::get as g;` — provenance is read off the name the file
  writes, so an alias is a known false negative rather than a guess.

The missing half — following `get(handlers::search)` across files — needs a Rust
symbol index comply does not have. Filed as #8399 (`needs-triage`).

## Shared levers, not local guards

`src/rules/rust_helpers.rs` gains `file_binds_name_to_module`, the crate-agnostic
form of the JWT and async-mutex `use`-graph resolvers that already lived there
(explicit binding wins over glob, `as` keeps the module, bare-crate import binds
no symbol). `rust_path_segments` becomes `pub` and flattens
`scoped_type_identifier` so type paths resolve; `root_node` becomes `pub` so the
new callers reuse it instead of hand-rolling a fourth copy. The four pre-existing
callers of `rust_path_segments` were verified bit-identical: a
`scoped_type_identifier`'s `path` field cannot itself be a nested
`scoped_type_identifier`, and the other call sites take `use_path_child`.

## Measurement

`tokio-rs/axum` + `atuinsh/atuin` + `rust-lang/crates.io`, 1168 Rust files:
**zero diagnostics, zero false positives.**

That number is a scan denominator, so here is the coverage one. 98 of the 1168
files carry both `axum` and a gated extractor name; within them **127 GET/HEAD
registrations of the resolvable shape** (bare name or inline closure) reach the
handler-resolution path — all in the axum repo, since atuin and crates.io route
exclusively through module paths. Those two still buy ~90 `map.get(k)` /
`headers.get(name)` call sites that the routing anchor correctly rejects, which
is the shape most likely to misfire.

End-to-end proof on unmodified real code: `axum/examples/mongodb/src/main.rs` is
silent as shipped; changing `read_member`'s last parameter from
`Path(id): Path<u32>` to `Json(id): Json<u32>` — a one-line diff, nothing else
touched — makes the rule report line 62. That handler is registered
`get(read_member)` with `State` first, so routing provenance, same-file `fn`
resolution, last-parameter typing and extractor provenance all execute on a real
axum signature.

31 unit tests (11 positive, 20 negative). Non-vacuity was proven by four mutation
builds, each predicting its failure set before running and matching it exactly —
including the two tests that assert message content and the new
`explicit-wins-over-glob` branch of the shared lever.

## Review

Two read-only Opus reviewers, three rounds.

| finding | disposition |
|---|---|
| Structural-soundness review | `SOUND` — no name heuristic, no allowlist |
| Extractor set too wide (`Form`, `Bytes`, `String`) | fixed — narrowed against the axum source |
| Missing `axum_extra::JsonDeserializer` | fixed |
| Parse-error regions yield phantom `fn` items | fixed — `is_error()`/`is_missing()` guard |
| Ambiguity test did not reach the `_ => None` arm | fixed — both candidates now body-taking |
| Hand-rolled `root_node` copy | fixed — the shared one made `pub` |
| `skip_in_relaxed_dir: true` mirrored the wrong sibling | fixed — `false`, matching `elysia-no-body-on-get`; a route that rejects 100 % of requests is a bug in an example too |
| The file-wide gate silently disarmed three negatives | fixed — all three now reach the extractor-membership check |
| The gate duplicated the extractor table | fixed — derived from the table |
| `explicit wins over glob` branch untested in a new `pub` seam | fixed — dedicated test |
| A `HEAD` route was told to become `POST` (RFC 9110 forbids it) | fixed — method-aware advice, both branches pinned |
| Cross-file handler resolution missing | out of scope → issue #8399 (`needs-triage`) |
| Per-call O(1) handler-shape pre-check | declined — duplicates `handler_last_parameter_type`'s accepted shapes; measured at ~90 ms for the whole rule on crates.io, so it buys nothing |
| `_ => false` vs `[] => false` asymmetry | declined — forced by slice-pattern exhaustiveness, a trailing `_` would be `unreachable_patterns` |
| `on(MethodFilter::GET, h)` unreachable | declined — a second argument position plus a `MethodFilter` parse is scope growth beyond the issue |
| `META.description` silent on the module-path blind spot | declined — descriptions state the violation, not the analysis frontier, repo-wide |

Full suite: 21013 passed, 0 failed. Clippy clean on every touched line.
`comply catalog` diffs identical to `docs/rules.md`.

body:
Option A from the discussion. Makes the multiplayer 3D roll look like the solo/bot roll — the dice **settle onto** the value instead of a number visibly changing.

Instead of re-skinning the resting die's face to the server value (which changed the printed number), the settle path now calls `refaceToServer`: once the server values arrive, each in-play die does a short settling fly that **rotates the real die** so its value face lands up. Numbers never change; materials stay canonical.

Face values are no longer streamed (`authFaced` stays false), so the spectator shows the right number just by following the streamed orientation with canonical materials — no re-skin on either side.

Server authority / anti-cheat is unchanged (values still come from the `rollDice` cloud function).

Merges auto-deploy to yamio.io in ~1–2 min. Test with two players (roller + watcher), 3D roll on. Things to check:

author: amitoj02
body:
Frontend half of the member-profile redesign. Backend companion: [lords-dashboard-backend #81](https://github.com/Amitoj02/lords-dashboard-backend/pull/81) — **merge that first**, this reads `bio` and `socialLinks` off its projections. Both are treated as absent-means-empty here, so a wrong deploy order is cosmetic rather than an outage.

The profile was a banner, a header row, and two columns of panels. Everything about a member was a row in a table: rank sat between "Handle" and "Joined" with no more weight than either, and the three tabs on the right were Gallery, Event History and RSVPs — two of which asked the same question in different tenses.

This rebuilds it to the "Member Profile - Final" design: **a dossier rail holding everything about who someone _is_, beside a column holding everything they have _done_.**

## What moved, and why

**Rank gets a plaque.** It is the one fact on the page that ranks a person against everyone else on the roster, and as a key/value row it read as no more important than "Events attended".

**Event History and RSVPs became one Activity list**, deduplicated by event id with the attendance winning. They were one question — what has this member been to — split by tense, and a member with three RSVPs and forty attendances got two controls where one was almost always empty. Listing a battle you RSVPd to and then turned up to twice, once as a promise and once as a fact, reads as two battles.

**The Service Record became the third segment.** It used to be a panel stacked under whichever tab happened to be open, which made the column's length depend on a control that had nothing to do with it. It is *offered only to someone entitled to it* rather than shown locked: unlike attendance, there is nothing behind a sign-in to promise a stranger, so a padlock would be a lie about what signing in buys.

**The tab strip became a segmented control.** This column already carries a panel header above it, and two horizontal rules twenty pixels apart read as a mistake.

## Bio and linked accounts

New on the page, both optional, both edited from `/account`:

- **Bio** — 280 characters, trimmed, whitespace-only treated as a clear. Renders nothing when blank.
- **Linked accounts** — Twitch, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Steam, Medal.tv, as a row of brand chips.

The member types a **handle**, not a URL, and the server builds the address — see the backend PR for why. `src/app/core/models/social-link.model.ts` **mirrors** the server's per-platform regexes so a member gets an error before Save rather than a 400 after it, **including the deliberate single-trim in `normalizeSocialHandle`** (so `@ panda` fails on both sides rather than being quietly repaired here and rejected there). The editor also takes the handle out of a pasted profile URL for all seven URL shapes, because "paste your channel link" is what people actually do and refusing it with "letters and numbers only" is correct and useless.

Discord is not one of the seven. It is bound separately from the enriched member, which is what keeps it gated.

## Gating

Guests do not see the Discord tag, last access, or RSVPs. **All three were already withheld and still are** — the point of the "anonymous body, signed-in enrichment" split is that the data is never fetched, so this is not a template hiding a field it was handed. The Discord chip is bound from `enriched` for exactly that reason: a guest gets no chip because there is no tag, not because a rule hid one.

What changed is that the page now *says* so. A shorter particulars list with nothing said about it reads as "this member has no history"; there is a line naming what is behind the sign-in instead.

**Joined date and events attended stay public.** They already were, and the SEO meta description is built from them on both the SPA and the crawler shell — the two must agree byte for byte or dynamic rendering reads as cloaking.

## Toolbar: four buttons down to two

A signed-in admin got Dashboard, My profile, Account and Sign out side by side — four peers, of which two were the same destination under different names ("Account" was Edit profile) and one was destructive and one slip of the mouse from Roster. Four equal-weight buttons is not a menu, it is a row of buttons the reader has to rank themselves.

Dashboard keeps its button because it is a different product. Everything that acts on *your* account moved behind your own face — both the smallest possible target and the clearest possible label for "these act on you". Dismisses on outside click and Escape.

At ≤820px the trigger is dropped and the panel becomes a plain section of the existing burger drawer: a dropdown inside a dropdown is a menu you have to open twice, and on a phone the second one would open off the bottom of the panel.

## Mobile

At ≤820px the rail comes apart: the identity block goes bare under the banner, **Honours moves above Particulars** (a stranger cares what someone has won before they care when they joined), and Particulars becomes a panel of its own with the heading it does not need on desktop. That interleaving uses `display: contents` on the three wrappers rather than a second copy of the markup — which is also why those wrappers are plain divs carrying no ARIA role: **an element that stops generating a box must not have been carrying meaning.**

## Two bugs found by walking the page, not reading the diff

- The banner kept the old `margin: 0 -32px` full-bleed, so it ran 1100px against a 1036px content box. Invisible while the header sat *below* it; the rail now overlaps the banner and puts both left edges in one glance 32px apart.
- The desktop grid's `align-items: start` carried into the mobile flex column, where it means shrink-to-fit on the cross axis — leaving Honours at 234px and Particulars at 268px inside a 351px page.

## Deliberately not done

- No "Viewing as" persona switcher from the mock — that is a design-canvas affordance, not a product feature.
- The anonymous projection was not narrowed further (joined date / events attended), per the SEO agreement above.
- `/account` still PATCHes via `HttpClient` directly rather than `MembersService.update()`; the new fields were added to both, but unifying them is a separate change with its own reasoning (see the class comment).

## Testing

**794 unit tests**, `ng lint`, the contrast guard, `prettier --check` and a production build all green.

Walked in a real browser against the live API as a **guest**, at 1200px and at a true 390px viewport: banner and columns flush, no horizontal overflow at either width, mobile section order correct, all panels full-width, Discord and Last Access absent with the gated note present, all seven chips rendering on server-built URLs.

**Not verified in a browser:** the signed-in, own-profile and staff views, and the account editor end to end. Minting a session token required reading `JWT_SECRET`, which I did not do. Those paths are covered by unit tests (Discord row, Last Access row, Activity unlocked, Service Record segment, admin actions, the whole account editor) but have not been seen rendered — worth a pass before this reaches main.

feat: Implement dynamic bandwidth allocation engine for hybrid event streams

Fixes #11486

## Description
This PR addresses the critical issue of venue WiFi networks collapsing during hybrid events when thousands of on-site attendees attempt to stream high-definition remote speaker feeds simultaneously. It introduces the `DynamicBandwidthEngine.jsx` component, a smart streaming architecture that aggressively preserves local bandwidth while ensuring remote attendees get the best possible quality.

## Changes Made
- Created `DynamicBandwidthEngine.jsx` in `src/components/events/`.
- Designed an interactive testing dashboard allowing organizers to toggle the simulated connection state between a "Remote Attendee" and an "On-Site Attendee".
- Implemented smart IP block detection simulation logic. When the component detects a local venue IP (e.g., `192.168.1.x`), it instantly triggers the bandwidth preservation protocol.
- Built a visual "Video Canvas Simulation" that clearly demonstrates the effect of the engine: Remote users receive a crisp 1080p60 feed at 6.5 Mbps, while On-Site users have their video dynamically downscaled and compressed (simulated via CSS blur and pixelation overlays) to 480p30 at 800 kbps, keeping the venue network stable while perfectly preserving audio sync.

body:
Closes #2153.

## What

Add `USER=klangk` and `LOGNAME=klangk` to the workspace container env list (`container.py:1303-1304`), alongside the existing `KLANGKWS_*` vars. Containers have no login process to set these, so without this fix:

- git falls back to `<uid>@<hostname>` for commit author (e.g. `1000@host` instead of `klangk@host`)
- Shell prompts and dotfile frameworks show nothing or the wrong name
- sudo/doas audit logging has no `$USER`

The klangk HOME-per-application-user design (where `HOME` is set to `/home/.users/<uuid>`) is unaffected — `USER` is the UNIX identity (always `klangk`), `HOME` is the per-user workspace directory.

- [x] `pytest src/klangk/klangkd-tests/tests src/klangk/klangkc-tests/tests -n auto` → **4122 passed, 100% coverage**.
- [ ] Manual: create a workspace, `echo $USER` inside the shell → should print `klangk`.

author: bbekshr
body:
Companion to `docs/seo-audit-prompt.md` (#119). That prompt audits what a browser receives; this one drives **Search Console itself** — the actions that exist nowhere else: sitemap resubmission, Validate Fix on the 404/5xx groups, the quota-limited indexing requests, and the Performance read that tells us whether Google has recrawled the retitled pages.

Docs-only. No product code, no protected paths.

## What it carries

- The live sitemap shape, pulled from production rather than assumed: `/sitemap.xml` → `sitemap-static.xml` (924), `sitemap-servers-1.xml` (10,000), `sitemap-servers-2.xml` (3,458).
- The #120 / #121 changes, so the audit doesn't re-report them.
- A cap of 10 indexing requests, spent on a named list of the six pages that actually changed.

## Two explicit "do not chase" notes

These are the reason the prompt is worth checking in rather than retyping:

1. **The indexed count is expected to FALL below 534 before it recovers.** Thin pages that were indexed are now `noindex`. Without this stated up front, the next person to open GSC reads the drop as a regression caused by the fixes.
2. **The soft-404 group is deliberate.** Bad slugs return `200` with a `noindex` meta because the root `app/loading.tsx` streams — documented Next.js behaviour, and the `noindex` prevents indexation. The prompt says to report it and stop, so nobody spends a cycle re-litigating a trade-off that was already investigated and priced.

body:
Conflict between:

- 1c560236fa78 "Rethink pg_dump's handling of object ACLs." (Tom
  Lane, backported from upstream PG15 commit 0c9d84427f into this
  GPDB branch) — rewrote ACL-command generation, renaming the
  revoke-items array from raclitems to revokeitems throughout the
  function (declaration, allocation, the other loop reference, and
  the final free()), while keeping the older `privswgo` argument on
  this particular call.

- f713ff7c646e "Fix pg_dump for GRANT OPTION among initial
  privileges." (Noah Misch, upstream PostgreSQL, 2021-01-16,
  back-patched to 9.6) — this is the commit that actually made NULL
  correct here: it changed this exact call from passing privswgo to
  passing NULL, and simplified the surrounding check from
  `privs->len > 0 || privswgo->len > 0` down to just
  `privs->len > 0`, because passing privswgo caused pg_dump to emit
  a malformed "REVOKE GRANT OPTION FOR ... ON" without the object
  name/semicolon for initial privileges that included a grant
  option. incoming still used the pre-backport array name
  (raclitems), which doesn't exist anywhere else in this file's
  current (post-1c560236fa78) code.

Took HEAD's revokeitems (matching every other reference to this
array in the file) together with incoming's NULL for the last
argument — restoring f713ff7c646e's fix, which 1c560236fa78's
backport had apparently dropped by carrying forward the older
privswgo-passing call. Confirmed against the REVOKE loop's own
(non-conflicting) code just below, which only checks
`privs->len > 0`.

author: rahadianagung-max
body:
Solves the reported problem: 2 categories that should run in **separate batches** (Women 09:00–12:00, Men from 14:00). Before, the schedule used one shared start time and packed all categories into a single continuous timeline — so setting Women to 09:00 pushed Men to ~10:00, and setting Men to 14:00 pushed Women to 16:00.

## Backend (`tScheduleEvent`)
- New optional **per-category start time**, stored in `Tournaments!K` and overridable via `body.categoryStarts { tid: "HH:MM" }`.
- Courts are now assigned **per batch**: categories sharing a start time share the court grid (= old behavior); a later start packs that category into its own window on the same courts. Each group keeps a **global startSlot** (batch offset + local slot) so clash detection stays on one timeline.
- The **base/earliest batch keeps the exact existing timeline** (including breaks); later batches start at their own time.
- Detects **court double-booking across batches** (a batch overrunning into a later one on the same court) → returns `courtCollisions`.
- `tListTournaments` now returns the stored per-category `startTime` for prefill.

## Frontend (`engine.html` + `engine/index.html`)
- **Section 6** shows a "Jam mulai per kategori (batch)" row per category (only when there's more than one). Blank = follow the event start; e.g. Women `09:00`, Men `14:00`. Sent as `categoryStarts`.
- Warns when the backend reports court collisions between batches.

## Safety
Backward compatible — with no per-category start set, it's a single batch and the schedule is byte-for-byte identical to before (base batch uses the untouched `slotTime`/breaks path). Category starts must be ≥ the event start. `node --check` passes on all three files.

**Usage:** Section 6 → set Women `09:00`, Men `14:00` → Generate. Women fills the courts 09:00→~12:00; Men fills them 14:00→end.

author: ariefsaid
body:
`/code-review` step 6 requires `bash scripts/pre-merge-check.sh` (exit 0) and says plainly that no
ledger plus no passing run means not reviewed, so no merge. **The script has not existed since
`3c84da8`**, which retired the old operating model and took the gate with it. That clause has been
unenforceable ever since — the most recent ledger records the gate as `NOT RUN — the script does not
exist in this repo`.

This is a **much smaller replacement, not a restore**. The archived version encoded an operating
model this repo retired, referenced a `review/` layout that no longer applies, and carried an
audit-register coverage gate that is a separate concern.

## What it does

One question: **was the review recorded?** Typecheck, lint, coverage, tests, design guards and the
audit register keep their own gates.

- Locates the ledger for the current branch (`docs/reviews/<branch>.md`, slashes → dashes).
- Works the required axis set out from `git diff origin/dev...HEAD` rather than hardcoding it:
  Standards and Spec always; Design on any `*.tsx`/`*.css`; Security on any auth/RLS/schema/`org_id`
  path; Acceptance when the governing spec carries acceptance-criteria ids.
- The governing spec is named by the ledger's own `**Spec:**` line, so the script never guesses
  which spec applies. An absent line **fails** — it is not an exemption.
- Checks each required axis carries a verdict, last verdict wins.

## The verdict vocabulary

`DEFERRED` is kept as a first-class verdict, **distinct from a pass**: it does not block, it is
never counted as a pass, it is always printed in its own "recorded, not reviewed" section, and it
**requires a stated reason** — a reasonless deferral is a silent skip wearing a verdict's clothes.
`NOT-RUN` stays blocking. Two different words for two different states, so "not reviewed" never has
to be written as `PASS`.

## The rule it inherits

From the archived script's own header:

> A check whose failure mode is silence is not a check: the error must never be quieter than the pass.

Every unresolvable condition is a loud non-zero exit — no branch (detached HEAD), no base ref, a
failed or empty diff, a missing ledger, an unreadable ledger, no `**Spec:**` line, a named spec that
cannot be opened — and an `ERR` trap catches the rest and names the line it died on.

Two traps from the archived script are carried forward with comments saying why: `if grep …; then`
rather than `grep … && var=true` (under `set -e` the latter kills the script when the grep finds
nothing — the gate dying exactly when it has something to say), and plain strings rather than bash
arrays (this repo's bash is 3.2, where `${#arr[@]}` on an empty array under `set -u` is an error).

## Proof it can fail

Every path exercised on a throwaway fixture branch, since a gate nobody has watched fail is not
evidence:

| Case | Exit |
|---|---|
| ledger absent | 1 — names the expected path |
| ledger present, all required axes carry verdicts | 0 |
| diff empty | 1 — "a gate that requires no reviews is not a gate" |
| `*.tsx` + auth path in diff, ledger has no `design:`/`security:` line | 1 — names both axes |
| spec carries criteria, ledger has no `acceptance:` line | 1 — names the axis |
| `DEFERRED` with no reason | 1 |
| `BLOCK` verdict | 1 |
| unrecognised verdict | 1 |
| ledger with no `**Spec:**` line | 1 |
| `**Spec:**` names a file that is not there | 1 |
| detached HEAD | 1 |

## Not in scope

**Not wired into CI, deliberately.** It is a local pre-merge gate; wiring it up is a separate
decision with its own cost and its own failure mode (a ledger written to satisfy a bot).

`shellcheck` is not on this machine's PATH, so the script has not been statically linted.

Draft: the review battery for this branch has not run — its own ledger records both axes as
`DEFERRED`, which is exactly the word this script exists to make sayable.

author: amritk
body:
The shipped AI.md files had gone stale in the way generated-and-committed
docs always do: silently, and only for the audience that cannot file an
issue about it. CI regenerates llms.txt and diffs it, which catches a stale
bundle — but a stale *source* regenerates perfectly, so an AI.md that never
mentions the subpath a release added stays wrong forever.

What had drifted:

- `@amritk/mini` documented neither `watch` nor `template`, nor the typed
  `matchRoute` / `buildPath` re-exports on `/router`, nor `Field` on
  `/forms`, nor the `/vite` subpath at all.
- `@amritk/mini-lynx` was missing `computed` / `effectScope`,
  `fadeTransition`, `keepAboveKeyboard` / `focusedField` and
  `HANDLER_PREFIX`.
- `@amritk/lynx-notifications` documented neither its `/testing` subpath nor
  the fake behind it, and had no Status section.
- All four native packages exported `MODULE` and `EVENTS` with nothing
  saying what they are for, and only `lynx-dialogs` showed how to wire a
  fake into `installNativeBridge` — the one thing a consumer testing its own
  screens needs.

Two accuracy fixes matter more than the additions. Every native package's
Status section claimed the Objective-C compiles against the real Lynx pod;
the macOS job was disabled on cost, so it now compiles only when somebody
runs `pod lib lint` by hand, and the docs say so. And `lynx-dialogs` carried
no Status section at all, so nothing in it told a reader that none of it has
run on a device.

`bun run check:ai-docs` is the guard: it reads each package's `exports` and
fails on a runtime export, a published subpath, or (for a package shipping
native sources) a Status section the AI.md never mentions. It runs early in
CI, before the build, because it needs neither. Exports no consumer ever
writes — the tree operations the JSX transform calls, and the like — are
listed in INTERNAL_EXPORTS with the reason, so a new export cannot join them
by accident.

Types are deliberately out of scope: an AI.md documents shapes by writing
them out, and requiring the identifier would push these files toward being a
second copy of the .d.ts, which is the one thing they must not become.

author: domdomegg
body:
## Problem

Mutating endpoints (`feed_item_spending_category_update`, `feed_item_note_update`, `savings_goal_delete`, `payee_delete`, and the savings-goal create/update/deposit/withdraw tools when the body is empty) failed with:

```
[{ "expected": "object", "code": "invalid_type", "path": [], "message": "Invalid input: expected object, received string" }]
```

**The action was actually being applied** — only the response validation failed. I confirmed this by retagging feed items and deleting a savings goal: all reported errors, all took effect. That's the dangerous shape of this bug, since a caller may reasonably conclude nothing happened and retry, or report a false failure to the user.

## Cause

Starling replies `204 No Content` (no `content-type` header) to these requests. That falls past the JSON branch of `parseResponse`, reaching:

```js
return (await response.text()) || 'Success';
```

With an empty body this returns the *string* `'Success'`. Every caller then runs `outputSchema.parse(result)` against a Zod **object** schema, which throws. The `"path": []` in the error was the tell — the mismatch is at the root of the value, not on any field, so it was never about the input arguments.

## Fix

Return the same `{success: true, ...}` object that the empty-JSON branch already returns. Non-empty text bodies still pass through as text, and error responses still throw.

## Tests

Adds `src/utils/starling-api.test.ts` — five tests against a local HTTP server covering a real 204, an empty JSON body, normal JSON, plain text, and the error path.

I verified the regression test actually catches the bug: against the previous code it fails with `expected 'Success' to be type of 'object'`, and passes with the fix. Full suite 18 passed / 1 skipped; lint and typecheck clean.

Not verified against the live Starling API (no local access token) — covered by unit test and code inspection.

body:
## Summary

`extractTextOperatorsFromContent`'s `operatorRegex` (in `lib/ingestion/runtime/pdf-extractor.ts`) used `(?:\\.|[^\]])*?` to match the body of a `TJ` array operand. Because `[^\]]` does **not** exclude the backslash character, a run of literal backslashes with no closing `]` can be partitioned by the regex engine as either single `[^\]]` characters or `\\.` escape pairs in exponentially many ways before it can conclude "no match" — classic catastrophic backtracking.

Measured locally: the exact pattern from this file takes ~1.1s at 42 backslashes and roughly doubles per additional character. A payload of a couple hundred backslash bytes is enough to hang the process for an unbounded amount of time.

**Why this is exploitable, not theoretical:** this scanner is the fallback text extractor used whenever `pdfjs-dist` fails to parse a file or returns empty text — both fully within an uploader's control (a malformed/corrupted PDF structure routes processing here). Any authenticated `reader`-role user can reach it via the standard `POST /api/upload` flow. Per the ingestion architecture (`docs/RAG_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` / README), ingestion runs in a single background worker polling a shared queue — a hang in this synchronous, single-threaded regex call blocks that worker process indefinitely, stalling ingestion for **every** user until the process is manually restarted. This is a genuine, low-cost denial-of-service vector against shared infrastructure, not just a slow query.

## Fix

Exclude the backslash from the "any other character" branch: `[^\]]` → `[^\]\\]`. This forces a backslash to be consumed only via the `\\.` escape alternative, removing the ambiguity that caused the backtracking blowup.

Verified (see test file) that this produces **identical matches** to the original regex on realistic PDF content-stream operators, including array operands containing escaped parentheses/backslashes (`[(A\(B\)C) 5 (D\\E)] TJ`), while collapsing the exponential-time payload to linear time (200 backslashes: >1s-scale-of-days before → 15ms after).

`operandRegex` and `streamRegex` in the same file were checked and are **not** vulnerable to the same ambiguity (their negated character classes already exclude backslash), so this PR only touches `operatorRegex`.

## Local verification

- `npx tsx --test tests/pdf-extractor.redos.test.ts tests/pdf-extractor.decompression-bomb.test.ts` — 3/3 pass (new ReDoS regression test + existing decompression-bomb test, confirming no regression in that neighboring fallback-extraction hardening)
- `npx tsx --test tests/*.test.ts` (`npm run test:security`) — 253/253 pass
- `npm run check` (eslint + `tsc --noEmit`) — clean
- `npm run build` (`next build`) — succeeds

## Vercel env vars

No new environment variables required.

## Auto-merge gate checklist

This PR is opened as a **draft** for human review — per updated operating instructions for this audit run, automated merging is out of scope this pass. Once Vercel preview / CI results are available they will be added as a comment here for the reviewing human to use as a merge gate; a person still needs to review and merge.

- [ ] Vercel preview build green (to be confirmed via comment)
- [ ] CI checks green (to be confirmed via comment)
- [ ] Human review and merge

## Out of scope

- Broader ReDoS/regex-safety audit of the rest of the codebase (only the two regexes directly reachable from untrusted PDF bytes in this fallback path were checked).
- `npm audit` reported 4 high-severity advisories in dependencies discovered while installing for this run; not investigated or fixed here — separate, unrelated finding worth its own scoped PR.

author: deskuma
blandisc
body:
La pantalla crema del arranque era la última reminiscencia del ADN «Instrumento» retirado. En su
lugar, el orbe de partículas del héroe se vuelve también la **entrada** de la app, su **ícono** y su
**estado de espera**: un solo objeto, tres momentos.

## Qué cambia

**1 · Launch screen.** `LaunchBackground` pasa de la crema `#F4F1E8` al blanco Liquid `#FEFEFD` — el
mismo color con el que arranca el primer frame de SwiftUI, así que ya no hay salto entre la pantalla
estática de iOS y la app.

**2 · La entrada.** Seis corrientes de partículas entran desde fuera de cuadro, se reúnen en el
centro-bajo, respiran un momento, suben al cénit rebasándolo 7 pt y asientan — y ahí el orbe se tiñe
del clima del día.

- El orbe **entra neutro**. Al arrancar, el veredicto todavía se está calculando: cualquier color
  sería una apuesta, y corregirla a la vista del usuario es peor que no decir nada. El gris es lo
  único honesto a los 0 ms, y el color llega como revelación.
- La vista **lee el veredicto en el instante del teñido**, no al montarse (por eso `clima` es un
  cierre y no un valor): a los 0 ms casi nunca está listo, y leerlo por frame dejaría que uno que
  aterriza a media revelación saltara de color.
- Un toque la salta. Con «Reducir movimiento» el orbe aparece ya asentado y teñido.
- Corre **una sola vez por proceso**: volver del segundo plano no la re-dispara.
- No bloquea nada: la app se construye debajo y la entrada se retira con un fundido.

**3 · Estado sin fuentes.** Hoy pinta el **orbe dormido** —el mismo objeto en tinta neutra, con su
nivel en cero, respirando lento y con una chispa verde ocasional— en lugar de la superficie clásica
«Instrumento», que enseñaba un héroe de sueño clavado en «—» que en ese estado nunca puede existir.
Sin contador de noches a propósito: el historial del Apple Watch puede sembrar la base de golpe, así
que prometer «N noches» sería falso.

**4 · Ícono.** El mismo orbe pleno de partículas, en verde, generado por un script versionado
(`Tools/generate-app-icon.py`) en las tres variantes que iOS pide.

## Arquitectura

La coreografía vive en `EntradaSimulacion`, **pura y sin SwiftUI** — misma frontera que
`EcosistemaSimulacion`. `cuadro(t:)` es función del tiempo y nada más, así que los criterios de
aceptación se afirman en `swift test` sin pantalla ni simulador.

El teñido **interpola en sRGB por componentes** (`LiquidColor.ParticulaRGB`) en vez de cruzar dos
capas en opacidad, que dejaba al orbe perdiendo densidad justo a medio teñido. Un test fija que la
entrada y el héroe usen el **mismo color por veredicto** — si se separaran, el usuario vería el orbe
cambiar de color al desaparecer la entrada.

## Verificación

- `Tools/verify.sh` verde (linters + `swift test` + build de app).
- 27 tests nuevos en `StrandDesignTests`.
- Dos rondas adversariales con Grok y DeepSeek, convergidas.

## Lo que queda para el dueño

Probar en el iPhone si **2.8 s** de entrada se sienten bien en el uso diario. Es un solo token
(`LiquidEntradaMotion.duracionTotal`) y toda la coreografía escala con él.

Closes FER-41

author: ammarrica
body:
A thumbs up/down after each match, tallied so that over many plays you can see what actually landed.

## The key is the pair, not the map

The tally is keyed on **(field, players per side)**. That's the whole point: Huge is a lonely trudge 1v1 and a proper match 6v6, so rating "Huge" as one thing would average away the only information worth having. `classic@1v1` and `classic@4v4` never merge, and most of the test's length exists to prove that.

The size comes from **the bodies actually fielded**, not `mode.per` — the warm-up lobby can put six a side on a 4v4, and rating what you played beats rating what you picked. `mapVoteKey` reads the roster.

## The prompt

Sits under the team panels on the result screen: *"Good map at this size? Classic · 2v2  👍 👎"*.

Voting is optional and unblocking — ignoring it is a valid answer, so there's no skip button and nothing waits on it. One vote per match; pressing swaps the buttons for the running tally so you can see what you've said about that pairing before.

Absent in drills, the tutorial and the idle demo, which have no map worth rating.

## The readout

Career Stats gains a **Maps rated** card, ranked best-first by net score:

```
MAPS RATED   5 pairings · 29 votes
CLASSIC · 2v2    👍 7  👎 1   +6
BIG · 6v6        👍 6  👎 0   +6
FUTSAL · 4v4     👍 4  👎 2   +2
LONG · 2v2       👍 2  👎 2    0
HUGE · 1v1       👍 0  👎 5   -5
```

Net rather than ratio on purpose: with a handful of plays a ratio swings wildly on a single vote. The empty state explains why the same map appears once per player count, rather than looking broken.

Stored in `localStorage` under `magnetball.mapvotes`.

## Tests

New `tests/mapvote.mjs` — the split between sizes, the size following the roster rather than the mode, one vote per match, accumulation, persistence, absence in drills, ranking, and the empty state. 50/50 suites pass.

author: oubliettesecurity
body:
There was nothing to run the detector against without sourcing data first — and every public corpus of real influence operations carries terms that make bundling one a problem:

| Source | Licence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ISI/USC ([Zenodo 14141549](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14141549)) | CC BY-**NC-ND** 4.0 | no commercial use, no derivatives |
| [FiveThirtyEight IRA tweets](https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/russian-troll-tweets) | **none declared** | no licence means no grant |
| [X/Twitter IO archive](https://blog.x.com/en_us/topics/company/2019/information-ops-on-twitter) | platform terms | availability changed after 2021 |

So this fixture is **text written for it and dedicated to the public domain (CC0)**. It ships inside the package with no encumbrance attached.

```
$ barbican detect -i examples/demo_corpus.jsonl
Examined 21 posts (embeddings: none).

2 coordinated cluster(s):
  [1] 5 posts, score 0.807   ferry-push-1..5   eastbank_1..5
  [2] 4 posts, score 0.804   levy-push-1..4    harbourwatch_1..4

$ barbican evaluate -i examples/demo_corpus.jsonl
  recall 1.0 | false_clusters 0.0 | n_campaigns 2
```

Both constructed pushes recovered, none of the twelve organic controls flagged.

## Honesty is the design constraint here

`examples/README.md` states plainly what this does **not** show: it demonstrates that coordinated pushes are structurally separable from organic conversation — **not** real-world detection performance. Ground truth is exact *because* the campaigns were constructed, which is precisely why these numbers are a demonstration and not a benchmark. Real-world validation stays a separate local exercise against a licensed source under its own terms.

The topic is a **fictional municipal dispute**, chosen over any real political subject so the fixture cannot be mistaken for, or repurposed as, commentary on real events.

## Tests

They pin the README's claims — both campaigns recovered, no control flagged, the exact metrics quoted — so a threshold change cannot silently make the documentation false. Another asserts every line of the corpus appears in the committed generator, so third-party text could not arrive later inside an opaque data blob.

**66 pass.**

author: marchelo23
body:
Part of #3. Part of #7.

## What changed

### Updated: `persistence/repository.ts`
Complete self-contained persistence layer including:
- Schema v1 with all tables (tenants, api_keys, pricing_rules, payment_links, payment_intents, webhook_deliveries)
- Partial unique index `(tenant_id, merchant_order_id) WHERE merchant_order_id IS NOT NULL`
- Unique index `(tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`
- Unique constraint `(tenant_id, payment_intent_id, event)` on webhook_deliveries for deduplication
- New field: `intent_secret TEXT NOT NULL` — enables deterministic re-derivation of clientSecret
- New field: `merchant_order_id TEXT` — optional WooCommerce/external order reference
- `updatePaymentIntentStatus()` returns `boolean` (true = state changed) for compare-and-set
- `markIntentExpired()` — marks locally expired intents without a provider round-trip
- `incrementPaymentLinkUseCountAtomic()` — atomic check-and-increment with BEGIN IMMEDIATE
- Tenant-scoped `revokeApiKey(keyId, tenantId)` — cross-tenant revocation is a no-op
- `pricingRuleById(tenantId, id)` — fixes Payment Link resolution bug from PR #40

### Rewritten: `services/payment-intent-service.ts`
- **Idempotent retry always returns a usable clientSecret** using HMAC-SHA256 deterministic derivation: `cs_ + HMAC(intentSecret, intentId + ':' + tenantId)`. Never returns empty string.
- Supports both backend-defined amounts (`amountSats`) and product-backed amounts (`productId`)
- Supports `merchantOrderId` for WooCommerce / ecommerce integrations
- Metadata size validated before storage (max 4 KB serialized)
- Payload hash covers ALL behavior-affecting fields: productId, quantity, amountSats, merchantOrderId, description, metadata, pricingRuleId, paymentLinkId
- **Compare-and-set state transitions**: terminal states never reversed by stale provider events
- **Duplicate watcher prevention**: watchers registry keyed by paymentHash, placeholder set before async subscribeToInvoice
- **Bounded recovery concurrency**: batches of 5, no thundering herd
- **Provider reconciliation before re-subscribing**: `getInvoice()` called first; detects settlement while offline
- Webhook events enqueued only when state actually changes (changed=true from repo)

## Tests (17/17 passing)
- Backend-defined amount creation
- merchantOrderId field
- Missing amount/productId rejected
- Amount bounds validation
- Metadata size validation
- Same idempotency key returns same intent with usable clientSecret on retry
- Changed payload with same key returns 409
- Idempotency scoped per tenant
- Settlement fires webhook once
- Duplicate/stale events do NOT reverse terminal state or duplicate webhooks
- markIntentExpired works correctly
- Terminal state preservation (compare-and-set)
- cross-tenant authorization denial
- Cross-tenant read returns undefined
- Offline settlement recovery on restart
- Bounded concurrency for 12 intents
