author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

A full security re-scan of the tree across every ecosystem it has one for, and every source this session can read. The result is one documentation commit, because **nothing in the dependency graph turned out to be movable** — and that conclusion was re-tested rather than re-asserted.

| Ecosystem | Scanner | Findings | Outcome |
| --------- | ------- | -------- | ------- |
| npm | `pnpm audit` (all / `--prod` / `--dev`) | 0 | clean — no `overrides` floor to raise |
| npm | osv.dev `querybatch`, 1591 lockfile packages | 0 | independent second database agrees |
| Go | `govulncheck` v1.6.0, all 4 `go.work` modules | 0 | modules declare zero third-party deps; the go1.26.5 stdlib is clean too |
| Rust | `cargo audit` 0.22.2 (419 crates) | 17 | 16 `unmaintained`, 1 `unsound`, 0 `vulnerability` — none fixable |
| Rust | osv.dev `querybatch`, 419 `Cargo.lock` crates | 17 | same set, exactly |
| Rust | OpenSSF Scorecard SARIF (run `30972346818`, commit `026dce4`) | 17 | same set, exactly |
| Python | — | — | no project (`pyproject.toml` absent) |

All 17 Rust findings are transitive through `tauri`, the workspace's only direct Rust dependency, and every one of them is blocked by a version wall Cargo prints rather than one anybody has to take on faith:

```
$ cargo update --dry-run
     Locking 0 packages to latest Rust 1.90 compatible versions

$ cargo update --dry-run --ignore-rust-version
     Locking 0 packages to latest compatible versions

$ cargo update -p glib@0.18.5 --precise 0.20.0
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `glib = "^0.18"`
candidate versions found which didn't match: 0.20.0
required by package `gtk v0.18.2`

$ cargo update -p urlpattern@0.3.0 --precise 0.4.0
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `urlpattern = "^0.3"`
candidate versions found which didn't match: 0.4.0
required by package `tauri-utils v2.9.3`

$ cargo add tauri@3 --dry-run
error: the crate `tauri@3` could not be found in registry index.
```

`tauri = "2"` already resolves to `2.11.5`, which is crates.io's `max_stable_version` — a tighter pin buys no newer transitive crate and only costs the next patch release, so the constraint shape stays as it is. The exit from the whole gtk3 family is an upstream Tauri release that leaves gtk3 ([tauri-apps/tauri#12561](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/12561), open and unassigned; the `tauri-cef` line exists only as a pre-release git tag and is not published to crates.io at all). Even `wry 0.56.0` and `tao 0.36.0`, the newest published, still declare `gtk ^0.18`.

The commit writes that down in `rba/apps/rba-desktop/CLAUDE.md` — the file this repo mandates for exactly this kind of non-obvious, expensive-to-re-derive mechanic. **No manifest, lockfile, or scanner configuration is touched.** No `deny.toml`, no allowlist, no `--ignore` flag: all 17 advisories keep being reported, which is the point.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change adding functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature causing existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Design system / component update
- [ ] Refactor / performance improvement

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [ ] UI tested (if applicable)
- [ ] Accessibility checked (if applicable)

**Test Steps:**

1. `node shared/tools/dev-cli/src/main.mjs workspace-gates` → `workspace-gates: all 12 gates green`
2. `pnpm nx format:check` → exit 0, no output
3. `pnpm nx affected -t lint test typecheck build --base=origin/main --skip-nx-cache` → `NX Successfully ran targets lint, test, typecheck, build for project rba-desktop`. Cache deliberately skipped so `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` really executed rather than replaying: `test tests::the_shell_identifies_itself_as_the_rba_product_not_the_workspace ... ok`.
4. `pnpm commitlint --from origin/main --to HEAD` → exit 0
5. `git push` ran the full pre-push gate: `NX Successfully ran targets lint, typecheck, test, build for 19 projects`, plus `repo-gates` green.

Every scanner claim above was itself probed rather than trusted. A scratch project pinned to `axios@1.6.0` makes `pnpm audit` report 29 vulnerabilities and makes osv.dev return 29 ids, so the zeroes on this tree are real answers and not a silent network failure. `govulncheck` had to be rebuilt under `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.5`: the default install resolves to go1.25.12 and then refuses to load packages needing go1.26 — it fails loudly rather than reporting a false clean, and the rebuilt binary reports `Govulncheck scanned the following 1 modules and the go1.26.5 standard library`.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

Not applicable — no UI change.

## AI-Assisted Development

- [x] This PR is AI-assisted (drafted or substantially written by an AI coding agent)
- [x] Each such commit carries its disclosure trailer: `Assisted-by: <tool>`, or `Generated-by: <tool>` where the tool produced substantially the whole commit

Claude Code, Opus tier.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented complex logic (where necessary)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] Tests pass locally: `pnpm nx affected -t lint test typecheck build e2e`
- [x] No unrelated code changes included
- [x] `CLA.md` clauses 4–6 are accurate for **this** pull request: I wrote this work, **I own the rights I am granting or have permission from whoever does**, anything I did not write myself is disclosed above, and my employer (if relevant) is on board

## Additional Notes

**What could not be read, stated plainly.** Three GitHub security endpoints refuse this session's token, so no alert list from the dashboard fed this sweep:

- `GET /repos/ecoma-io/ecoma/code-scanning/alerts` → `403 {"message": "Resource not accessible by integration"}`
- `GET /repos/ecoma-io/ecoma/dependabot/alerts` → `403 {"message": "Resource not accessible by integration"}`
- `GET /repos/ecoma-io/ecoma/secret-scanning/alerts` → `403 {"message": "Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy."}`

CodeQL's job logs _are_ readable and were read (run `30972346814`, all three legs success), but they report only coverage and diagnostics, never alert counts — so **CodeQL findings, if any exist, are outside what this sweep could see.** Their coverage lines are worth a reviewer's eye regardless: the Go leg scanned 16 of 21 Go files, the JS leg 148/156 JavaScript, 118/123 TypeScript, 81/84 Vue and 15/15 Actions files, with zero extraction errors.

**One finding recorded, and deliberately not claimed as a mitigation.** `RUSTSEC-2024-0429` (the `glib` unsoundness) is the only one of the 17 whose reachability is checkable, and it appears unreachable here: `glib::Variant::array_iter_str` is the sole public constructor of the affected `VariantStrIter` (`VariantStrIter::new` is `pub(crate)`), and across the resolved sources of all 419 crates the only callers are inside `glib`'s own doc example and unit tests. That is a source-level grep, not a call-graph proof — a call reaching it through a macro or a re-export would not show. It changes nothing about the advisory's status, and the project `CLAUDE.md` records it as a check to re-run, never as a verdict to rely on.

**Two scanners this session could not add, and did not.** `cargo audit` and `govulncheck` were installed ad hoc into the toolchain rather than wired into the repository — no new dev dependency, no new Nx target, no config file. The findings above are reproducible with those two commands from any machine that has them.

**Scorecard's other zeroes are out of scope here.** The same SARIF scores `Code-Review 0`, `Maintained 0` and `Branch-Protection 0`. Those are repository posture rather than vulnerabilities, and branch protection already has a branch of its own

body:
Новое правило `bind-deps-in-objects.md` плюс строка в таблице README.

## Смелл

Модуль, который представляет собой **россыпь функций с общим первым аргументом**. Этот общий аргумент и есть объект, который просится наружу. Клиент, база, бот или стор, протянутые через вызов за вызовом, — это аргумент конструктора в маскировке, а поведение без объекта-владельца — то, чему следующий агент пишет вторую копию.

Три формы, каждая с парой BAD/GOOD, как требует формат:

1. зависимость в списке параметров;
2. сущность, которую рендерят посторонние функции;
3. модуль в роли синглтона — модульное изменяемое состояние плюс функции над ним, то есть класс с удалённым конструктором.

## Раздел «когда свободная функция уместна» — несущий

Без него правило читается как «оборачивай всё в классы» и меняет дублирование на церемонию, что хуже исходного. Чистые хелперы над примитивами, фабрики под контракт фреймворка и контекст-менеджеры над ambient-состоянием остаются как есть.

## Почему оно проверяемо, а не декларативно

Это единственное правило здесь, достаточно механическое для хука — ровно то, что предписывает раздел README «Rules vs. hooks» для дешёво-детектируемых и дорогих смеллов. **ANON003** в `baski_lint` роняет сборку на этой самой форме, а имена собственных коллабораторов проект объявляет у себя в `pyproject.toml`.

Правило написано не из теории: оно выведено из применения ко всей кодовой базе одного проекта, и ANON003 нашёл там ровно одно оставшееся место.

author: tedks
body:
## Summary

Root-causes and fixes the 2026-08-04 outage where the daemon was down for ~9.5 hours despite the health-check/restart automation from #102 correctly detecting it and retrying every 20 minutes.

**Root cause chain:**
1. Disk filled to 100% from ordinary project growth, unrelated to the bot.
2. That killed the bot's control-API socket and gateway connection — correctly detected as unhealthy.
3. The restart's `nix develop --command dune build` needed to re-fetch a source path from the network, because nothing pinned the devShell's dependency closure as a GC root. Our own `nix-collect-garbage -d`, run unconditionally every 20 minutes, is free to evict it between ticks.
4. With disk at 100%, there was no room to refetch — every restart attempt failed identically, forever, until I found and cleared a stale ~12GB npm cache by hand.

**Fixes:**
- Refresh a persistent GC root (`nix develop --profile ...`) for the devShell before every GC pass, so `nix-collect-garbage` can never evict what a restart needs to rebuild.
- Fix a diagnostic gap found while investigating: the daemon's launch/runtime output was redirected into one fixed path that every restart *attempt* truncated, including failed ones — so each 20-min retry during the outage silently clobbered the still-running old daemon's own log output. Each attempt now gets its own timestamped file under `daemon-logs/`, pruned by count.

Verified manually: freed the npm cache, confirmed the missing nix store path fetched successfully and the daemon came back healthy (`gateway_connected: true` via the control-API health query); created and confirmed the GC root is now registered (`nix-store --gc --print-roots`); unit-tested the log-pruning logic in isolation.

## Test plan
- [x] Confirmed no GC root existed for this repo's devShell prior to the fix (`nix-store --gc --print-roots` had nothing for discord-agents).
- [x] Created the GC root via the new script logic and confirmed it's registered.
- [x] Ran the updated script manually against the live (healthy) daemon — GC-root refresh + cleanup path executes cleanly, `bash -n` passes.
- [x] Unit-tested the timestamped-log pruning logic (15 dummy files → correctly keeps newest 10).
- [ ] Let a real unhealthy→restart cycle exercise the new per-attempt log path in production (no way to test this without disrupting the live bot; will confirm on the next genuine restart).

author: cremeni25
wormeyman
body:
Adds a third skill: `refactoring`. Language-agnostic; built against a TypeScript SPA, a forked TS monorepo, and a C# solution at once.

## Why another one

Published refactoring skills agree on the criteria - knowledge duplication is bad, deep nesting is bad, do not refactor speculatively. The gap is that they are **criteria without a method**: all of them rest on "abstract what would change together", then leave you to eyeball whether two files would change together.

So this one ships `scripts/co-change.sh`, which measures it from git history. It also assesses the test safety net before trusting "behavior-preserving under existing tests", carries an exception list for duplication that must NOT be collapsed, and treats "no refactor needed" as a reportable result.

## I A/B tested it, and it corrected me

Three realistic prompts against two real repos, each run with and without the skill, graded by a separate agent told to mark strictly and verify claims against the repos.

**18/18 assertions with it, 11/18 without**, costing ~25% more tokens and ~80s more per run. But the aggregate hides the finding:

| case | with | without |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Split a 2,700-line file (repo is a fork) | 6/6 | **1/6** |
| Modernise imperative C# (transpiles to Lua) | 6/6 | 5/6 |
| Survey a Vue app and rank the work | 6/6 | 5/6 |

Two cases barely separate - those repos document their own constraints in CLAUDE.md, and a careful agent finds them either way.

The first is different in kind. Without the skill the model produced a confident, well-evidenced nine-module split plan, correctly analysed churn, found the characterisation-test harness - and never ran `git remote -v`. The repo is a fork 399 commits ahead of a live upstream. It also called the safety net "unusually good" and staked the recommendation on it, while the suite it named never runs in CI.

**Two things I got wrong and have fixed here:**

1. I predicted the co-change script would be the differentiator. It is not - the model reached for git history unprompted without it. The README now says so.
2. The real edge is constraints **not visible in the source** - fork status, whether a suite actually runs in CI, generated files. Reading code more carefully never surfaces those. The skill now spends thirty seconds on repository provenance (`git remote -v`, ahead/behind, submodules) *before* reading any code.

## Validation

- `co-change.sh` reproduces by measurement a coupled pair found manually in a third repo, and correctly leaves seven near-identical file pairs below threshold.
- Lockfile/manifest noise filter added after testing surfaced it ranking top.
- Shell syntax checked, script executable, no em/en dashes, young-repo guard verified firing.

## Known limits

One run per cell, so single-run noise is possible. The grader flagged two verdicts as judgment calls (neither flips a case). Two of the three cases are near-saturated and would need redesigning to measure anything further. No assertion tests whether the primary *recommendation* was correct - they test constraint recognition.

`references/repo-notes.md` records verification commands and traps for the three repos so they do not have to be rediscovered.

author: joeldickson
body:
Closes #46. Ingestion-side schema changes are tracked in #47.

`getCommonMetadata()` already captured timing, git, host and CPU beautifully, but every event described **one compilation**. So "how long from `git pull` to a working app?" was unanswerable, install time was invisible, and in dev mode `closeBundle` never fires — meaning **time to a usable dev server was not measured at all**.

`packages/webpack-plugin` is deliberately untouched, per the issue's non-goal.

## What lands

A new `type: "command"` event on `COMMAND_ENDPOINT` (default `http://compilation-metrics/command`):

| `phase` | What it measures | Emitted by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install` | Package manager run, plus cold/warm and lockfile change | install hooks (npm, yarn, pnpm) |
| `devserver` | Time until the dev server is listening | Vite, Rsbuild, Rspack watch |
| `clientready` | Time until the app is usable in the browser, with DCL and FCP | Vite, Rsbuild |

Plus a `sessionId` on **every** event type — including the existing `webpack`, `vite`, `vitehmr`, `rspack` and `rsbuild` payloads — so those phases stitch into one timeline. Purely additive; no existing payload changed shape.

Aborted runs are recorded too: Ctrl-C produces a `devserver` event with `signal: "SIGINT"`. A developer who gave up waiting is the most interesting point on the chart.

## Answers to the issue's open questions

**1. Which package manager?** All three. Every lockfile shape is hashed, all three are detected from `npm_config_user_agent`, and §4b (scraping npm's own `--timing` logs) is built since npm is in the set — that is where you find out a Playwright browser download or a `node-gyp` rebuild is the actual cost.

**2. Option A vs B — cold coverage wanted, so A.** A root `preinstall`/`postinstall` pair gives the exact span and a trustworthy `coldInstall` flag. Option B still ships and needs no repo change; when the root hooks are present the bundled one **stands down**, so one event is produced rather than two. On a genuinely cold clone the preinstall file does not exist yet, the `try/catch` swallows it, and the bundled hook falls back to process start time — cold clones are still measured, just less precisely. Every install event carries `measurementSource` (`preinstall` / `postinstall` / `npm-timing`), because the inferred route systematically undercounts and **the two must not be aggregated together**.

**3. Vite range — widen.** Peer is now `vite >=4.0.0`, `rollup >=3.0.0`. Prebundling detection is tri-state and simply absent under Rolldown rather than guessing, and never reaches into `server._optimizedDeps`.

**4. Rspack endpoint — fixed.** `rsbuild`/`rspack` now post to `/rspack` as the README always documented, instead of the webpack endpoint. ⚠️ **If your dashboards read Rspack data off the webpack endpoint, they need repointing** — #47 covers keeping both paths working during the transition, and it is worth checking how much existing "webpack" volume is actually rsbuild, since that skews historical webpack numbers.

**5. `spooledAt` — kept as a first-class field, and raw data preferred over precomputation.** `npmTimers` ships the raw map rather than a rollup, and #47 argues for a child table over storing a fixed subset.

## Never on the critical path

This is most of the design, because telemetry that slows people down gets deleted from configs:

- **Install and signal-handler events are spooled**, not sent — a small local NDJSON file, delivered by the next dev server or build. An install never waits on the network; a dying process never loses the race with an in-flight POST. Capped at 256 KB, events older than a week dropped rather than accumulated.
- **1500 ms timeout on every POST.** Off-VPN, nothing hangs. This was mandatory before emitting anything from the install path.
- **Git metadata cached** until the repository actually changes (a statSync fingerprint over `HEAD`/ref/packed-refs/config), replacing three synchronous `git` spawns per HMR event.
- **Session id resolved once per process**, and its keepalive touch is deferred via `setImmediate` — so the HMR path performs zero synchronous filesystem writes and zero process spawns.
- **Signal handlers write synchronously and get out of the way**: they remove themselves and re-raise the signal if nobody else is listening, so Ctrl-C behaves exactly as it would without the plugin. Merely attaching a `SIGINT` listener would otherwise suppress Node's default exit and leave the dev server hanging.
- `stats.toJson()` in the Rsbuild plugin no longer serializes the entire compilation on every rebuild.
- Startup chatter is behind `DEVFEEDBACK_DEBUG`. **No new stdout/stderr at the default log level.**

## Testing

64 tests, 12/12 turbo tasks green (`check-types` + `test`). New coverage: session lifecycle and TTL rollover, spool round-trip including size cap, age cutoff and malformed lines, lockfile hashing and package-manager parsing for all three managers, git cache invalidation on commit and branch switch, and the new dev-server/client-ready/abort paths in both plugins.

Beyond unit tests, the install hooks were verified end-to-end against real temp repos: the cold path, the `--self` stand-down, and this repo's own `pnpm install` running the bundled hook without noise or failure.

One bug found and fixed during that smoke test: priming the session before reading state made `coldInstall` always report `false` on the Option B path, because `getSessionId` writes the very state file that was about to be checked.

## Rollout notes

- **pnpm blocks dependency lifecycle scripts by default.** Allow it once during dev machine bootstrap in `~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml` (`allowBuilds`, or `onlyBuiltDependencies` on pnpm 10 and earlier) so repos stay untouched.
- The exact-install tier needs `agoda-devfeedback-common` as a **direct** devDependency — under pnpm a transitive dependency is not resolvable from the repo root.
- Install events arrive on the *next* dev server or build start, not immediately. Nobody watches an install dashboard in real time.
- `--ignore-scripts` skips install capture entirely.

## Summary

Fix the dashboard startup freeze introduced by PR #33.

## Root cause

The Chromium-operation script installed a `MutationObserver` that watched child-node changes across the dashboard. Its callback rewrote the **Uninstall Chromium** button's `textContent` even when that text was already correct. author: mikewills
body:
First of the two licence-tracking features. A team-scoped watch list of **any call sign at all** — club members, family, people who never tested with this team. Deliberately not tied to `Candidate` or `VolunteerExaminer`.

Scope as agreed: **screen only**, no email; **every role**, scoped to their own team(s), since everything shown is public FCC record data; **call sign or FRN**, call sign preferred.

Tracking VEs' own licences is the separate, not-yet-built half.

## Verified live before designing it

Against `W1AW`, on the endpoint the candidate watcher already uses:

- **`expired_date` is returned** — it was simply never mapped. `UlsLookupResult` had `grant_date` and `effective_date` only, because nothing before this needed a term end.
- **Call-sign lookup works.** The client parameter is named `frn`, but the endpoint resolves either. That is what makes call-sign-first entry possible without a second step.
- The response also carries a full postal address. **Deliberately not mapped** — nothing here needs it, and not holding it avoids the question. Name/call sign/FRN are public FCC record data, same class as `Candidate.CallSign`, which the PII purge already keeps.

FCC's own `data.fcc.gov` License View API 301s to `www.fcc.gov` and returns Akamai 403 — same edge block as `wireless2`. Not pursued further.

## The part worth reviewing carefully

**ULS reports that a renewal is pending. It never reports that one was issued.** A renewal leaves the call sign, the operator class and the grant date untouched — the only thing that moves is the expiration date.

So it is a two-step state machine: on first sighting, record `RenewalPendingSinceUtc` **and** anchor `ExpiredDateWhenRenewalFiledUtc` to the expiry as it stands; on a later poll, declare it issued only once the current expiry passes that anchor. Without the anchor the only available test is "is the expiry in the future?", which is true for a licence renewed years early.

Three details each bought by a specific failure mode, all pinned by tests:
- **Confirmation is tested before the still-pending branch** — FCC can leave the application listed after granting, and the row would otherwise stick on "renewal pending" long after the renewal landed.
- **`RenewalPendingSinceUtc` never creeps forward** while pending, or "pending since" is always today and the wait is invisible.
- **A failed lookup does not stamp `LastCheckedUtc`** — stamping it would park the row for a full refresh interval on the strength of an error.

## One unverified assumption, flagged

`application_purpose` is matched against `RO`/`RM`. Those are FCC's documented codes and the field is documented as present, but **no record with a pending renewal has been observed live** — W1AW had none. It is matched case-insensitively against a set so an unexpected value degrades to "not a renewal" rather than throwing or false-positiving. If detection ever appears not to fire, check this first.

Thresholds — 90-day renewal window, 2-year grace — confirmed with Mike.

## Also

- Status is **derived, not stored**, like Session "Completed". Precedence matters: cancellation outranks a future expiry, because a cancelled record keeps its expiration date and would otherwise read as comfortably Active.
- Adding a licence resolves it **synchronously** and refuses to save if it doesn't exist, so a typo is caught while the person who typed it is still there. Three failure cases are worded differently on purpose — telling someone their valid call sign doesn't exist because ExamTools was down would be worse than useless.
- Migration is one new table, clean `DROP TABLE` down path, no changes to existing tables.
- The table carries `class="cards"` + `.table-scroll`, consistent with #104/#105.

`dotnet build`: 0 warnings. `dotnet test`: **620/620**, 22 new.

Not verified: the page rendered with real data behind a login.

body:
Task: feat-workspaces-impl-001 (research: feat-workspaces-research-001 · plan: feat-workspaces-plan-001)

Workspaces group projects one level above the project switcher — and they **isolate**: the active workspace's projects and their tasks are the entire visible world (board, list, graph hubs, files roots, demo groups, pickers, command palette). Requestor decisions baked in: switcher lives inside the Cmd+P popover; all existing projects migrate to a default **Personal** workspace; strict isolation (no cross-workspace view); Root/"No project" tasks are pinned to Personal.

## What's in here
- **Backend**: `workspaces.json` registry with an undeletable `personal` default (`ensureDefault`), `workspace` field on project entries (backfilled at boot, stamped on register/auto-discovery), workspace CRUD routes with guards (default undeletable; non-empty delete blocked with a count), and `PUT /api/projects/:id/workspace` for reassignment (Root 403s).
- **Isolation core**: `useTasks` returns the workspace-scoped list under the historical `projects` name, so every consumer isolates at the source; `allProjects` serves management UI. One shared rule everywhere: anything the registry can't place resolves to Personal — a task/root/demo group can never vanish from every workspace. Stale project selections reset to All on switch *and* at load.
- **UI**: workspace header row in the ProjectAnchor popover (switch, inline create/rename, guarded delete), per-project "move to workspace" hover action beside Archive, Switch-workspace commands in the palette. "No project" is hidden from create/task modals outside Personal so a task can't be filed somewhere invisible.
- **Compatibility invariant**: until a second workspace is created, everything lives in Personal and behavior is unchanged — the whole pre-existing e2e suite runs untouched (one helper addition: mockCoreApi routes `/api/workspaces`).

## Test plan
- Backend: 357/357 (`node --test`), including 9 new registry/migration tests; live route smoke against a throwaway backend verified all guards.
- e2e: 97 passed + 9 skipped — the 92-test baseline unchanged plus 5 new `workspaces.spec.js` tests (isolation swap, Root pinning, persistence + stale-selection reset, move-project flow, delete guards + inline create).
- Lint: repo baseline unchanged (the pre-existing repo-wide eslint drift is untouched by this diff).

author: scttfrdmn
body:
Detached mode could not create a bastion, in either of its two paths. Fixing
that surfaced two further defects in the init script itself, and one more that
needs its own issue (#229).

## #227 — the init script does not fit in any delivery mechanism

The script is a whole program: ~32 KB of shell wrapping an ~850-line embedded
Python orchestrator. Measured against the limits it was being pushed through:

| | size | limit | |
|---|---|---|---|
| CloudFormation parameter | 42,740 B (base64) | 4,096 B | **10.4x** |
| `RunInstances` UserData | 32,435 B | 16,384 B | **2.0x** |

So `create_stack` rejected the parameter outright and EC2 refused the direct
path. gzip does not rescue it — 34 KB compresses to 8,333 B, inside EC2's limit
and still double CloudFormation's.

**Fix:** upload the script to S3, and put only a fetch shim in UserData. The URL
is **presigned** rather than an `aws s3 cp` against the instance's own role,
because the direct path attaches no instance profile at all (#229) — a
credentialed fetch would have rescued only the CloudFormation bastion. One
mechanism now fixes both.

Two things follow the ownership pattern #100 established for the serverless
security group:

- The staging bucket is provider-scoped, created on first use, and deleted on
  cleanup **only if this mode created it**. A caller-supplied bucket is reused
  and kept.
- Staged-script cleanup is gated on `preserve_bastion` alone, not on the bastion
  having been created. A script staged for a bastion whose creation then failed
  is still collected — that was a real leak the first draft had, caught by the
  integration test asserting `_script_key is None`.

Both limits are now asserted at render time, so a future edit to the script
cannot silently reintroduce this: substrate enforces neither limit, so the
failure would otherwise appear only against live AWS.

## #225 — the script aborted on its first install line

It ran under `set -e` and then:

```sh
apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip jq awscli || yum install -y ...
```

On Amazon Linux 2023 — the default AMI family — `apt-get` does not exist, so the
left side failed; and `awscli` is not an installable package there (CLI v2 ships
preinstalled, the v1 package was dropped), so the right side failed too. `set -e`
aborted, and the manager script, its systemd service and the idle-shutdown timer
were never installed. The instance still reached `running` and the stack still
reported `CREATE_COMPLETE`.

The install now dispatches on the available package manager. The package list is
**three corrections deep**, each found by booting a bastion rather than by
reading the shell:

- **`python3-boto3`, not `pip install boto3`.** The manager imports boto3 at
  module scope and no AMI ships it, so the original line could not have produced
  a working bastion even had every package in it resolved. But installing via pip
  means first installing pip, and `dnf install python3-pip` pulls in
  **python3.11** and repoints `/usr/bin/python3` at it — which breaks `dnf`
  itself and AWS CLI v2, both python3.9 scripts, with `ModuleNotFoundError: No
  module named 'dnf'`. AL2023 packages boto3 for the system 3.9.
- **`cronie`.** AL2023 installs no cron daemon.
- **no `python3` in the list.** Already present, and naming it invites the same
  3.11 substitution.

Prerequisites are now verified by *outcome* rather than by installer exit status
— the pip failure was an installer that succeeded and left the system unable to
run its own tools. And the script ends by touching
`/var/run/parsl_bastion_ready`: that sentinel is the only positive evidence
UserData ran to the end, since instance state, status checks and stack status are
all indifferent to it. That indifference is exactly why this went unnoticed.

## #225 (second defect) — the idle timer was registered on no schedule

Even with cronie installed:

```sh
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '...') | crontab -
```

left `/var/spool/cron/root` at **0 bytes** on a fresh bastion. `crontab -l` has
nothing to list there and exits non-zero, so the subshell contributed nothing and
the append landed nowhere — while every command in the pipeline exited 0. So
`idle_timeout` could not work, and with the default `preserve_bastion=True`
nothing else reclaims a bastion.

Now an `/etc/cron.d/parsl-idle-shutdown` drop-in, which has no read-modify-write
step and so no empty-input case. The prerequisite check now requires a *running*
daemon (`systemctl is-active crond`) rather than the `crontab` client being on
`PATH` — the client's presence said nothing about whether the drop-in would ever
be read.

## Verification

**Against real AWS** (`us-east-1`, account `942542972736`), which is the only
thing that could prove any of this — the limits are enforced nowhere else:

- A bastion stack reached `CREATE_COMPLETE`, from a UserData shim under 4,096 B.
- A direct-path bastion launched (`i-00d0e5d844dbb24aa`, `i-03b164844d451a4a1`).
- The two E2E tests that previously errored during construction now pass:
  `test_cleanup_removes_the_bastion_when_not_preserving` (198.98 s) and
  `test_cleanup_keeps_the_bastion_when_preserving` (213.59 s).
- On the fixed bastion: bootstrap status `OK`, sentinel present, python3 3.9.25
  intact, boto3 1.40.31, `aws-cli/2.33.15` intact, `dnf 4.14.0` intact, `crond`
  active, and **`parsl-bastion-manager.service` active** — the orchestrator loop
  starting for the first time.
- The cron drop-in **fired**, which the drop-in merely existing does not prove:

  ```
  CROND[25601]: (root) CMD (/usr/local/bin/parsl-idle-shutdown.sh)
  CROND[25600]: (root) CMDEND (/usr/local/bin/parsl-idle-shutdown.sh)
  -rw-r--r--. 1 root root 11 /var/run/parsl-last-activity
  ```

  The activity file is the script's own output, so it ran rather than merely got
  scheduled.

**Against substrate**, which caught a defect a mock could not: botocore's
*presigner* emits SigV2 even when `client.meta.config.signature_version` reports
`s3v4`. A SigV2 URL is rejected by every region created after 2014, and substrate
answers **501**. `Config(signature_version="s3v4")` is now passed explicitly. The
integration test does a real `put_object` and then a real
`urllib.request.urlopen` of the URL extracted from UserData, asserting the body
matches — that HTTP GET is the assertion that needed an emulator.

A second real defect came from the same rewrite: the size assertion assumed a
**175 B** presigned URL, the length with static keys. Under session-token
credentials it is **1,064 B** (the token alone ~664 B). Measured, then the
assertion rewritten against the worst case — otherwise it would have passed in
development and failed for anyone using a role.

Unit tests are pure rendering arithmetic (no session, no fake AWS): they pin what
the shim contains and that it fits, and each shell assertion records the live
finding it corresponds to.

Suites: **1253 unit passed / 2 skipped**, **136 integration passed**, ruff clean,
mypy **59 errors** (under the 76 baseline).

Live resources from this work were swept: zero `parsl-*` stacks, buckets,
instances, `parsl-ephemeral-ssm-role-*` and `parsl-bastion*` roles remain.

## Filed, not fixed here

**#229** — the direct path attaches no instance profile, so
`parsl-bastion-manager.py` crash-loops on `NoCredentialsError` every 10 s
(`Restart=always`). Verified on both live bastions: `IamInstanceProfile` is
`null` and IMDS returns 404 for `iam/security-credentials/`. Three signals read
healthy — `systemctl is-active` says `active` between crashes, the UserData
sentinel is present, and SSM says `Online` (this account has Default Host
Management Configuration set, which registers instances with *no* profile). So
the bastion is reachable over SSM while unable to make a single AWS call of its
own. The staged-script fix here is deliberately unaffected, since a presigned URL
needs no instance credentials; what has never worked is the manager loop after
boot, which has no live coverage.

closes #227
closes #225

## What changed

### Live embeds

- presents example choices as a full-width tab strip at the top of the homepage embed
- keeps Eval, Run, connection state and Open in Playground in a separate compact control row
- hides the redundant `Preparing Hara kernel` toast on homepage live cards; the connection indicator remains the loading signal
- removes expected-result comments such as `; => 42` from editable examples so the live result is shown only once
- softens the resize affordance and browser scrollbars

### Kernel mode picker

- replaces the Java / Native / Web select menu with an accessible tablist
- uses the generated design direction: a clear active rail, concise runtime subtitles and a persistent content panel
- supports click, Arrow keys and Home/End navigation
- becomes a compact horizontal three-tab row on mobile

### Canvas fixes

- fixes `studio.node/run-task` and handler lookup by dereferencing their atom registries once rather than trying to dereference the resulting vector
- changes Pong to use a top-level `(require [studio.draw :as draw])`, so InstaREPL evaluation of that line is valid instead of producing `unbound symbol: studio.draw`
- keeps the canonical `.hal` source and bundled browser source exactly synchronized

## Validation

- homepage contracts cover runtime tabs, tab ordering and the hidden progress toast
- Pong contracts cover locally evaluable namespace setup and correct node task startup
- live snippet contracts prevent duplicated expected-result comments and source drift
- Site CI runs the full website test suite and Astro production build

body:
Part of #22

## Summary
- centralizes production logging behind bounded, allowlisted structured events with nested secret redaction as defense in depth
- disables raw Fastify request logging and never logs request/response bodies, invoices, payment hashes, metadata, provider responses, or arbitrary exceptions
- normalizes provider and public API errors to stable Cherito categories without exception text or production stack traces
- requires explicit 0600 bootstrap-key delivery in production and development; the key is never written to logs or stdout
- minimizes public diagnostics and requires merchant authentication for node identity/synchronization details
- rejects ambiguous or malformed LND credential sources and documents the limits of environment-name checks
- adds privacy, retention, metrics, browser, and audit-log guidance

## Verification
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm run test` (91 tests passed: 86 gateway, 5 SDK)
- `pnpm run build`

## Remaining issue #22 work
Issue #22 also requires tenant-configurable database retention jobs, data export/deletion workflows, and Payment Link `noindex` behavior once Payment Links are part of the canonical branch. Those lifecycle features are intentionally outside this logging-focused PR, so this PR does not claim to close #22.

author: jpmvale
body:
Fecha a metade da pendência técnica aberta em #5: o backup do Mongo às 06:00 e a extração das 07:00 existiam **só** na VPS.

```
infra/
  bin/run-extractor.sh            extração das faturas, 07:00 UTC
  bin/backup-mongo.sh             dump do credit-card, 06:00 UTC
  crontab.expense-analyzer        as duas entradas, comentadas
  instalar.sh                     instala/atualiza, ou confere (--conferir)
```

Os scripts foram copiados como estão rodando — o `--conferir` contra a VPS confirma que batem byte a byte com `~/bin`.

## O recorte

Só o que é deste projeto. `com-alerta.sh`, `enviar-r2.sh` e `deploy.sh` servem também `coda` e `kindred`; trazê-los para cá poria a infra de outros projetos num repositório público onde ninguém que mexe neles iria procurar. O `infra/README.md` lista o que ficou de fora, por quê, e confirma que nenhum deles guarda segredo (tudo vem de `~/.secrets-vps`).

## O que o teste pegou

O instalador foi exercitado contra um `crontab` de mentira, em seis cenários. Dois resultados mudaram o desenho:

**1. A primeira instalação duplicaria os dois jobs.** As entradas antigas continuam fora do bloco, e acrescentar o bloco não as remove — backup e extração passariam a rodar duas vezes por dia. Cron não reclama de entrada repetida, e a segunda extração toparia com o lock de `syncRuns` e falharia por um motivo sem relação com a causa. O instalador agora detecta e se recusa:

```
Estas entradas já existem no crontab, fora do bloco gerenciado:
      6:0 6 * * * .../backup-mongo.sh
      15:0 7 * * * .../run-extractor.sh

Instalar assim as DUPLICARIA — cada job rodaria duas vezes por dia.
```

`--adotar` remove as antigas e assume o controle. É o estado desta VPS hoje.

**2. O crontab é reescrito por bloco marcado, nunca por arquivo inteiro** — um `crontab <arquivo>` apagaria as quatro entradas dos outros projetos junto.

Cenários cobertos: instalação com órfãs, adoção, idempotência (rodar duas vezes não muda nada), `--conferir` alinhado, `--conferir` com script editado à mão, e máquina limpa sem crontab nenhum.

## Ainda não instalado

Este PR só versiona. Aplicar na VPS é `infra/instalar.sh --adotar` depois de um deploy que carregue o commit — e isso mexe no crontab de produção, então fica para uma decisão explícita.

author: pcjun97
body:
Extends the existing Moes ADCBZI01 definition (added in #11560) to the `_TZ3210_rundhkxp` firmware.
Additive only — the already-supported `_TZ3210_sxtfesc6` variant is untouched.

### Changes
- **Fingerprint:** add `_TZ3210_rundhkxp` (previously fell through to the generic `TS030F`).
- **`configure`:** add `tuya.configureMagicPacket` + reporting. The definition had no `configure`, so it never polled the EF00 datapoints — `battery`, `illuminance`, `total_time`, `total_distance` stayed N/A. This unit exposes no `genPowerCfg`, so only `closuresWindowCovering` is bound (binding cluster 1 throws `invalid ep`).
- **`calibration` control:** new enum (`stop` / `calibrate` / `calibrate_reverse`) on the `tuyaMotorReversal` (0xF002) vendor attribute for travel-range calibration; the definition previously had no calibration control. The attribute is re-declared via `tuya.clusters.addTuyaClosuresWindowCoveringCluster()`.

### Testing
Tested on a `_TZ3210_rundhkxp` unit: recognition, open/close/stop/position, battery and illuminance reporting, and calibration (free-run to the open end, then `stop` to store the limit) all working. **Not** verified on `_TZ3210_sxtfesc6` (I don't own one) — but all changes are additive and inert if that firmware differs.

### References
Resolves Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt#31261. Same device also reported in Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt#31551. Button calibration behaviour documented in Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt#24605.

### Disclaimer
The device behaviour was reverse-engineered and debugged, and this definition written, with the assistance of Claude.

## Por qué bloquea el despliegue

El perfil `postgres` levantaba `NotImplementedError`. La task definition de ECS Fargate corre con `SPARK_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND=postgres`, así que **el contenedor moría en el arranque**. Sin esto no hay agente en la nube.

Había un segundo fallo del mismo tipo, más silencioso: el enum `Environment` solo aceptaba `local` y `agentcore`, y la task definition inyecta `SPARK_ENVIRONMENT=dev|prod`. Pydantic habría rechazado el valor y `Settings()` reventaba en el import, antes incluso de llegar a la persistencia.

## Resolución del DSN

`src/persistence/secrets.py` (nuevo), siguiendo el patrón que ya usa `src/auth/secret_loader.py`:

1. **`SPARK_POSTGRES_DSN`** como override local, usado verbatim. Estaba declarado en `settings` pero no lo leía nadie. Ahora sirve para probar el perfil contra un Postgres de docker sin cuenta AWS (hard rule #7).
2. **SSM → Secrets Manager → DSN**, camino de producción. La ruta es el contrato ADR-0002 `/spark-match/{env}/config/db-secret-arn`, la misma que lee `03-backend`.

El DSN lleva dos parámetros y los dos importan:

| Parámetro | Por qué |
|---|---|
| `sslmode=require` | RDS PostgreSQL 15+ rechaza conexiones sin cifrar |
| `options=-csearch_path%3Dagent` | Que las tablas de LangGraph no caigan en `public`, donde viven las migraciones del backend |

Usuario y contraseña van percent-encoded: una contraseña con `@` o `:` partiría el DSN en dos. Hay un test para eso.

## Schema `agent`

`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS agent` antes de los `setup()`, porque esos corren DDL.

Lo crea el agente y no una migración del backend, a propósito: el backend es dueño de `public` y no tiene por qué conocer las tablas de LangGraph. Comparten base de datos; no comparten namespace.

`postgres` es además el único perfil donde el **store de largo plazo** también sobrevive un restart — `sqlite` solo persiste el checkpointer, porque LangGraph no tiene un `BaseStore` sobre sqlite.

## Config

- `Environment` suma `dev` y `prod`.
- `db_secret_ssm_param` nuevo.
- `jwt_secret_ssm_param` pasa de `/spark-match/secret/jwt-arn` a `/spark-match/dev/config/jwt-secret-arn`. **La anterior no existe en ninguna cuenta AWS**: el parámetro nunca se habría resuelto.

## API

`/docs`, `/redoc` y `/openapi.json` quedan apagados fuera de `local`: publicaban el esquema completo de la API sin pedir autenticación. La listener rule del ALB (`modules/agent-service`) también los bloquea, pero eso protege solo la ruta por el ALB.

## Dependencias

`langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` y `psycopg[binary,pool]`. El extra `binary` evita compilar libpq en la imagen ARM64 del Dockerfile.

## Verificación

- **369 tests en verde**, `ruff check`, `ruff format` y `mypy` limpios.
- 7 tests nuevos que cubren el cableado con dobles, sin base real: override local, construcción del DSN desde el JSON de Secrets Manager, `sslmode`, `search_path`, percent-encoding de caracteres reservados, y los dos casos de payload inválido.
- `memory` y `sqlite` siguen corriendo sin AWS (hard rule #7): `boto3` se importa dentro de la función, no a nivel de módulo.

## Lo que no cubre

La conexión real contra RDS no se puede probar sin el RDS. Eso se valida en el rollout a dev.

author: jwiegley
body:
Closes #218.

Mac Lane *CWM* §I.2, the remark on p. 10: the set-based definition of a
category says exactly that a category is a **monoid for the product over its
object set** — composable pairs `A ×_O A` — the germ of internal categories and
of monoids in spans. Verified absent: the tree had no internal-category
definition, only prose disclaimers (`Construction/Enriched.v:83-85`,
`Theory/DoubleCategory.v:115`).

New file `Theory/Category/Monoid.v`, beside `Raw.v` and `Semi.v` — the
directory that collects re-presentations of the `Category` class, each with a
round trip as its payload. (Not `Construction/Span/Monoid.v`: nothing here is a
construction inside an ambient category.)

```coq
Graph                     (* two-sorted: objects strict, arrows a setoid *)
Composable G              (* the fibred product A ×_O A, with its UMP *)
SpanMonoid G              (* unit + multiplication, boundary + monoid laws up to ≈ *)
Category_from_SpanMonoid  : SpanMonoid G → Category                    (* unconditional *)
Category_SpanMonoid       : ∀ C, HomRigid C → SpanMonoid (Category_Graph C)
Category_monoid_iso       : C ≅[Cat] Category_from_SpanMonoid (Category_SpanMonoid C rigid)
```

## Honesty about strength

**Direction one needs nothing** — no UIP, no hypothesis, axiom-free.

**Direction two carries an explicit `HomRigid` hypothesis** (transport of a
morphism along object-equality proofs is proof-independent), implied by UIP on
objects (`HomRigid_of_ObjUIP`), which is axiom-free by Hedberg whenever object
equality is decidable — the discipline of `Construction/Grothendieck/Strict.v`.
The obstruction is real and **isolated at `sm_mul_respects`**: multiplying
along two different proofs of one composability equation composes with two
transports differing by a loop at the *intermediate* object, which the arrow
equivalence's freedom at the two outer objects cannot repair. In the set-based
reading Mac Lane intends, `O` is a set and the question does not arise.

**Round trips**: objects match definitionally in both directions (`eq_refl`);
arrows one way on the nose, the other up to `≈`; and starting from a `Category`
the comparison assembles into an isomorphism in `Cat`. In this library that is
the *same* strength as an equivalence of categories (Cat's hom-setoid is
`Functor_Setoid`; `Theory/Equivalence.v` converts the two freely) — and it is
the strongest packaging available, a `StrictCat` isomorphism being out of reach
without funext. The genuinely extra content is in the construction: both
functors identity-on-objects, one hom leg definitional.

**The necessity of `HomRigid` is itself a theorem** (added after audit):
`arrow_mul_respects_forces_UIP` — discharging the hypothesis uniformly in `C`
entails UIP for every type, via an `option A` countermodel whose `None` has
provably contractible loops by encode-decode, pinning the composite in a rigid
corner.

The universe story is measured rather than asserted (`Set Printing Universes`):
`Graph@{o a p}` keeps object and arrow levels independent.

Explicitly out of scope, per the issue: the general internal-category theory
over pullbacks, and functors between these presentations.

## Verification

- All constants "Closed under the global context" — zero axioms
- Full `make` green on Rocq 9.1: **487/487** `.vo`
- `make todo` identical at base and HEAD (89 = 89); admitted count unchanged
- New file registered in `_CoqProject`; CLAUDE.md index updated

author: solarcloud7
body:
The ledger was the one file left with no ceiling — the same shape this work has spent its time removing everywhere else. At the measured **~614 bytes per transfer** it grows slowly, but slow-and-unbounded is still unbounded.

Rotates the live file at **32 MB keeping 8 generations**: a stated ~288 MB ceiling, roughly half a million transfers. The bound is asserted in a test rather than left in a comment, because rotation is the only thing in this design that can delete audit history.

## The property that matters isn't the renaming

It's that rotation must not lose anything. **The loader now reads every generation, oldest first**, so a rotated transfer stays in the index and stays listed.

A loader that read only the live file would silently delete the history the ledger exists to keep — the exact failure the detail/ledger split was built to avoid, reintroduced by its own retention. Mutation-killed: stop reading the generations and three tests go red.

Two smaller decisions:
- Rotation runs **inside the queued write**, so a rename can never interleave with an append to the same path.
- **Size-based, not age-based** — the cost being bounded is disk, and rows arrive at whatever rate the cluster transfers. An age rule would erase a quiet cluster's entire history while failing to bound a busy one.
- Damage reports now name **which generation** they're in; a byte offset alone is ambiguous once more than one file exists.

## Entry slimming: deliberately not done

It was on the plan, and I'd told you I'd build it. Re-measuring first changed the answer:

| | when it was designed | now |
|---|---|---|
| detail store | 7.62 MB, **unbounded** | 1.97 MB on disk / 1.23 MB compact, **capped at 100** |
| slimming saves | ~40% of unbounded growth | **~0.46 MB** (`sourceVerification` is only 0.05 MB of it) |

The cost is unchanged: a fold-on-write / rehydrate-on-read asymmetry, plus a re-captured testkit fixture containing a late-verdict transfer to pin the keep-it-when-it-differs branch.

Retention already solved the problem slimming existed for. Taking on a permanent read/write asymmetry to save 0.46 MB of an already-bounded file is the wrong trade — I'd rather say so than build it because it was on the list. Worth revisiting if `transaction_log_detail_entries` is ever raised sharply.

Suite 330 pass / 0 fail; nine guards pass; all three build targets compile.

author: marchelo23
body:
Part of #9. Part of #10. Part of #21.

## Base and architecture

Rebuilt directly on current `main` after #37, #38, and #39. The old stacked commits and duplicate Payment Intent implementation were removed.

The resulting layer is:

`Payment Link -> canonical Payment Intent -> bounded Lightning provider -> authoritative transition/outbox`

The widget can only create through a public Payment Link or observe a scoped Payment Intent. It never receives a merchant API key and browser events are explicitly non-authoritative for fulfillment.

## Payment Links

- authenticated create/get/list/update/disable/rotate-slug routes, all tenant scoped
- fixed, open-amount, and donation modes with decimal-string satoshi validation
- 192-bit random public slugs and bounded deterministic pagination
- strict public response and request allowlists; merchant-owned fields cannot be overridden
- durable route/tenant/payload-bound creation idempotency
- atomic SQLite capacity reservation and Payment Intent/use-count commit
- concurrent `maxUses` enforcement; provider failure releases capacity
- expiry, disable, anti-indexing headers, and immediate old-slug invalidation
- distinct public IP, tenant, and link rate-limit policies

## Generic widget

- framework-independent Web Component with Payment Intent and Payment Link modes
- fixed links have no editable amount; open/donation modes collect bounded input
- scoped Authorization-header status requests, SSE reconnect, bounded polling fallback
- cleanup on terminal state/disconnect and duplicate-subscription prevention
- safe text-only rendering, local QR, BOLT11/deep links, countdown, copy controls
- accessible dialog/status/keyboard/focus behavior and extensible messages map
- stable safe events: `cherito:payment-created`, `pending`, `settled`, `expired`, and `error`
- npm ESM/browser/types entries and plain HTML example

## API and provider hardening

- strict Zod schemas, 16 KiB body limit, byte-bounded notes/metadata, and unknown-field rejection
- explicit trusted-proxy configuration; forwarded client IP is ignored by default
- separate auth, Payment Intent, Payment Link, webhook, and SSE policies
- hard Lightning call concurrency and queue limits
- global/per-tenant SSE connection limits with idempotent release
- production provider factory; only LND is selectable today
- LND polling is no longer advertised as native invoice streaming

## Webhooks

- canonical `t=<unix>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex>` raw-payload signatures with constant-time verification
- fresh monotonic timestamp/signature per attempt and stable logical event ID across retries
- existing #37 same-transaction terminal transition/outbox invariant preserved
- authenticated get/configure/disable/rotate/failed-delivery/replay/test APIs
- signing secrets returned only when created or rotated
- HTTPS in production, URL credential rejection, full IPv4/IPv6 private/reserved checks
- DNS resolution validates all addresses and the actual connection uses a pinned approved address
- redirects disabled; connection/total timeout and response bytes bounded

## Verification

Local repository commands pass:

- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm run test` (101 gateway, 5 widget, 5 SDK)
- `pnpm run build`

Tests cover fresh invoices, bounds/tampering, tenant isolation, idempotency, concurrent use limits, provider failure, trusted proxies, property-style malformed input, provider/SSE bounds, widget modes/fallback/cleanup/XSS/accessibility, signature/retry identity, SSRF/DNS pinning/redirect/timeout/response limits, and existing Payment Intent recovery/outbox invariants.

## Remaining limitations

- The built-in rate limiter is single-process; multi-replica deployments need a shared atomic implementation.
- Existing webhook signing-secret columns in current `main` are plaintext. This PR does not misuse the Payment Intent cipher or invent a second crypto format; purpose-separated encryption/migration remains dependent on #19.
- As with providers that offer no idempotent invoice-create primitive, a process crash after the provider accepts an invoice but before local persistence can leave an orphan provider invoice. Capacity reservations are safely released at startup, but provider-side idempotent creation is needed to close that external transaction gap completely.
- LND is the only production provider selected by the factory.

These limitations are why #9, #10, and #21 remain `Part of`, not `Closes`.

author: jwaldrip
body:
Verified the current MCP revision against the live spec rather than the notes in `docs/`. **`2026-07-28` is current, and it is the revision that made the protocol core stateless**: no `initialize` handshake, no session, no `Mcp-Session-Id`. Every request declares its own version in `_meta` and the server accepts or rejects each one independently.

That suits Relic exactly, because it already held nothing between calls. The server can now be restarted, round-robined behind a load balancer, or run one-shot without a client noticing.

## What was missing

The stdio-only server pinned the right revision but did not implement it:

- **Per-request version validation**, with `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` (`-32022`) carrying the supported list so a client can retry rather than guess.
- **`server/discover`** in the shape the revision mandates.
- **Dual-era support.** The handshake-based revisions are still answered, because a client that only speaks the newest revision is unusable in most of the agents this product exists to serve.

## The HTTP transport enforces the headers rather than accepting them

`MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, and `Mcp-Name` must agree with the body, with the base64 sentinel decoded before comparison, and a mismatch is refused with `-32020`. A gateway routing on the header while the server executes on the body is a split-brain with security consequences, not a cosmetic inconsistency.

`Origin` is validated to defeat DNS rebinding, and the bind is loopback by default: this process can read any file its user can, so putting it on a network interface hands that reach to the network.

`GET` and `DELETE` return `405`, since sessions and standalone streams are gone in this revision. An unknown method returns `404` with `-32601`, which is what distinguishes a modern server from a legacy one that simply does not host the path.

## Why this is not a hosted MCP server

Worth stating in the README, since it is the question everybody asks: a remote server would have to receive your file in order to encrypt it, which destroys the product. Zero-knowledge is a consequence of the encryption happening on the machine that already holds the plaintext, not a feature layered on top. The transport can be stdio or HTTP; the process runs next to the file either way.

## Verified live

Both transports were driven against the deployed service, including a real publish over each. 406 tests.

## Security fixes

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| Dashboard showed platform-wide metrics (all-tenant revenue, recent repairs/invoices with links) to **any** staff user | Metrics injected only for superusers; non-superuser staff get the plain model index |
| User Management page listed every user across all tenants for any staff user | Superuser-only (403 otherwise) |
| Stripe Connect accounts page exposed every shop's Stripe account status to any staff user | Superuser-only |
| Platform Config page let **any staff user change platform fee percentages** (GET and POST) | Superuser-only, verified by POST test |
| `Deactivate users` bulk action could deactivate superusers or your own account | Never self; staff/superusers only deactivatable by superusers |
| `/admin/login/` had no rate limit (app login is throttled, admin login was stock Django) | 10 POSTs / 5 min / IP → 429 |

## Bug fixes
- **User Management roles were always "Unassigned"**: the template probed `user.technician_set`/`customeruser_set`, which don't exist (both relations are OneToOne → `.technician`/`.customeruser`), and Django templates fail silently. Roles are now computed server-side with prefetches.
- Custom admin views now pass `admin.site.each_context()`, so the RSWR site header/sidebar render instead of the "Django administration" fallback; duplicate page h1s removed.
- `admin_dashboard`: `now`/`month_start` hoisted out of the tenants try-block (latent NameError swallowed by except).
- Audit log user link + search-result links use `{% url %}`/`reverse()` instead of hardcoded `/admin/...` paths.

## UI overhaul
- New shared stylesheet `static/css/rs_admin.css`: design tokens (light **and** dark via the admin's `data-theme` mechanism), stat tiles with status accent strips, card tables, labeled status badges, filter pills, buttons.
- All five custom admin pages rewritten on the shared system: dashboard index, global search, user management, Stripe Connect accounts, platform config. Emoji/inline-style clutter removed; values wear ink colors with accent strips carrying state; badges always pair color with a label.
- Verified visually in light + dark mode with seeded data (dashboard, search results, user management, connect accounts, platform config).

body:
## Что и зачем

Четыре бага из живого плейтеста владельца. Каждый разобран до причинной цепочки с файл:строка (следствие: 4 следователя + архивист по свежим мерджам + скептики), починен минимально и заперт тестом. Пять коммитов — по одному на баг + доводка по вердиктам скептиков.

### 1. «Корабли не видят пути вообще» — `fix(core)` право прохода
Гейт D2 (#452) резал кратчайший путь ПОСЛЕ построения, а Dijkstra дипломатию не знал: один мирный узел на единственном кратчайшем пути читался как «пути нет вообще». Боты walk-in-захватами быстро засеивают узлы — к середине партии флоты не ходили никуда, включая свои планеты. Теперь `planRoute` принимает предикат вето (цель намеренно исключена — посадка на мирный мир по-прежнему отбивается как право прохода, чтобы работал warPrompt), а movement при сработавшем гейте перепланирует маршрут В ОБХОД мимо топологического кэша (дипломатический маршрут зависит от владельцев и стансов — в кэш не кладётся). Отказ остаётся только когда обхода нет. Клиентское зеркало: warPrompt «объявить войну» больше не выскакивает, когда войны не нужно. Ключ `err.no-right-of-way` добавлен в обе локали (код долетал сырым английским). Тесты-ромб — у гейта #452 их не было вовсе: обход берётся; обхода нет → отказ; цель мирная → отказ; война открывает прямую; детерминизм обхода.

### 2. «Технология постоянно открывается и закрывается» — `fix(proto)`
Окно #tech живо ререндерится каждые ~500 мс безусловным innerHTML, а у `.tt-mwin` анимация появления стояла на самом классе — каждый тик пересоздавал модалку и переигрывал `ttpop`: досье «схлопывалось и выпрыгивало» дважды в секунду. Анимация переведена на одноразовый класс `.pop` (ставится только на реальное открытие), у repaint появился кэш разметки в духе `lastCmdHtml`. Проверено вживую: модалка пережила три ререндера **тем же DOM-узлом**, анимация сыграла один раз.

### 3. «Налоговую управу можно поставить несколько раз + отказы без остановки» — `fix(proto)`, два дефекта
**Дубль:** замок плитки действовал только на `pcUi() && !NET` (на телефоне и на сервере плитка оставалась кликабельной), а кодекс проверял только «уже стоит» — СТРОЯЩЕЕСЯ здание ещё не в `p.buildings`, и «Построить здесь» предлагал второй экземпляр всю стройку. Замок теперь везде + одна точка опоры в `enqueueBuild` (любой вход, включая будущие). **Отказы без остановки:** это не очередь (она consume-on-issue) — это покадровый `autoEngage()`: флот с авто-штурмом у мира, с чьим владельцем МИР, пережимал обречённый штурм 60 раз в секунду → `E_FORBIDDEN` → тост + звук (слышимым цикл сделал SND-1). Добавлено зеркало гейта из `serverDrivers.ts` — там этот же гейт уже стоял с комментарием «the driver re-issued the doomed pair on every wake», но в клиентский близнец отзеркален не был. Скептик нашёл ВТОРОЙ такой же цикл — `resolvePendingMerges` без consume-on-reject; закрыт через возврат исхода из `playerOrder`. Ключи `err.already-built/queued/paused` добавлены в локали.

### 4. «Текстурки заполненности трюма съезжают» — `fix(proto)`
У стоящего флота поза радиальная, и хвост (пипсы трюма, «×N») смотрел ВНУТРЬ орбиты. После ужатия кольца (44→31, на дальнем зуме ×0.5 = 15.5px) ряды пипсов легли прямо на спрайт планеты. Для стоящей позы хвост разворачивается наружу — не касается диска ни при каком радиусе кольца; в полёте без изменений. Геометрия вынесена в `markerTail.ts` и заперта тестами (включая «без разворота — воспроизведение бага»).

## Проверка

- [x] `pnpm run check` зелёный — 2357 тестов, 201 файл (было 2341/199 на main)
- [x] Живая сборка: приказы движения уходят, техно-досье не мигает, дубль налоговой невозможен (плитка серая, `enqueueBuild` отсекает), гейт-паритет и i18n целы
- [x] Ядро: изменение движения детерминировано (тест на идентичность повторного вызова), чистота не тронута, RouteCache не отравлен дипломатическими маршрутами
- [x] Зоны: core (движение) + proto (UI) + локаль — сознательно один PR: это пакет плейтест-фиксов владельца, коммиты атомарны по багам

author: schmug
body:
Adopts the autonomous issue→fix→merge loop from [schmug/shipofclaudius#63](https://github.com/schmug/shipofclaudius/pull/63).

## ⚠️ WIRED, NOT ARMED

`secrets.FACTORY_GH_TOKEN` does not exist, so the `advance` and `land` jobs **no-op with a clear notice** rather than half-running. Nothing can auto-merge today, and three independent things still gate that — see [`.factory/README.md`](.factory/README.md):

1. **`fix-verified` is human-minted.** `requireFixtureEvidence: false` because this repo has no reproduction harness, so the reproduce phase has no mechanical definition of done.
2. **The write token must be a distinct identity from @schmug.** GitHub forbids self-approval, so a code-owner token can never satisfy `require_code_owner_review` on `main-protection`. That's #299.
3. **There is no rollback lever.** Production deploys leave GitHub entirely via the Cloudflare Git integration, so a bad auto-merged change can't be reverted from here.

## What's here

**`.factory/gate.json`** — the merge gate's config, read from `main` on every run and never from the PR. The denylist mirrors `.github/CODEOWNERS` and **adds** the security/money paths that aren't currently code-owned: `src/auth/**`, `src/account/**`, `src/billing/**`, `src/webhooks/**`, `src/rate-limit-do.ts`, `mta-sts-worker/**`, `scripts/routine-gate/**`. `.factory/**`, `.github/workflows/**` and CODEOWNERS are added *automatically* by the gate and cannot be removed by this file — a PR must never be able to widen the rules it's judged by.

**`.github/workflows/factory.yml`** — `killswitch` → `advance` → `land`.

The `land` job **runs no model at all**: it's `gh` plus a zero-dependency Node program, so text injected into a public issue body has nothing to act on — an injected instruction cannot move a `<=` comparison. It checks out the **base** ref, never the PR head, which is what makes the `pull_request_target` trigger safe; there's no `npm ci` and no build step in it. `workflow_dispatch` inputs are allowlist-validated before they reach the driver's prompt, and all GitHub context flows through `env:`, never interpolated into `run:` bodies. Action SHAs match the existing pins so the action-pin integrity check passes.

**`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`** — the repo had none at all. The bug form makes the ` ```scope ` block **required**, which is the gate's single most common escalation cause.

## Verified end to end

Ran the real gate binary against this exact `.factory/gate.json`:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| A clean, in-scope PR | **exit 0 — merge** |
| **Real PR #653** (dependabot) | exit 2 — unallowlisted author, no `fix-verified`, no `Closes #N`, `mta-sts-worker/**` risk path, 382 lines > 250, no scope block |
| Self-editing `.factory/**` / `.github/workflows/**` / CODEOWNERS | exit 2 — `no_risk_paths` |
| Touching `src/analyzers/**` · `src/shared/scoring.ts` · `src/billing/**` | exit 2 — `no_risk_paths` |
| Scope drift · oversize · pending required check · `BLOCKED` merge state | exit 2 — the matching condition |

That exercise also caught a real bug in the gate package (`gh api` takes no `-R`, which would have failed `ci_green` on every PR forever) — fixed upstream in shipofclaudius#63 before this PR was opened.

## Settled empirically while wiring this

`.github/CODEOWNERS` is **enforcing**, not advisory. The `main-protection` ruleset is `active` with `require_code_owner_review: true`, `required_approving_review_count: 0`, one required check (`check`), and **no bypass actors**. `CLAUDE.md` is correct; `MAINTAINERS.md`, `docs/OSPS-DEVIATIONS.md` and `.claude/workflows/pr-triage.js` all say advisory and are wrong. Filed separately rather than mixed into this PR.

## Not in this PR

The reproduction harness, the coverage floor, the rollback lever, the bot identity, and the `src/index.ts` bottleneck are filed as follow-up issues.

author: mcinb
body:
Closes #75

## What

`annotate_style_from_image` made one vision call per page in a serial loop, so a
document's styling pass cost N × round-trip latency for no reason — the pages are
independent, each touching only its own elements' `dg:style`. They now fan out
over a bounded thread pool.

Rather than add a fourth hand-rolled `ThreadPoolExecutor` to this package, the
shape is extracted into one internal helper (`dgml_core/concurrency.py`) and
`ocr.extract_text_ocr` migrates onto it too.

## Notes for review

**The helper takes no policy flag and no callbacks.** The existing fan-out sites
use three different failure policies, but that difference belongs to the *unit of
work*, not the executor — a fail-fast executor over a function that never raises
*is* a best-effort executor. What can't be pushed into `fn` is
cancel-pending-on-first-failure, which is load-bearing in the OCR path, so the
executor owns that and callers wanting per-item independence make `fn` total.

**OCR behavior is preserved.** Same worker cap, same first-`BaseException` /
cancel-pending / drain / re-raise. Two deltas, both benign: aggregation now runs
in page order (the counters are order-independent sums), and `max_concurrency=1`
now runs inline on the calling thread. `tests/test_ocr.py` is unmodified.

**Style pages are fully independent** — `_styles_for_page` returns its error
rather than raising, so nothing is ever cancelled and every page runs. Output is
byte-identical to the serial version: workers see only `str`/`Path`/`LLMConfig`,
and every read of and write to the XML tree happens on the calling thread, in
document order.

**Per-page failures are no longer silent.** They were swallowed by a bare
`except Exception: continue`. They're now named on stderr under `--debug`, with a
model-unreachability failure summarized once rather than once per page (reusing
`llm.is_model_reachability_error`).

## Deliberately not done

- No cancellation on the style path — page independence was judged more important
  than the retry storm a bad `api_base` causes. Easy follow-up if it bites.
- Concurrency is a keyword arg, not a config key, mirroring `extract_text_ocr`.
  It exists so tests can force the serial path.
- `grounded._run_phase3` and `generation/pipeline.py` keep their own pools.

## Measured

On a 6-page OCR document (`gemini/gemini-flash-lite-latest`, 3 alternating
serial/parallel reps to spread API-latency drift across both arms, median):

| | runs (s) | median |
|---|---|---|
| serial (`max_concurrency=1`) | 13.23, 14.75, 12.53 | **13.23s** |
| parallel (`max_concurrency=8`) | 3.44, 3.85, 3.00 | **3.44s** |

**3.8× — 9.8s saved.** All 6 pages issue a real vision call in both arms; the
gain is wall-clock overlap of network latency, nothing else.

How to read it: with 6 pages under an 8-worker cap they all dispatch at once, so
wall-clock collapses to the slowest single page and 6× is the ceiling here — 3.8×
means per-page latency varies by roughly that factor. A longer document trends
toward the 8-worker cap rather than beyond it, and a 1–2 page document sees
nothing (it takes the inline path and spawns no thread at all).

## Testing

`scripts/verify.sh` green — ruff, format, `mypy --strict`, `pytest` (**1490
passing**), license audit. No dependency changes.

21 new tests. The ones that make this safe to merge: determinism of the
serialized output parametrized over `{1, 2, 3, 8}` workers with calls completing
out of order; failure isolation asserting *all* pages still ran; and one
`style_annotate` usage row per page end-to-end, asserted as a sorted set since
append order is now completion order.

Both parallel-dispatch guards use a `threading.Barrier` with a timeout, so a
regression fails fast instead of hanging CI — verified by mutation (forcing
`DEFAULT_STYLE_CONCURRENCY = 1` fails the dispatch test).

No public API or output-schema changes; `dgml_core/__init__.py` is untouched.
