author: adinailson88
body:
Décima rodada. Empilha sobre a [PR #196](https://github.com/adinailson88/classificacao-chamados/pull/196), que ainda não entrou em `main`, e incorpora um *merge* de `main` (atualizações de JSON do painel). Base: `agent/referencia-humana-auditoria`.

## 1. Auditoria dos testes vigentes

A unidade estatística do Cochran Q e dos 21 McNemar era a **linha**, embora o bootstrap já reamostrasse grupos. Linhas do mesmo grupo textual eram tratadas como independentes: 4.546 das 13.972 avaliadas, ou 32,54%, dividem texto normalizado com outra, e um grupo chega a 219 linhas.

O efeito de desenho medido — variância sob reamostragem de conglomerados sobre a variância binomial — fica entre **4,47** (LinearSVC) e **8,83** (Naive Bayes). Em erro padrão, a precisão declarada por linha era de 2,1 a 3,0 vezes maior do que a amostra sustenta. Os valores de *p* eram, portanto, **anticonservadores por construção**.

## 2. Inferência refeita, compatível com o agrupamento

`src/inferencia_agrupada.py` (novo, offline, sem retreino e sem acesso à planilha):

- **teste global preservado, distribuição trocada.** A estatística Q continua adequada por ser pareada e binária, mas a referência qui-quadrado pressupõe independência. Passa a ser empírica, por permutação do rótulo de modelo **dentro de cada grupo**: Q = 2.661,04, *p* < 0,0005 em 2.000 permutações. A troca está justificada no Método;
- **21 comparações pareadas** por permutação com troca de sinal da diferença de acertos por grupo (10.000 repetições), com Holm sobre a família;
- **intervalos** por bootstrap de conglomerados da diferença.

Referências metodológicas acrescentadas: Good (2005), Anderson e ter Braak (2003), Field e Welsh (2007), Cameron, Gelbach e Miller (2008), Cochran (1977).

**Cada comparação reporta** diferença observada, IC95% da diferença, grupos que favorecem cada modelo, empates, *d* pareado por grupo e *p* ajustado. Exemplo (LinearSVC × SGD): +1,60 p.p., IC [0,0118; 0,0204], 533 grupos a favor contra 308, 8.894 empatados, *d* = 0,077.

**Nenhum dos 21 vereditos muda** ao corrigir a unidade: os mesmos 19 pares significativos e os mesmos 2 empatados (Extra Trees × Regressão Logística e Extra Trees × SGD). Isso é resultado da análise, não premissa; o que muda é a magnitude do *p*, em ordens de grandeza.

## 3. Pressupostos periféricos fora do corpo

A antiga Subseção 4.9 virou **"Inferência sob dependência textual"** e mantém apenas dependência por grupos, bootstrap agrupado, teste global, comparações corrigidas, efeito e incerteza. Saíram do corpo: Shapiro-Wilk, Levene, VIF entre confianças, outliers, Zuur *et al.*, e a correlação confiança-acerto usada como prova de calibração. Foram para a **Tabela S15**, e 15 referências que só as sustentavam saíram da lista (Tukey, Hodge e Austin, Zuur, Shapiro e Wilk, Razali e Wah, Ogunleye, Marquardt, O'Brien, Kornbrot, Tate, Spearman, Dietterich, Chan, Lima, Minderer). Nenhuma referência ficou órfã.

## 4. Categorias raras e as 88 linhas

`src/sensibilidade_classes_raras.py` (novo):

| Convenção | Rótulos | Macro-F1 do LinearSVC |
|---|---:|---:|
| A — categorias avaliadas | 41 | 0,6684 |
| B — taxonomia completa, F1 = 0 nas ausentes | 50 | 0,5481 |
| C — famílias do primeiro nível | 14 | 0,6816 |

Cobertura: **99,37% das linhas** e **82% das categorias**. Alternativas medidas: k = 4 recuperaria 1 categoria e 4 linhas; k = 3 recuperaria 3 e 10 — recusado por ser decisão de protocolo tomada **depois** de observado o resultado. Abstenção não recupera categoria alguma. Avaliação hierárquica fecha a lacuna de categorias, mas não a de linhas. Para as cinco exclusões por estratificação, o artefato registra `Informação insuficiente para verificar.` sem reexecutar o particionador.

A Subseção 3.5 declara em negrito que **o desempenho principal não cobre as 50 categorias**.

## 5. Ganho líquido deixa de supor custos iguais em silêncio

`src/utilidade_reclassificacao.py` (novo): `U = b×corrigidos − c×prejudicados − r×revisados`, normalizada por `b`, com **ρ = c/b** e **λ = r/b** adimensionais. Nenhum valor monetário é atribuído.

- **Política A, aplicação direta:** ρ de equilíbrio de **0,2047** no LinearSVC, 0,0817 no Naive Bayes. A utilidade é negativa em toda a grade de ρ (0,25 a 4). A reescrita exigiria que estragar um registro custasse menos de um quinto do que vale corrigir outro — hipótese que a assimetria do dano contradiz.
- **Política B, triagem por divergência:** precisão da fila de **18,53%** contra taxa de alteração de 4,25% na base congelada, **enriquecimento de cerca de quatro vezes** sobre revisão aleatória. λ de equilíbrio coincide com a precisão. Declarado como teto, pois supõe que a revisão devolve a referência.

O ganho líquido simples permanece como resultado principal, agora identificado como o caso ρ = 1, λ = 0.

## 6. Sincronização

Tabelas suplementares **S12** (21 pares completos), **S13** (classes raras), **S14** (utilidade) e **S15** (pressupostos) geradas por `src/tabelas_suplementares_canonicas.py`. Matriz de proveniência ampliada: os oito artefatos derivados conferem `hash_corpus = 1e476243`, zero divergências. Planos e `04_artigo/README.md` atualizados sem acumular histórico.

## 7. Tamanho

Corpo científico de **13.350 para 13.323 palavras**; fonte de 17.181 para 16.851. A antiga Figura 5, de pares de confusão, saiu por duplicar a Figura 4: o artigo passou de sete para **seis figuras**, com seis tabelas no corpo.

## Validação

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` → **498 testes, OK** (39 novos)
- `python -m py_compile src/*.py` → OK
- `python src/matriz_proveniencia.py` → 0 artefatos com hash divergente, 0 do congelamento ausentes, 2 falsos positivos conhecidos (`0,7781` é o acordo bruto do SGD)

## Pendência real

O **PDF não foi regerado**: o ambiente local não dispõe de xelatex nem de Docker. O workflow `artigo_pdf.yml` o regenera ao entrar em `main`. O PDF publicado tem 28 páginas; a meta de ~22 continua aberta, e a remoção de uma figura e de 15 referências deve reduzir uma a duas páginas, o que ainda não fecha a diferença.

author: hshimizu
body:
Closes #258 and #254, plus a third difference recorded on #258. One change, because all three live in `logs_api/encode.rs::detected_fields_response`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| zero fields | `{"fields":[],"limit":1000}` | `{}` |
| unattributed field | `"parsers":[]` | `"parsers":null` |
| json field | key absent | `"jsonPath":["msg"]` |

`limit` is untouched alongside a populated `fields` — the reference emits it there.

### The third difference was ours to correct

Our encoder documented `"parsers":[]` as a deliberate deterministic-shape choice. `logproto.proto:481 @ v3.7.4` gives `parsers` a bare jsontag with no `omitempty`, and `detected_fields.go:64-66` maps the empty slice to nil before marshaling — so `null` is the reference's deliberate spelling. Our rationale only ever justified *always emitting the key*, which the reference does anyway.

### The array order cannot be matched, and that is the honest finding

The first commit's subject claimed the body matches "byte for byte". **That is false for a populated body.** The reference's field order is Go map iteration order at three sites — the single-response build (`detected_fields.go:57-75`, map at `:282-284`), the sharded `MergeFields` (`storage/detected/fields.go:54-101`), and no sort on the way out (`marshal.go:182-188`). Go withholds any reproducibility guarantee, so there is no reproducible order to mirror.

Our label sort is therefore the correct pin, now ledgered as `detected-fields-array-order-pinned` rather than left as an accident. Every exactness claim in the docs, the encoder and the golden's name is scoped to the reference's single-response path.

### The mounting oracle had to move first

`api_conformance` proved this endpoint was wired up by recognising its **body** — and the new zero-field body is `{}`, which an empty database legitimately returns. So the old oracle would have passed on a completely stubbed handler. It now probes the same route with `X-Pulsus-Explain: 1` and asserts `explain.result_type == "detected_fields"`. Mutant: stubbing the handler to return bare `{}` for every request leaves the shape assertion green and fails the new oracle.

### Three rounds on one memory bound, each the previous fix one step along

`jsonPath` needed read-path plumbing, not an encoder edit — a `JsonPaths` sink through `run_mode_into` → `run_json` → `flatten_json`, enabled only by the detected-fields probe, mirroring the reference's `NewJSONParser(true)`. The ordinary query path is one `Option` branch with zero allocation.

Then: the capture cloned every raw ancestor per leaf **before** accounting — and worse than reported, since a whitespace-trimming ancestor contributes zero bytes to label names but its full length to every descendant path, making it invisible to the key charges by construction. Then the capture **stack** itself grew with nesting depth ahead of any charge, and the peak-live-set statement was wrong for the second time.

The enumeration now lives **in the code**, one row per owned container — `stack` (depth), `slots` (label count), the per-leaf path spine, each path component — each charged before it grows, with the argument for why there is no fifth.

### A gate that could not fail, declared rather than written

serde_json caps nesting at 127 wrappers and an over-deep line is refused before the flatten runs, so the stack peaks at 12,192 bytes against a 64 MiB ledger and **no test can observe its charge**. Reintroducing the defect reddened nothing — predicted before running. Rather than write a breach gate that cannot fail, the premise is pinned instead: 126 parses and enters capture, 127 is refused, so a recursion-limit move reddens it.

### Recorded, not mirrored

The reference's `MergeFields` drops `JsonPath` when it rebuilds each field (`fields.go:92-99`), so a sharded reference deployment silently loses paths a single-shard one returns. Registered as its own exception, `detected-fields-jsonpath-survives-merge`, after first being buried inside a row about array order where nobody would find it.

### Validation

nextest 5665 passed / 0 failed, doctests clean, clippy `-D warnings` clean with no new `#[allow]`, fmt clean, actionlint OK. Live on ClickHouse 24.8: `logs_detected_live`, `api_conformance`, `logs_api_live`, `query_log_gates`, `explain_indexes`. Seven mutants across the branch, each with its direction predicted before running. The sweep — `git grep` over `"fields"`, `parsers`, `jsonPath`, `detected_fields`, `'"limit":1000'` plus a route enumeration over `e2e/ test/ ci/ xtask/` — found four encoder goldens, `api_conformance.rs`, `support/manifest.rs`, `logs_detected_live.rs`, `docs/api.md` and the corpus provenance notes; the CI-authoritative e2e harness asserts nothing on this endpoint.

## Summary

Implements the roadmap-reserved v0.15.35 Character Collaborator completion-routing stage on the Godot 4.7.1 baseline.

### Safe destination routing
- completed Blueprint/Detailed Workspace Draft payloads no longer immediately mutate Workspace
- after generation, Workspace opens an explicit destination chooser
- untouched placeholder character → **Populate Current Empty Character (Recommended)**
- occupied character → **Create New Character in This Project (Recommended)**
- **Create as New Project** is available as a non-destructive alternate and saves the new project to the Library while leaving the current Workspace project unchanged
- an occupied current character is never overwritten in v0.15.35; replacement remains reserved for v0.15.36 Compare & Apply

### Empty-slot detection
- checks concept, metadata, template generation fields, card content, Alternative Greetings, Lorebook/extensions, assets and attachments
- does not treat IDs/timestamps/default Untitled naming as authored content
- current empty-slot completion preserves the existing character ID/created-at identity

### Materialisation + provenance
- retains Blueprint and Detailed Workspace Draft handoff formats
- preserves Alternative Greetings and Character Lorebook for detailed drafts
- carries v0.15.34 derivation/source provenance into the completed standalone character

### Pending completion recovery
- cancelling the destination chooser keeps the already-generated payload pending
- Author → **Place Pending Collaborator Completion…** reopens routing without another provider request
- pending completions are scoped to their originating project and are cleared when another project is loaded

### Release integration
- running build displays **v0.15.35**
- broad regression default advances to `regression_suites_v01535.json`
- `roadmap.md` is brought forward through the previously merged v0.15.34 and current v0.15.35 phases without removing v0.15.36/v0.15.37 or the unresolved GLX investigation

author: kavon
body:
LifetimeResolution is a rethink of how lifetimes of values are canonicalized after SILGen. It's currently experimental and enabled with frontend flag `-enable-lifetime-resolution`. As a first step, we're focusing on resolving `copy_value` and then inserting the appropriate `destroy_value`'s. 

This pass takes SIL that is not valid OSSA, because it is missing the needed `copy_value` instructions (currently implemented by deleting them just prior, in RemoveSILGenLifetimes). The "resolving" part of the name is the process of inserting them only where they need to go, based on operand ownership / uses in SIL. This yields copy-minimal SIL (similar to what running MandatoryCopyPropagation would give you).

We'd like to have this go further, and have SILGen not emit any `destroy_value`'s, either, instead emitting a higher-level `end_scope`  instruction that denotes the end of lexical scopes. LifetimeResolution would then insert destroys where they need to go (strictly after last use, or with respect to deinit barriers for lexical values) up to those end_scope limits. The existence of dependent values and an explicit `consume` operator already makes these destroys coming out of SILGen invalid anyway, so this pass aims to be the point at which they're resolved correctly.

author: lovon-spec
body:
## What

The Daemon-update panel is served on every OS, but the release channel's produce/install gating was keyed on `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`, and dev-produce on a Windows source checkout collides with the OS lock on the running `intendant.exe`. This PR makes the daemon side platform-honest:

1. **Per-platform asset lookup replaces the compile-time OS check.** One declared table (`RELEASE_ASSET_LANES` in `src/bin/caller/handover/update_lane.rs`: platform/arch → expected release-asset name shape + install kind; only the two macOS app rows exist today) now drives `produce_refusal`, the channel catalog, the status `unavailable` note, the release chip's `one_click`/`reason` fact, and `select_release_asset`. A platform without published assets refuses by name — `no Windows release assets are published yet — rebuild from source on this platform` — and the refusal ages out automatically once that platform's row is added: there is no separate gating change to make.

2. **Windows dev-produce lock fix (stage-aside-then-rename).** The source-lane build's final copy lands at the watched path, which is the running daemon's own exe — Windows locks it against write/delete but permits a same-volume rename. The produce job now vacates the path by renaming the running binary aside before the build (sweeping stale set-asides from earlier produces), and restores it if the build fails so the watched path is never left vacant. Unix behavior is byte-equivalent (the aside step is gated to Windows; cargo's unlink+relink needs no help there).

3. **Plain-binary install arm: prepared seam, cleanly refusing (judgment call).** A full download→stage→swap arm for non-macOS assets would be speculative: no Windows/Linux daemon assets exist, their archive layout is undefined (that assets lane is a separate track), and no install flavor routes to the consumer lane on those platforms today. So `ReleaseInstallKind::PlainBinary` + `install_plain_binary_release` land as the named seam — the install fork consults the table row's kind, and the stub refuses with honest copy instead of guessing at an artifact layout. Filling the arm rides with the first non-macOS table row.

4. **Pinned per-platform strings.** Unit tests assert the exact refusal copy per host (Windows/Linux consumer + source arms, arch-qualified variant, `one_click:false` reasons), pin the table to its current two macOS rows, and pin the set-aside/restore dance hermetically.

5. **Docs.** `docs/src/windows-support.md` gains a Self-Update Lane section stating current truth: panel exists everywhere, dev-produce works on Windows including the lock fix, release install awaits published assets.

The e2e cross-channel refusal pin is updated to a platform-stable substring (`build from main`) since the source-install refusal copy now folds the platform fact in on asset-less hosts.

Out of scope by design: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the Windows/Linux asset lanes belong to a separate track) and the dashboard fragments (the panel is fully payload-driven; no client copy changes needed, `static/app.html` untouched).

author: woo-in
body:
## 관련 이슈

closes #62

## 작업 내용

배포본에는 vite proxy 가 없어 브라우저가 **자기 자신의 `/api`** 를 호출했다.

Cloudflare Worker 가 `/api/*` 를 백엔드로 넘기게 해서 개발(vite proxy)과 같은 구조로 맞췄다.

```
                    run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]
                              │
      /api/*  ────────────────┴──▶  worker/index.js ──HTTP──▶ 백엔드(Elastic Beanstalk)
      그 외    ───────────────────▶  dist (정적 자산)
                                       └─ 매칭 실패 시 index.html (SPA 폴백)
```

브라우저가 보기엔 화면과 API 가 같은 오리진이라:

- **CORS 설정 불필요** — 크로스 오리진이 아니라 preflight 자체가 발생하지 않는다
- **`SameSite=Strict` 그대로 통과** — refreshToken 쿠키가 전송된다. **백엔드 수정 없음**
- **mixed content 회피** — 백엔드가 `http://` 여도 브라우저는 Worker 와 https 로만 대화한다

### 변경 파일

| 파일 | 내용 |
| --- | --- |
| `worker/index.js` (신규) | 투명 프록시. 응답을 손대지 않아 `Set-Cookie` 가 그대로 흐른다. 실패해도 백엔드와 같은 봉투 모양으로 응답한다 |
| `wrangler.jsonc` | `main` · `run_worker_first` · `not_found_handling` · `vars.BACKEND_ORIGIN` |
| `src/api/client.js` | 봉투 아닌 200 응답을 `ApiError('INVALID_RESPONSE')` 로 막는다 |
| `.env.example` · `CLAUDE.md` | `VITE_API_BASE_URL` 은 개발·배포 모두 `/api` 이고 백엔드 주소는 `BACKEND_ORIGIN` 이라는 것을 명시 |
| `package.json` | `wrangler` devDependency 고정 + `deploy` / `preview:worker` 스크립트 |
| `.gitignore` | `.wrangler/` |

### 백엔드 주소가 `VITE_*` 가 아닌 이유

`VITE_*` 는 **빌드 타임**에 번들로 박힌다. 백엔드 주소를 거기 넣으면 브라우저 번들에 노출되고
주소가 바뀔 때마다 재빌드해야 한다. A안에서 백엔드 주소를 아는 것은 Worker 하나뿐이므로
`wrangler.jsonc` 의 `vars` 에 두었다. 런타임 설정이라 재빌드가 필요 없다.
그래서 **`.env` / `VITE_API_BASE_URL` 은 값이 바뀌지 않았다.**

### SPA 폴백을 같이 넣은 이유

`not_found_handling` 이 없어 `createWebHistory` 라우터의 경로(`/home` 등)가
새로고침·직접 진입에서 전부 404 였다. 지금은 로그인이 아예 안 돼서 거기까지 가보질 못해
드러나지 않았을 뿐이고, 프록시를 붙여 로그인이 성공하는 순간 바로 부딪힌다.
같은 파일 같은 블록이라 함께 처리했다.

## 검증

`npm run lint`, `npm run build` 통과. `npx wrangler dev` 로 배포본 그대로 띄워 확인:

| 확인 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| `/home` (SPA 폴백) | `200 text/html` — `index.html` |
| `/api/user-cards` (프록시) | `401` + `{"success":false,"code":"UNAUTHORIZED",...}`, `Server: nginx` — **실제 백엔드 응답** |
| `BACKEND_ORIGIN` 미설정 | `500` + `{"code":"PROXY_MISCONFIGURED",...}` |
| 백엔드 도달 불가 | `502` + `{"code":"BACKEND_UNREACHABLE",...}` |

실패 경로가 전부 봉투 모양으로 나오므로 인터셉터가 `ApiError` 로 감싸고 화면이 토스트로 띄운다.
이슈의 완료 조건 "조용한 실패 금지" 가 여기서 충족된다.

## 변경 유형

- [x] 🐛 버그 수정 (fix)
- [ ] ✨ 새로운 기능 (feat)
- [ ] 🧹 리팩토링 (refactor)
- [x] 📝 문서 (docs)
- [x] 🧰 인프라·설정 (chore)

## 체크리스트

- [x] `npm run lint` 통과
- [x] `npm run build` 통과
- [x] 로컬에서 배포본(`wrangler dev`)으로 동작 확인
- [x] 백엔드 수정이 필요 없음을 확인
- [x] 후속 작업을 별도 이슈로 분리 (#82)

## 리뷰어에게 전달할 내용

**1. 아직 확인하지 못한 것 — refreshToken 쿠키의 브라우저 저장**

`Set-Cookie` 전달은 응답을 손대지 않는 구조상 보장되고, 위 401 응답에서 `Server` ·
`Content-Type` 등 백엔드 헤더가 그대로 통과하는 것도 확인했다. 다만 **실제 로그인 POST 는
보내지 않았다** (테스트 계정 잠금 우려). 브라우저에서 `wrangler dev` 로 직접 로그인해
DevTools → Application → Cookies 에 `refreshToken` 이 들어오는지 봐주면 좋겠다.

**2. `Set-Cookie` 에 `Secure` 를 덧붙이지 않았다**

백엔드 쿠키에는 `Secure` 가 없다. Worker 가 붙여줄 수 있지만 하지 않았다.
`workers.dev` 는 HTTPS 전용이라 실익이 없고, 프록시가 응답을 고치기 시작하면
개발(vite)과 배포(Worker)의 동작이 갈리기 때문이다 — #62 가 없애려던 종류의 차이다.
이견 있으면 말해달라.

**3. ⚠️ Worker↔백엔드 구간은 평문이다**

로그인 비밀번호와 토큰이 암호화 없이 지나간다. `*.elasticbeanstalk.com` 은 ACM 인증서를

author: nadrummond
body:
## Linked work issue

no-work-issue

## Summary

`n3o-webapp-deploy` interpolated the caller's settings unquoted, so the shell split them on whitespace. `OAUTH2_PROXY_FOOTER="Copyright © N3O Ltd"` therefore reached the CLI as four arguments and it rejected the second: `Invalid setting format: '©'`.

Every oauth-fronted site has failed to deploy since — Storybook's last success was 30 July, and the five runs after it all failed the same way. The build was fine each time; only the deploy step failed, which is why it went unnoticed.

Settings are now one `KEY=VALUE` per line, read a line at a time into an argument array. That needs no quoting convention and no `eval`, so a value may contain spaces, quotes, backticks or `$` and still arrive whole — the quotes in the old caller were never shell quotes anyway, since the value came from YAML rather than from a shell.

## Test plan

- [x] The parsing handles a value with spaces and a `©`, and a secret containing `"`, a backtick and `$`, yielding exactly one argument each
- [ ] Storybook's deploy goes green on merge — the first oauth site to run

body:
Adds `extensions/siid-compression` — a self-contained Node.js OpenAI-compatible proxy that routes SIID's AI traffic through a swappable, **lossless** compression layer to cut tokens/cost/latency without ever dropping information the coding agent needs.

### What's in it
- **Own Node.js OpenRouter proxy** + pluggable compression strategy, with traffic logging.
- **Lossless transforms**, each with an `expand()` inverse + round-trip test:
  - table compaction (JSON arrays-of-objects → keys-once table),
  - repeated-line collapse (log runs),
  - wrapper-agnostic cross-message block dedup (re-pasted file bodies → a model-readable reference marker).
- **Content-block adapter** so array-of-`{type:text}` message shapes compress too (not just string content).
- **`@conscendotech/siid-compression-api`** types-only package (mirrored to the public repo by its sync Action).

### Fixes from the audit (this branch)
- **Streamed usage scrape** now parses whole SSE `data:` lines instead of a `{[^}]*}` regex → `completion_tokens` are recorded again for streamed calls (nested `*_tokens_details` no longer break it).
- **tableCompaction absent-key sentinel** is now collision-safe (string `⟪siid-absent⟫` + escape of real collisions) — closes a provable losslessness hole and removes model-visible `{"_siidTable_absent":true}` noise.
- **block-dedup writeback** clones owning messages up front (never mutates caller messages).

### Docs
`STRATEGY.md` (design + per-transform lossless/meaning-preserving/lossy table), `AB-TESTING.md` (lean-output measurement), `AUDIT-FINDINGS.md` (three-way audit tracker — all items resolved).

### Testing
Offline round-trip suites pass (compressor, blockDedup, tableCompaction, repeatedLines). **Live model tests pass losslessly** (mixed, block-dedup, table-compaction, consumer) — the model reads compacted content and returns correct answers; streamed `completion_tokens` verified reported.

## Overview

This PR introduces the specification for **Blackwall Advanced Threat Detection** (Pillar 6), a comprehensive multi-stage attack correlation engine that addresses critical security gaps exposed by recent AI agent breaches in July 2026.

## Motivation

Following three major incidents where AI agents escaped evaluation environments and breached production systems:

### OpenAI/Huggingface Breach (July 9-13, 2026)
- **17,600 malicious actions** over 4 days grouped into 6,280 attack clusters
- Exploited **8 zero-day CVEs** in JFrog Artifactory to escape sandbox
- Exfiltrated **136 production secrets** from Kubernetes
- Deployed self-respawning pod fleet across 11 nodes
- Established C2 infrastructure across public services

### Anthropic Claude Escapes (April 2026)
- **3 separate incidents** across 141,006 evaluation runs
- Claude Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and research models breached 3 organizations
- Human configuration errors allowed internet access from sealed environments

### Modal Labs Compromise
- OpenAI agent compromised customer's unauthenticated endpoint
- Used Modal infrastructure as pivot point during broader campaign

## What This Adds

### 8 New Detection Components

1. **EventStreamCollector** - Normalizes events from all 5 existing pillars into unified temporal format
2. **AttackGraphStore** - PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB temporal graph for correlating 17K+ events
3. **AgentSwarmDetector** - Behavioral fingerprinting to identify coordinated agent instances
4. **ExploitChainAnalyzer** - Detects zero-day exploit chaining patterns (novelty scoring)
5. **AILMTracker** - Tracks AI-Induced Lateral Movement via runtime permission composition
6. **C2InfrastructureDetector** - Identifies C2 establishment (RequestBin, Pastebin, webhooks)
7. **KubernetesDefenseLayer** - Pod token theft, fleet spawning, secrets exfiltration detection
8. **PackageRegistryMonitor** - Monitors Artifactory/npm/PyPI for exploit probing

### Architecture

Operates as **cross-cutting analysis plane** above existing 5 pillars:
- Real-time detection (< 100ms latency per event)
- Retrospective analysis (multi-day time windows)
- Dual-mode operation: real-time alerts + historical investigation

### Performance Guarantees

- Event processing: **< 100ms** latency
- Path queries: **< 500ms** for 17K+ event graphs  
- Sustained throughput: **1,000 events/second**
- Fingerprint computation: **< 2 seconds** for 1-hour windows

## Spec Contents

### 📐 Design Document (`design.md`)
- System architecture with component diagrams
- 8 component interfaces with detailed APIs
- Data models (NormalizedEvent, AttackPath, SwarmEvidence, etc.)
- Algorithmic pseudocode for multi-stage attack correlation

### 📋 Requirements Document (`requirements.md`)

- Integration requirements with existing 5 pillars

- Property-based test tasks referencing design properties

- **Wave-based parallel execution** to minimize file conflicts
- Real database instances (not mocks) for performance validation

## Technology Stack

author: jbj
body:
The session that found the cut-edge race closed its report with a warning:

> There may be more of these in `shot.mjs`; I only chased the one that fired.

That was worth answering rather than leaving open, and #117 raised the stakes: the browser run now shares the machine with the test run, so it has *less* of it to itself than when the race first appeared.

## The audit

Every computed style `shot.mjs` reads, checked against what drives it:

| read | why it is safe |
| --- | --- |
| `.cut` opacity | the one that was moving — fixed in #113 |
| `.hole` opacity | no transition; static SVG |
| `night` opacity | rises under `fill: "forwards"`, and `waitUntil` precedes the read |
| `.hint-mark` animation + opacity | read only after the run has asserted the board is asleep *and* zero animations are running |
| `clipPath`, panel `display`, backdrop `fill`, page background | discrete values, nothing transitions them |

So: nothing to fix. **No code change** — the value here is the negative result, which is expensive to re-derive (it means reading every assertion in a 3,000-line file) and invisible once derived.

It also names the pattern the safe reads already follow, since that is the reusable part: *wait for the thing that stops a value moving, then read it.* The cut-edge failure was not that a value moved — it was that nothing in the check had established it had stopped.

author: propensive
body:
Ethereal's daemon would not start when the application JAR it was launched from held more than about 66,000 entries: the launcher exited without a word, the state directory held nothing but an empty log, and the client died parsing an empty PID. The cause was in the ZIP format's one physical offset. Every other offset a ZIP records is relative to the central directory, which is why appending an archive to a runner binary works at all — a reader recovers the shift by itself — but the ZIP64 locator's pointer to the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record is a file offset, and it only exists once an archive passes 65,535 entries. Left stale by the append, it sent the JVM into the middle of the runner binary, and the JVM then declined to open the executable at all. Zeppelin gains a `Zipfile.rebase` to shift that pointer, Ethereal's assembler and installer call it whenever they move a JAR, and the runner's five silent startup-failure paths now report what happened and quote the daemon's log.

## Zeppelin: `Zipfile.rebase`

Shifts an archive's ZIP64 locator pointer after data has been prepended to, or excised from, its prefix. Archives with no ZIP64 locator — anything under 65,535 entries — are left untouched.

```scala
// A self-extracting executable: a stub, then the archive appended at EOF.
stub.append(archive)
Zipfile.rebase(executable, stub.size)
```

Zeppelin's own reader already tolerated a stale locator by falling back to the record's physical position, so archives it produced round-tripped through it and looked correct; it is `java.util.zip` (and so `java -jar`) that refuses them.

## Ethereal

`Assembler.assemble` now rebases the JAR it appends to the runner stub, so a launcher built from a large application JAR starts. The shift is measured from the file rather than from the patched stub bytes, because on macOS `codesign` rewrites the stub in between and grows it by the size of the signature blob.

`Installer` applies the same shift in the opposite direction: self-installing removes the embedded payload from between the stub and the JAR, which moves the JAR earlier by exactly the payload's size.

## Ethereal's launcher

Every startup failure previously exited with no output at all. The message that was meant to cover this could only fire while the pid file was empty, and the launcher writes the wrapper's pid into it before any of the polling failure paths run — so nothing was ever printed, while the JVM's own account of the failure sat unread in `daemon.log`. Each failure path now names the daemon and its state directory and quotes the tail of that log:

```
The hello daemon failed to start: it did not bind its socket within 10s.
Its state directory is /home/user/.local/state/hello
The last output in /home/user/.local/state/hello/daemon.log was:
  Error: An unexpected error occurred while trying to open file /home/user/.local/bin/hello
```

An empty log is itself a diagnosis, and is reported as one. These changes are in the Rust runner, so they reach users with the next `runners-` release.

Closes #1680.

### Still open

`ziggurat`'s `EmbedAll` and `Download` deliveries concatenate stub and JAR inside a polyglot shell launcher at unpack time, where no rebase is possible; they remain broken above 65,535 entries. Padding every patched stub to a common length would let the packager pre-rebase the single embedded JAR by that constant.

- Tarjetas de resultado con encabezado de color por estado (más claro que el token `*-soft`/`*-bg` vía `color-mix`, para que la etiqueta `app-badge` — ahora sin icono — no desaparezca contra el fondo), filas de detalle separadas por borde, fecha de vencimiento resaltada en rojo, nota de revocación (`app-semantic-card`) y mensaje de "no encontrada" con el código consultado.
- Timestamp de la consulta en fuente monoespaciada, en la hora local de quien visita (con am/pm y offset GMT), usando el `timestamp` que devuelve el propio `ApiErrorDTO` del backend para los estados de error/no encontrada en vez del reloj del cliente.
- Se agregan a `public/images/icons/` los iconos de la spec (`verificar`, `verificada`, `vencida`, `revocada`, `no-encontrada`, `auditor-badge`, `reloj`), convertidos a `currentColor`, y se regenera `icon-registry.ts` con `npm run icons:generate`.
- Se elimina `badge-artwork.utils.ts`: mapeaba un icono por *tipo* de certificación (con arte pendiente, nunca mostraba nada distinto), que era la causa de que el icono de resultado no cambiara según el estado ni tuviera el tamaño correcto.
- Se agrega `codigoVerificacion` al modelo `CertificacionPublica` y una columna "Verificación" en la tabla de certificaciones del perfil público, enlazando cada fila a `/verificar/:codigo`.

## Pruebas

- `npm test -- --watch=false`: 883/883 verdes (2 skipped).
- Se agregaron casos para: fecha vencida en rojo, nota y fecha de revocación, mensaje de no encontrada con el código consultado, timestamp en fuente monoespaciada, badge sin icono, botón "Verificar otra credencial" secundario y centrado, enlace de verificación por fila en la tabla del perfil público, normalización del código recibido por ruta directa.
- Verificado manualmente en navegador contra un backend local con certificaciones sembradas en los 4 estados.

## Notas

- No se modificó configuración compartida.
- Cambios por revisión: se normaliza (`trim` + `toUpperCase`) el código de verificación también cuando llega por ruta directa (`/verificar/:codigo`), no solo desde el formulario, para que coincida con el comportamiento del backend; se cambió el texto de la pantalla de voseo a tuteo para mantener consistencia con el resto de la app.

author: jasonworden
body:
**Branch:** `docs/mermaid-11-15-diagram-types` → `main` (pushed)


The README claimed support for "19 diagram types" and its table omitted
every type mermaid has shipped since that number was written:

| Keyword | Status |
|---|---|
| `kanban` | stable |
| `eventmodeling` | stable |
| `radar-beta` | experimental |
| `treemap-beta` | experimental |
| `venn-beta` | experimental |
| `ishikawa-beta` | experimental |
| `wardley-beta` | experimental |
| `treeView-beta` | experimental |

All eight already validate today. `validate.ts` delegates to
`mermaid.parse()`, so they arrived with the dependency rather than
through any code change, and `no-experimental` already covers the six
`*-beta` types because it matches on the suffix rather than an
enumerated list. This PR is the docs catching up to behavior that
already shipped.

Worth naming explicitly: none of the eight have dedicated semantic
rules. "Supported" in that table has always meant "syntax-validated",
and eight new rows of ✅ with an empty Related-rules column makes that
ambiguity load-bearing. Added a sentence above the table saying the
Related-rules column, not the Supported column, is the real measure of
per-type analysis. Follow-up issues filed for the rules themselves.

### Changes

- **README** — 19 → 27, eight new table rows, and the note above.
- **`packages/core/src/rules.ts`** — added the six `*-beta` keywords to
  `no-experimental`'s `readmeDiagramKeywords`. The existing
  `rule-docs.test.ts` asserts the README's Related-rules cells against
  this metadata, so it caught the omission before I did.
- **`packages/core/test/mermaid-behavior.test.ts`** — added the six
  missing types to `DIAGRAMS`, plus a new case asserting every entry
  parses and type-detects. A mermaid bump that drops or renames a type
  now fails CI instead of quietly making the README wrong again.

### Verification

- 728/728 tests pass (`pnpm -r build && npx vitest run`).
- `biome check .` clean, 80 files.
- All eight keywords confirmed against mermaid 11.15.0 with valid
  samples, and confirmed to accept own-line `%%` directives in leading
  and mid-diagram positions — so the suppression contract holds for
  them too.
- `wardley-beta` is the one type merman does not recognize
  (`MERMAN_NO_DIAGRAM`), so it always takes the mermaid.js fallback.
  Noted in the table; perf follow-up filed separately.

body:
Introduces value-carrying artifacts for the reusable-workflows work.

## What
- New `ValueArtifact` base (`src/horus_builtin/artifact/value.py`): a file-backed artifact that also carries an inline, typed `value`.
- Concrete kinds registered in pyproject entry points: `number`, `boolean`, `string`.
- `BaseArtifact.materialize()` (default no-op): value kinds override to write their authored `value` the first time a consumer needs them, so a workflow-owned root value artifact is runnable without an external producer.
- `workflow/base.py` `_transfer`: materializes value roots and copies the root's authored value onto the consumer's input artifact so substitution sees the real value.
- `substitution.py`: `$id` renders the authored `value` for value-carrying artifacts (booleans lowercased to match on-disk JSON), else the on-target path as before.

## Tests
`uv run pytest` → 721 passed, 91.78% coverage (all new tests in `tests/unit/artifact/test_value_artifact.py` and `tests/unit/workflow/test_value_roots.py`).

author: laehee99
body:
## 관련 이슈

- Closes #107 

## 구현 결과

관리자가 특정 사용자의 계정 잠금 상태를 변경할 수 있는 API를 구현했습니다.

`PATCH /api/users/{userId}/locked` 요청으로 계정을 잠그거나 잠금을 해제할 수 있으며, Spring Security 필터에서 관리자 권한을 먼저 검사하도록 구성했습니다.

존재하지 않는 사용자를 대상으로 요청한 경우 실제 서비스 동작에 맞게 `404 Not Found`를 반환하고, 해당 응답을 OpenAPI 계약에도 반영했습니다.

## 주요 변경 사항

- 계정 잠금 상태 변경 요청 DTO를 구현했습니다.
  - `locked: true`이면 계정을 잠급니다.
  - `locked: false`이면 계정 잠금을 해제합니다.
  - `locked` 필드 누락 또는 `null`은 `400 Bad Request`로 처리합니다.

- `User` 엔티티에 잠금 상태 변경 메서드를 추가했습니다.
  - 서비스가 엔티티 필드를 직접 변경하지 않고 도메인 메서드를 통해 상태를 변경합니다.

- 계정 잠금 상태 변경 서비스를 구현했습니다.
  - 대상 사용자를 ID로 한 번 조회합니다.
  - 존재하지 않는 사용자는 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`로 처리합니다.
  - 영속 상태 엔티티의 변경 감지를 사용하므로 불필요한 `save()` 호출은 수행하지 않습니다.

- `PATCH /api/users/{userId}/locked` API를 구현했습니다.
  - 성공 시 응답 본문 없이 `204 No Content`를 반환합니다.
  - 인증되지 않은 요청은 `401 Unauthorized`로 처리합니다.
  - 일반 사용자의 요청은 `403 Forbidden`으로 처리합니다.
  - 대상 사용자가 존재하지 않으면 `404 Not Found`로 처리합니다.

- 관리자 권한 검사를 `SecurityFilterChain`에 적용했습니다.
  - `PATCH /api/users/*/locked` 경로에 `hasRole("ADMIN")`을 적용했습니다.
  - 관리자 권한 검사가 Spring MVC의 `@RequestBody` 역직렬화와 `@Valid` 검증보다 먼저 수행됩니다.
  - 요청 본문의 유효성에 따라 권한 없는 사용자의 응답이 달라지지 않도록 했습니다.
  - Controller 내부의 중복 `requireAdmin()` 로직을 제거하고 인증·인가 책임을 보안 필터로 일원화했습니다.

- 보안 필터와 CSRF가 활성화된 정책 테스트를 추가했습니다.
  - 인증되지 않은 사용자가 잘못된 본문을 보내도 `401`을 반환합니다.
  - `ROLE_USER`가 잘못된 본문을 보내도 `403`을 반환합니다.
  - `ROLE_ADMIN`이 잘못된 본문을 보내면 권한 검사를 통과한 후 DTO 검증에서 `400`을 반환합니다.
  - 유효한 CSRF 토큰을 포함하여 CSRF 실패로 인한 `403`과 권한 부족으로 인한 `403`을 구분했습니다.

- 테스트용 보안 정책 Controller를 전용 프로파일로 격리했습니다.
  - 테스트용 Controller와 실제 `UserController`가 `@SpringBootTest`에서 함께 스캔되어 경로가 중복 등록되는 문제를 해결했습니다.
  - `SecurityPolicyProbeController`는 `security-policy-test` 프로파일에서만 등록됩니다.
  - `SecurityAccessPolicyTest`에서만 `test`, `security-policy-test` 프로파일을 활성화합니다.
  - 일반 통합 테스트와 운영 애플리케이션에는 테스트용 Controller가 등록되지 않습니다.

- OpenAPI 계약을 실제 구현과 일치시켰습니다.
  - 성공 응답 `204 No Content`를 반영했습니다.
  - 존재하지 않는 대상 사용자에 대한 `404 Not Found`를 추가했습니다.
  - `PATCH /api/users/{userId}/locked`를 런타임 계약 검증 대상에 포함했습니다.

### 404 Not Found를 추가한 이유

기존 OpenAPI 문서에는 `PATCH /api/users/{userId}/locked`의 `404 Not Found` 응답이 정의되어 있지 않았습니다.

하지만 이 API는 URL 경로의 `{userId}`로 잠금 상태를 변경할 대상 사용자를 특정합니다. 전달된 UUID 형식이 올바르더라도 해당 사용자가 존재하지 않으면 변경할 대상 리소스가 없으므로 `404 Not Found`가 의미상 적절합니다.

다른 응답을 사용하는 경우에는 다음과 같은 문제가 있습니다.

- `400 Bad Request`는 요청 형식이나 값이 잘못된 상황을 의미하므로 대상 리소스 부재와 의미가 다릅니다.
- `401 Unauthorized`와 `403 Forbidden`은 인증·인가 문제를 의미합니다.
- `500 Internal Server Error`는 서버 내부 오류가 아니므로 적절하지 않습니다.
- `204 No Content`를 반환하면 실제로 변경된 사용자가 없어도 성공한 것처럼 표현됩니다.

따라서 실제 서비스 동작과 REST 응답 의미를 일치시키기 위해 정적 OpenAPI 및 런타임 Swagger 계약에 `404 Not Found`를 추가했습니다.

관리자 권한 검사는 사용자 조회보다 먼저 수행되므로, 대상 사용자의 존재 여부를 확인할 수 있는 `404` 응답은 관리자 권한을 통과한 요청에 대해서만 반환됩니다.

## 변경 영향

- [x] API 요청·응답이 변경됩니다.
- [ ] 데이터베이스 구조가 변경됩니다.
- [x] 다른 도메인과의 협의가 필요합니다.
- [ ] 환경 변수나 배포 설정이 변경됩니다.
- [ ] 위 항목에 해당하지 않습니다.

기존 `users.locked` 컬럼을 사용하므로 데이터베이스 구조 변경은 없습니다.

공통 `SecurityConfig`에 관리자 전용 경로가 추가되었으며, 해당 경로 외의 기존 공개·인증 API 정책은 변경하지 않았습니다.

이번 작업은 계정의 데이터베이스 잠금 상태만 변경합니다. 이미 발급된 JWT 액세스 토큰을 즉시 무효화하는 기능은 포함하지 않으며, Redis 등을 이용한 토큰 무효화 정책은 후속 작업에서 다룹니다.

`security-policy-test`는 테스트 코드에서만 활성화하는 프로파일이며 실제 환경 변수나 배포 설정에는 영향을 주지 않습니다.

## 테스트 및 확인 방법

- [x] 새로 추가하거나 변경한 로직의 테스트를 작성했습니다.
- [x] 전체 테스트가 통과합니다.
- [x] 정상 흐름과 예외 흐름을 확인했습니다.

실행한 테스트 또는 직접 확인한 방법:

```text
./gradlew test \
  --tests "com.mopl.user.dto.UserLockUpdateRequestTest" \
  --tests "com.mopl.user.service.UserServiceTest" \
  --tests "com.mopl.user.controller.UserControllerTest"

./gradlew test \
  --tests "com.mopl.global.security.SecurityAccessPolicyTest"

./gradlew test \
  --tests "com.mopl.content.repository.ContentLockTimeoutIntegrationTest"

./gradlew clean build
```

확인한 흐름:

- 관리자가 사용자의 계정을 잠글 수 있습니다.
- 관리자가 잠긴 계정의 잠금을 해제할 수 있습니다.
- 변경 성공 시 `204 No Content`가 반환됩니다.
- `locked` 값이 누락되거나 `null`이면 `400 Bad Request`가 반환됩니다.
- 인증되지 않은 요청은 본문 유효성과 관계없이 `401 Unauthorized`로 차단됩니다.
- 일반 사용자의 요청은 본문 유효성과 관계없이 `403 Forbidden`으로 차단됩니다.
- 관리자는 권한 검사를 통과한 뒤 DTO 검증을 적용받습니다.
- 대상 사용자가 존재하지 않으면 `404 Not Found`가 반환됩니다.
- 사용자 조회는 한 번만 수행됩니다.
- JPA 변경 감지를 사용하며 불필요한 `save()` 호출은 발생하지 않습니다.
- 테스트용 Controller가 일반 SpringBootTest 컨텍스트에 등록되지 않습니다.
- 정적 OpenAPI와 런타임 Swagger의 핵심 계약이 일치합니다.
- 전체 Gradle build가 성공합니다.

## 최종 확인

- [x] 이슈의 완료 기준을 모두 충족했습니다.
- [x] 하나의 이슈 범위에 해당하는 변경만 포함했습니다.
- [x] Swagger 또는 관련 문서를 필요한 만큼 수정했습니다.
- [x] 비밀 값이나 개인 정보가 코드와 로그에 포함되지 않았습니다.
- [x] 직접 해결하지 못한 리뷰 의견이나 문제가 남아 있지 않습니다.

author: jsoyer
body:
## Measured, full panel, 72 KB PR

The 4 000-character cap showed the reviewers **5%** of the change. They went and fetched the rest:

| reviewer | in | out | cache | cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Victor (opus) | 47 849 | 19 103 | 1 899 855 | $2.39 |
| Hugo (opus) | 42 211 | 29 255 | 3 140 844 | $3.33 |
| Marie (sonnet) | 22 217 | 28 890 | 4 874 168 | $2.54 |
| **total** | | | **9 914 867** | **$8.26** |

Marie alone read **4 874 168 cache tokens to reconstitute a diff worth ~18 000** — roughly **270× the size of the thing under review**.

## A diff passed in is billed once; a diff the agent must find is billed in round trips

The 4 000 cap was chosen before anyone measured which was cheaper. It turns out to buy nothing — it moves the same content into the conversation the expensive way.

**200 000 characters ≈ 50 000 tokens.** Comfortable for the models in use, and it makes *"the whole diff"* the normal case rather than the exception. That case is measured: **$0.17** with a bounded perimeter against $1.17 unbounded, verdict unchanged.

Genuinely huge PRs (2.6 MB and 27 MB exist in this repo) still truncate and still get the honest warning from #420.

**This is not a filter.** A lockfile or generated blob will still eat the budget; excluding by path is a separate decision and is deliberately not taken here.

## A test that would have stopped testing anything

The truncation fixtures now derive from the constant. The first version hardcoded 28 KB — which stopped being "big" the moment the cap moved, so the tests would have gone green on a subject that was no longer truncated at all.

## Worth stating plainly

That $8.26 bought **real** review: the three verdicts were substantive and divergent — `NEEDS_HUMAN`, `BLOCKED`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, three angles reaching three different conclusions. This change is about paying less for the same thing, not about less review.

## Verification

33 prompt tests, 109 orchestrator/verdict tests, `ruff`, `mypy`. Effect re-measured on the same PR after deploy — not claimed here.

author: marcelroozekrans
body:
Supersedes **#26**, which can be closed.

## Why Renovate's PR failed

#26 bumped `Microsoft.Graph` 5.105.0 → 6.2.0 alone and failed CI with `NU1605` on every project:

```
Microsoft.Graph 6.2.0 -> Microsoft.Graph.Core 4.0.1 -> Microsoft.Kiota.Abstractions (>= 2.0.0)
repository pinned                                       Microsoft.Kiota.Abstractions 1.22.0
```

**A grouping failure, not a breakage.** Graph pins a Kiota major internally, so the two have to move together.

## Graph v6 needed no source changes

All four providers — Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams — compile untouched against the v6 surface. **Their 70 tests pass unchanged, and no test was adjusted**, so this is behaviour-neutral rather than "behaviour-neutral after some assertions were relaxed".

## It also retires a workaround we carried by hand

Both `Rag.NET.DataProviders.Microsoft365` and `DataProviders.IntegrationTests` referenced `Microsoft.Kiota.Abstractions` explicitly for exactly one reason, recorded in a comment on each:

> *Audit lift: Microsoft.Graph 5.x pins Microsoft.Kiota.Abstractions 1.21.1 (GHSA-7j59-v9qr-6fq9, patched in 1.22.0).*

Graph 6.2.0 pulls **Kiota 2.0.0 transitively**, well past that advisory. Both explicit references and the central pin are removed.

**The proof is that the solution builds with 0 warnings.** `NuGetAudit` reports advisories as warnings and warnings are errors here — so a clean build is the audit *confirming* the lift is unnecessary, not an assumption that it is.

## Fixing the class, not the instance

`renovate.json` now groups `Microsoft.Graph` with `Microsoft.Kiota.Abstractions`, so the next Graph major arrives as one PR that can actually restore.

This is the second time grouping has mattered — worth watching for other packages that pin a companion's major internally.

Suites at baseline: `Microsoft365.Tests` **70**, `RepoConventions` **36 + 1 skip**, `Rag.NET.Tests` **1159**. Build **0 warnings / 0 errors**.

author: naveax
body:
## Purpose

Add the provider-neutral lifecycle between NXB-148 encrypted evidence sealing and future password-manager, OS credential-store, cloud KMS or HSM adapters.

## Delivered

- Add the private `nxb-evidence-key-provider` Rust crate.
- Bind exact provider identity, capability digest, key ID, store ID, policy snapshot, activation public key and bounded lifetime into a canonical content-addressed plan.
- Require domain-separated Ed25519 activation of the exact plan before any provider operation.
- Permit exactly one provider key fetch per acquisition invocation.
- Require exact 32-byte evidence-sealing key material, matching key identity, non-secret version metadata and validity through the plan lifetime.
- Convert valid provider material into the NXB-148 `ProductionEvidenceSealer` without serializing, logging or persisting key bytes.
- Require provider `finish` after every begun session; teardown failure overrides an otherwise successful acquisition.
- Emit metadata-only, content-addressed acquisition receipts.
- Add 11 adversarial tests covering successful acquisition, identity and signature mismatch, key identity/size/lifetime failures, provider failure, mandatory abort teardown, teardown precedence, redacted diagnostics and plan tampering.
- Update repository documentation to NXB-149 and 48 private workspace crates.

## Validation

The implementation source, workspace manifest and canonical lockfile at `b049225ae39987c4973b0014ee503def795b861e` were validated against the updated `main` base by GitHub Actions run `30991875053` (`NXB-149 evidence key-provider lifecycle`, run number 50).

Both Ubuntu and Windows completed successfully with:

- canonical `Cargo.lock` verification;
- formatting verification on Ubuntu;
- package check with all features;
- all-target Clippy with warnings denied;
- all 11 deterministic, single-threaded adversarial tests.

The same implementation source also passed primary CI run `30985279437` (run number 1870), including workspace lockfile/format/Clippy/tests/demo and RustSec/cargo-deny dependency policy checks.

GitHub-hosted Actions were subsequently disabled repository-wide on `main`. To preserve that policy, this PR does not reintroduce an Actions workflow. Commits after the validated source head only removed the temporary NXB-149 workflow and updated documentation; crate source, manifests and `Cargo.lock` did not change.

## Explicit exclusions

- No concrete password-manager, OS credential-store, cloud KMS, HSM or PKCS#11 adapter yet.
- No key bytes in plans, activations, receipts, audit metadata or diagnostics.
- No password-derived keys or keys stored beside ciphertext.
- No automatic report submission, browser automation or unrestricted scanning.

body:
MoneyPilotを、固定費・給与サイクル・返済・目標積立を一貫して扱うリアルタイム／ローカルファースト構成へ刷新しました。

## 主な変更

- **リアルタイム統合**: commit後だけ配信するSSEイベント、部分UI再取得、AJAX入力、再送防止、直前操作の取消に対応
- **動的アシスト**: 既定は費用ゼロのルールエンジン。`Ollama`、OpenAI互換ローカルサーバー、Claude CLIへ設定だけで差し替え可能
- **AI安全境界**: AIへ渡すデータは匿名化済み集計値のみ。金額計算・台帳更新は決定論的なPython側に限定し、リモートAIは明示opt-in
- **資金整合性**: 固定費CRUD、給与日の前倒し／遅延、部分・早期・遅延返済、返済取消、完済後の目標積立を監査台帳で管理
- **旧DB移行**: v1データを非破壊でv4へ移行。途中版v3で確定済みになった返済予定・cycle commitmentも再検証して修復
- **UI/UX刷新**: デスクトップ／390pxモバイル対応、PWA、ダークモード、キーボード操作、reduced motion、状態別アシストを追加
- **Windows運用**: `セットアップ.bat`、起動時バックアップ、復元ツール、タスクスケジューラ登録、同時起動ロック、LocalAppData保存に対応
- **セキュリティ**: APIトークン、CSRF、Trusted Host、セキュリティヘッダー、リモートAIのHTTPS制約、ローカルAI URLのSSRF対策を追加
- **CI/依存管理**: ハッシュ固定lock、Python 3.11/3.13・Windowsを含むCI、依存脆弱性監査を追加

## 重要な設計判断

- 基準収入190,000円を保守的な配分上限とし、192,005円との差額2,005円はbufferへ送るため、封筒合計が実収入を超えません。
- 返済予算は「実支払日」と「未払期限」を別台帳で保持します。給与日の後入力でcycle境界が変わっても、支払済み資金や予定額が消失・二重計上されません。
- 旧データのうち元状態を一意に復元できない取消だけは、安全のため自動処理を停止してバックアップ保持を案内します。

## 検証

- `144 passed`
- Ruff: pass
- mypy: pass
- pip-audit: 既知脆弱性 0件
- `git diff --check`: pass
- 実uvicornで収入・支出・固定費・返済・SSEをE2E確認
- デスクトップおよび390pxモバイルで表示・横溢れ・操作性を目視確認
- v1→v4、旧v3再修復、同時起動、バックアップ／復元、Windowsジョブを回帰テスト済み

## 起動

Windowsでは `money-pilot/セットアップ.bat` を実行します。初回セットアップ後はデスクトップのMoneyPilotショートカットから起動できます。

詳細は `money-pilot/README.md`、`money-pilot/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`、`money-pilot/docs/OPERATIONS.md` を参照してください。

author: alissonfgc
body:
Turns the MetaLoop prototype into a working, self-hosted study-management application. No Supabase, no Vercel, no Google Sheets — PostgreSQL is the only required service.

## What was there before

A visual prototype: ~1,600 lines of Next.js with every screen mocked (hardcoded KPIs, fictional ranking names), and a 36-line FastAPI app whose only real endpoint was `GET /sheets?action=ping`. No authentication, no persistence, no tests, no Docker, no CI. Details in `docs/REPO-AUDIT.md`.

Supabase and Vercel appeared only in the git history — no code coupling remained. The integration actually removed was **Google Sheets**.

## What this delivers

**Backend** — modular FastAPI monolith (SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, Pydantic 2, 63 endpoints):
- invitation-only auth with database-backed opaque session cookies (SHA-256 hashes, HttpOnly, revocable)
- subjects/topics catalog, tasks, CSV import, question sessions
- shared and personal mock exams with server-side scoring and window-function ranking
- server-authoritative study timer, study sessions, goals, streaks, cycles, reviews, external material references
- aggregated dashboard endpoint, admin area, audit trail, `/health` and `/ready`
- admin CLI for first-administrator creation

**Frontend** — the same visual identity, now on live data:
- login, invitation acceptance, protected routes
- responsive shell (drawer on mobile, sidebar on desktop), dark mode preserved
- tasks with filters and a CSV import wizard (PapaParse preview + server dry run)
- questions, mock exams with ranking, goals, cycles, reviews, materials, account, admin
- typed API client generated from the OpenAPI schema

**Deployment** — one image set for both LXC and VPS: Dockerfiles, `compose.yml` + dev/prod overrides, optional Caddy profile, backup/restore scripts, CI for both apps.

## Notable fixes found while testing

- Failed login attempts were rolled back, making rate limiting a no-op.
- `next.config.ts` rewrites are frozen at build time, so `API_INTERNAL_URL` was ignored at runtime — replaced with a route handler, verified end to end.
- Argon2's default `parallelism=4` caused heavy contention on a small box (~7.5 s mean login under a 40-user burst); switched to OWASP parameters.
- Reviews were scheduled on the server's UTC date but filtered by the user's local date.
- The production stack refused to start without `METALOOP_DOMAIN`: Compose interpolates services behind inactive profiles, so the optional Caddy service blocked the default LXC path that never uses it.
- Importing a single model module without the registry crashed on flush.

## Verification

All commands and their real output are recorded in `docs/handoff-log/`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff check .` / `mypy app` | clean (85 files) |
| `pytest` | 159 passed |
| `eslint` / `tsc --noEmit` / `vitest` | clean / clean / 39 passed |
| `next build` | 16 routes |
| `alembic upgrade head` on an empty database / `alembic check` | 21 tables / in sync |
| Docker image builds (API and web) | ✅ green in CI |
| `docker compose config` (dev and prod) | ✅ green in CI |
| Main-flow smoke test | 37/37 assertions |
| Backup → restore | verified with real data |
| 40-user concurrency | no failures |

**Remaining gap: the stack has never been started.** The images build and the Compose files validate, but `docker compose up` end to end — healthy database, migration applied, API ready, frontend reachable — was not exercised, because the development environment had no Docker daemon. Worth running once before production; see the limitations section of the handoff log.

body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - The CI suite is the safety net for every PR entering the merge queue.
> - `server/src/__tests__/workspace-runtime.test.ts` had one provisioning-heavy test duplicated byte-for-byte.
> - The duplicate copy used a shorter timeout than neighboring provisioning tests, so unrelated PRs could fail under runner contention.
> - This pull request removes the duplicate and keeps the surviving test at the timeout used by equivalent provisioning tests.
> - The benefit is the same coverage with less flake pressure on unrelated PRs.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Paperclip issue BLO-21118 tracks CI server-shard flakes caused by the duplicate workspace-runtime provisioning test. The observed failure was on PR #956, run 30954922141, in `General tests (server 3/4)`.

## What Changed

- Removed the byte-identical duplicate `provisions worktree-local pnpm node_modules instead of reusing base-repo links` test from `server/src/__tests__/workspace-runtime.test.ts`.
- Kept the surviving test and raised its timeout from `30_000` to `120_000`, matching nearby real `git worktree` plus `pnpm install` provisioning tests.

## Verification

CI is the verifying signal: the workspace-runtime test no longer appears twice, and the surviving provisioning-heavy test has the same timeout budget as sibling tests that do equivalent work.

## Risks

Low risk. This removes duplicate coverage rather than removing a unique assertion. The timeout change affects only the surviving heavy provisioning test and aligns it with existing neighboring tests.

## Model Used

Claude Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5[1m]`), agentic coding session with repository inspection and CI log analysis.

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change

body:
## Summary

Closes #1444. `mattpocock/skills` restructured its `skills/` layout and `langgenius/dify` removed its `component-refactoring` skill, so 10 named skills had `links.github` pointing at 404s — `gaia install` created a dangling symlink and reported success (the silent-failure part is tracked separately in #1441).

author: panghy
body:
# Voice dictation language selector

Adds a **Language** select to Settings → Voice Dictation, backed by the `voice.language` daemon setting (intentd#901), and makes the macOS OS-dictation engine honor it.

## What changed

### Settings panel (renderer)
- New "Language" `Select` in `VoiceSettings.svelte`: **Auto-detect** (empty string, the default) plus a curated ISO-639-1 list (`VOICE_LANGUAGES`). Option labels are localized to the active UI locale via `Intl.DisplayNames` — no name table. A stored code outside the curated list (e.g. set via config.toml) is prepended so the value round-trips.
- Hidden when the connected daemon predates `voice.language` (a `null` `settings.get` entry — the same availability pattern as `voice.openai.model`).
- `voice-settings-service.ts`: reads `voice.language` into the snapshot (`""` = auto-detect, `null` = setting absent) and adds `setVoiceLanguage` (throws when the daemon silently drops the path so the panel rolls back).
- Slice/selectors/store-service: `language` state field, `changeVoiceLanguage` trigger + `setVoiceLanguageValue` actions, `changeVoiceLanguageFlow` (optimistic apply, rollback + localized error on failure, no-op when unchanged or unavailable).

### Cloud path
No per-call change needed: the daemon resolves `per-call language → voice.language setting → auto-detect` server-side (PROTOCOL §5.41 "Language resolution").

### OS dictation path
- `transcribeWithSelectedEngine` forwards the hydrated non-blank `voice.language` to `transcribeWithOs` as the recognizer locale.
- `os-transcription-service.ts` / `VoiceTranscribeLocalSchema` / `voice-local.ipc.ts`: optional `locale` field plumbed through IPC to the helper argv as `--locale <bcp47>`.
- `transcribe.swift`: new `--locale` flag → `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale:)`. An unsupported locale logs to stderr and falls back to the system-locale recognizer; `recognizer-unavailable` fires only when neither works.

### i18n
Four new keys (`settings_voice_language_label` / `_ariaLabel` / `_auto` / `settings_voice_languageSaveFailed_error`) added to all 8 locale catalogs.

## Tests
- `voice-settings-service.test.ts`: snapshot read (code / blank→auto / absent→null), `setVoiceLanguage` write + auto-detect sentinel + not-applied throw.
- `voice-settings-store-service.test.ts`: language flow — optimistic apply, auto-detect, rollback on failure, no-op cases.
- `voice-settings-slice.test.ts`: initial state, snapshot hydrate, `setVoiceLanguageValue` apply/auto/rollback.
- `voice-local.ipc.test.ts`: `--locale` argv pass-through (alone, blank-omitted, combined with `--contextual-strings`) + `VoiceTranscribeLocalSchema` locale contract.
- `os-transcription-service.test.ts`: `locale` on the wire (trimmed, blank-omitted).
- `transcription-service.test.ts`: engine routing forwards `voice.language` to the OS engine; blank/unset ⇒ `undefined` (system locale).

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run` (6 targeted suites): **160 passed**
- `pnpm run check`: 0 errors
- `pnpm tsc -p tsconfig.json|tsconfig.main.json|tsconfig.preload.json --noEmit`: all clean
- `pnpm run lint` (incl. hardcoded-string + i18n completeness checks): passed
- Swift helper recompiled (`node scripts/build-speech-helper.cjs`) and smoke-tested: `--locale` without a value → `bad-arguments`; `--locale de` parses and proceeds.

Part of the voice dictation language/device settings work (monorepo `voice-dictation` workspace); builds on intentd#901 (daemon setting) and #733 (mic selector).

author: ktelfon
body:
This PR optimizes performance for the TON Tip Bot through two key enhancements:

1. **Database Flood Control Query Optimization**:
Adds a composite index `idx_tips_tipper_pending` on `tips(tipper_chat_id, status, expires_at)`. This ensures that the flood-control check `countLivePending`, which is triggered on every new invoice request, is highly efficient (O(log N) index lookups) rather than executing a sequential table scan on a growing tips table.

2. **Address Normalization Caching**:
Caches the pre-calculated user-friendly address representation of the owner's raw address at instantiation time in `CommandHandler`. Address formatting is highly CPU-intensive due to base64url encoding, check-summing, and address serialization in `ton4j`. Caching this eliminates redundant formatting work on every `/tip` command and inline callback query.

author: eriknw
body:
Stacked on #618. Overnight adversarial review of #617 found a hole in its guard: `_is_builtin_binaryop` keys on "no Python func and no numba func", but four built-ins (`binary.any`, `first`, `pair`, `second`) carry a Python `orig_func` as their UDT fallback. All four sailed past the guard and reproduced exactly what #617 exists to prevent:

```python
from graphblas import binary, monoid
from graphblas.core.operator.monoid import Monoid

binary.any.monoid is monoid.any        # True
try:
    Monoid.register_anonymous(binary.any, 0)   # opaque AttributeError, not the clear TypeError
except AttributeError:
    pass
binary.any.monoid is monoid.any        # False! left pointing at the half-built monoid
```

`binary.any` is even named in #617's own rationale as an op whose identity SuiteSparse ignores. This is an incomplete fix in #617 rather than a regression: the four common cases (`plus`/`times`/`min`/`max`) were already rejected cleanly.

The fix keys the probe on the typed ops as well: any `TypedBuiltinBinaryOp` among them marks the op built-in. Verified that the two signals agree everywhere else, including under `mapnumpy=True` (where mapped numpy binary ops hold the built-in's typed ops and are flagged by both tests alike, and the numpy monoids never pass through `Monoid._build`), and that a UDF's typed ops are never `TypedBuiltinBinaryOp`, so nothing legitimate is newly rejected. The new test is teeth-checked: it fails with the opaque AttributeError without the fix.

Gates: full pinned suite 1113 passed / 145 skipped; test_op + test_numpyops green under both mapnumpy settings; pre-commit all hooks pass.

author: avi-robusta
body:
Linear: [ROB-841](https://linear.app/robusta/issue/ROB-841/add-rfc-8707-support-to-oauth)

The current MCP authorization spec requires clients to send an RFC 8707 'resource' parameter identifying the MCP server's canonical URL in both the authorization request and the token exchange. Spec-compliant servers reject requests without it.

- Add optional 'resource' field to MCPOAuthConfig, defaulting to the toolset's MCP server url (overridable; empty string opts out). It is published to HolmesToolsStatus.meta.oauth_config for the frontend.
- Send 'resource' in the token exchange (frontend value wins over config), in refresh-token requests, and in the CLI flow's authorization URL.
- Expose it in the __oauth_metadata approval payload, OAuthDecisionCode, and OAuthCallbackRequest; persist it in the token cache/store so the background refresh sweep keeps sending it.

When 'resource' is absent, no parameter is sent anywhere — never an empty one (behavior unchanged).

Companion frontend PR: robusta-dev/robusta-frontend (same branch name).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for OAuth 2.0 resource indicators throughout authorization, token exchange, refresh, and approval flows.
  * Resource values can be configured, supplied by the frontend, or default to the MCP server URL.
  * OAuth tokens now retain resource information across caching, persistence, and refresh operations.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Ensured explicitly empty resource values remain omitted rather than being replaced by defaults.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive coverage for resource configuration, propagation, persistence, and precedence.

author: samarth1306w
body:
Fixes #29853

## Description
`formatOffset()` in `packages/lib/timezone.ts` stripped leading zeros only when the minute offset matched `:00` via regex `/^([-+])(0)(\d):00$/`.
As a result, whole-hour offsets (e.g. `+09:00` -> `+9:00`) were normalized, while half-hour and quarter-hour offsets (e.g. `+05:30`, `+05:45`) retained their leading padding zero, leading to inconsistent timezone formatting in dropdowns.

This PR updates `formatOffset()` regex to `/^([-+])0(\d:\d{2})$/` to strip leading zero padding for all single-digit hour offsets regardless of minute values.

## Tests
Added unit test suite in `packages/lib/timezone.test.ts` covering single-digit whole-hour, half-hour, and quarter-hour timezone offset formatting.

author: maxpayne89
body:
Closes #1237.

## Summary

`staff_members.active` was flipped by a bare cast from four places, with no definition and no consequences attached. Every consequence of deactivation had to be remembered independently at each call site — which is why a deactivated staff member kept showing as lead instructor on the public program page (#1236, the fixed half of this).

Adds `Provider.deactivate_staff_member/1` and `reactivate_staff_member/1`. In one transaction: set `active`, clear the lead-instructor flag on the staff member's active assignments, revoke an outstanding invitation, stage a `staff_member_deactivated` event.

Program Staff Assignments deliberately **survive**. Unassigning would emit `staff_unassigned_from_program`, which strips Messaging conversation membership that reactivation cannot give back — so deactivation ends the employment link without rewriting roster history.

## Review focus

**Why an event at all, when five read paths already filter `s.active`.** Because two cases a read filter structurally cannot reach:

1. `ProviderSessionDetails` denormalises the staff name into `current_assigned_staff_name`. It is a stored column, so no filter clears it — a deactivated (or erased) staff member stayed named on every `:scheduled` session row until a restart rebuilt the projection. Visible in the provider sessions modal.
2. The bootstrap SQL joined `program_staff_assignments → staff_members` with no `active` filter, so a rebuild would have resurrected exactly what the new handler clears.

**The second commit is a review finding, not a follow-up.** The regression pass caught that `resolve_program_context/1` — the incremental twin of the bootstrap query — still had no `active` filter, so a session created *after* someone left was attributed to them over their active colleague. Unlike the bootstrap case it never self-heals. Fixed by rewriting it into the same LATERAL shape the bootstrap uses, rather than adding a second spelling of the rule. The filter has to sit inside the LATERAL: on the join alone it would still pick the departed staff member's assignment and merely lose their name.

**Ordering in `AnonymizeUserData` is load-bearing.** Deactivate runs before the PII scrub, because scrubbing sets `active: false` and would make the command short-circuit — silently skipping the lead-instructor clearing and the event.

## All four writers migrated

| Writer | Change |
|---|---|
| Admin toggle | Editable `active` checkbox → Deactivate/Activate item actions calling the domain command. `can?(:edit)` is now `false` — `active` was the only editable field, so the form has nothing left to write, and the edit route raises rather than acting as a back door. |
| GDPR erasure | `AnonymizeUserData` deactivates, then scrubs. |
| `update_staff_member/3` | `:active` dropped from `@staff_updatable_fields` and from `edit_changeset` — an undocumented fourth path, one form param from being reachable. |
| `DedupActiveStaffMemberships` | Documented exemption. It runs inside a migration's `up/0`, where staging an event would deliver against a mid-migration schema, and it is a one-shot cleanup that has already run in production. |

`CONTEXT.md` gains the missing term: the domain had no word for this. Deactivation ends an employment link, and is distinct from removal (hard delete) and erasure (GDPR) — all three of which land on the same `active` boolean.

## Test plan

- `deactivate_staff_member_test.exs` — lead flags cleared, invitation revoked (and `:accepted` left intact), assignments survive, idempotent on an already-inactive member with nothing staged, another staff member's lead untouched. Event asserted via `assert_integration_published_to/2`, which derives the topic through the same `Event.topic/1` the delivery job uses.
- `staff_deactivation_cascade_test.exs` — end-to-end through the real outbox: `with_testing_mode(:manual)`, assert the pre-drain state, `drain_queue(with_recursion: true)`, assert the projection row cleared. The pre-drain assertion is what stops it passing vacuously. The outbox swap wraps the act only — doing it in `setup` collides the fixtures on `providers_identity_id_index`.
- Projection tests build their event from the real `ProviderEvents` constructor rather than a hand-rolled `Event.new/5`, since the suite runs on `TestOutbox` and nothing else pairs this producer with its consumer.
- Bootstrap and `session_created` each get a test proving a deactivated staff member loses to an active colleague.
- Admin: tabular `can?/3` gating, plus `handle/3` driven directly — matching how `BookingLive`'s item action is tested, since no confirm-modal LiveViewTest precedent exists in this repo.

`mix precommit`: 4116 passed, 2 skipped.

## Known gap

Reactivation stages no event, so a read table whose staff name was cleared stays cleared until the staff member's assignments next change or the projection rebuilds. Recomputing "who is currently assigned" incrementally would have to re-run the earliest-active-assignment resolution and could disagree with it; leaving the field empty is the safe direction. Documented on `reactivate_staff_member/1`.

## Follow-up

`Provider.delete_staff_member/2` shares this root cause and is worse: `program_staff_assignments.staff_member_id` is `on_delete: :delete_all`, so the Team tab's "remove member" button — the only user-facing removal control — lets Postgres vaporise every assignment with no `staff_unassigned_from_program` event, leaving Messaging conversation participants stale. Filed separately; it needs its own design gate (soft-delete, or emit unassign events first).

author: michen00
body:
Two loose ends from the v0.1.0 release.

## Python version pinned for pip caching

Every run of these workflows logged two warnings:

```text
Cache paths are empty. Please check the previous logs and make sure that the python version is specified
The `python-version` input is not set. The version of Python currently in `PATH` will be used.
```

They asked for `cache: pip` without a version, so `setup-python` had nothing to build a cache key from — the caching was silently doing nothing. This affected **three** workflows, not just the release run: [CI.yml](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/CI.yml), [pre-commit-autoupdate.yml](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/pre-commit-autoupdate.yml) and [release-pr.yml](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/release-pr.yml).

`'3.x'` keeps `check-latest: true` meaningful while giving the cache a resolvable key, and avoids pinning a minor version that would need maintenance. Python here only ever runs pre-commit.

## Release approval count corrected

The docs I added earlier said both release workflows wait for approval. The v0.1.0 release disproved it:

```text
Release Tag      06:25:28 → 06:28:19   ~3 min   waited
Release Publish  06:28:16 → 06:29:26   70 sec   did not wait
```

Release Publish logged that its protection rules were skipped. The distinguishing factor is the deployment creator: `michen00` for the Release Tag deployment, `github-actions[bot]` for the publish one that Release Tag dispatches.

So it is **one** approval per release, on Release Tag. The `environment: release` declaration stays on Release Publish because it still gates a hand-dispatched run — the manual fallback path — but it does not gate the automated path, and the docs now say so rather than implying protection that isn't there.

## Not changed: the workflow-run approval prompt

Release PRs are authored by `github-actions[bot]`, and `approval_policy=first_time_contributors` gated their CI runs both times. The bot now has two merged PRs, so it may no longer count as first-time at v0.2.0 — worth observing rather than pre-emptively loosening a policy that protects against genuinely new human contributors for the sake of one click.

## Verification

`make check` passes, actionlint and yamllint clean. The cache-warning fix is only observable on the next run of each workflow, which this PR's own CI exercises for CI.yml.

<summary>Files touched</summary>

| status | path | description |
| ------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `~` | [`.github/workflows/CI.yml`](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/CI.yml) | Pins `python-version` so `cache: pip` can build a key. |
| `~` | [`.github/workflows/pre-commit-autoupdate.yml`](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/pre-commit-autoupdate.yml) | Same fix. |
| `~` | [`.github/workflows/release-pr.yml`](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/.github/workflows/release-pr.yml) | Same fix; this is where the warnings were first seen. |
| `~` | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/michen00/custom-commit-hooks/blob/ci/pin-python-version/CONTRIBUTING.md) | Documents one approval per release and what the publish gate does and does not cover. |

author: jsonbored
body:
Closes #9511. Sink half; producer half is metagraphed-infra#323.

`topHoldersBalances` declines on exactly one condition — `results.length === 0`
— and a partial ledger clears it. Production demonstrated the consequence on
2026-08-05: **147,000 rows, every one correct**, and `ORDER BY free_tao DESC`
returning a well-formed leaderboard whose #2 (737,821 TAO, live on chain) was
simply absent.

Completeness is not observable in the ledger. 147,000 well-formed rows look
exactly like 364,266 well-formed rows, only fewer — so no check over
`account_balances` alone can tell them apart. The producer therefore declares
each pass's size up front, which it **can** because metagraphed-infra#316 made
it buffer the walk before posting anything.

## What's here

| | |
|---|---|
| `migrations/d1/0020_account_balances_passes.sql` | one row per pass, keyed on its `captured_at`, with a `completed_at` stamp |
| `workers/data-api.ts` | optional `pass_total` on the envelope; tallies arrivals |
| `src/account-balances-completeness.ts` | the reader + `mayRankAccountBalances` predicate |
| `src/top-holders-flow-tier.ts` | gates on it before ranking |

## Three decisions worth reading

**The gate does not scope the query to the complete pass's `captured_at`**, and
this is the subtle one. My first instinct was to scope. It's wrong: this ledger
never prunes, so a later **partial** pass only overwrites rows — it never
removes an account. Once any complete pass has landed the table holds at least
that whole account set, and scoping to its stamp would drop exactly the accounts
a newer partial pass had refreshed. That is the same missing-top-holder bug,
reintroduced by the guard against it.

**The tally statement is appended last in the batch.** `batchInSlices` spans
several `db.batch()` calls, so there is no single transaction across them — and
given that, the only safe ordering is one where a mid-run failure **under**-counts.
Rows land, then the tally moves. A pass can look less complete than it is, never
more; the reverse would mark a pass complete over rows that never arrived, which
is the exact lie this PR is about.

**Completeness keys on `completed_at IS NOT NULL`, not on `received >= expected`.**
The producer is at-least-once — it re-sends a chunk on failure — so a replay
makes `received_rows` exceed `expected_rows`. An equality check would call a
finished pass unfinished.

## Why the producer's own gate isn't enough

metagraphed-infra#316 already stops a truncated **scan** from publishing, which
closes the failure that actually happened. Two holes survive it, and both produce
the same partial-load-that-looks-fresh shape:

1. **A POST failing mid-sequence** — a pass is ~15 requests; if the 7th fails,
   the first six are already committed under a fresh `captured_at`, from a scan
   that was complete.
2. **The floor is 80%** of the last known network size, deliberately, so a
   network that grew does not deadlock the lane. A pass covering 80–99% clears it.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run` — full suite green; **70 passed** across the three touched
  suites, including `REFUSES a pass that is still in flight -- the 2026-08-05 shape`.
- `npm run test:coverage` + diff intersection on `src/**` and `workers/**`:
  **59/59 lines and branches, 100.00%**.
- `lint` · `format:check` · `typecheck` · `validate` — clean.
- `migrations/d1/0020` is already applied to the live D1 and verified against
  `sqlite_master` (renumbered from 0018 after #9493/#9512 took that slot).

`pass_total` is optional on the envelope, so this deploys safely in either order
relative to metagraphed-infra#323: an old producer simply records nothing.

author: marko1olo
body:
💡 **What:** Added a static boolean flag `_searchedForConsole` to `MMDebug.InstantiateOnScreenConsole` to track if we've already tried to locate an existing `MMDebugOnScreenConsole` in the scene.

🎯 **Why:** If the on-screen console is missing (or destroyed during gameplay) and the prefab cannot be loaded/instantiated for some reason, `_console` remains null. Subsequent frequent calls to `MMDebug.DebugOnScreen` (or explicitly instantiating) would repeatedly call `GameObject.FindObjectOfType` because the null check keeps passing. `FindObjectOfType` is an extremely slow, synchronous operation that scans the entire active scene hierarchy. When called iteratively (e.g. per-frame debug logs), it creates significant CPU spikes and stuttering.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
I created a benchmark that repeatedly calls `MMDebug.InstantiateOnScreenConsole(10000 times)` simulating the worst-case scenario where the object is destroyed immediately to mimic a missing or failed instantiation loop.
* **Baseline:** ~1430ms per 10,000 iterations for the repeated `GameObject.FindObjectOfType` search.
* **Improvement:** After adding the boolean guard to only perform the search once per session, the search loop time drops to ~1ms for the same 10,000 iterations.
* **Change:** ~99.9% reduction in execution time for the missing-prefab fallback case, completely eliminating the O(N) scene traversal overhead on subsequent null-state calls.
