author: morganmcg1
body:
<!-- senpai-assignment:v1 {"assignment_id":"maple-2026-08-05a-nax-stage2-double-buffer","base_ref":"codex/mlxfast-maple-20260804-advisor","base_sha":"279b6e2409a2ca92f7b874e08a3dabc2c6ff4a0b","head_ref":"maple-fern/nax-stage2-double-buffer","head_sha":"be2a5a21cf9dd95060890d1d9594842473baa71b","repo":"morganmcg1/mlxfast-challenge_senpai","revision_id":"r2","schema_version":1,"student":"maple-fern"} -->

## Why this is the assignment

maple-tanjiro's PR #34 measured the four biggest M5 block rates *in situ* by differencing official receipts. Three of the four are already at or above their hardware ceiling and have nothing left in them. One is not:

| block | moved | measured | ceiling | excess |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attention qkvo QMV (decode) | 802.16 MB | 651.8 GB/s | 610 GB/s | ~0 (107% of nominal) |
| attention qkvo dense GEMM (prefill) | 1460.29 GFLOP | 65.74 TFLOP/s | 56 peak | ~0 (117%) |
| routed-expert QMV (decode) | 552.08 MB | 546.2 GB/s | 610 GB/s | +0.106 ms |
| **routed gather-GEMM (prefill)** | **17,666 MB / 1005 GFLOP** | **408.4 GB/s = 23.23 TFLOP/s** | **34.7 TFLOP/s byte ceiling** | **+14.30 ms** |

That +14.30 ms is **42.1% of the honest ~34 ms prefill residual** and it is the single largest attributable item anywhere in the scored window, on either axis. dS for this block is 43.2619 +/- 0.402 ms across 39 routed layers. At prefill elasticity 0.362, recovering all of it is +5.3% of score; recovering a third is +1.8%. The campaign needs +1.0% to +2.0% to make promotion a coin-flip, so a third of this one block is the whole campaign.

You get this arm on tanjiro's own recommendation.

## The roofline, corrected

Do not use nominal 17,666 MB. I had an independent analysis done against the real route histogram (`research/prefill-512-route-histogram.txt`, 76 records x 256 experts, 4096 rows each) and the nominal number is wrong in **both** directions:

- **20.26% of (layer, expert) pairs get zero rows and are never read at all.** The binary search finds an empty run, the k-loop never executes (`fp_quantized_nax.h:1699-1727`). Those weights cost zero bytes.
- Chunk re-reads for experts with >64 rows are only **1.080x** (sum of ceil(r/64) = 16,758 vs 15,514 non-empty pairs).

Net actual weight DRAM = 17.666 GB x 0.8613 = **15.22 GB** => real DRAM floor at 610 GB/s = **27.9 ms**.

Separately, the MMA side pads to the 16-row hardware fragment (`SM = BM/WM = 16`, `steel/gemm/nax.h:27-28`). Issued rows / useful rows = 453,120 / 311,296 = **1.456x**, so the MMA floor is **26.1 ms issued** against 17.9 ms useful.

Put those together:

```
fully-serial D + M      = 27.9 + 26.1 = 54.0 ms
measured                = 43.26 ms      (0.80 of fully-serial)
perfect-overlap bound   = max(D, M)     = 27.9 ms
recoverable gap         = 43.26 - 27.9  = 15.4 ms
```

The kernel is realising only **~41% of the achievable staging-vs-MMA overlap**. That is the deficit. It is not a bandwidth problem and it is not a FLOP problem.

### Refuted - do not spend time here

I had hypothesised that weights were re-read once per column tile. **That is false and I verified the line myself.** `wl = w + y_col * K_w` with `y_col = tid.x * BN` (`fp_quantized_nax.h:1631-1634`) means each threadgroup owns one (expert, column-tile) pair and column tiles read **disjoint** 64-column weight slabs. Weights are never re-read across N. Only the 1.080x chunk factor exists. Do not write a fix for this.

Also refuted: load imbalance / long tail (<1 ms; the worst record is one expert with 505 rows = 8 chunks = 4.2% of that record's chunks, against 4,096-8,192 TGs per dispatch); scale-plane access cost (`fp_quantized_nax.h:391-470`, negligible); insufficient accumulator concurrency (TN=4 already gives four chains with dual-issue MMA pairs, `nax.h:1012-1031`).

## Hypothesis

**The `_nax` expert gather-GEMM serialises weight staging against MMA because `Ws` is single-buffered. Double-buffering it so tile k+1 stages while tile k is consumed by MMA recovers 3-8 ms of dS, bit-exactly.**

Mechanism, from `fp_quantized_nax.h:1744-1795`: each k-iteration does device-load A -> `barrier` -> all 128 threads stage the 64x64 weight tile into the **single** 9,216 B `Ws` buffer (`:1611-1618`) -> `barrier` -> MMA reads from `Ws`. Two barriers per k-iteration, and the next iteration's staging has a WAR hazard against this iteration's MMA. Nothing can overlap.

Corroborating evidence in our own tree: `quantized.cpp:1277-1287, 1445-1450` records staging at ~50 LSU ops per thread per k-iteration against ~40 on the compute side, and calls staging **"39.5% of prefill"**. This is H1 of `research/PREFILL_NAX_ANALYSIS.md`, now quantified.

Apple tech talk 111373 documents that Family-9+ shares one cache hierarchy across threadgroup and device memory, so a barrier-staged threadgroup tile buys **no locality** on this hardware - it is pure serialisation cost. A third-party M5 INT8 study measured 2.23-2.77x from deleting barrier-staged TG tiles entirely.

## Why this is bit-exact, with shipped precedent

`DARKBLOOM_SWIGLU_REGLOCAL` is **default ON and already won** in this exact kernel. Its own note: "register-local swiglu epilogue in `fp_gather_qmm_rhs_expert_nax` ... reads gate/up straight from the MMA Dtile fragments instead of round-tripping them through threadgroup memory with two barriers per column tile ... values are bit-identical (same bfloat casts of the same Dtile floats, same expression chain, same store addresses)".

So removing threadgroup round-trips and barriers from this kernel is a **shipped, bit-exact, winning transformation class**. You are applying the same class to the staging side instead of the epilogue side.

Double-buffering changes only the barrier schedule. Identical values, identical MMA issue order, identical epilogue, identical store addresses. Your `max_abs_diff` must be exactly 0, not "small".

## The arm is already pre-plumbed and inert

`DARKBLOOM_STAGE2_GATHER` exists on the host side and does nothing:

- `jit_kernels.cpp:1130-1155` parses the env var once and injects `#define DARKBLOOM_STAGE2_GATHER 1` into **expert-kernel JIT source only** (`get_qmm_nax_kernel`, `:1227-1257`, gated on `_expert_` in the kernel name, so every other JIT lib stays byte-identical).
- `quantized.cpp:1683-1702` prints the dispatch-site ground truth, where "active" requires **both** the flag **and** `expert_aligned`.
- The kernel-side `#ifdef` blocks were **stripped for byte budget**, not because they lost. `research/nezuko-harvest-report.md`, solver `4bf4f794` mechanism 4: "Strip two dead NAX gather arms (`DARKBLOOM_GATHER_XMAJOR`, `DARKBLOOM_STAGE2_GATHER`) and pin the fold OFF ... not a speed change: it is submission-surface budget ... ~33 KB ... removing it is what made room for mechanisms 3 and 5".

I grepped: `DARKBLOOM_STAGE2_GATHER` appears **only** at `quantized.cpp:1683,1692` and `jit_kernels.cpp:1130,1148,1155`. It is absent from `fp_quantized_nax.h` and from the `mlx-generated` twin. **There is no prior stage-2 measurement in this checkout** - the referenced `notes/exp-stage2.md` is an upstream-solver file we do not have. You are not re-running a known negative.

### The confound that makes this urgent

Our own tree documents why an earlier stage-2 result may have been an artefact: the trace exists because "those function constants only ever reached the non-expert kernel" - "the exact confound that made the STAGE_WIDEST/WIDELD arms measure their own control."

So: **you must confirm the `mlxfast: fusion active: stage2_gather` stderr line before you believe any A/B number.** If that line does not print, you measured the control against the control.

## Deliverable A - implement F1 and get one ranked receipt

Implement double-buffered weight staging behind `DARKBLOOM_STAGE2_GATHER`:

- `Ws[2][BN * BK_padded]` = 18,432 B, under the 32 KB threadgroup cap.
- Stage tile k+1 while MMA reads tile k. Drop the second barrier per k-iteration.
- Prologue stages tile 0; the loop alternates parity; epilo

author: mekenthompson
body:
## What

Flips **ON** the already-built, already-tested FK-race dead-letter **recovery sweep** (merged in #4083/#3795) by durably pinning its two enable knobs onto the `switchroom-hindsight` container's environment.

`docker/hindsight-maintenance.sh` (Section 7) already POSTs each dead-lettered `retain` op — the ones the engine MISclassified as a deterministic failure during the `unit_entities` `ForeignKeyViolation` race (#3794), which sit `status='failed'` with an intact `task_payload`, `retry_count=0`, `next_retry_at IS NULL` and are never revisited by the worker's claim loop — back to the engine's own `/v1/default/banks/{bank}/operations/{op}/retry` endpoint (`failed` → `pending`). The worker then re-picks it up, re-runs extraction, and the **STALLED** (not lost) memory finally lands.

The candidate query is scoped **exactly** to the FK-race signature:
`operation_type='retain' AND status='failed' AND task_payload IS NOT NULL AND retry_count=0 AND next_retry_at IS NULL`.

The two knobs (`SWITCHROOM_HINDSIGHT_REQUEUE_DEAD_LETTERS`, `SWITCHROOM_HINDSIGHT_REQUEUE_MAX`) were read **only** from the script's process environment and defaulted **OFF** — nothing in `src/` surfaced them, so the sweep never ran on the fleet.

## The change

- `src/setup/hindsight.ts`: pin `SWITCHROOM_HINDSIGHT_REQUEUE_DEAD_LETTERS=1` and `SWITCHROOM_HINDSIGHT_REQUEUE_MAX=25` in `hindsightContainerEnvPairs()` (docker-run path) and its compose twin, backed by `HINDSIGHT_DEFAULT_REQUEUE_DEAD_LETTERS` / `HINDSIGHT_DEFAULT_REQUEUE_MAX` constants.

**Why 25/tick:** each requeued op re-runs LLM fact extraction (real spend). Steady-state FK-race rate is ~zero (zero in the last 48h) and the historical backlog was ~14-23, so 25/tick is a safe ceiling that clears a realistic burst without risking a large unexpected LLM spend if the classifier regresses.

## Scope

Recovery half **only**. The classifier **prevention** fix is an engine change (`memory_engine.py`) tracked in **#3797** and is explicitly **out of scope** here — `memory_engine.py` / `Dockerfile.hindsight` are untouched.

## Test

Guard added to `src/setup/hindsight-recreate-env-survival.test.ts`: asserts both pins land on the launched container's env against the **real** derivation (`hindsightContainerEnvPairs`), on both GPU verdicts, with an empty `hindsight.env`, and survive a recreate. Verified **fails-red** without the pins (`env.get(...)` returns `undefined`) and **passes** with them. Sweep behaviour itself is already covered by `tests/docker/hindsight-maintenance.test.ts`.

## ⚠️ Operational caveat — RECREATE, not restart

Env is baked at `docker run -e` **creation** time, so a plain `docker restart` will **not** pick this up. The running `switchroom-hindsight` container needs a **recreate** — via `switchroom memory --restart` (recreates through `startHindsight`) or the next `switchroom apply`. First sweep lands **~30min** after recreate (`REFRESH_S=1800`, `docker/hindsight-entrypoint.sh`).

author: ewen-poch
body:
## Problem

ACP Runtime still owned the complete context-replacement transaction and live Specialist-switch policy. That kept stable application Session identity, provider attachment replacement, and cleanup sequencing coupled to the Runtime facade as the file continued to grow.

## Proposed change

Add a stateless `AcpSessionReplacementWorkflow` and delegate the two existing Runtime entry points to it:

- explicit context reset;
- live Specialist switch, including Claude-only provider Session replacement.

The workflow coordinates existing owners and delegates fresh provider publication to `AcpProviderSessionAdopter`; it does not become a new fact store.

## Scope and non-goals

- Preserve the public Runtime, Coordinator, IPC, shared type, and response contracts.
- Preserve stable application Session IDs and replaceable provider protocol Session IDs.
- Preserve Claude live-switch reset and Codex/OpenCode prefix-only behavior.
- Preserve Permission grants while cancelling old provider requests/correlations.
- Preserve #754 replay, Notebook continuity, and staged Claude handoff behavior in their existing owners.
- Do not change persistence, data models, Electron/Web/CLI/Task capabilities, user interaction, Specialist management, Permission policy, or Compute behavior.
- Do not implement Issue #458 orchestration interfaces or durable orchestration state.

## Ownership and sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runtime
    participant Replacement as Session Replacement Workflow
    participant Registry
    participant Owners as Permission / Prompt / Context / Interaction
    participant Adopter as Provider Session Adopter

    Runtime->>Replacement: reset(request) under operation lease
    Replacement->>Registry: reserve stable App Session ID
    Replacement->>Registry: renew and verify generation
    Replacement->>Owners: cancel/reset/supersede old provider state
    Replacement->>Registry: dispose provider and detach reverse alias
    Replacement->>Adopter: adopt with the same App Session ID
    Adopter->>Registry: publish replacement provider attachment
    Replacement->>Registry: release reservation in finally
    Replacement-->>Runtime: existing contextReset response
```

Production raw is 334 lines, within the ARD-21 330–450 target and below the 550 hard split threshold. `runtime.ts` decreases from 3,267 to 3,121 lines.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

All listed checks ran after the final material edit and after rebasing onto `origin/main` `c3eae9d3`.

- Replacement transaction plus Runtime application-command, IPC, and Coordinator facades -> targeted four-file Vitest set -> 97/97 passed (including workflow 6/6).
- Runtime reset/Specialist/replacement integration -> targeted `src/main/acp/runtime.test.ts` selection -> 18/18 sandbox-compatible tests passed; the loopback context-reset case passed separately outside the sandbox (1/1).
- Latest-main Web remote-access compatibility (#767) -> `npm test -- --run src/main/remote-access/pairing.test.ts` -> 5/5 passed.
- Node process contracts -> `npm run typecheck:node` -> passed.
- Changed source/test lint -> ESLint -> 0 findings.
- Changed source/test formatting -> Prettier check -> passed.
- Patch integrity -> `git diff --check` -> passed.
- Manual Standards review -> 0 findings.
- Manual Spec/compatibility review -> 0 findings.

## Review focus

- The reservation remains live through asynchronous adoption and is released on every outcome.
- Cleanup order prevents old provider aliases, Permission correlation, media usage, context usage, applied model, or stale interaction cleanup from reaching the replacement turn.
- Specialist projection remains intentionally eager/non-transactional, matching existing behavior.
- The workflow coordinates owners without duplicating their state or adoption logic.

## Uncovered risks

- The complete local suite was not rerun on the exact head; the online PR Gate is authoritative for the full platform and consumer matrix.
- Cross-platform process/runtime behavior remains CI-covered rather than reproduced locally.
- Future Issue #458 orchestration remains constrained to consume existing application interfaces; this PR introduces no orchestration API, schema, wire format, or UI.

body:
> **Merge order: this PR merges FIRST.** Its paired half, imbue-ai/mngr-internal#282, depends on the switch added here and merges after. The two branches share a name (`danver/mind-153-snapshot-determinism`), which is how mngr-internal's CI pairs them for its snapshot builds.

## Summary

- **Bake `xvfb` + `xclip` into the base image** (`setup_system.sh`). `[program:xvfb]` execs Xvfb directly at boot, so a snapshot, restore, or fresh boot that raced the deferred env.d install carried a service that could never spawn — `supervisorctl restart all` failed with `xvfb: ERROR (spawn error)` (the failure behind mngr-internal#218, and a false-FAILED for any real user restoring during the install window). A binary that static service config promises at every boot must exist in the image; xvfb+xclip are a few MB, and only the heavy Fortress/Chromium stack stays deferred. The unit's xvfb step remains as an instant no-op for rootfses built from pre-bake images, so old/new images and old/new units interoperate in any combination — no rollout ordering between the repos.
- **Add a `DWT_SKIP_BROWSER_UNIT=1` opt-out to the env.d browser unit** so environments that never use the browser stack (the minds CI snapshot producer) skip the whole unit including the hundreds-of-MB Fortress download. The switch is re-evaluated on every boot per the env.d contract (no marker files); clearing it converges the browser stack on the next boot.
- Comment hygiene: the unit's "not required by any boot-time service" rationale and `[program:xvfb]`'s "retries until the binary exists" comment were stale once the xvfb service existed.

Linear: MIND-153. Context: imbue-ai/mngr-internal#218. Paired PR: imbue-ai/mngr-internal#282 (sets the switch from the snapshot producer, removes the deferred-install wait, and reworks the restore verification).

## Testing

This repo's CI is green (changelog gate + test suite). Consumed end-to-end by the paired PR's CI: mngr-internal#282's `build-minds-snapshot` clones this branch by name and minted a browser-free snapshot in 6m12s, and `test-minds-snapshot` passed the full resume suite against it — including the backup-restore test from the original failure — in 4m26s.

Add a fifth gold-calibration pool candidate `dtw` (constrained + stochastic Gumbel DTW GR↔typewell alignment, `src/dtw_align.py`), porting the distinctive technique of the public DWT/training notebooks numpy-only. The per-well conservative gate makes the addition strictly non-regressive (worst case: the gate never picks `dtw`, champion unchanged).

## Changes
- `src/dtw_align.py` — Sakoe-Chiba band-constrained DTW (radii 20/50/100/200 ensembled) + stochastic Gumbel tracebacks (K=12, T=3.0) → per-row mean + std uncertainty shrinkage. numpy-only, `__file__`-independent, deterministic (fixed RandomState seed). *(committed in ada0521)*
- `src/calibrate.py` `_gold_candidate_pool` — add `dtw` candidate. *(ada0521)*
- `kaggle/rogii-claude-baseline.py` — exec-compatible byte-identical port. *(ada0521)*
- `tests/test_dtw_align.py` (+ kernel↔src byte-match). *(ada0521)*
- `champion.json`, `docs/champion-selection.md`, `docs/ai/experiment_ledger.jsonl`, `docs/ai/dtw_logs/` — promotion record + confirm evidence.

## Verification
leak-free fold-0 toe-holdout confirm (156 wells / 746,360 rows, weight 0.75):

| Pool | Gold RMSE | Gate wells | Beats blend/pf |
| --- | ---: | ---: | :---: |
| `{blend,pf,ml,poly,beam,dtw}` (this PR) | **11.073634** | 44 | yes (11.173 / 11.225) |
| `{blend,pf,ml,poly,beam}` (prior champion) | 11.073964 | 43 | yes |

`dtw` improves the gold confirm RMSE by **−0.00033** and wins the heel backtest on **+1** well. Determinism verified: an independent background repro run is byte-identical (same RMSE and 44 well ids). A marginal 4th-decimal improvement whose real value is an extra low-risk alignment viewpoint; expected real-LB effect negligible but structurally non-regressive.

## Related Issues
- Parent: SOT-2438 · This: SOT-2444 · Sibling pattern: SOT-2442 (beam, PR#25)

- [x] pytest 63 passed (kernel↔src byte-identity incl. `tests/test_dtw_align.py`)

author: marcelveldt
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Changing the volume of an AirPlay speaker right around the moment playback starts could leave the speaker at its old level while Music Assistant already showed the new one, with nothing correcting it afterwards.

When a speaker connects, Music Assistant re-sends the current volume to it (and repeats that 2 seconds later, because some speakers ignore the first one). Two things went wrong there:

- `volume_set` sent the command to the speaker *before* storing the new level. The resync reads that stored level, so it could read and push the old value while the send was still in flight.
- The repeat 2 seconds later had its value fixed at connect time, so it replayed the old level over anything changed in the meantime — including a mute.

**Related issue (if applicable):**

- n/a — spotted during review of #5312

## Types of changes

<!--
Tick exactly one box. CI (.github/workflows/pr-labels.yaml) derives
the label from the ticked box and applies it automatically; the
release-notes generator uses that same label to slot this change
into the next release notes.
-->

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) — `bugfix`
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) — `new-feature`
- [ ] Enhancement to an existing feature — `enhancement`
- [ ] New music/player/metadata/plugin provider — `new-provider`
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) — `breaking-change`
- [ ] Refactor (no behaviour change) — `refactor`
- [ ] Documentation only — `documentation`
- [ ] Maintenance / chore — `maintenance`
- [ ] CI / workflow change — `ci`
- [ ] Dependencies bump — `dependencies`

### Changes

- Store the new volume level before sending it to the speaker
- Let the delayed volume resend read the current level when it fires, so it can no longer replay a stale value or undo a mute
- Regression tests for both

## Checklist

- [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- [x] `pytest` passes, and tests have been added/updated under `tests/` where applicable.

author: bartosz-do
body:
## Summary

- Replace the dead `.stylelintrc` with `stylelint.config.mjs`. The old file extended `stylelint-config-twbs-bootstrap/scss`, a subpath that was removed in v15 — running it failed with `ConfigurationError`. A JS config also lets every disabled rule carry a comment explaining why.
- Add `stylelint`, `stylelint-config-twbs-bootstrap` and `@stylistic/stylelint-config` as dev dependencies, and add `lint:scss` / `lint:scss:fix` scripts to the root and to `@tabler/core`. `css-lint` now runs stylelint before `find-unused-sass-variables`, so the existing Lint workflow picks it up with no CI change.
- Prettier keeps ownership of SCSS formatting. All `@stylistic` rules the Bootstrap config pulls in are switched off, otherwise the two tools rewrite each other's output on every file.
- Apply `--fix` across 87 SCSS files: property order, `::before`/`::after` notation, short hex, quotes, keyframe selectors.

## Preview

- **URL:** [preview link](https://tabler-git-stylelint-init-tabler-io.vercel.app/)
- **How to test:** The autofix touched almost every component stylesheet, so the point of the preview is to confirm nothing moved. Compare a few dense pages against `dev` — [`/cards.html`](https://tabler-git-stylelint-init-tabler-io.vercel.app/cards.html), [`/form-elements.html`](https://tabler-git-stylelint-init-tabler-io.vercel.app/form-elements.html), [`/tables.html`](https://tabler-git-stylelint-init-tabler-io.vercel.app/tables.html) — and check an RTL page, since 54 `/*rtl:*/` control comments were reformatted to `/* rtl: */`.
- The compiled `tabler.css` was diffed against `dev` line by line. Every change is equivalent output: `:before` → `::before` (214), `#ffffff` → `#fff` (~250), rtl comment spacing (54, verified both forms parse the same in rtlcss), `currentColor` → `currentcolor`, `from`/`to` → `0%`/`100%`, font quotes and `font-weight: normal` → `400`. Gzipped `tabler.min.css` goes from 75.5 kB to 75.3 kB.

## Notes / rollout

- **`pnpm lint` fails on this branch.** 87 violations remain in Tabler's own SCSS and are not fixed here: 59 `declaration-no-important` (18 of them in `utils/_colors.scss`, which generates utility classes), 7 `selector-max-type`, 5 redundant `&`, and a tail of single hits. They need either a code fix or a file-level `// stylelint-disable` with a reason. Merging before that turns the Lint job red.
- Dependency majors are pinned on purpose. `@stylistic/stylelint-config` is held at `^2` and `stylelint` at `^16` to match what `stylelint-config-twbs-bootstrap@16.1.0` loads. On `@stylistic` v5 stylelint rejects every file with `Unknown rule @stylistic/…`, and on stylelint 17 the whole twbs chain reports unmet peers and the rule count drifts.
- `core/scss/tests/**` is excluded from linting. Those are sass-true fixtures that spell out the exact CSS a mixin must emit, so an autofix rewrites the assertion. Bootstrap excludes its own `**/tests/` for the same reason. One fixture was updated by hand in `_caret.test.scss` to follow the `::after` change in the caret mixin.
- Files copied from upstream Bootstrap (`core/scss/bootstrap/**`, `core/scss/mixins/bootstrap/**`) are exempt from `order/properties-order`, to avoid sync noise on every Bootstrap bump.
- Four rules are disabled globally because their autofix produced wrong code: `import-notation` turned `@import url($google-font-url)` into a literal string and broke the Sass build, and `value-keyword-case` lowercased real font names (`BlinkMacSystemFont`) and `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility`.
- No changeset yet. `@tabler/core`'s shipped CSS changes, so a `patch` changeset probably belongs here.

Closes #2721

## They are not equally proven, and the cards say so

**1. Saved booking reported as an error** — strongest. Pinned by four tests that fail if the guard is removed, including one checking a genuine failure still reports as a failure. Cannot silently regress.

**2. Half-saved edit** — real fix, weaker evidence, and I have written that on the card rather than glossed it. The code landed and nothing regressed, but **no test covers "change the service AND move onto a taken slot"**, so CI could not have caught a mistake in this specific fix.

Your click-through in PR #792 is the confirmation:

- [ ] Two appointments, same therapist, 09:00 and 11:00
- [ ] Edit the 09:00: change **Serviço** *and* set the time to 11:00, save
- [ ] Take the conflict warning, press **Cancelar**

author: philippe-ths
body:
Closes #789.

## What

The vendored AI workflow was updated 3.12.0 -> 3.13.0 (one `scripts/update.sh` run per installed tool: gemini, codex, copilot, claude). Every vendored file is gitignored and local-only, so `.gitignore` is the sole tracked file the update touches — and it came back wrong.

The installer rewrites its managed block to `shared + <that tool>` paths **and strips those paths from anywhere else in the file**, including the hand-maintained "AI workflow and skills" section put there to survive it. After four sequential runs only the last tool's paths were ignored: `.gemini/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.codex/` and `AGENTS.md` showed as untracked, so a later `git add -A` would have committed vendored tooling.

This restores them, adds `.vscode/` (copilot, never listed) and `GEMINI.md` (created by the gemini install), and corrects the section comment to say the entries must be re-checked after every updater run rather than claiming they are safe from it.

## Verification

- `git check-ignore -q` passes for all fourteen vendored paths (`.claude/ .codex/ .gemini/ .vscode/ .agents/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md ai-workflow.md .ai-policy/ .githooks/ .github/copilot-instructions.md .github/hooks/`).
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` stays tracked (the `!.github/workflows/` negation still wins over `.github/*`).
- `git status --porcelain` shows only `.gitignore` modified.
- `.ai-policy/scripts/project-validation.sh`: 24/24 pass, including the two new 3.13.0 assertions that `block-pr-merge.sh` blocks a PR merge on both the shell and MCP routes.

No product code changes, so the backend/frontend suites are unaffected by this diff; CI runs them anyway.

## Not verified

The updater's stripping behaviour itself is upstream in `philippe-ths/ai-coding-workflow`; nothing here prevents the next update from clobbering the section again. The procedure is the mitigation.

Neuer Abschnitt 2 in `docs/10-style-storytelling.md`:

author: ajianaz
body:
## What

Trust feedback feature — lets users mark a memory as **helpful** or **unhelpful** via the Uteke endpoint `POST /memory/feedback`.

## Why

Uteke v0.12.0 exposes `/memory/feedback` but Corin never adopted it. User feedback adjusts the memory's importance score (+0.05 helpful / -0.10 unhelpful), enabling community-driven ranking without manual importance editing.

## Changes (6 files, +136/-2)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `uteke_client.rs` | `memory_feedback()` method — POST to `/memory/feedback` |
| `commands.rs` | `memory_feedback` Tauri command (lock, clone, call, map error) |
| `lib.rs` | Handler registration in `generate_handler![]` |
| `types.ts` | `MemoryFeedbackResponse` interface |
| `ipc.ts` | `memoryFeedback()` invoke wrapper |
| `MemoryDetail.svelte` | Thumbs up/down UI with delta display and toast feedback |

## How it works

1. User opens a memory in the detail panel
2. New "Was this helpful?" bar appears below metadata
3. Click thumbs up = POST feedback helpful = importance +0.05
4. Click thumbs down = POST feedback unhelpful = importance -0.10
5. Delta shown as colored badge (+5% green / -10% red)
6. Buttons disabled after click (one vote per session)

## Validation

- cargo fmt --all pass
- svelte-check 0 errors (44 pre-existing warnings)
- Lucide icons verified (thumbs-up.svelte, thumbs-down.svelte)
- Cora review no issues
- CI will validate on PR

## API Reference

POST /memory/feedback
Request:  id + feedback ("helpful" or "unhelpful")
Response: id + feedback + delta + importance

Closes #207

author: xylar
body:
<!--
Thank you for your pull request.
Please add a description of what is accomplished in the PR here at the top:
-->

## What was broken

mache picked a machine's queue, partition or QOS entirely on its own, from the machine's list of available targets and the number of nodes a job wanted. There was no way for a caller to say "I want the debug QOS for this job." Tools built on mache worked around that by reaching into mache's own config: deep-copying it, rewriting the list of available targets down to the single one they wanted, calling mache, and then second-guessing whatever came back. That is fragile -- it depends on config details that are mache's business, and it duplicates logic mache already has.

The workaround also could not tell the difference between "this machine has no debug QOS" and "debug exists but this job is too big for it," so users got misleading messages about why they did not get what they asked for.

Frontier had a second, simpler problem: its config listed one partition, `batch`, with no limits attached and no QOS at all. Nothing recorded that Frontier has a debug QOS, an `extended` partition, or any wall-clock limits, so no caller could request a debug configuration there no matter how it asked, and nothing could tell a job that its wall time was longer than the scheduler would accept.

## What this fixes

Callers can now request a specific queue, partition, QOS or constraint directly, and mache either honors it or explains, in a sentence meant to be printed as-is, why it could not. A request is treated as a preference rather than a demand: if it cannot be honored, mache falls back to the machine's default and reports `honored = False` along with a `reason`, instead of failing. The three reasons are distinct and accurate -- the target does not exist on this machine, the job would be clamped to fewer nodes than the caller allows, or the requested wall time is longer than the target permits. A constraint has no node or wall-clock limits of its own, so it is checked only against the machine's list of available constraints, but it behaves the same way otherwise.

mache also now caps a desired wall time at the selected target's limit, so callers no longer need their own copy of that arithmetic.

Frontier gains the partitions and QOS that OLCF actually documents: the `extended` partition (24 hours, up to 64 nodes) alongside `batch`, and the `normal` and `debug` QOS (2 hours). Because Frontier's wall-clock limit on `batch` depends on job size -- 2 hours up to 91 nodes, 6 hours to 183, 12 hours above that -- machine configs can now express a limit that varies with node count instead of a single number. `batch` and `normal` remain the defaults, and an unqualified request resolves to exactly what it did before.

## What this means for downstream tools

Polaris can delete its config-rewriting workaround and pass its `[job] partition` / `qos` / `queue` / `constraint` settings straight through, printing `reason` when a request is not honored. Placeholder values such as `<<<default>>>` are understood as "no request", so config-driven callers do not need to guard against unset options.

`SlurmSystem.get_slurm_options()` and `PbsSystem.get_pbs_options()` still return the same tuples they always have, but are deprecated in favor of `resolve_slurm_options()` and `resolve_pbs_options()`, which return objects that can gain fields without breaking positional unpacking. One behavior change worth flagging: when a QOS restricts the node count more than the partition does, the returned node count now reflects that stricter limit. This version is 3.11.0.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/` -- 264 passed. (The `pixi run` wrapper fails in this environment with a lock-file version error unrelated to these changes, so tests and hooks were run with the interpreter in `.pixi/envs/default`, which is the same environment.)

- `pre-commit run --files <all changed files>` -- all hooks pass.

A **Who makes this** section, placed immediately before the licence - which is where the copyright holder is already named, so this explains who that is instead of leaving `Copyright (C) 2026 Fundacja Reborn` as a bare line.

Hung on what the projects genuinely have in common rather than bolted on as an advert: *software should not have to see your data in order to be useful to you*. It ends on the source repository rather than on a claim - "host it yourself rather than take our word for any of the above" is the right register for people who arrived here looking for something that does not phone home.

body:
## O que muda
Fecha a sequência PR10-15 (Cadastro de Colaboradores, Arquivamento e Escopo
por Unidade — ADR-0002 §10) com o mesmo rigor aplicado ao PR9 para a
fundação (PR1-9):

- Novo `tests/test_outsourced_extension_end_to_end_journey.py`: os testes de
  PR10-15 cobrem cada peça isoladamente (módulo/permissões simplificadas,
  rota do Cadastro de Colaboradores, arquivamento, filtro de Colaboradores
  Arquivados, relatório de headcount). Este arquivo verifica que as peças
  funcionam **juntas**, na mesma jornada que um Administrador Geral e um
  Administrador Local realmente percorrem:
  - módulo `terceirizados_colaboradores` oculto por padrão → bloqueado
    mesmo com a permissão técnica;
  - Administrador Geral habilita `module_visibility` para o perfil → sem
    `module_unit_scope` configurado, qualquer Unidade acessa;
  - Administrador Geral restringe o módulo a uma Unidade específica → só
    aquela Unidade acessa para `admin`/`user` — `general_admin` nunca é
    escopado por Unidade;
  - Cadastro de Colaboradores simplificado grava na mesma tabela
    `employees` (nunca CLT);
  - arquivar a empresa terceirizada bloqueia novo cadastro contra ela;
  - arquivar o colaborador o expõe em "Colaboradores Arquivados" sem afetar
    CLTs;
  - relatório de headcount reflete ativos/arquivados;
  - desarquivar a empresa libera novo cadastro de novo;
  - isolamento multi-tenant de ponta a ponta (module_unit_scope, empresa,
    colaborador e relatório de um tenant nunca vazam para outro).
- `docs/adr/ADR-0002-cadastro-simplificado-terceirizados.md` atualizado como
  documentação final: linha de Status na abertura do documento e nova seção
  **§10.6** marcam os 6 PRs da extensão (10-15) como "(implementado)", cada
  um com o resumo técnico do que foi entregue — mesmo padrão já usado pela
  seção 7 para os PRs 1-9 da fundação.

## Tipo
- [x] test (regressão) + docs

## Checklist
- [ ] `flutter analyze` e `flutter test` passam (se tocou em `flutter/`) — N/A, PR não toca em `flutter/`

- [x] Regra de negócio permanece **centralizada no backend** (não migrei lógica para o app) — PR só adiciona testes e documentação, nenhuma rota/service nova
- [x] Isolamento **Multi-Tenant** preservado (tenant_id / company_id / unit_id respeitados) — coberto pelo novo teste de isolamento
- [ ] Migrations acompanham índices/constraints/RLS quando aplicável — N/A, sem migrations neste PR

- [x] Documentação/CHANGELOG atualizados quando aplicável — ADR-0002 §10.6 é o objeto principal deste PR

## Impacto Multi-Tenant
Nenhum — só testes e documentação. O novo teste de isolamento confirma que
`module_unit_scope`, empresa terceirizada, colaborador e relatório de
headcount de um tenant nunca vazam para outro.

1. `pytest tests/test_outsourced_extension_end_to_end_journey.py -q` e depois

author: citizenkaro
body:
Item 4 of holonym-foundation/internal-docs#1984.

`packages/sdk/README.md` said:

> Currently targeting **Aztec Alpha**, which settles on **Ethereum mainnet**.

Now:

> Currently targeting **Aztec mainnet**, which is still in alpha, settling on **Ethereum mainnet** (chain id 1). The active deployment and its Aztec node version are recorded in `src/contracts/deployments.json`; see `package.json` for pinned Aztec package versions.

**The defect is ambiguity, not the word "alpha".** Aztec mainnet is in alpha, so the original wasn't false about maturity. It reads as a *network name*, though, which leaves an integrator unable to tell whether the SDK points at mainnet or at something pre-mainnet. Naming the network and keeping alpha as a maturity caveat fixes that.

**No version pinned, deliberately.** An earlier revision of this PR wrote "Aztec v5 mainnet, deployment `5.0.0_2026-07-21`". A README ships frozen into every published npm version, so a pinned deployment id is stale the next time we deploy — and `0.1.0` shipping "Aztec Devnet 4 on Sepolia" is what this ticket exists to clean up. `deployments.json` is the authority and updates itself.

This line is on `main` and in published `0.2.1`, so it's the first thing an integrator reads on npm.

## One correction to the ticket

#1984 also claims this file hardcodes Sepolia in the quickstart (`chainId: 11155111`, an `eth-sepolia` RPC). That is **not** true of `main` or of published `0.2.1` — both use `chainId: 1, // Ethereum mainnet`, with no Sepolia reference.

It was true of `0.1.0`, pulled from npm to check: `l1RpcUrl: 'https://eth-sepolia...'` at :19, `chainId: 11155111` at :43, "Aztec Devnet 4 on Sepolia" at :274. `0.2.0` fixed the quickstart and left only this prose line behind, so that half of item 4 is already done.

## Left alone deliberately

Item 5 asks whether mainnet-only is a gap or by design. Both `deployments.json` entries are `name: "mainnet"`, `l1ChainId: 1`. No "mainnet only" line added here: if the answer is "gap" and a testnet deployment lands, that line is immediately wrong. It belongs in the developer docs once @Muzzamil1 or @AnmolBansalDEV answers.

Draft, per this repo's `CLAUDE.md` — eng reviews and merges.

body: Applies the app-side pieces of Cloudflare's [Agent Development Lifecycle](https://blog.cloudflare.com/agent-development-lifecycle) post. Most of what the post asks for (programmatic operations, reproducible tests, worktree isolation, recorded decisions) this repo already has; the two real gaps were that CI never proved the app *boots*, and that a red CI run on an agent-authored PR sat idle until a human typed `@claude`. ## 1. Headless harness e2e smoke — CI's runtime gate A Playwright smoke over the browser dev harness (`dev:harness`): the real renderer UI on the in-memory fixture Bridge, no Electron, no backend. - `apps/desktop/e2e/harness-smoke.spec.ts` — three tests: renderer boots and the sidebar tree lists the fixture vault; opening a note renders its content; palette full-text search finds a note **by body content** (proving the wasm-sqlite FTS knowledge engine answered, not the name filter) and opens it. ~13s wall clock. - `apps/desktop/playwright.config.ts` — webServer boots the harness with `--strictPort` so a port collision fails loudly instead of asserting against a stale server. One retry in CI only; locally a flake fails so it gets fixed. - New `e2e-harness` CI job (ubuntu — the harness is a plain browser page). Deliberately **not** part of `pnpm verify`: the static gate stays the six browser-free steps. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/development.md` updated so the "verify mirrors CI" wording stays truthful. - Wiring: `test:e2e` script, `@playwright/test` devDep, tsconfig include, knip entries, gitignore for `test-results/`. ## 2. `ci-autofix.yml` — push-based recovery for agent PRs `workflow_run` on CI failure, scoped to same-repo `pull_request` runs on `claude/*` branches (human branches keep the opt-in `@claude` flow). Runs `claude-code-action` against the branch with a prompt that reads the failed logs, reproduces the failing gate step, fixes the actual cause (never weakens a gate), formats first, re-runs, and pushes. Guardrails: a two-strikes rule (two consecutive `fix(ci):` commits → comment instead of push), per-branch concurrency with cancel-in-progress, `--max-turns 50`, and an explicit "if it's also red on main, say so instead of pushing" escape. ## Verification - `pnpm format:fix && pnpm verify` — green (node 24; the container's default node 22 pollutes the cloud suite's `drizzle-kit export` capture with an engine warning, which is environmental, not from this diff). - `pnpm -F @repo/desktop test:e2e` — 3/3 passing against the preinstalled chromium (`@playwright/test` 1.56 matches the chromium 1194 build). Not adopted from the post, on purpose: feature flags / gradual rollout (wrong shape for a desktop product with one deployer) and removing human deploy gates (contradicts recorded decisions — owner-only cloud deploy, manual notarized releases). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01TDLT8wr3w7knJqxXJ4oorZ --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01TDLT8wr3w7knJqxXJ4oorZ)_ --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a runtime CI gate that proves the desktop app boots, and auto‑wakes our fixer on red CI for `claude/*` PRs. Also adds a branch‑tip safeguard and a 60s timeout on a long server test to keep CI stable. - **New Features** - Headless Playwright smoke over the browser dev harness to verify renderer boot, sidebar listing, opening a note, and FTS search. Runs as Ubuntu job `e2e-harness`; kept out of `pnpm verify`. Adds `@playwright/test`, `test:e2e`, and a Playwright config. - New `ci-autofix.yml`: on failed same‑repo `pull_request` runs for `claude/*`, run `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` to read logs, reproduce the failing gate (includes `e2e-harness` via a Chromium install), format first, fix, re‑run, and push. Guardrails: two‑strikes on `fix(ci):`, per‑branch concurrency, no push if also red on `main`, and skip when the failed run’s commit ≠ branch tip. - **Bug Fixes** - Server hydration scaling test: add a 60s timeout to avoid macOS CI timeouts on shared runners; assertions and invariants unchanged. Written for commit 1cc63cb68467508aced25911bcc7c68a331b7603. Summary will update on new commits.

author: nlouty
body:
## Summary

Two related max_tokens changes:

1. **`proxy.auto_max_tokens` (new, default 40000)** — auto-routed requests (exact `model: "auto"` or any model with `auto = TRUE`) are now capped by this global limit at admission time. Previously they were checked against `unknown_model_max_tokens` (20480) or the entrance model's own `max_tokens`, neither of which reflects the serving target that routing actually picks.

2. **`proxy.default_max_tokens` 18528 → 28528** — the minimum `max_tokens` for chat requests. Missing values are injected and non-VIP requests below the value are bumped up (unchanged behavior, new value).

## Changes

- `router/services/admission.py`: `check_max_tokens` gains an `is_auto` flag; auto requests use `auto_max_tokens` instead of the entrance/unknown limit.
- `router/views.py`: passes `is_auto` (literal `"auto"` or `auto = TRUE` model) into the check; the same flag is now shared with the concurrency check.
- `router/config.py` / `config.yaml` / `docs/configuration.md` / `README.md`: new `proxy.auto_max_tokens: 40000`; `default_max_tokens` bumped to 28528.
- Tests: new admission tests for auto limits (unit boundary + end-to-end), parser tests updated to 28528, and affected proxy/context-overflow/identity/concurrency tests now create models with `max_tokens=65536`.

## Behavior note

Because the parser forces chat `max_tokens` ≥ `default_max_tokens` (28528) and admission rejects requests above the model's `max_tokens`, **any model with `max_tokens` < 28528 can no longer serve chat requests** (including VIP requests that omit `max_tokens`). Verify production models have `max_tokens` ≥ 28528.

author: njuoyx
body:
## 背景

#19 方案二：单测喂手工输入、系统测试跑手工序列，漏掉的 bug 都藏在**没人想到的操作序列**里——#17（直播中关录制再开不恢复）当初就是用户报出来的。本 PR 把序列编排交给 Hypothesis：一个 `RuleBasedStateMachine` 驱动**真实应用**打 fake B 站服务器（复用 #12 的 FaultConfig 故障注入），每步之后内联检查 #19 方案一同款的不变量；序列打破任何一条，Hypothesis 自动收缩出最小复现。

## 规则集（用户和 CDN 能做的事）

| 规则 | 动作 |
|---|---|
| add_task | 给房间加录制任务 |
| begin_live / end_live | 开播 / 下播 |
| enable_recorder / disable_recorder | 录制开关 |
| start_monitor / stop_monitor | 监视开关 |
| break_stream | CDN 中途掐断连接（下次连接断一次） |
| bad_bytes | CDN 掺入非 FLV 字节（段落诚实收尾） |
| send_danmaku | 观众发弹幕（连着的客户端必须收得到） |
| let_time_pass | 放一段时间（后台任务推进、增长窗口累积） |

## 不变量（每步之后检查）

1. **声称在录 ⟹ 磁盘在涨**（`GROWTH_GRACE`=3s，复用方案一常量）；
2. **dl_total 在涨 ⟹ 磁盘跟上**（同 3s 窗口）；
3. **录制开着 + 房间在播 ⟹ 1s 内录起来**——检查自己**主动等满**窗口（轮询到点），不赌 Hypothesis 后续恰好排到足够的步数：健康的 enable 是同步拉起录制的，等满只发生在真卡死时；
4. **弹幕客户端自称连着 ⟹ 刚发出的弹幕 2s 内到账**——后台监视器不敢查这条（分不清"没收到"和"没发过"），状态机自己就是发送方，借口不成立；客户端掉线或录制停止即取消义务。

故障收尾段的诚实停顿：坏字节后录制器停下等新开播周期（`test_data_corruption.py` 记录的取舍），计数器冻结是故意的——这段挂起不变量 2/3；重新启用录制、重启监视器或下播即解除。本测试用 `no_invariant_monitor` 标记豁免后台监视器（它按自己的时钟采样、不懂这条规则，会对着同一段诚实停顿误报）。

## #17 还原验证（验收标准）

把 8520222（「启用录制时，正在进行的直播要立刻接上」）还原成修复前的实现后，**无人提示**，状态机自动找到失败序列并收缩为（在最终预算 max_examples=16 下复验，输出与预算翻倍前完全一致）：

```
add_task → begin_live → bad_bytes → disable_recorder → enable_recorder
[recorder enabled + live ⟹ eventually recording]
enabled and live, given 1s to start, yet nothing is recording
```

其中 `bad_bytes` 是探索路径上的偶发前缀；去掉它的裸核心 `add_task → begin_live → disable_recorder → enable_recorder` 同样命中——正是用户上报的「直播中关掉录制再打开，什么都没发生」。恢复修复后该测试稳定绿。

## 测试放置与预算（unit vs system）

放在 **tests/system**：状态机驱动的是完整应用（真 HTTP、真事件循环、真落盘），与系统测试共享 fake 服务器与故障注入，语义上就是系统级；且它每步都要等真实异步落地，进 unit/component 门禁会拖慢每次提交的反馈。预算：`max_examples=16`、`stateful_step_count=10`、`derandomize=True`（种子取自测试名，任何机器任何时刻跑的序列完全一致——找到过的 bug 永远找得到，绿 run 不靠运气）、`database=None`。

预算取 16 而不是更小：derandomize 固定种子下 8 个例子从头到尾没人下过播，`end_live` 这条规则和它牵头的挂起解除路径成了死路；16 个例子让**全部 11 条规则至少走一次**（含 send_danmaku 3 次、end_live 1 次）。

## CI 时长影响

- 状态机绿 run：**约 40s**（本地多次实测 38.3 / 38.4 / 38.6s，derandomize 下确定复现）。
- 系统套件整体：约 84s → 约 122s（+约 40s，仅影响 st.yml；ci.yml 的 unit/component 门禁不受影响）。
- 失败场景（bug 存在时）会因收缩重放花几分钟——那正是它该慢的时候，且绿 run 永远见不到（derandomize 下确定性）。

## 变更清单

- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`：dev 依赖加入 hypothesis（锁文件仅新增 hypothesis + sortedcontainers）。
- `tests/system/conftest.py`：`no_invariant_monitor` 标记豁免后台监视器。
- `tests/system/test_stateful_exploration.py`：状态机本体（约 560 行含文档注释，11 规则 + 4 不变量）。
- `.gitignore`：`.hypothesis/`、`.stateful_tmp/`（沙箱 /tmp 只读，临时目录放工作区内）。

## 验证记录

- 质量门禁（ruff / ruff format / mypy strict / pytest unit+component / import smoke）：全绿（1154 passed）。
- 系统套件全量：112 passed, 2 xfailed。
- 状态机绿 run 连测多次稳定（同一 derandomize 序列）；还原 #17 后必现失败并给出上述最小复现，且在 max_examples=8 与 16 两档预算下收缩结果一致。

author: sonicah
body:
Closes #2336

PSD returns club names title-cased, so federation prefixes lose their capitals — `Ksc Blankenberge`, `Kfc Eppegem`, `Kvk Ieper`, and our own **`Kcvv Elewijt`**. The BFF passed them straight through, so every surface that renders a club name showed the flattened form.

## Changes

`normaliseClubName()` in `apps/api/src/psd/transforms.ts` uppercases known federation prefixes wherever they sit in the name (`Peutie Fc` → `Peutie FC`), capitalises after a hyphen (`Erpe-mere` → `Erpe-Mere`), and pre-passes the legacy letter-spaced `K c v v` spelling the token pass can't reach. It's idempotent, so an already-correct `localName` passes through untouched.

Normalising at the transform sites rather than at decode time is deliberate (issue decision 1): decoding would also rewrite player names, competition labels, and any future name-ish field, for no extra coverage.

The web-local `formatClubName` — shipped with the poster rebuild because a lowercased prefix reads as a typo at print size — is gone, along with its `CLUB_ABBREVIATIONS` set and test block. Story and test fixtures are re-cased to what the BFF now emits.

## Two deviations from the spec, both flagged for review

**1. `KWS` added to the prefix set.** Decision 2 says no exception map, and decision 4 framed the port as verbatim-plus-one-pre-pass. But `"Kws Club Lauwe"` ships in our own season fixture list and still rendered flattened — the exact bug this issue exists to fix. It's a prefix-set token, not a name→name map, and without it the re-cased fixtures would contradict the "as the BFF now emits" AC. One-line revert if you disagree.

**2. A second consumer-side re-caser was found and removed.** The issue's grep found `formatClubName`; it missed `normalizeTeamName` in `apps/web/src/lib/mappers/match.mapper.ts` (`name.replace(/^Kcvv\b/i, "KCVV")`, applied to BFF-supplied match names). It's a guaranteed no-op now, and leaving it would have shipped the "consumers must not re-case" rule already violated. Removed with its test case; its `"Kcvv Elewijt"` / `"Kfc Turnhout"` input fixtures were re-cased since they misrepresented BFF output.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @kcvv/api lint && type-check && test` — clean, **453 passing**
- `pnpm --filter @kcvv/web check-all` — clean, **3301 passing** across 290 files, build compiles

New BFF tests cover federation prefixes, prefix-in-any-position, hyphenation, the `K c v v` legacy case, idempotence, the ordinary-words no-op, and all three transform sites — including that the ranking site normalises the **resolved** `localName || name` rather than one branch.

## Review gate

`/code-review` (both axes) and `/simplify` (reuse · simplification · efficiency · altitude) ran on the branch. The spec axis came back clean — all ACs met, no scope creep, and the issue's claim that `service.ts:895` (`OpponentHistory`) is covered for free was independently verified (it reads off an already-transformed `Match`). A grep for other emission sites found none: `sync/psd-sanity-sync.ts` writes own-club *team* docs, which aren't federation-prefixed.

**Applied:** the `normalizeTeamName` removal above · a `toMatchTeam` builder now backs four of the five sites, so match-side normalisation is by construction rather than by remembering — the reviewer's point that five hand-wired sites leave an unenforced invariant, which is how the web copy drifted in the first place · the Scheurkalender test now feeds **raw** PSD casing and asserts it survives, which actually proves the absence of local re-casing (the first version asserted a normalised fixture renders as itself — tautological) · `token.toUpperCase()` no longer computed twice · stale reference to `formatClubName` in the locked poster spec · `apps/api/CLAUDE.md` records where casing lives.

**Skipped:** pruning pro-league-only prefixes (`KAA`, `RC`, `AS`) from the allowlist. Worth knowing: the set matches any token at any position, so a club whose name ends in the Limburg municipality **As** would become `AS`. Under the old scope that set only met proofread poster opponents; it now meets every club in every ranking table. No instance exists today, and decision 2 rules out a name map — flagging rather than pre-emptively fixing.

**Not a finding, but worth recording:** an orphaned `next dev` on :3111 from a previous session had been running ~23 h and was starving the vitest workers — `check-all` failed on a *varying* set of unrelated page tests (`/jeugd`, `/evenementen`, `/ploegen`) with 5–12 s timeouts, on this branch **and** on untouched `main`. Killing it made all 3301 pass. Worth remembering before chasing a phantom regression.

## Summary

- Pin the exact AR6, Copernicus Marine, GOCO06S, EGM2008, and regional DEM control inputs required by the selected vertical methodology.
- Validate large logical source sets through checksum-locked manifests and fail closed before generic acquisition can misuse them.

## What changed

- adds one shared, lightweight speech-text module for conservative normalization and non-prose risk classification
- detects the locked identifier, URL, and contents/list patterns that failed in the experiments without rewriting identifiers or ordinary dates
- adds a saved-script Audit control showing entry-level categories, exact normalized previews, transformations, and an explicit audio-validation state
- recommends targeted transcription or human listening for risky entries while reporting that preflight itself did not run ASR
- removes mean pitch as a fallback gender classifier
- replaces unsupported fixed epoch, sample-count, and Clone-versus-LoRA quality claims with evaluation and blind-listening guidance
- adds regression coverage derived from the measured failure probes

## Why

The replicated experiments showed that identifiers and other non-prose material fail far more often than ordinary prose, broad number normalization can worsen identifiers, pitch is too unstable to serve as a gender boundary, dataset size is not a monotonic quality proxy, and neither Clone nor LoRA won consistently across voices.

## User impact

Users can audit saved scripts before generation and see exactly which entries need extra listening or transcription review. TTS normalization remains conservative and traceable. Voice selection no longer guesses gender from a numerical pitch boundary, and training guidance points users toward retained evaluation evidence instead of unsupported heuristics.

No ASR dependency, automatic voice promotion, production threshold, or fabricated human result was introduced.

author: andreialexandruparaschiv
body:
## What

Adds a **flag-gated** data source that fetches the offsite cited URLs (YouTube, Reddit) from the **Semrush-backed Serenity URL-Inspector** endpoints exposed by **spacecat-api-service** (the Elements proxy, `src/controllers/elements.js`) and feeds them into the existing offsite pipeline **unchanged**.

Epic: [LLMO-6488](https://jira.corp.adobe.com/browse/LLMO-6488) · Story: [LLMO-6709](https://jira.corp.adobe.com/browse/LLMO-6709) · Plan: #2779

**Spec (PR template §4):** `docs/specs/2026-08-05-offsite-cited-urls-semrush-source.md` · **ADR:** `docs/decisions/002-offsite-cited-urls-semrush-source.md` (both added in this PR).

## Why a loader

The downstream pipeline (`selectTopUrls` → `addUrlsToUrlStore` → DRS → cited/youtube/reddit-analysis) only understands one input contract: `allUrls: Map<url, { count, domain }>`. The Semrush API returns a shape-incompatible response (structured JSON, per-hostname, requires auth + brand/org resolution + week→date mapping, carries exact citation counts). The loader is the single, isolated adapter that turns that into the exact map the pipeline already consumes — so **everything downstream is reused untouched**.

## How

- **New** `src/utils/offsite-brand-presence-semrush.js` → `loadCitedUrlsFromSemrush()`:
  - Calls `GET {SPACECAT_API_URI}/v2/orgs/:spaceCatId/brands/:brandId/serenity/brand-presence/url-inspector/domain-urls?hostname=…` for each offsite hostname (`youtube.com`, `reddit.com`).
  - Builds `allUrls` with **`count = row.citations`** (exact; not recounted by repetition), reusing the existing `classifyAndNormalize` for URL normalization, owned-URL filtering and domain bucketing → **the same map shape** as today.
  - `spaceCatId` from `site.getOrganizationId()`, `brandId` via `resolveBrandForSite`, date window via `getDateWindowForPreviousWeeks`.
- **Handler** (`offsite-brand-presence/handler.js`): gated by `OFFSITE_BRAND_PRESENCE_SEMRUSH_ENABLED`. Flag **off** = today's PostgREST → SharePoint path (no behavior change). Flag **on** = **Semrush-first with automatic fallback**: if the loader yields no usable URLs (auth failure, no brand, outage, empty), it falls back to the legacy `loadBrandPresenceData` so a Semrush problem can never silently zero out offsite. `selectTopUrls` (per-surface top-70, ranked by citations) is **unchanged** in every case.
- `domain-urls` requested with `pageSize=100` (covers the per-surface top-70 in one page).
- **`export classifyAndNormalize`** from the enrichment module for reuse.

## Endpoint & auth — via spacecat-api-service, not a raw gateway

These are first-class api-service routes (`elementsController.listDomainUrls`, `listCitedDomains`, …). The loader calls **api-service** — the same host the worker already targets via `SPACECAT_API_URI` — rather than hardcoding the `llmo.experiencecloud.live` edge.

Auth is simple: the loader mints a **service IMS token** via the existing `ImsClient` and sends `Authorization: Bearer`. The Elements proxy's `resolveElementsImsToken` authenticates IMS callers directly and **forwards the token to Semrush** (its fallback path — see `requireImsBearer`), so **no `x-promise-token` is required** for a service caller. (A promise token is forwarded only if the platform later threads one onto the context, for non-IMS callers.)

> Remaining validation (not a code blocker): confirm the worker's **service** IMS token is authorized by the upstream Semrush gateway. Flag stays off until verified end-to-end.

## Platform coverage

Omitting `platform` does **not** aggregate across engines (the proxy resolves an absent value to a single default engine). The loader queries the **full offsite provider set** mapped to serenity models via `SEMRUSH_PLATFORM_BY_PROVIDER` (`google-ai-mode`, `search-gpt`, `microsoft-copilot`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `google-ai-overview`, `perplexity`) and **sums citations per URL**. Override with `OFFSITE_SEMRUSH_PLATFORMS`. Validating the map upstream is [LLMO-6710](https://jira.corp.adobe.com/browse/LLMO-6710).

## Reliability

- **Per-request timeout (10s) + concurrent requests** (`tracingFetch`), so a hung/slow upstream can't stall the audit past the timeout or serialize behind other calls.
- **Any per-request failure → loader returns `null` → full legacy fallback.** A partial Semrush result (e.g. YouTube ok, Reddit failed) is never shipped as success.
- **Truncation warning** when a full page (`>= PAGE_SIZE`) is returned (server-side citations sort is assumed, not confirmed).
- Path segments URL-encoded; brand resolution uses `resolveBrandResultForSite` to log "confirmed no brand" vs "transient failure" distinctly.

## Behavioral parity with the legacy path

There are two `classifyAndNormalize` functions: the enrichment one (hostname match + normalization) and the stricter `handler.js:170` one (adds `YOUTUBE_URL_REGEX` / `REDDIT_URL_REGEX` + `isExcludedCitedHost`). The loader normalizes with the former and **re-applies both regexes** (`handler.js:199-204`) so the Semrush path drops non-thread Reddit URLs (e.g. `/settings`) and lookalike YouTube hosts (e.g. `music.youtube.com`) exactly like the legacy path. A test asserts this. `isExcludedCitedHost` only affects the top-cited bucket and will be applied when that bucket is added.

## Scope / follow-ups

- ✅ **YouTube + Reddit** (fixed hostnames, one `domain-urls` call each).
- ⬜ **Generic "cited" bucket** — needs a `cited-domains` discovery hop; follow-up under LLMO-6709.
- ⬜ **Region scoping** — loader sends no region; legacy spans `ACCEPTED_REGIONS` (6 markets). Documented as a known gap (LLMO-6710); must close before non-US parity.

## Config

| Env | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `OFFSITE_BRAND_PRESENCE_SEMRUSH_ENABLED` | (off) | `"true"` switches the source to Semrush |
| `SPACECAT_API_URI` | `https://spacecat.experiencecloud.live/api/v1` | api-service base (standard worker override) |
| `OFFSITE_SEMRUSH_PLATFORMS` | full provider set (`SEMRUSH_PLATFORM_BY_PROVIDER`) | override: comma-sep engines to query + sum |

## Testing

- New `test/utils/offsite-brand-presence-semrush.test.js` — **100% coverage** on the loader (happy path, per-platform sum, owned-URL filtering, all precondition guards, per-request error handling).
- Extended the handler test with flag-on cases (map + null).
- Full suite green: **9411 passing**, coverage gate (100% lines/branches/functions/statements) satisfied.

author: develephant
body:
## Overview

Completely redesigned the Desktop Buddy Studio from a manual frame-by-frame sprite editor into an **automation-focused project builder**. The new workflow prioritizes importing organized asset folders over manual editing, enabling users to build complete buddy projects in minutes.

## Problem

The original studio required users to:
- Add frames one-by-one via gr.ImageEditor
- Manually manipulate frame order (move left/right buttons)
- Separately configure each animation state
- No support for buddy type selection, backgrounds, foreground, or icons
- Poor fit for the actual use case: importing pre-drawn animation sequences from organized folders

## Solution

**4-tab automation workflow:**
1. **Project Setup**: Name, buddy type (static/shadow-box), canvas size → create project
2. **Import Assets**: Point to folder with state subfolders (idle/, walk/, happy/, etc.) → auto-detect & batch import
3. **Configure**: Per-state FPS, loop toggle, preview animations, upload backgrounds (day/night), foreground
4. **Build & Export**: Assign icons, generate sprite.json, export to sprites/ directory

## Changes

### Backend
- **SpriteProject** (`studio/project.py`): Added `buddy_type`, `backgrounds` (day/night dict), `foreground`, `icons` dict
- **sprite.json format**: Extended to include buddy_type, backgrounds, foreground, icons fields
- **sprite_io** (`studio/sprite_io.py`): 
  - New `auto_detect_states(folder)` - scans for state subfolders
  - New `import_from_folder(project, folder)` - batch loads frames from organized structure
  - Updated `load_sprite`, `export_sprite`, `export_zip` to handle all new fields
- **Sprite loader** (`sprite.py`): Now loads and exposes buddy_type, backgrounds, foreground, icons; added methods `background()`, `foreground_layer()`, `icon_path()`

### Frontend
- **app.py** (`studio/app.py`): Complete rewrite with 4-tab Gradio UI
  - Removed frame-by-frame editing UI (gr.ImageEditor, frame manipulation buttons)
  - Added project creation dialog, folder import, state configuration, animation preview
  - Clean handler functions for each workflow step

### Config
- **pyproject.toml**: Removed studio from workspace members (not a separate package)

## Verification

- ✓ All Python syntax validated
- ✓ Studio app builds successfully
- ✓ Sprite loader imports without errors
- ✓ Auto-detect and import functions work as expected
- ✓ Export/zip functions handle new fields

## What This Enables

- **One-click buddy creation** from organized asset folders
- **Future extensibility** - easy to add new states, backgrounds, or buddy types
- **Groundwork for visual programming** - structure is ready for Blockly integration
- **Full sprite.json support** - day/night backgrounds, foreground, icons, buddy type now supported throughout the pipeline

## Migration Notes

Existing sprite.json files without the new fields will continue to work (graceful defaults). New projects leverage the full feature set automatically.

author: lumiere001
body:
Refs #184 — 이 Issue 의 선행 단계이며 여기서 닫히지 않는다.

## 무엇을 고치나

**#184 가 전제한 "회수"가 제품에 없었다.** 현재 `권한 회수` 는 역할을 STAFF→STUDENT 로 한 칸 내릴 뿐이고 `RoleRequest` 를 `REVOKED` 로 만들지 않는다. `REVOKED` 를 만드는 유일한 함수는 spec 에서만 호출되는 죽은 코드였다.

이 PR 이후 회수는 **`User.role` 을 `null` 로 비우고 `RoleRequest` 에 새 `REVOKED` 행을 삽입**한다.

## 왜 삽입인가 — 그리고 왜 **조건 없이 항상**인가

기존 `APPROVED` 행을 덮어쓰면 관리자 상세의 요청 이력에서 **"누가 언제 승인했는가"가 사라진다.** 이 숫자는 장학금 근거가 되므로 이력을 지우지 않는 쪽을 택했다(Tech Lead 결정).

**삽입은 조건 없이 항상 한다.** "APPROVED 가 있을 때만"으로 만들면 **직접 부여된 STAFF**(신청 없이 관리자가 올린 사람 — 전이표가 허용하는 실재 경로)를 회수했을 때 행이 안 생기고, 그러면

1. 병합된 [#675](https://github.com/JNU-SWCU/oss-hub/pull/675) 의 시드 가드(`roleRequests: { none: { status: REVOKED } }`)가 무력화돼 **다음 로그인에 권한이 되살아난다**
2. 재신청이 `findLatestRequest === null` 로 막힌다
3. 화면에 회수 안내가 뜨지 않는다

## 지시받은 것보다 한 칸 더 좁혔다 — `pendingState === NONE`

"STAFF 일 때만 허용"으로 두면 **`STAFF + PENDING 요청 + desiredRole:null + REJECT`** 조합이 통과한다(REJECT 분기 조건이 `current.role !== STAFF && desired.role === STAFF` 라 false). 그러면 요청 쓰기 자리를 REJECTED 가 차지해 **역할만 비고 REVOKED 행은 없는 계정**이 생긴다 — 위 1번을 정확히 재현하는 상태다.

그래서 `STAFF && pendingState === NONE` 으로 좁혔다. **대기 중 요청은 먼저 결정하고 회수는 그다음**이며, 대기 요청이 있는 상태의 회수는 409 다.

## 과거 마이그레이션을 되돌리는 것이 아니다

⚠ 마이그레이션 `20260721190000_add_user_account_status` 가 legacy 의 `role IS NULL` + REVOKED 조합을 `role='STAFF'` + `DEACTIVATED` 로 **되돌려 놓았다.** 그 SQL 과 회귀 테스트를 읽어 이유를 확인했다.

당시 되돌린 이유는 **회수와 비활성을 구분해 담을 자리가 없었기 때문**이다. legacy 회수 표현은 `role IS NULL` 뿐이었는데 그 값은 "아직 아무 역할도 못 받은 신규 가입자"와 글자 그대로 같아서 회수된 사람을 알아볼 방법이 없었다.

지금은 구분자가 **셋** 있다.
- `RoleRequest` 의 `REVOKED` 행 — #675 가 이미 로그인 시드 가드에서 이것을 회수 판정 근거로 쓴다
- `User.accountStatus` — 회수(권한 박탈)와 비활성(계정 정지)이 별개 축이 됐다. 당시 둘을 합쳐 놓은 것 자체가 자리가 없어서 한 임시 조치였다
- `User.selectedRole` — 2026-08-04 #569 로 추가돼 "무엇을 골랐는가"가 `role` 과 분리됐다

즉 그때의 결정을 뒤집는 것이 아니라, **그때 없던 구분자가 생긴 뒤 원래 의도(회수 = 권한 박탈, 비활성과 별개)로 복귀**하는 것이다. 기존 마이그레이션 회귀 테스트는 그대로 통과한다.

## ⚠ 이 PR 만 배포하면 사용자에게 보이는 변화가 **없다**

프런트 `adminAccessRevokeTargetRole` 이 STAFF 에 대해 `'STUDENT'` 를 하드코딩해 돌려주므로 **`desiredRole: null` 을 보내는 경로가 프런트에 아예 없다.** 화면은 계속 STUDENT 강등으로 동작하고 새 회수 능력은 UI 에서 도달 불가한 채 놓인다.

위험은 "말과 다른 파괴적 동작"이 아니라 **"고쳤다고 보고했는데 사용자에게는 아무 변화가 없음"** 이다. **PR3·PR4 와 묶어서 배포해야 한다.**

### PR4 선행 조건

프런트 `features/roles/admin-access-api.ts` 의 `AdminAccessDecidedRequest.status` 는 `APPROVED | REJECTED` 뿐이고 런타임 파서도 그 둘만 통과시킨다. 지금은 null 요청 경로가 없어 드러나지 않지만, **PR4 가 회수 버튼을 null 요청으로 바꾸기 전에 그 타입과 파서를 `REVOKED` 까지 넓혀야 한다** — 아니면 회수 성공 응답을 파싱하다 화면이 터진다.

## 지시와 다르게 판단한 것 (Codex 교차리뷰에서 전부 `reject` 판정)

- **`toAdminAccessDecidedRequest` 를 넓히는 대신 `toAdminAccessRequestWrite`(`NONE`/`DECIDE_PENDING`/`INSERT_REVOKED`)로 바꿨다.** 회수의 행 id 는 삽입 **후에야** 생겨 `{id, status}` 반환형에 맞지 않는다. 타입으로 갈라 두면 회수를 PENDING 전용 CAS 경로에 얹으려는 시도가 컴파일에서 막힌다.
- **`roles/role-request-transition-rules.ts` 와 spec 을 삭제했다.** spec 에서만 호출되던 죽은 코드이고 회수를 "APPROVED 행 갱신"으로 적고 있어 INSERT 확정으로 무효가 됐다. `roles/AGENTS.md` 가 이것을 "원본"이라 서술하던 행과 존재하지 않는 파일 행도 정정했다.
- **감사 로그의 `before.requestStatus` 에 `APPROVED` 를 채우지 않는다.** APPROVED 행이 파괴되지 않는 것이 이 결정의 요지이고, 직접 부여 STAFF 에겐 APPROVED 가 없어 **거짓 기록**이 된다. 대상은 새로 삽입된 REVOKED 행의 id 다.

## 검증

| 검사 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| `lint` · `typecheck` · `prettier` | 통과 |
| `pnpm --filter backend test` | **202 suites / 2226 tests** (suite 수 감소는 죽은 코드 spec 삭제분) |
| `pnpm --filter backend test:integration` (실 DB) | **51 suites / 254 tests** |
| `pnpm --filter frontend test` · `typecheck` | 통과 (프런트 무수정 — 계약이 하위 호환임을 확인) |

**변이 검증 6종 — 전부 의도한 테스트만 빨간불.**

| 되돌린 것 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| 삽입을 "APPROVED 가 있을 때만"으로 | 통합 5건 (승인이력 보존 · **직접 부여 STAFF 회수** · HTTP · 동시 회수 · 로그인 경합) |
| 전이표의 STAFF 예외 제거 | 단위 10건 (oracle 6칸 + fixture 2 + 서비스 2) |
| `pendingState` 조건 제거 | 단위 9건 |
| 감사에 `APPROVED` 채우기 | 단위 1건 (+ 지역 타입이 좁아 순진한 형태는 컴파일도 안 됨) |
| 회수 삽입을 트랜잭션 밖 별도 커넥션으로 | 통합 8건 |
| 효과 상수의 **값** 변경(`UNCHANGED`→`NO_CHANGE`) | 오라클이 컴파일 실패 |

### 경합 테스트가 헛돌 수 있었다 — 실험으로 확인하고 고쳤다

리뷰에서 "대기자 **수만** 세면 무관한 세션의 대기로도 통과할 수 있다"는 지적을 받았다. 실제로 그런지 실험했다 — 무관한 잠금 대기 한 쌍을 만들고 로그인은 아무와도 겹치지 않게 둔 뒤 두 술어를 같이 쟀다.

| 술어 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| 옛 단언 `count(waiters) > 0` | **true — 통과(false pass)** |
| 새 단언 `pg_blocking_pids` 지목 | **false — 거름** |

지금은 두 트랜잭션의 백엔드 PID 를 각자 트랜잭션 안에서 잡아 **`회수 PID = ANY(pg_blocking_pids(로그인 PID))`** 가 참이 될 때까지 기다린다. 강화 후 통합 3회 완주에서 타이밍 실패 0회다.

같은 이유로 **오라클의 기대값을 리터럴로** 바꿨다. 상수를 재사용하면 효과 상수의 **값** 자체가 바뀌는 변이를 양쪽이 함께 따라가 **409건 전부 초록으로 통과**했다(실측).

### 원자성 롤백 테스트 2건

"CAS·삽입·감사가 한 트랜잭션"이 이 PR 의 핵심 주장인데 실패 시 함께 되돌아가는지가 안 덮여 있었다. 삽입 직후 실패·감사 기록 실패 두 경우에 `role` 이 STAFF 그대로이고 `RoleRequest` 가 0건임을 확인한다.

> 트랜잭션 밖으로 빼는 변이에서 경합 테스트가 타임아웃으로 죽는데, **그 원인 자체가 증거다** — 별도 커넥션의 `RoleRequest` INSERT 가 FK 검사로 대상 User 행 잠금을 필요로 해 회수 자신의 `FOR UPDATE` 에 막혀 영원히 대기한다.

## 이 PR 에서 뺀 것

- **actor RBAC TOCTOU** — Codex 가 blocker 로 지적했으나 `origin/main` 과 대조하니 해당 코드가 **바이트 단위로 동일**해 선행 존재다 → [#687](https://github.com/JNU-SWCU/oss-hub/issues/687)
- **프런트 파서** — PR4 (위 선행 조건)
- **PR 분해** — 전이표·oracle·fixture 는 계약이 물려 있어 쪼개면 중간 상태에서 CI 가 빨간불이 된다

author: al-unsoldgroup
body:
Release prep for **v1.5.0**, which ships the Cloudflare Worker line of work (PRs #12–#28) as a published version.

## What's in the release

The optional, single-tenant **remote Deployment**: the whole MCP tool registry served from a Worker in the operator's own Cloudflare account, on a D1 storage driver that passes the same FTS ranking conformance suite as the local `node:sqlite` driver. Cron sync + a queued Job engine (O(N) work becomes a Job id, not a command handback), MCP OAuth with an operator allowlist, encrypted Google tokens at rest, Trigger rules with signed webhooks, a minimal A2A surface, and a `mail-index export` → D1 seed path so a new Deployment starts with the local index's history instead of re-syncing Gmail.

The local CLI + stdio path is unchanged and stays the default.

## This PR

- **`CHANGELOG.md`** (new) — Keep a Changelog format. Thorough v1.5.0 entry with Added/Fixed/Changed/Security/Upgrading sections, plus back-filled 1.0.0–1.4.0.
- **`README.md`** — v1.5 status line, a v1.5 feature TIP, the v1.4 TIP demoted to historical, and the Documentation index now lists `INSTALL-worker.md`, `WORKER-SEED.md`, `PLAN-worker.md`, and the changelog.
- **`docs/PUBLISHING.md`** — rewritten release section: the release is now **one pushed tag** end to end (`release.yml` → npm with provenance + `.mcpb` + GitHub Release → `registry-publish.yml` via OIDC), no interactive `mcp-publisher login`. Documents the four-version-fields-in-three-files trap and adds post-release verification.
- **Version bumps** to 1.5.0 in `package.json`, `manifest.json`, and **both** `server.json` fields.

### Fixed along the way

`server.json` had never been bumped past `1.0.0`, so the MCP Registry entry advertised the launch version through four releases. It now tracks the package version, and PUBLISHING.md calls the trap out explicitly.

## Verification

`pnpm test` 427/427, `pnpm run lint` clean, `pnpm run typecheck` clean (core + Worker).

## After merge

Tag `v1.5.0` on main to trigger the publish.

author: alwaysmiddle
body:
## Design sync — component re-diff (the "components next" follow-up)

Second half of the design sync. The token pass shipped in #83; this is the full component re-diff + new ports you asked for.

> **Stacked on `chore/design-sync-2026-08-04` (#83).** Based on that branch so the shared `PROVENANCE.json` edits don't conflict. GitHub auto-retargets this to `main` once #83 merges — review/merge #83 first.

### Re-diff of all 17 vendored DS component ports
- **9 clean:** CountBadge, AppHeader, DomainDot, TrailChip, StepDot, WalkCard, BinMark, PillButton, Toolbar.
- **6 drifted, adopted (DS is source of truth):**

| Component | Drift adopted |
|---|---|
| TreeRow | text caret glyph → drawn `caretStyle` (exported) |
| InstrumentRow | text bullet glyph → drawn `bulletStyle` (exported) |
| EdgeLegend | CSS bar → `EdgeDash` SVG with `crispEdges` |
| NodeChip | `lit` shadow stacks ring under lift |
| SectionLabel | count `--fw-regular` → `--fw-medium` |
| PresetButton | inactive border always `--border-rule` |
| DocHeader | restored `|| var(--text-1)` title-colour fallback |

- **PaneHeader:** adopted the DS **auto-hide close** — the `✕` is hidden while a pane is at rest and appears on pointer/focus inside it, so a dormant pane wears an unbroken frame. Falls back to a 500 ms grace (this app has no `window.PKT_SB`).

The recurring DS direction is clear: load-bearing **text glyphs move to drawn geometry** (caret, bullet), and sub-pixel rendering is hardened (crisp dash, stacked lit shadow).

### New port
- **InstrumentGroup** (+ `FamilyColumn`) — the palette family grouping. Reuses `caretStyle` from TreeRow so the palette and the tree draw nesting the same way. Added to the `@/ds` barrel alongside `EdgeDash`.

### Tooling
- `eslint.config.js`: relax `react-refresh/only-export-components` for `src/ds/**` — DS components ship colocated style helpers (`caretStyle`, `bulletStyle`, `FamilyColumn`) that siblings import by name; splitting them out would diverge from the DS module shape for a dev-only HMR nicety.

### Deferred: LeafMark (blocked on the asset, not the code)
`assets/leaf.png` (1870×841) exceeds DesignSync `get_file`'s 256 KiB cap (returns truncated) and no copy exists in the workspace, so the binary can't be pulled through any available channel. **To unblock:** download `assets/leaf.png` from the DS project and drop it at `src/ds/chrome/leaf.png`; the port is then trivial (Vite asset import, drop the DS `base` prop). Not landed here because a component importing a missing asset slips through `npm run verify` yet breaks `npm run build` — recorded in `PROVENANCE.json`.

### Verification
- `npm run verify` green — typecheck, lint, **155 tests**.
- Studio shot driver renders every change correctly (drawn bullets/carets, crisp dashes, auto-hidden pane close); only the 5 pre-existing stale-expectation asserts remain.

body:
…s CSV

For an ISP onboarding to WIFI.OS who already ran PPPoE by hand, and for moving client data out. Enterprise-grade on purpose:

Import (adopt existing /ppp/secret users off the router):
- PREVIEW first — reads the router's secrets and shows which are new, which WIFI.OS already manages, and the plan each maps to (matched by MikroTik profile name).
- The ISP tweaks name + plan per row, then imports the selected ones.
- IDEMPOTENT — a username already managed is skipped, so a re-run never duplicates.
- PER-CLIENT isolation — one bad row is recorded and skipped, never aborting the batch.
- NON-DISRUPTIVE — DB-only adoption keeping the router's exact password (read fresh, server side); the client's live session is never touched.
- Gated behind can-transact (an unverified ISP can't bulk-activate) and audited.

Export: stream every client to CSV — a portable backup / migration out.

New adapter capability list_pppoe_secrets (MikroTik reads /ppp/secret; dummy for tests). 5 new endpoint tests (preview flags, adopt+skip, idempotency, no-plan skip, CSV). Full suite 825 green, schema clean.

author: gurgant
body:
Emit the response metadata the API emits, and only where it emits it

U42, U18, U40 off the drift backlog, plus two residuals from earlier PRs of
mine. All measured on the running stack first; all six mutation-proven.

U42 -- the audit said "every mock error body omits instance". Both halves are
wrong, and applying it as written would have traded one drift for its mirror:

  PRESENT  FluentValidation 400, domain 404/422/400, JWT 401  (the API's own
           handlers, which each assign Instance = Request.Path)
  ABSENT   framework model-state 400, deserialisation 400, terminal 404,
           BFF 401, BFF step-up 403

One mock site already emitted it -- through `extensions`, which appended it
AFTER traceId instead of before. So instance is a fingerprint of WHICH HANDLER
answered, like the title and the traceId format. Threaded through the 28
API-shaped sites, deliberately left off the 9 BFF-shaped ones.

Member order came with it: ProblemDetails serialises declared members first,
then Extensions in insertion order, so the answer is errorCode THEN traceId.
The mock had traceId first, which matches neither handler.

U18 -- the reveal is the one response carrying an unmasked account number and
the only one given cache directives (ASVS 14.3.2). Measured, with a neighbour
as the control:

  GET /api/accounts/{id}/full-number -> Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache
  GET /api/accounts                  -> neither header

U40 -- `TransferId = outgoingTransaction.Id`: the response names the debit row
it just wrote. The mock minted a synthetic id belonging to no row, so the
follow-up GET was a 404 under MSW and a 200 in production:

  POST /api/transfers/internal -> transferId 019fd135-37c7-78d4-9d7b-8afcde4c6e3f
  GET  /api/transactions/019fd135-…    -> 200, type "TransferOut"

The audit also called this a collision with the deposit block. It is not --
every block indexes off transactions.length, which strictly increases, so no
two writes can draw the same index. Sharing the base is still worth removing.

Two things earlier PRs of mine missed, both found by measuring rather than by
re-reading:

- #77 aligned IdempotencyException.KeyMissing and left KeyInvalid paraphrased.
  Real: "The 'Idempotency-Key' header must be a valid UUID."
- #78 fixed the renameAzureTag envelope and left the unreadable-body one. An
  unreadable body never reaches a validator, so the answer is the FRAMEWORK
  envelope, and an ABSENT body is keyed by the EMPTY STRING where only a
  malformed one is keyed `$` -- a sixth key shape, after Name, at, $, $.type
  and FluentValidation's camelCase. Both hosts agree.

CodeRabbit then caught that `raw.trim()` put a whitespace-only body in the
absent branch. Measured before accepting: "   " reaches System.Text.Json and
fails there, so it is `$`. Fixed and covered.

The contract assertions run on mock AND real, including the ABSENCE of
instance -- without that half, the sweep the audit invited would still pass.
