author: mako987-cyber
body:
Il sito passa da vetrina personale a **strumento di vendita**: si inizia a proporre servizi di cloud engineering a contesti banking e finance, e il viola elettrico della PR #8 comunicava creatività consumer invece che affidabilità infrastrutturale.

## La struttura, prima della grafica

Il problema più grosso non era la palette. **La root non vendeva**: chiedeva *"Cosa vuoi fare? — Portfolio o provati il giochino retrò"* e firmava *"Aniello's Playground"*. Un lead che arrivava da LinkedIn atterrava su un bivio tra portfolio e giochi retrò.

- **`/` diventa la home commerciale**: proposta di valore, prove, CTA unica verso i contatti.
- **Le prove erano sepolte.** `4+ anni`, `200+ dispositivi`, `−40% ticket` esistevano già ma stavano in una card laterale dell'hero; ora sono il primo argomento dopo la proposta di valore.
- **Navigazione unica** su tutte le pagine — `Home · Servizi · Progetti · Profilo · [Contatti]` — con Contatti come **bottone** e non come link di testo: in una nav di servizi professionali la CTA deve staccarsi.
- **`pages/portfolio/home.html` non è stato cancellato** ma è diventato un redirect a `/`: quell'URL potrebbe già essere stato condiviso.

## La professionalità sta nella sobrietà, non nella tinta

Il grafite/smeraldo (`#0d1117` / `#161b22`, accento `#10b981`) conta meno di tre scelte strutturali:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Aurora** | dal 40% al **12-18%** |
| **Movimento di fondo** | **rimosso** — legge consumer e distrae dalla lettura; sparisce anche il compositing continuo |
| **h1** | da `clamp(2.8rem, 6vw, 6rem)` su 11ch a `clamp(2.05rem, 3.8vw, 3.4rem)` su 20ch |

La misura precedente dell'h1 era spettacolare ma spingeva ogni contenuto sotto la piega. Ora proposta di valore e prove stanno nella prima schermata.

**Lo smeraldo è dosato**: solo CTA, stati attivi e valori numerici. È il difetto tipico dei siti "professionali" fatti male, colorare tutto finché l'accento non significa più niente.

## Monogramma AM

A e M fuse in **un unico percorso continuo**: il piede destro della A è anche il montante sinistro della M. Monocromatico, nessun gradiente — deve reggere su fattura, firma email e slide, non solo su schermo.

**A 16px il monogramma impasta.** Verificato rasterizzando i provini, non a occhio: il favicon usa la sola **A** a quella taglia e il monogramma completo a 32 e 48.

## Bug trovati e risolti

1. **La CTA "Contatti" era illeggibile in tema chiaro.** `.nav-menu a` ha specificità 0-1-1 e sovrascriveva il colore di `.btn--primary` (0-1-0), lasciando la CTA con il colore dei link di testo sopra il fondo pieno. Risolto con `:not(.btn)` — necessario, non cosmetico.
2. **Il link "Progetti" funzionava in produzione e si rompeva in locale**, per via del livello che `trailingSlash` aggiunge all'URL servito rispetto al path del file. Ho eliminato la classe di bug passando **tutti i riferimenti interni a path assoluti**: niente più calcoli di profondità per pagina, nessuna divergenza fra locale e deploy. Verificato che ogni riferimento risolva.
3. **Space Invaders era rimasto senza navigazione**: il suo header aveva un link "← Progetti" al posto del `<nav>`, quindi non veniva agganciato.
4. **Copy fattualmente sbagliate**: il titolo di Space Invaders diceva "VAPORWAVE" e "NEON ARCADE TRANSMISSION", descrivendo un design rimosso due iterazioni fa.

## Contatti

`placeholder@example.com` sostituito da **`TODO-EMAIL` in un unico punto**, e il link GitHub generico (`https://github.com`) corretto sul profilo reale.

## Note per chi revisiona

- ⚠️ **Finché `TODO-EMAIL` resta, il sito non ha un canale di contatto funzionante.** È in [`pages/portfolio/contact.html`](pages/portfolio/contact.html), sostituibile con una riga.
- **Ho toccato una copy oltre il perimetro concordato** (era "visivo + gerarchia", senza riscrittura testi): quella di Space Invaders. Era una descrizione fattualmente errata di sé stessa, non una scelta di posizionamento — ma è reversibile.
- **Le copy di servizi e profilo restano in registro da curriculum** (elenco di tecnologie invece che problema → esito → prova). Escluse per scelta: sono il candidato naturale per il passo successivo.

author: g-garciac2022
body:
## #91 · Registro automático de integraciones

Closes #91

R1.9 —escrito al ordenar la extensibilidad en #86— dice que añadir una fuente de
datos o una señal de análisis **no debe obligar a modificar las herramientas
existentes**. La mitad de interfaz ya estaba cumplida por el envoltorio uniforme
de señales; la de servidor no: `main.py` listaba los `register()` a mano, así que
añadir una integración obligaba a editarlo. Poco código, pero exactamente lo que
el requisito dice que no debe hacer falta.

### Qué incluye
- `backend/integrations/discovery.py`: recorre el paquete, importa el `tool` de
  cada uno y llama a su `register(mcp)`. Añadir una integración pasa a ser crear
  su paquete.
- `backend/main.py`: cinco líneas de registro pasan a dos.
- 7 tests en `tests/integrations/test_discovery.py`.

### El chequeo de salud queda fuera, y no como excepción
Al plantearlo apareció la pregunta de si `health` debía moverse a
`integrations/` para que el descubrimiento lo encontrara. La respuesta es que
**no**: no envuelve ninguna API externa, es infraestructura básica — del mismo
tipo que el *healthcheck* de un contenedor.

Y eso lo deja **fuera del alcance de R1.9 por definición**, porque el requisito
habla de «una fuente de datos o una señal de análisis». Que `main.py` lo registre
explícitamente no es un caso especial que disculpar: es la separación correcta, y
las dos líneas que quedan significan algo.

```python
discover_integrations(mcp)  # todo lo que haya en integrations/
health.register(mcp)  # núcleo, no integración
```

Esto además resuelve para #97 la misma pregunta, que allí aparecía como «¿qué
integración de origen tiene `health_check`?». Respuesta: ninguna.

### Un paquete roto no tumba el servidor
Si una integración falla al importarse o su `register` lanza, se anota y se sigue
con las demás — misma postura que con las señales en `/analyze`, y lo que piden
R1.8 y R2.8. El arranque registra qué se descubrió y qué falló, porque una
integración caída deja al sistema con menos herramientas **en silencio**: sin ese
log, la única pista sería una tool que ya no aparece.

### El test que demuestra el requisito
`test_un_paquete_nuevo_aparece_sin_tocar_main` crea una integración de mentira en
un directorio temporal y comprueba que aparece sola. Para no ensuciar el
repositorio, extiende el `__path__` del paquete `backend.integrations` —la lista
donde Python busca submódulos—, de modo que el import funcione de verdad sin
copiar ficheros dentro del proyecto.

Sin ese test, R1.9 sería una afirmación; con él es comprobable.

### Notas
Verificado que el servidor real sigue sirviendo **las 11 tools** por `stdio` tras
el cambio: el descubrimiento registra las mismas cuatro integraciones que estaban
escritas a mano.

El resultado del descubrimiento (`registered`, `failed`, `degraded`) se devuelve y
se registra al arrancar, pero **no se expone por HTTP**. Publicarlo es decisión de
#97, donde encaja con cómo refleja el contrato un servidor caído.

Descubierto de paso: `ruff format` también formatea el Python dentro de los
bloques de código de Markdown, así que el `README.md` entra en la comprobación de
estilo del CI.

112 tests en verde.

author: wkich
body:
**Follow-up to #222.** Closes the deferred items called out in #222's final review, plus four robustness fixes surfaced by the first end-to-end dogfood runs of the autonomous runner. No papai runtime code changed — only `mutation-improve/`, `scripts/mutation/json-readers.ts`, and tests.

## Runner robustness fixes (dogfood-driven)

- `2b20cac` — ignore `.mutation-improve/` runtime scratch directory.
- `678b15e` — wrap `runIteration` in try/catch so a thrown exception (`AgentRunError`, git failure, Stryker crash) routes through `failIter` instead of leaking the worktree + its `mutation-improve/<runId>-iterN` branch and dropping the failure from run state.
- `70684ef` — wire the previously-parsed-but-unconsumed `--reset-worktree` flag to `resetRunWorktrees`, which sweeps stale `<runId>-iterN` worktrees left by a crashed/killed prior run (keyed by runId so concurrent runs sharing a repo are undisturbed).
- `71697e7` — throw on non-zero Stryker exit code in `measureMutationScore` so a crashed mutation run can't return a stale report's score.

## Deferred hardening items (from #222 final review)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-mutation-improve-hardening-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-mutation-improve-hardening.md`. Three non-blocking items bundled as one test-first hardening pass:

1. **Parser coverage + NaN guard** (`04786bd`, `c92f35d`) — `parseCliArgs` had uncovered branches (unknown arg, missing value, non-integer `--count`, default config path). Worse, a non-numeric `--threshold=` silently set `config.threshold = NaN` — the CLI override bypasses the Zod `[0,1]` range check — which made gate ⑤ reject every iteration. Guarded with `Number.isFinite` (rejects `NaN` **and** `Infinity`) and added the missing characterization cases.
2. **Typed-error retry** (`aa491aa`, `68fff09`) — `measureMutationScore` decided whether to retry by regex-matching error-message *wording* emitted by a foreign module (`scripts/mutation/json-readers.ts`); a routine rephrasing of that prose would silently disable the retry. Introduced `ReportReadError` (thrown by `readStrykerReport`) and re-keyed the retry on `instanceof ReportReadError || err.code === 'ENOENT'`. The trigger set is preserved exactly (report-missing `ENOENT` and wrong-shape retry; `JSON.parse` SyntaxError / plain errors / non-zero Stryker exit propagate); only the coupling to sibling prose is removed. The dead `malformed` regex alternative matched nothing and is gone.
3. **Cross-workspace contract guard** (`2ff15fb`) — `mutation-improve` consumes a broad surface of `review-loop/src/*`. TypeScript catches symbol removal/rename at compile time, but there was no guard against behavioral drift and `contracts.test.ts` only tested the two Zod schemas. Added a behavioral tier (`LiveRenderer.log` passthrough; `createShellExec`+`runBuildCheck` exit→passed mapping) and a runtime inventory tier of the consumed symbols so drift fails loudly in mutation-improve's own gate. Deliberately **no** facade / shared workspace — `cli.ts` keeps its direct imports (composition root); the spec's Tier-B arity claim was retired (`02750f4`) since arity is compile-checked at the call sites.

## Verification

- `mutation-improve` 61/61; `review-loop` 289/289 (no shared-file change this round); `scripts/mutation` 171/171; root suite 11097/0; `bun check:full` lint/typecheck/format/knip clean.
- Four per-task reviews + a final whole-branch review (merge-ready: **yes**, no critical/important findings). Retry trigger-set preservation verified case-by-case against the prior regex path.
- All edits are test-only or minimal source changes; the score-reader retry's behavior is unchanged by construction.

author: blotus
body:
Add new helpers to allow scoring of a request:
 - `AddRequestScore(points, reason)`: add points for the given reason. Can be negative (eg, because something in the request is trustworthy)
 - `RequestScore()`
 - `RequestScoreReasons()`
 - `RequestScoreFor(reason)`
 
This allows to write more granular appsec configs and to use weaker signals to make a decision whether an IP is coming from a bot or not (eg, `utc_timezone` is set. It's very unusual, but blocking based only on this would be too harsh):

```
inband:
  on_challenge_submit:
    - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("cdp")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(100, "cdp")
    - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("webdriver")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(100, "webdriver")
    - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("webdriver_writable")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(100, "webdriver_writable")
     - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("headless_screen_resolution")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(50, "headless_screen_resolution")
     - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("gpu_mismatch")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(30, "gpu_mismatch")
    - filter: EvaluateMismatches().Has("high_cpu_count")
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(30, "high_cpu_count")
    - filter: RequestScore() >= 75
      apply:
        - 'RejectSubmission("request score " + string(RequestScore()) + ": " + join(RequestScoreReasons(), ","), "verbose")'
```
 
 While currently targeted towards the challenge mode, it can also be used to score any request:
 ```
  - filter: req.Header.Get("Accept-Language") == ""
      apply:
        - AddRequestScore(15, "no_accept_language")
```

## Outcome
- replace the decoded-video backpressure queue with a capacity-1 `keepLatest` timeline slot
- release stale NVDEC leases before the next burst and count replaced frames explicitly
- stop scaling NVDEC output surfaces with network `bufferMs`; retain the fixed four-surface decoder bound
- add a reproducible delayed-output backlog scenario to the existing short `tools/interop.ps1` harness

## Root cause
When caller input connected before a listener output peer, SRT buffered media while backend construction waited for the output peer. Startup then delivered a burst. The decoded-frame queue retained more mapped NVDEC frames than the GPU could map, so the pipeline failed before normal queue backpressure with `cuvidMapVideoFrame64` code 205.

body:
Authored by Claude Code (Opus 5) at the owner's keyboard.

Picks up the detached-submit fix released as tollbooth-dpyc **0.80.1** (SDK #178/#179), which
unblocks #341.

## Why hand-bumped instead of left to Renovate

The shared preset schedules `"* 0-6 * * 1"` — **Mondays only** — with `dependencyDashboard:
false`, so there is no checkbox to request an earlier run. Today is Wednesday, so #341 would
have stayed `blocked/upstream` until 2026-08-10 while every scheduler tick kept 409'ing.
Renovate will find the pin already at 0.80.1 when it next runs and do nothing.

Extras preserved (`[nostr,prefect]`), and `uv.lock` regenerated with `--refresh-package
tollbooth-dpyc` — a plain `uv lock` 404s on a wheel PyPI has only just published.

## What lands

`start_async_job` used to call `submit(claim, closure_b64)` even for kinds with **no**
`job_spec`, so `closure_b64` stayed `None`. Prefect rejects that on its parameter schema, and
the dispatch-failure handler swallowed the 409 as a generic `in_process_fallback`. After this,
runner-only kinds run their registered in-process runner directly, with no Prefect hop and no
409.

## What this does NOT change — stated so #341 closes on accurate grounds

The scheduler launches **`resolve_post_body`**, which is runner-only by design:
`register_job_spec` in `server.py:1391` covers **`resolve_dynamic_block`** (the single-block
FE preview) only. So post resolution stops making a pointless round trip, but still runs
in-process and still dies with its container.

Durable execution for a multi-block post build is a design question, not a null check — a
closure seals ONE declarative HTTP request, while building a post is N model calls with
control flow between them. Worth its own issue rather than being quietly assumed fixed here.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/` — 352 passed
- `ruff check .` — clean
- Post-merge, the tick summary should carry no `degraded: in_process_fallback` /
  `PrefectHTTPStatusError` for `resolve_post_body`. That is the behavioural check, not the sha.

## The bug

`gc hook <agent>` serves work routed to **other agents**, and to **other rigs**.

The work query filters on `gc.routed_to`, but under the native-store fallback that predicate is not applied — so the filter silently does nothing. `--claim` is unaffected; this is the bare read path only.

Reproduced 2026-08-05 at the live v62-db/v53-binary skew. `gc hook gascity/builder` returned five beads and **one** belonged to it:

| bead | actually routed to |
|---|---|
| `ga-5hdwl6` | `gascity/deployer` |
| `ga-drlztz` | `beads/reviewer` — **a different rig** |
| `ga-77refr` | a reviewer session |
| `ga-20zoji` | nothing at all |
| `ga-2a46gb` | `gascity/builder` ✅ |

## Why it costs real money

This is the mechanism behind the phantom-wake burn (`gm-ob7is`). The agent wakes, is handed work that is genuinely not actionable by it, **correctly declines**, and pays a full turn with full cache-read to discover that. Measured ~119K cache-read per message on `beads/builder`, with wake gaps shrinking 6:10 → 2:46 — it accelerates rather than settling.

The skew is global, so every rig over-serves at once. Four rigs currently show `ready > 0` with `in_progress = 0`. Two agents were suspended by hand to stop the bleeding. Prior art for the magnitude: #4630, 522 measured no-op wake cycles in 44.7h.

## Why a post-filter in gc, and not a store fix

Deliberate, for three reasons:

1. It holds whether or not the store honours the predicate.
2. It does **not** require the gc/bd pin to move, which is under an explicit operator ruling (2026-07-30) not to touch unilaterally.
3. **#5030 would not fix this either.** Its pin (`bf97b73`, top migration `0059`) reaches v59 against a **v62** database, so gc would still fall back and the predicate would still be dropped. Closing the skew needs a beads release at v62 — which is where beads `main` already sits.

When the skew is eventually closed this becomes redundant, but stays correct.

## Fails open, everywhere

A filter that can silently empty an agent's queue is a worse outage than the over-serving it replaces. So:

- unparseable or non-array output → returned unchanged
- non-object candidates → kept
- **empty `routed_to` → KEPT.** Unrouted work is legitimately claimable, and the legacy workflow-target path (`routedToOrLegacyWorkflowTarget`) depends on it
- no identities threaded → byte-identical to previous behaviour, which keeps every other `doHook` caller safe

Only a `routed_to` that *positively names someone else* is dropped. `rig/role` and `rig--role` compare equal, so an agent's own work can never be dropped over a spelling difference.

## Tests

7 new in `cmd_hook_foreign_route_test.go`:

- the exact live five-bead shape above
- own-work preserved across all four spellings (exact, session-form identity, session-form route, case)
- identity matched from anywhere in the set
- fail-open on five malformed inputs
- `doHook` reports no-work when only foreign candidates remain
- `doHook` still reports work when one bead is genuinely ours
- `doHook` unchanged when no identities are threaded

Existing `-run Hook` and `-run 'Route|Routed|Dispatch|Assigned'` both pass. `make build` and `go vet` clean.

Fixes ga-lmy6yj. Unblocks gm-ob7is.

body: ## Summary Ports `sas/03_sas_risk_scoring.sas` (STEP 1 → STEP 6) and its `connect_teradata` / `log_step` / `validate_table` macro dependencies to a runnable PySpark package. `python -m risk_scoring.driver` reproduces the SAS program end-to-end against the committed extracts, and `python validation/compare_to_oracle.py` diffs the result against the reference output. **Parity against `data/03_sas_data_products/customer_risk_scores.csv`: 407/407 rows, 0 mismatches on every deterministic field** — composite score, all five components, `RISK_TIER`, `SCORE_DELTA_30D`, `REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG`, `WATCH_LIST_FLAG` — and an identical tier distribution (LOW 290 / MODERATE 113 / ELEVATED 4). 164 unit tests. Both entry points fail closed: the driver exits 1 when the STEP 5 gate aborts or the connection is misconfigured, the comparison exits 1 when the exact regime fails, so either can gate CI as written. Two findings the diff alone won't tell you, both detailed in [`docs/validation_report.md`](docs/validation_report.md): **1. The oracle disagrees with the SAS source on risk drivers.** Whenever the clamps are inactive, `CREDIT_RISK_COMPONENT` and `(100 - BUREAU_SCORE_COMPONENT)` are the same number, so array index 0 and index 3 tie on nearly every row and the tie rule alone decides the top-2: ``` SAS: strict `>` walked in array order -> first index wins -> CREDIT_UTILIZATION oracle: -> BUREAU_SCORE (294/407 primary, 407/407 secondary) ``` This port follows the SAS source. Chasing the oracle was rejected: no simple rule reproduces it (last-index-wins still leaves 9 primary / 16 secondary mismatches), so its ordering looks like an unstable sort rather than a specification. `compare_to_oracle.py` reports these two columns in their own section and excludes them from the verdict. **2. The logistic model has nothing to fit.** `PAYMENT_LATE_CNT` is `0` for all 478 staging rows, so `DEFAULT_FLAG = (PAYMENT_LATE_CNT > 2)` is `0` for all 407 active customers — a single-class target. Stepwise selection reports "no predictors entered", the intercept-only MLE is emitted (`PROB_DEFAULT = 0.0`), and a `WARNING` is logged. The oracle emits a constant `0.05`, which is not reproduced because nothing in the SAS program computes it. The divergence does not propagate: `WATCH_LIST_FLAG` needs `PROBABILITY_OF_DEFAULT > 0.5` and a CRITICAL tier, neither of which occurs, so that column matches exactly and is gated by the verdict rather than treated as distribution-only. **This dataset therefore does not exercise the model**; stepwise was validated separately against the real feature distributions with a synthetic non-degenerate target (recovered intercept -2.281 / slope +2.244 against a true -2.0 / +3.0). ### What's here | Module | Replaces | | --- | --- | | `risk_scoring/ingestion.py` | STEP 1 `WORK.RISK_RAW` + STEP 2 `WORK.RISK_FEATURES` | | `risk_scoring/model.py` | STEP 3 `PROC LOGISTIC ... selection=stepwise` | | `risk_scoring/scoring.py` | STEP 4 composite score, tiers, top-2 drivers, flags | | `risk_scoring/validation.py` / `audit.py` / `sink.py` | `%validate_table`, `%init_audit`/`%log_step`, STEP 6 `DELETE` + `PROC APPEND` | | `risk_scoring/connections.py` | `connect_teradata.sas` LIBNAMEs — `JdbcBackend` (Teradata) and `CsvBackend` (local extracts) behind one `Connections` | | `risk_scoring/driver.py` | the STEP 1→6 program itself, plus the `PROC FREQ` tier report | | `validation/compare_to_oracle.py` | new: oracle diff, stdlib-only | Notable ported semantics: SAS treats missing as less than zero, so imputation is `isNull() | (col <= 0)` and both division guards are `when(denom > 0, ...).otherwise(1.0)`; `%validate_table`'s asymmetry is preserved exactly (row-count and duplicate-key failures abort and short-circuit the remaining checks, null checks only warn); `where COL is missing` is true for blanks, so string null checks count blanks too. **No credentials in source.** The `{SAS004}XXXX` placeholders are gone; `JdbcBackend` resolves `$TD_PASSWORD` from the environment per operation and redacts it from every log line. `CsvBackend` needs no credentials, which is what makes the local parity run possible. ### Deliberate deviations - `min_rows` comes from `PipelineConfig.min_rows`, still **defaulting to the SAS 1000**. The committed extract yields 407 rows, so a literal port aborts STEP 5 on the only data available; local runs pass `--min-rows 400`. - STEP 6 is a single `mode("overwrite")` and is therefore idempotent; the SAS `DELETE` + `PROC APPEND FORCE` pair was not (a failure between them left the target empty). `COLLECT STATISTICS` is dropped. - `PROC APPEND FORCE` silently dropped columns the target lacked; the sink raises `SinkContractError` naming them instead. - MLlib exposes no p-values for `LogisticRegression`, so the score-test entry and Wald exit statistics driving `selection=stepwise` are computed in-module from the observed information matrix. **Open recommendation, not actioned here** because the task mandated `LogisticRegression`: `GeneralizedLinearRegression(family="binomial", solver="irls")` *is* Fisher scoring and *does* expose `coefficientStandardErrors`/`pValues`, so switching would remove the optimiser, standard-error and chi-square deviations at once. ### Environment discrepancy The reference generator named in the task — `run_demo.phase3_python_analytics`, imported by `export_data.py` from `local/duckdb/` — **does not exist**: there is no `local/` directory and a filesystem-wide search finds only unrelated copies in other checkouts, so `export_data.py` is broken on `main` as committed. The committed *output* CSV was used as the oracle instead, which is why finding 1 could only be diagnosed by inference rather than by reading the reference source. ### Testing ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest tests/ -q # 164 passed python -m risk_scoring.driver --min-rows 400 # 407 rows loaded python validation/compare_to_oracle.py # verdict: PASS, exit 0 ``` Independently re-run from two fresh clones and fresh virtualenvs, including adversarial checks that the parity harness can actually fail (perturbed numerics, mutated flags, deleted rows) and that an aborted validation leaves the previous output untouched. Report in the PR comment below. Built by four parallel child sessions against [`docs/pyspark_migration_contract.md`](docs/pyspark_migration_contract.md), then integrated here: #51 (ingestion), #54 (model), #53 (scoring), #52 (validation/audit/sink). author: taigfs
body:
Follow-up to **#105**, from the 2026-08-05 sweep for runtime `raw.githubusercontent.com` config reads (companions: `dfl-harness#467`, `internal-skills#6`, `dfl-infra#441`).

## First, the good news

**#105 worked.** Verified against the **published tarball**, not the source: `@devfellowship/components@3.0.1`'s `dist/cli.js` has **zero `fetch(` calls**, the vendored schema is inlined, and the only `raw.githubusercontent` string is the schema's `$id`. `ux-paths validate` is genuinely offline. Nothing here fixes a live break.

There are also **two** copies of this CLI, and the other one is fine: `dfl-ux-paths:cli/lib/load-schema.ts` has always read `schema/v1.json` off local disk, so it was never affected.

## ⚠️ Now the part that matters: this repo's CI is a no-op

The generic **Install / Build / Test / Typecheck / Lint** steps all probe for a `package.json` at the **repo root**. There isn't one — everything lives in `packages/ui`. So every step prints `⚠️ No … found, skipping` and the job reports **`✅ CI passed`**.

Verified on run [30941973561](https://github.com/devfellowship/dfl-components-cli/actions/runs/30941973561):

```
⚠️ No package.json found, skipping install
⚠️ No build script found, skipping
⚠️ No test script found, skipping
⚠️ No typecheck script found, skipping
⚠️ No eslint config found, skipping
✅ CI passed
```

**So the vitest suite added in #105 — written specifically to stop this bug recurring — has never run.** The guard had the same shape as the bug it was guarding against: a check that quietly stopped checking and reported success. Exactly the pattern this sweep exists to kill.

## What this PR adds

**`packages/ui/scripts/check-cli-bundle-offline.mjs`** — asserts on the artifact users actually execute. The #105 unit test spies on `globalThis.fetch`, which is necessary but not sufficient:

- it covers only the module it imports, not the whole CLI surface;
- it catches `fetch` and nothing else — a future `https.get`, `node-fetch`, `undici` or `axios` sails straight past;
- it runs on **source**. Users run `dist/cli.js`, built by a separate tsup config.

The check also asserts the vendored schema **is** inlined: a bundle with no network I/O *and* no schema would be a `validate` that silently accepts everything — strictly worse than the 404 it replaced, because nothing would complain. `dfl-flows-engine` has the same bundle-level defence, and it is why that repo never acquired this bug.

A missing `dist/cli.js` is an **ERROR** telling you to build, never a skip.

**A CI step that actually runs.** Installs and builds explicitly in `packages/ui`, **no `continue-on-error`**, and also runs `vitest run src/cli/` — so the #105 suite (32 tests) finally executes.

## What this PR deliberately does *not* do

Repair the generic steps. Pointing them at `packages/ui` immediately turns the repo **red**: 9 test files fail to load on a React/JSX resolution problem entirely unrelated to the CLI (`Failed to resolve import "react/jsx-dev-runtime"`). That is a real fix and deserves its own round rather than being smuggled in here. It is flagged loudly in a comment block in `ci.yml` instead of being papered over.

## Verification

```
$ npm run build:cli && node scripts/check-cli-bundle-offline.mjs
OK: dist/cli.js is offline-safe — no network primitives, vendored schema inlined,
    1 identity-only raw.githubusercontent reference.

$ npx vitest run src/cli/
Test Files  5 passed (5)     Tests  32 passed (32)
```

Negative tests, run locally — the guard bites in all three directions:

| injected | result |
|---|---|
| `await fetch("https://example.com")` appended to the bundle | exit **1**, points at the line |
| `dist/cli.js` removed | exit **2**, "this is a failure, not a skip — run `npm run build:cli`" |
| unmodified bundle | exit **0** |

body:
Companion to **zimmertr/Kubernetes-Manifests#593**. `CLAUDE.md` requires a deploy-flow change to update `docs/CICD.md` in the same PR, and the flow spans two repos, so the manifest change comes back here.

## Why the manifest changed

`docs/CICD.md:286` described the functional gate as "a real `/api/analyze` through Overpass and Open-Meteo". That coupling blocked **every deploy** on 2026-08-05, measured against production:

```
$ curl -s -X POST https://bluebirdforecast.com/api/analyze -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '<the exact body the AnalysisTemplate sends>'
{"detail":"Open-Meteo quota reached. Try again later."}
HTTP 429
```

No `results` key, so `len(result.results) >= 1` cannot evaluate true; `failureLimit: 0` aborts the analysis; the rollout is blocked. Including a 1.0.0 cut.

The quota was exhausted by one day of development against Open-Meteo, which is the exact cost issue #224 already documents.

## What changed here

The table row now reads `/api/destinations` through Overpass, and a short paragraph records why the gate stops short of a forecast and what that trades away. The honest version of the trade is in the text: discovery proves that *this* image serves in *this* cluster, the forecast path is covered by the suites at PR time, and Overpass becomes the single upstream a deploy depends on.

## Merge order

This is docs-only and safe to merge in either order, but it describes the state **after** KM#593. Merging this first leaves the doc briefly ahead of the manifest.

## STRINGS PENDING APPROVAL

**None.** Documentation prose only; no user-facing application string is added or changed.

author: trevor-42
body:
## What

Whenever Timelapse or heavy AI metadata is enabled, the result card showed two contradictory numbers: **busy-hour peak exceeded the "if all saturate at once / absolute max" ceiling**. A camera cannot peak above its own stated maximum.

## Why

`ceilingMbps` summed only each camera's *video* encoder ceiling (`activeKbps × vsrc`). But `peakKbps` adds the Timelapse stream and AI event metadata on top of that video number. Timelapse is a second continuous stream uploading alongside the main one, so a camera's true simultaneous max is `video ceiling + timelapse + AI` — exactly what `peakKbps` already reflects. The ceiling figure was understating the max by omitting both.

## Fix

One line in `totals()`: accumulate the real per-camera max (`ceiling + tlKbps + aiKbps`) into the saturation total, so `ceiling ≥ peak` always holds. The video encoder cap inside `camMetrics()` is untouched, so per-camera avg/peak numbers do not move.

## Verification

Node self-check on the model:

- Reference deployment (12 R200, 4 R410 +LPR, 2 R600, 8 R230 archive-off) unchanged: **31.6** sustained, **68.9** peak, **100** recommended. Its ceiling corrects **96.0 → 96.2** to count the R410 LPR metadata it was previously dropping.
- R600 + Timelapse + High: was peak **13.21** > ceiling **12.00**; now peak **13.21** = ceiling **13.21**.

## Reviewer note

author: colinsohn
body:
Ran a real whissle.ai agent through the half-duplex path (`--agent whissle_voice`) end to
end — ElevenLabs-voiced gpt-4o user simulator → LiveKit room → Whissle STT/LLM/TTS, tools
delegated back over the data channel and executed by tau2. Two harness bugs surfaced; both
are fixed here. The product finding from the run is recorded below.

## What's fixed

**1. The `voice` extra is required, and the run now fails fast without it** (`ef0f88e`)

`livekit-agents` (which brings `livekit.rtc`) lives in the `voice` optional extra, but both
Whissle guides said to install with a plain `uv sync`. Following the docs, every task fails
identically — and only *after* the run is underway:

```
livekit.rtc is required for the whissle provider but failed to import: No module named 'livekit'
```

- `WHISSLE_HALF_DUPLEX.md` / `WHISSLE_VOICE.md`: install line is now `uv sync --extra voice`,
  with the failure text spelled out and a troubleshooting row for it.
- `run_hd.sh`: preflight `import livekit.rtc` next to the existing env-var guards, so a bad
  install costs a second instead of a whole run.

**2. Each spoken turn is recorded once, not three times** (`24c9de8`)

`_on_data` read the agent's words from both `bot-transcription` and `bot-output`. Agents that
emit both carry the same words twice, and the `bot-output` stream can itself replay a turn —
so a real retail run recorded every utterance **3×** (`bot-transcription`=5, `bot-output`=18
in one session). That pollutes both what the user simulator reads back and what
communicate-info scoring matches against.

`bot-output` is now what it was always meant to be: a **fallback** for agents that never emit
`bot-transcription` (the companion agent, notably), plus a bounded recency window
(`deque(maxlen=32)`) so a self-repeating stream is recorded once while a line legitimately
said again later in the call still gets through.

New `tests/test_voice/test_audio_native/test_whissle_transcript.py` — 6 tests replaying the
message sequences captured from the real run. Non-vacuity checked: with the fix stashed,
`test_bot_output_ignored_when_transcription_present` and
`test_repeated_bot_output_stream_is_not_duplicated` fail. Full `tests/test_voice/`:
**111 passed, 69 skipped**, no regressions. Confirmed live too — the verification run logged
**0** `bot-output`-sourced lines where the previous run logged 18.

> Scoring note: the triplication predates the recorded `results/whissle/VOICE_RESULTS.md`
> Pass^1 = 0.20, so that number was measured against a tripled transcript.

## The product finding: ASR on spelled identifiers

Retail task 0 — reward **0.0**, 364s, termination `user_stop`, **0** agent errors, 0 user
errors. DB match ✗, read 0/4, write 0/1. The three tool calls the agent made:

```
run 1  find_user_id_by_name_zip {first_name: 'Youssef', last_name: 'Rossi', zip: '19122'}   → User not found
run 1  find_user_id_by_name_zip {first_name: 'Youssef', last_name: 'Rossi', zip: '199122'}  → User not found
run 2  find_user_id_by_name_zip {first_name: 'Youssef', last_name: 'Rossi', zip: '191222'}  → User not found
```

The record is `yusuf_rossi_9620` — **Yusuf** Rossi, zip **19122**. The agent's reasoning and
tool use were correct at every step: right tool, right argument shape, re-asked instead of
guessing, offered a transfer when it stayed stuck. Only the ASR failed. `Yusuf → Youssef` is
deterministic across runs; the zip corrupts differently on each re-spell (a digit doubles).

Not a harness, key, or contract problem — the text path with the identical `system` + `tools`
injection returns a clean tool call:

```
POST /api/bench/agent-turn → {"reply":"","tool_calls":[{"name":"find_user_id_by_email",
  "arguments":{"email":"sara_doe_496@example.com"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use"}
```

This independently corroborates the existing `VOICE_RESULTS.md` root cause (`W2378156` heard
as `W0378156`, then `W237856`) with a **name** rather than an order ID — so it's spelled
alphanumerics generally, not an ID-format quirk. The actionable direction there still holds:
alphanumeric-tuned ASR, read-back-by-digit confirmation, or preferring email-based auth for
ID-heavy voice flows.

## Verified working end to end

`wsk_` key auth · `POST /api/bench/voice/start` → live LiveKit creds · room join ·
ElevenLabs caller audio published · Whissle STT→LLM→TTS responding · `bench-tool-call`
delegated → tau2 `env.step()` → `bench-tool-result` returned.

## Not in this PR

A full-suite retail Pass^1. The single-task smoke run is what's behind the numbers above;
the long run lands as a follow-up commit with a `results/whissle/` write-up. No credentials
are committed — all three live in the git-ignored `.env`.

author: y3owk1n
body:
## Description

This PR removes the last place a mode command's flags were written down by
hand. The flag tables for hints, grid, recursive_grid, scroll and
monitor_select were kept by hand in five separate command sections, so a flag
added to a mode reached the binary without reaching the documentation — and a
reader had no way to tell which of the two was right.

There is now one mode flag reference, generated from the same declaration that
registers those flags on the command line, and rewritten by `just genflagref`.
The per-command sections keep their prose and point at it. The mode synopses
stop re-listing flags that are documented one section above, so they cannot
drift either.

Two architecture guardrails hold the arrangement: one fails when a declared
flag is not offered by exactly the modes that accept it, when a command offers
a flag nothing declared, or when a mode has no command at all; the other
regenerates every page carrying the reference and fails while any of them is
stale. Two new simulation journeys cover the other end — a hotkey binding
carrying flags, asserting each one took effect, and a binding the grammar
refuses, asserting nothing activates and nothing is drawn.

## Related Issues

Closes #1192

## Target Platform

- [x] Platform-agnostic (shared logic, no OS-specific code)
- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Linux
- [ ] Windows

## Type of Change

- [ ] `feat` — New feature
- [ ] `fix` — Bug fix
- [ ] `refactor` — Code restructuring (no behavior change)
- [ ] `perf` — Performance improvement
- [x] `docs` — Documentation only
- [ ] `test` — Adding or updating tests
- [ ] `chore` — Build, CI, dependencies, tooling

## Command and documentation surface

No command, flag, config key or default changes. Every flag the binary accepts
before this PR it accepts after, spelled the same way.

One new development command:

```bash
just genflagref     # rewrites the generated region of docs/CLI.md
```

Run it after adding, removing or re-wording a mode flag. The architecture test
fails while the page is out of date, and names the flag that is missing.

## Cross-Platform Checklist

- [ ] OS-specific files use correct build tags (e.g., `//go:build darwin`)
- [ ] No darwin imports from untagged (shared) code — [The One Rule](https://github.com/y3owk1n/neru/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#the-one-rule)
- [ ] Stub implementations added for other platforms (returning `CodeNotSupported`)
- [x] N/A — This PR does not touch platform-specific code

## General Checklist

- [x] Code formatted (`just fmt`)
- [x] `just ci` passes — the exact checks CI runs (format check, lint, vet,
      tests including `-race`, vulnerability scan, build)
- [x] Tests added/updated for new or changed functionality
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Commit messages follow [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

## Additional Context

The guardrails were checked by breaking them on purpose and reverting:

- a flag declared without regenerating the page fails the reference test,
  naming the flag;
- a flag hand-registered on a command fails the registration test on every
  command that offers it;
- a declared flag skipped during registration fails it the other way;
- the CLI-owned `--debug` hand-added to grid fails, because the exemption is
  scoped to the modes allowed to offer it rather than to the flag name.

The flagged simulation journey was likewise checked against a deliberately
dropped modifier, so it is not passing vacuously.

The generated table gives up the per-flag `Default` column the hand-written
tables carried, since a declaration cannot render a configured default; those
defaults now live in prose under the table. `pflag` moves from an indirect to a
direct dependency — the registration guardrail enumerates a command's flags.

body:
[FCFIELDS-90](https://folio-org.atlassian.net/browse/FCFIELDS-90) - Add LOOKUP custom field type
  
## Purpose

This adds a new `LOOKUP` custom field type that stores the UUID of a record in another
FOLIO app (Organizations, Users, …), so host modules and finder plugins can render and resolve
that reference.

## Approach

- **Schema** - new `LOOKUP` value in `ramls/customFieldTypes.json`, new
  `ramls/lookupField.json` sub-object with a required `refEntityType` (open-ended lowercase
  string, mirroring `customField.entityType`), referenced as an optional `lookupField` property
  on `ramls/customField.json`.
- **Definition validation** - `LookupDefinitionValidator` (`@Component`, auto-discovered via the
  `Validatable` list injection) checks `LOOKUP_ALLOWED_FIELDS` and then explicitly requires
  `lookupField` and a non-blank `refEntityType`, since `onlyHasAllowedFields` only rejects
  disallowed sub-objects and cannot enforce required ones.
- **Value validation** - `LookupFieldValueValidator` enforces the repeatable contract
  (`List` when `isRepeatable`, non-`List` otherwise) and a format-only UUID check.
- **Interface** - `custom-fields` bumped `3.1` → `3.2` in `ModuleDescriptor-template.json`
  (additive schema change), with a matching `NEWS.md` entry under *New APIs versions* / *Features*.
- **Tests** - `LookupDefinitionValidatorTest` and `LookupFieldValueValidatorTest`, plus
  `lookupField.json` / `lookupRepeatableField.json` fixtures under
  `src/test/resources/fields/model/`, matching the per-type test convention.

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [4c6895a7-a374-4da5-9c6f-9acf69a1a7bf](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/4c6895a7-a374-4da5-9c6f-9acf69a1a7bf?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/4c6895a7-a374-4da5-9c6f-9acf69a1a7bf?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in cmd_lab View ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in the authenticated `cmd_lab` view in `introduction/views.py`. ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application passes user-controlled data into an operating system command without strict validation or escaping. An attacker can use shell metacharacters or crafted arguments to run arbitrary commands with the privileges of the application process. This can expose sensitive data, alter system state, or provide a path to broader compromise. ## Changes Made The `cmd_lab` view in `introduction/views.py` previously took the posted `domain` value, interpolated it into an `nslookup` or `dig` command string, and executed that string with `shell=True`, which made the input a command injection sink. The fix now normalizes the submitted domain, strips any leading scheme or `www.` prefix, and rejects values that do not match a hostname, `localhost`, or IPv4 pattern before any lookup runs. It also changed the command construction from a shell string to an argument list, and it executes `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False` so the input is passed as data rather than interpreted by the shell. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from Sonar remediation for pythonsecurity:S2076: - **Prevent command injection by sanitizing/validating user input**: The fix strips protocol prefixes, normalizes the domain, and rejects anything that does not match a strict `re.fullmatch(...)` allowlist before any command is built, which directly implements the guidance to ensure the input does not contain malicious commands. - **Do not construct the OS command from user-controlled data**: The command is now assembled as an argument list (`['nslookup', domain]` / `['dig', domain]`) and executed with `shell=False` in `subprocess.Popen`, which removes shell interpretation and aligns with the secure remediation approach for command injection. No new libraries were required; `re` and `subprocess` were already present in the file, so there was no manifest dependency update needed. The change is stylistically consistent with the existing Python/Django view code and uses the standard library approach expected by the guidance.

author: luizstruct2flow
body:
Your acceptance pass, plus the fix for the item you rejected.

## Acceptance

TASK-001, 003, 005, 006, 007 → `done/`. **TASK-002 → `doing/`**, rejected: commits still land without naming their item.

## Why TASK-002 failed, precisely

The hook was never wrong. It is **client-side**, and that is the whole defect:

| Path | Checked before |
|---|---|
| local `git commit` | ✓ hook fires |
| CI on the PR | ✗ ran `tests/commit-msg-gate/test.sh` — exercises the hook against **fixtures**, never reads this repo's commits |
| **GitHub squash merge** | ✗ subject composed server-side from the **PR title**, where no client-side hook can exist |

`5fe89e0` went through that third row — on `main`, **after** the gate shipped, with a subject the hook rejects. Everything older is pre-gate Conventional Commits and not a violation of a rule that didn't yet exist.

The shape is one this repo keeps rediscovering: **the check and the thing it protects were two different objects.** A test of the hook is not a test of the commits.

## The fix

- **`scripts/lib/commit-subject.sh`** — one definition of the rule, sourced by both the hook and the checker. It lived inside the hook, which forced any second checker to copy the regex. Two copies are two rules that drift while each passes its own tests — the same argument TASK-005 used to delete `INDEX.md`.
- **`scripts/check-commit-subjects.sh`** — reads real subjects (`--range`, `--stdin`, `--subject`). Fails closed on an unreadable range, an unknown mode, and on an **empty** range, which usually means a shallow clone or wrong base and would otherwise report a vacuous green.
- **CI** — checks the PR title (load-bearing), the branch's commits, and what landed on `main`. Adds `edited` to `pull_request` types: it isn't a default, so a title changed after a green run would have merged unchecked.

The title is passed via the **environment**, never interpolated into the `run` block — it's attacker-controlled on a fork PR, and `${{ }}` substitutes before any shell sees it.

Verified against real history rather than fixtures: the checker rejects `0097c85..5fe89e0` naming the offending subject, and passes `5fe89e0..aaae771`.

## Two things the gate caught, both kept

1. **`--range` piped into `while` runs in a subshell** — every violation counted would have been discarded on exit and the check would report clean. Now redirected from a temp file, and reports every offender rather than only the first.
2. **Three branch-guard assertions failed** claiming the guard had fired in a derived project — a serious TASK-003 regression, except it hadn't fired at all. Its fixture copies `commit-msg` but not the rule the hook now needs, so every fixture commit was refused by the *wrong hook*. A suite that infers a cause from an outcome is only as sound as its assumption that nothing else produces that outcome.

## Gate

43 stages green. 188 s — over the 180 s SLO warning for the fifth consecutive run, `signal-dispatch` at 75 s. Non-blocking, nothing demoted.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce overly-sensitive global circuit-breaker behaviour so evolution is protected without halting safe exploration.
- Differentiate between truly dangerous/critical violations and routine invalid mutations or infrastructure failures.
- Surface a clear, dedicated event when the breaker opens for security reasons so operators can react distinctly from degraded-mode throttles.

### Description
- Raised default global circuit breaker threshold and shortened cooldown by updating `policy.yaml` and the default payload in `_default_policy_payload()` to set `circuit_breaker_threshold` to `15`, `circuit_breaker_cooldown_seconds` to `60`, and added `circuit_breaker_critical_threshold` (`3`) and `circuit_breaker_invalid_mutation_threshold` (`15`).
- Extended `RuntimePolicy` schema and serialization to include `circuit_breaker_critical_threshold` and `circuit_breaker_invalid_mutation_threshold`, and wired them into `MutationGovernancePolicy` construction and defaults.
- Modified `MutationGovernancePolicy.record_violation()` to only count violations that are security-relevant (ignore `infrastructure` and low/info severities, and non-dangerous invalid mutations), and to use a lower `critical` threshold when severity == `critical`.
- Emit an explicit `governance.security_circuit_breaker_opened` event (in addition to the legacy `governance.circuit_breaker_opened`) when the breaker opens for security reasons, and update life loop logging/publishing accordingly.
- Updated tests to cover the new behaviour and thresholds in `tests/test_immune_response.py`, and adapted assertions in `tests/test_loop.py` and `tests/test_values_schema.py` to validate the security event and new categories.

### Testing
- Ran targeted pytest runs including `tests/test_immune_response.py`, `tests/test_skill_quarantine.py`, `tests/test_values_schema.py` and relevant `tests/test_loop.py` cases; the modified test suite reported all tests passing (`25 passed`) with warnings only.
- Verified new tests assert that three non-dangerous invalid mutations do not open the global breaker, that multiple critical violations open the security circuit breaker, and that the cooldown is configurable via `circuit_breaker_cooldown_seconds`.
- Confirmed `governance.security_circuit_breaker_opened` events are emitted alongside the legacy `governance.circuit_breaker_opened` for compatibility with existing consumers.

body:
## Was

Auflösung des BEOBACHTEN-Punkts aus #168 („4 tief analysiert"-Anomalie): Die Sparse-Map-Prüfung fand eine **echte Lücke** im Klassen-Filter des Scan-Sets.

**Befund:** `collectScanSymbols` zählte nur explizite `> 0`-Regler als aktive Klassen. Beim **Handeln** gilt ein fehlender Regler aber als 1 (`klemmeGewicht(undefined)`). Sparse Maps entstehen real: Der Auto-Regler (`snapshotEquity.ts`) schreibt `{...bestand}` zurück, und ältere Konten kennen neu hinzugekommene Klassen nicht. Ein Konto mit lückenhafter Map wurde dadurch still auf die Schatten-Quote (20 %) verengt — dieselben Klassen im Scan abgeschaltet, im Handel aktiv.

**Fix:** Logik als pure, exportierte Funktion `aktiveKlassenAusGewichten` extrahiert — fehlend = aktiv (exakt wie beim Handeln), inaktiv nur bei ausdrücklich 0; ein Konto ohne Regler macht den Filter weiterhin gegenstandslos (`null`).

## Verifikation

body:
Part A of the billing-term & price-display design. Part B (annual prepay for hosting) found real money defects in whole-branch review and is being reworked separately — this PR is deliberately scoped to the presentation-only half, which is clean and independently shippable.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-billing-term-and-price-display-design.md`

## What this does

Domains are billed **yearly** (a `.com` is KES 1,500/yr) — that doesn't change. What changes is how the price is *displayed*: a `.com` now shows as **KES 125/mo**, with "billed annually at KES 1,500" always shown beneath it, on both the domain search results and the checkout order summary.

- `monthlyEquivalentKes(yearlyKes)` = `Math.ceil(yearly / 12)` — rounds **up**, so the advertised monthly figure can never annualize to less than what's actually charged. Only `.africa` is non-exact (2,500 → 209/mo, not 208).
- Disclosure is mandatory everywhere the derived figure appears — never a bare "KES 125/mo" with no annual total. This matters under Kenya's Consumer Protection Act 2012 and avoids the chargebacks a bare monthly figure invites.
- Hosting/database products are untouched — they're genuinely billed monthly already, so nothing about their display changes.
- **No billing code touched.** Same catalog products, same charge, same renewal behavior.

## Known, disclosed limitation

There's no frontend test runner in this repo, so the backend test covering `monthlyEquivalentKes` inlines its own copy of the arithmetic rather than importing the real function — it would not catch a `Math.ceil` → `Math.round` regression. A designated e2e assertion (checking `.africa` renders exactly 209, not 208) exists in a later commit on the reworked Part B branch, but hasn't run live yet (no backend credentials in the dev environment). Worth adding here too, or verifying manually before this goes live.

## Verification

- Backend: 418 tests passing, 0 failures
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from one pre-existing, unrelated `Portal.tsx` error

author: hardcoreerik
body:
User-reported via two crash dialogs (the excepthook added in round 2 doing exactly its job):

```
AttributeError: Slot 'MonitorPage::_on_ranking_node_selected(int)' not found
RuntimeError: libshiboken: Internal C++ object (_RankRow) already deleted
```

## Root cause

`RankingsPanel.update_rows()` ran on a 2-second timer and **destroyed and rebuilt every row on each tick**. A click landing while a refresh was in flight could hit a row mid-teardown: the `RuntimeError` is the direct hit; the `AttributeError` is Qt's meta-object system failing to resolve a slot further up the same signal chain (`row.clicked` → `panel.node_selected` → `MonitorPage._on_ranking_node_selected`) on an object it can no longer look up cleanly. Same race, two symptoms depending on exact timing.

## Fix

`RankingsPanel` now **pools row widgets and updates them in place** via `set_data()` instead of destroying and recreating them every refresh. A row representing the same rank across two refreshes is the same `QObject`, so it's never live-deleted out from under an in-flight click. Rows beyond the current result count are hidden, not deleted — growing back to a previous count allocates nothing new.

Also:
- Added a `shiboken6.isValid()` guard in `_RankRow.mousePressEvent` as a second layer, and the same guard in `distribution_panel.py`'s `_DistRow`, which has the **identical** destroy-and-rebuild pattern on its own refresh cycle and was one timing coincidence away from the same crash.
- Fixed a latent test-suite bug found while writing the regression test: three test files construct a bare `QCoreApplication`, but Qt's app singleton is shared across `QCoreApplication`/`QApplication` — whichever test file runs first wins it. A later test constructing a real `QWidget` on top of a non-GUI `QCoreApplication` crashes the interpreter **natively** — no Python traceback, just an abnormal exit code (reproduced 3 times to confirm). `conftest.py` now creates the stronger `QApplication` before any test module gets a chance to create a weaker one.

## Tests

9 new tests in `test_rankings_panel.py`, including one that reproduces the actual scenario rather than just calling `update_rows()` synchronously: a real `QTimer` driving refreshes on the Qt event loop, with a click delivered through Qt's own event system (`QTest.mouseClick`) while refreshes are in flight.

288 tests pass (was 279 — 9 new, 0 broken). `ruff` and `mypy` clean. Rebuilt and verified against a live radio.

author: zntznt
body:
## UX Conformance

- **P1 Predictable** — ✅ a section that looks like a list now behaves like one wherever it appears; the door no longer depends on whether the author put a total line above the rows.
- **P2 Discoverable** — ✅ the argument. `+ Add` is the visible front door to a shipped capability, and 58 of 77 shipped sections had no door at all. The only remaining path was an undocumented keystroke (click a point, press Enter), which the issue names as its workaround.
- **P3 Reachable** — N/A. No new control; the existing `.addrow-affordance` keeps its markup, keyboard path and announcement.
- **P4 Responsive** — ✅ a capability that silently isn't there reads as absent. Five real lists shipped with no way to add a row and nothing saying why.
- **P5 Coherent** — ✅ no new syntax, no new rule, no new door. It narrows which rows `inferRowShape` reads, extending reasoning #1281 already applied.

**Acceptance tests:** the Freelance costing starter in the filed report goes from **0** add-row doors to **3**, driven in a real browser; the door is then clicked and adds a row. Census across all 14 starters before/after. `node --test tests/test.mjs` green at **2062**; `node --test tests/browser.mjs` green at **7**.

**Regression:** 0 sections lose a door. Prose sections still correctly refuse. #1281's placeholder-row and `created`/`edited` behaviour pinned unchanged.

---

## The report, and how much bigger it is

The issue says Freelance costing renders no `+ Add` doors "while every other starter does." Measured across **all 14 starters, 77 heading sections**:

| | count |
|---|---|
| sections with a door | 19 |
| **sections with no door** | **58** |

Freelance costing is where the reporter noticed. `My week` — cited in the issue as one that *does* work — has the identical defect in its Habits section. Not a starter quirk: a rule that disagrees with the house authoring style everywhere.

## Cause

`inferRowShape` counts a tag or prop as a column only when **every** row carries it. That's what makes a shape reliable. But every starter writes a section the same way — total or note on top, rows beneath:

```
## Habits
  One small win, picked for me: {grammar ...}     <- no tags, no props, no checkbox
  Stretch for five minutes #habit
  Read ten pages #habit
```

One prose line fails the every-row test and takes the whole shape to `null`.

## The fix, and which half does what

Both halves extend reasoning **#1281 already applied** (a blank placeholder row isn't a data row; `created`/`edited` are bookkeeping, never a user column):

1. **A commentary row is not a member of the list it sits above.** A row with no tags, no data props and no checkbox says nothing about the shape either way.
2. **`check` joins `created`/`edited` as machinery.** It holds an assertion about the *section*, not a value of a row. A `+ Add` form asking someone to fill in "Check" is as wrong as asking them to fill in "Edited".

**Measured separately rather than bundled.** With half 2 reverted, the Freelance costing section **is still doorless** — its health-badge row survives the commentary filter, then fails the every-row test for `hours`. Half 1 fixes four sections; **half 2 is the one that fixes the reported case.**

## A kind test, not a tolerance

"Tolerate a minority of non-conforming rows" needs a fraction, and a fraction here is the unmeasured constant **#1132** bans. The rule asks what a row *is*, not how many disagree:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| sections with no shape | 58 | 53 |
| gaining a door | | **5** |
| losing a door | | **0** |

The five: `Habits`, `Claims and their sources`, `Open threads`, `Hours logged so far`, `Prototype card set`. The 53 still doorless are prose sections, which correctly refuse — dropping rows that carry nothing cannot manufacture a shape.

## Two measurement errors of mine, caught not shipped

Both the same class: **measuring a text space the running app never has.**

1. **The first pin fixture wrote the expression unfolded.** `node.text` holds `[[math:key]]` once a pill exists. Written as `{= sum("#task", …)}`, `rowContentTags` read the `#task` *inside the expression* as a tag on that prose row — the pin failed against correct code.
2. **The census walker folded too much.** It replaced every `{…}` with a token, but `{prop hours: 9}` becomes a `node.props` entry, not a token. Eating it silently reduced the ratchet to the tag half, and it went **green** when a mutation stripped `#task` off a shipped row. A pin that cannot fail is not a pin (#1133) — caught only by running that mutation. The walker now lifts prop/date declarations into props and asserts the **columns** as well as the tag.

## Verification

A driven check joins the committed browser smoke (#1427) rather than being proved privately: the pure core says a section *has* a shape and says nothing about whether a door reaches the screen, and the reported symptom was a DOM count. It asserts the door renders **and clicks it** — a door that renders and does nothing is the #1021 shape in a new costume. Confirmed red pre-fix, green after.

Six mutations, each asserting its target present first, all red at the named pin: revert the commentary filter; drop `check` from the skip set; bypass the helper at the column call site; strip a tag off a shipped starter row; strip a column off one; empty the OPML harvest.

## Corrected on the issue

The issue's second claim — that capture routing to the inbox is part of the bug — is **by design**. The capture bar's job is to take a thought without leaving where you are; routing it into whatever document is open is what it deliberately does not do. Recorded so the next reader finds the reason rather than an apparent oversight.

Recorded as **UXP-325**. Fixes #1428.

author: feruzm
body:
Second of three long-standing panel/UI defects.

On a touch screen `:hover` latches after a tap and stays until the reader taps something else. A tapped tag keeps its dimmed look, a tapped button keeps its hover fill, and both read as still selected. It is the kind of bug nobody reports, because it looks like the app is confused rather than broken.

## What was actually bare

Measured against the **deployed** stylesheet rather than assumed:

- 57 `:hover` rules total, **31 guarded, 26 bare**.
- Tailwind v4 already wraps its own `hover:` variants in `@media (hover: hover)`. Three such blocks were present, covering `hover:border-theme`, `group-hover:opacity-100`, `dark:hover:bg-gray-700` and the rest.
- The 26 bare ones were **exactly** the hand-written CSS: `globals.css`'s `a:hover`, three rules in `components.css`, and six blocks in `blog-markdown.css`.

So this is not "add a guard everywhere"; it is finishing the job Tailwind already does for its own utilities.

## Scope of what went inside the guard

Only appearance. Nothing affecting layout, and nothing a reader needs in order to operate the page, because a device reporting no hover never gets any of it. The markdown anchor-link reveals (`h1:hover .anchor`) are hover-only affordances that were already unreachable on touch, so guarding them changes nothing there.

## Verification

**Built the app and measured the output**, which is the check that matters:

```
hover guards: 12   total :hover: 66   UNGUARDED: 0
```

Against 26 unguarded on the live site. Local builds need `config.json`, which is gitignored, so I seeded it from `config.template.json`; neither it nor `dist/` is committed.

A test asserts the invariant over every stylesheet by tracking brace depth and which at-rule opened each level. It also **checks its own detector** against a bare rule and a gated one, since a source scan that silently finds nothing passes exactly as well as one that works. Mutation-checked by unwrapping a guard: only that file's case fails.

## One existing test needed teaching

`parseBlocks` in `theme-appearance-tokens.test.ts` treated an at-rule body as opaque, so moving the button hover inside `@media` hid `.btn-theme-primary:hover:not(:disabled)` from every assertion about it and failed with "components.css has no such rule". It now recurses into at-rules rather than discarding them, which is the fix rather than relaxing the assertion.

825 tests pass, 60 files. Typecheck clean apart from the pre-existing gitignored `config.json` error.

author: octobercomms
body:
## What & why

OMI's Shopify order fetch already pulled `total_discounts`, per-order refunds and the full `customer` object — but only revenue, orders and AOV ever reached the client Data page. The rest was computed-and-dropped or fetched-and-unused.

This surfaces it. **No new API scopes, no extra requests** — it aggregates fields that already ride the same order fetch as revenue, so it's pure upside for every connected store.

## Changes

- **`connectors/shopify.js`** (pull) & **`connectors/shopifyApp.js`** (webhook): add `total_discounts`, `discounted_orders`, and `new_customer_orders` / `returning_customer_orders` / `guest_orders` to the summary. New-vs-returning comes from Shopify's per-order `customer.orders_count`. Both connectors kept shape-identical so everything downstream treats app- and OAuth-sourced stores the same.
- **`routes/salesTraffic.js`**: roll refunds, discounts, new-vs-returning and a merged top-products list across every connected store into a `result.ecom` block, with derived `refundRate` / `discountRate` and net revenue (net derived from summed gross − refunds so it holds for multi-store clients).
- **`ClientSalesTrafficPage.jsx`**: render a second stat strip (net revenue, refund rate, discount share, returning share) and a **top products by revenue** table under the existing KPIs.
- **`docs/october-mi-shopify/DATA-ENRICHMENT.md`**: advisory-first tiered plan (Tier 0 shipped here; Tiers 1–2 and write-back deferred).

## Posture

Advisory-only, read-only. Write-back (customer tagging, product/inventory edits) stays a deferred, explicit opt-in that would require new scopes and a consent step — never a silent scope bump.

## Note on the webhook refunds path

`shopifyApp.js` reads refunds off `ORDERS_UPDATED` order payloads (Shopify fires an order update on every refund), so refunds are already captured correctly. `REFUNDS_CREATE` is intentionally left out of the read topic filter — its payload is a refund object, not an order, so folding it into the order-keyed aggregation would create phantom orders.

## Verification

- Backend files pass `node --check`.
- Frontend `npm run build` clean.
- Headless (Playwright) render of the Data dashboard with a stubbed `ecom` payload: the new stat strip and top-products table render, values correct (refund rate, net revenue, product rows), **zero console errors**.

author: rnegron
body:
## Problem

- `detect_flaky_checks` keys flakiness on the raw GitHub job name.
- A sharded job reports one GitHub job per shard, labeled `(i/N)`, and the shard count drifts between runs.
- Each shard key is gated by `min_flaky_runs = 3` alone, so a job that recovered 3 times can report nothing.
- One sweep tick (2026-07-28) emitted:

| Job | Shard keys | Signals |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product tests (warehouse-sources, events schema legacy) | `(1/4)` `(1/5)` `(1/6)` | 3 |
| Storybook visual regression - chromium | `(1/16)`…`(16/16)` | 16 |

## Changes

- Strip the `(i/N)` label from the grouping key and `source_id` wherever it appears. For product tests it sits mid-name, so the match is unanchored.
- Count distinct run ids, not query rows, so one bad run cannot clear `min_flaky_runs` alone.
- The shard spread counts shard indices, so `(1/4)` and `(1/6)` read as one shard slot.
- `extra.job_name` keeps the worked example's real job name, which downstream investigation queries filter on.

> [!NOTE]
> Ledger keys change shape, so the first post-deploy sweep re-emits currently-flaky sharded jobs once. Self-heals at the next Monday week boundary.

## How did you test this code?

- New tests use real rendered job names: one signal per sharded job, and a single 3-shard run stays below the threshold.
- `TestCISignalDetectors`: 10 passed locally.

None.

author: khromov
body:
Implements PLAN.md: removes the three amplifiers that turned a single wrong-empty driver read into a user-visible `Queue <name> does not exist` failure (the intermittent `bun-driver / bun: '1'` CI failure on `distributedDatabaseTest > should handle high concurrency without duplicates`, root-caused to Bun 1.3.x returning empty result sets for committed rows under mixed concurrent load — fixed upstream in Bun 1.4).

## Changes (all in `src/manager.ts`, no SQL touched)

1. **Write-through on `createQueue`/`updateQueue`** — instead of evicting, both now read the row back (`#refreshQueueCacheEntry`) and populate the cache. The read-back (not the requested options) is cached, so `createQueue` on an existing queue still preserves the surviving row's config (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` semantics). In-process create→send flows never take the miss path anymore, which deletes the observed failure window (the ~50-lookup storm right after creation).
2. **Corroborated negative lookups in `getQueueCache`** — an empty per-name lookup is re-verified once before concluding the queue does not exist. A truly missing queue answers "absent" twice and still throws the same error from the same call sites; positive results are never re-read.
3. **Two-consecutive-empties rule in `onCacheQueues`** — an empty refresh snapshot no longer wipes a non-empty cache unless the next refresh confirms it. Any non-empty snapshot still prunes missing names immediately via the full rebuild.

One addition beyond the plan's literal code: any positive row read re-arms the empty-refresh guard (`#cacheQueueRow` resets `#lastRefreshEmpty`). Without it, a legitimately-empty first refresh (fresh install, no queues yet — the common case) would leave the guard disarmed exactly in the create-then-send window for the first queue.

Also adds the silent wrong-empty variant to ISSUES.txt #3.

## Tests

New `test/queueCacheTest.ts` (runs on every backend) covers all six planned cases: write-through with zero live lookups on create→send, no-op create caching the surviving row rather than the ignored request, a single lying-empty lookup not failing `send()`, a genuinely missing queue still throwing (with exactly two corroborating lookups), one empty refresh keeping the cache / two consecutive wiping it / a truthful one reinstalling, and `updateQueue` write-through with no later lookup.

## Verification (local, Bun 1.3.14)

- `bun run tsc`, `eslint .`, plans snapshot byte-identical (no SQL changes), `schema.json` untouched.
- All matrices green: standard (1024 passed), `test:distributed` (1018), `test:pglite` (913), `test:sqlite` (703), `test:bun` (1008) — the bun-driver suite passing first-try on 1.3.14 itself.
- Reproducer loop on Bun 1.3.14: `DB_TYPE=bun vitest run test/distributedDatabaseTest.ts -t "high concurrency"` — **6/6 pass** (baseline failed ~2 of 3); `multiMasterTest` under `DB_TYPE=bun` — 3/3 pass.

märks det aldrig eftersom maskinen är långsammare; CI-maskinen hinner logga två
set inom samma millisekund.

KONSEKVENSEN VAR INTE KOSMETISK. AI-kontraktet skickar passets set i ordning, och
systemprompten säger uttryckligen att "en till" syftar på senaste setet i
currentWorkout. Med kolliderande tidsstämplar var "senaste" slumpmässigt, så
"en till" kunde upprepa fel övning och logga fel vikt. Det är precis den sortens
tysta datafel projektet är byggt för att undvika.

Det inträffar inte när en människa trycker på en knapp — men det inträffar varje
gång fritextvägen tolkar "bänk 90x5, 90x5, 90x5" och loopar tre skrivningar utan
paus. Alltså i appens snabbaste och mest använda väg.

Fixen är i två lager. logSet garanterar nu strikt växande tidsstämplar inom ett
pass: kolliderar nu() med senaste setet skjuts den fram en millisekund. Det gör
ordningen KORREKT och inte bara stabil. Sorteringen får dessutom en tiebreak på
id, vilket gör ordningen deterministisk även för rader som skrevs innan.

Kapplöpningen är utskriven i koden: två samtidiga anrop kan läsa samma max.
JavaScript är enkeltrådat och båda anropsvägarna är sekventiellt awaitade, så det
kan inte inträffa i dag — men skulle skrivningar parallelliseras hör beräkningen
hemma inne i transaktionen.

Testet är verifierat mot buggen: med tidsstämpelfixen urkopplad faller det.

Verifierat: 239 enhetstester, 30 E2E, typecheck, lint gröna.

author: admoblord
body: ## The prune I added was only covering half the problem There are **two** Artifact Registries, and I had only pruned one: ``` line 12: ARTIFACT_REGISTRY: us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/... # workflow default line 281: ARTIFACT_REGISTRY: africa-south1-docker.pkg.dev/... # production job override ``` The production job overrides the default, so the prune step only ever touched africa-south1 — created Jul 24. **Every image pushed before the region move is still sitting in us-central1, never pruned**, which is very likely the bulk of the $19.64 line. That also explains why the first prune run reported "nothing to prune": the new registry genuinely has ≤10 images while the old one has months of them. Pruning now covers both registries. ## `scripts/cleanup_idle_cloud_spend.sh` Everything else needs `gcloud`, which I have no credentials for — so this is one script that does it, **dry run by default**. ```bash ./scripts/cleanup_idle_cloud_spend.sh # show the plan ./scripts/cleanup_idle_cloud_spend.sh --apply # delete the safe set ./scripts/cleanup_idle_cloud_spend.sh --apply --drop-standby ``` **Safe set** — no behaviour change: | | | |---|---:| | Managed Kafka cluster | −$60.64 | | Stale images in both registries | most of −$16.23 | **`--drop-standby`** additionally removes the whole us-central1 footprint — the old production and staging Cloud Run services, then the VPC connector (in that order, since deleting a connector still in use fails). Opt-in, because that region is your rollback target. It has likely never been exercised — there is no `develop` branch, so staging never deployed — but afterwards africa-south1 is your only production. ### It will not delete a bus that is still in use The script queries the **running service** before touching Kafka and refuses if it is still on it: ``` live event_bus = kafka Refusing to touch Kafka: the running service still reports 'kafka'. Deploy the Redis-bus change first, then re-run. 1. Managed Kafka cluster skipped (see safety check above) ``` Right now production reports `event_bus = redis`, so it will proceed. ### Memorystore is deliberately left alone The script reports the tier but never deletes it, and says why: twenty modules plus the event bus depend on Redis for presence, idempotency, rate limits and auth revocation, and with `maxScale: 10` in-process state would be ten disconnected copies — rate limits stop limiting and revoked tokens keep working. If it prints `STANDARD_HA`, dropping to Basic roughly halves that $32. Removing the line entirely means migrating `REDIS_URL` to a serverless Redis over TLS first, which also frees the africa-south1 VPC connector — that connector exists only to reach Memorystore's private IP. ## Verified Ran against a stubbed `gcloud` covering both paths: the delete plan is correct for Kafka, both registries and the us-central1 services, ordering puts the VPC connector last, and the safety gate refuses Kafka when the live bus is still `kafka`. `bash -n` clean. Nothing here runs automatically — the only automatic change is the prune step now covering both registries. ## After running it ``` Kafka -$60.64 Artifact Registry (both) most of -$16.23 us-central1 (optional) -$4.52 connector + standby Cloud Run already scale-to-zero as of the last deploy Memorystore -$16 (Basic) or -$32 (migrate off), your call ```

author: mthines
body:
## Why

The tool-failure lesson lookup **post-filtered the SessionStart-injected set** with a literal substring matcher (`relevantLessons` + `matchesQuery`), so it could only ever resurface a lesson that was already going to be shown. A directly-relevant lesson in a sibling scope, one past the per-scope read cap, or a paraphrase the literal matcher missed (`connect` ↔ `connection`) was unreachable.

This is Tier 1 of the retrieval-quality work discussed re: "Postgres vs vector DB" — most of the recall gap is recoverable with the FTS we already have, before any embeddings.

## What

- New **`relevantLessonsFromStore(store, scope, terms)`** — one `store.search` per distilled failure term across the scope hierarchy, run concurrently, best-effort (a throwing/absent store contributes nothing → falls back to the write-nudge alone).
- New pure **`rankRelevant(resultsPerTerm, readOrder, cap)`** — dedupes the union by `scope::key`, ranks by term-match count then scope specificity, caps at 3. Total on junk input.
- Matching is **delegated to the store**: server-side FTS (with stemming) for remote, full-scope substring for local. **No schema change** — reuses the existing single-needle `search` contract untouched.
- `relevantLessons` / `matchesQuery` retained as pure primitives (still used by `search`).
- The integration mock server's `/memories/search` endpoint now narrows by the query term, matching real FTS behaviour (the old path relied on client-side narrowing, so the mock could return everything).

## Tests

`packages/cli/test/hooks.test.mjs` + `hook.integration.test.mjs` (653 pass):
- `rankRelevant`: more-terms-first ordering, dedupe + specificity tie-break, totality on junk, cap.
- `relevantLessonsFromStore`: **retrieves a match the injected set would miss** (the point of the change), no-match fallback, best-effort on a throwing/absent/searchless store, no-query guards.
- Integration failure path now exercises the store-query path end-to-end.

## Docs

No user-facing docs / `llms.txt` change applies — internal hook behaviour, no new command, flag, tool, or config surface. The three now-stale `CLAUDE.md` passages describing the failure path are updated in this diff.

## Follow-up

Stops at Tier 1 deliberately. If the FTS recall lift holds up, Tier 3 (pgvector hybrid rank) plugs into this same `relevantLessonsFromStore` seam — the single place a semantic ranker would live.

author: maonakamoto
body:
Two grafts from #170, which found the same root cause independently while #171 was in flight. #171 (merged, and it shipped itself — see below) fixed the mechanism; this adds the two things it was missing.

**`branches: [main]` on the `workflow_run` trigger.** A PR's CI is not a ship signal. Filtering at the trigger beats creating a Deploy run whose only job is to skip — and those skipped runs are precisely what made the outage hard to read: the deploy history looked busy while nothing shipped.

**The CLAUDE.md rule.** This is the important half. That the `GITHUB_TOKEN` no-cascade rule bites *one level deeper* — the re-armed CI run is itself token-created, so nothing chains off it either — is not something the next person re-derives from a green CI badge and a stale site. The class already cost two sessions independently today. The note also records that deployment is a reconciler rather than a trigger, and that "merged" is not "live".

Credit to #170 for both; closing it as superseded.

## Verified live

The reconciler from #171 shipped itself, which is the end-to-end proof:

```
[auto-merge] main is at ec2d0d19; last successful deploy was da212284 — shipping
```

`da212284` was the last thing that reached the box — merged by a human token at 17:19. Everything auto-merged after it was stuck.
