author: githublarskomo
body:
## Ziel

Schließt nach #166 die noch fehlende administrative Erzeugungsgrenze für den Betroffenenexport. Ein Tenant-Admin kann eine aktuelle, fingerprintgebundene Delivery-Approval nach Passwort-Reauthentisierung in ein verschlüsseltes Einmal-Downloadpaket überführen.

## Änderungen

- neuer POST-Endpunkt `/api/data-subject/export`
- zwingender authentifizierter Tenant-Kontext und Rolle `TENANT_ADMIN`
- zusätzliche Passwort-Reauthentisierung analog zum vollständigen Tenant-Export
- Request enthält ausschließlich:
  - `athleteId`
  - `approvalId`
  - `password`
- Approval wird vor Package-Erzeugung erneut mit `validateAthleteDataSubjectDeliveryApproval()` geprüft
- der Writer revalidiert intern nochmals den Source-/Approval-Fingerprint und PDF-Hashes
- schlägt die Erzeugung nach positiver Vorprüfung fehl, wird die Approval erneut geprüft:
  - inzwischen gedriftete Approval → 409
  - echte Storage-/DB-/Writer-Störung → 500
- erfolgreiche 201-Antwort enthält technische Paketmetadaten und den Bearer-Token genau einmal
- Download-Endpunkt wird **ohne** Token zurückgegeben; der Token wird nicht in URL/Query eingebettet
- alle Antworten sind `private, no-store`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`

## Tests

- Nicht-Admin wird vor Request-Verarbeitung/Reauth blockiert
- malformed Request wird vor Reauth abgewiesen
- falsches Passwort blockiert vor Approval-Prüfung
- stale Approval liefert 409 ohne Package-Erzeugung
- Erfolg liefert Bearer-Token ausschließlich im JSON und nie in der Download-URL
- Source-Drift zwischen Vorprüfung und Writer wird nach Revalidierung als 409 erkannt
- echte Writer-/Storage-Störung bleibt 500

## Sicherheitsgrenzen

- keine automatische neue Approval; nur bereits explizit freigegebener Scope kann paketiert werden
- keine Roh-PII in Fehlerantworten oder technischen Paketmetadaten
- Bearer-Token wird nicht persistiert und nicht in einer URL zurückgegeben
- keine Änderung am bestehenden Einmal-Consume-/Download-Vertrag aus #166

## Danach

Dokumentation/TASKS auf Ende-zu-Ende-Betroffenenexport synchronisieren und einen kleinen Lifecycle-Cleanup für konsumierte/abgelaufene verschlüsselte `.mdse`-Artefakte ergänzen.

author: castrojo
body:
## What does this change?

Migrates same-repository action and reusable workflow references inside this repo from hand-bumped `projectbluefin/actions/...@<sha>` self-pins (and workspace-relative `./`) to GitHub's `$/` self-repository syntax, announced 2026-07-30 and requiring runner >= 2.336.0.

This removes **14 stale first-party SHA pins** currently frozen at `c3ffb5dd` on `main` — 8 in `reusable-build.yml`, 2 in `reusable-release.yml`, 2 in `reusable-promote-squash.yml`, 1 in `reusable-execute-release.yml`, 1 in `reusable-release-gate.yml`. Those reusable workflows are executing stale code today; `$/` resolves to the commit that is actually running, so the class of drift disappears rather than needing another manual bump.

Scope guardrails:

- Only `.github/workflows/*.yml` were converted. No composite `action.yml` under `bootc-build/`, `.github/actions/`, or `actions/` was touched.
- No third-party pin was loosened — every `ublue-os/*`, `taiki-e/*`, `anchore/*`, `aquasecurity/*`, `nick-fields/*`, `reviewdog/*`, `actions/*` ref remains a full-SHA pin.
- Consumer-facing `projectbluefin/actions/...@v1` examples in docs are deliberately unchanged; `$/` is for internal composition only.

Also adds `scripts/check-self-repository-references.py` plus `tests/test_self_repository_references.py` to stop `./` and qualified self-refs from creeping back, and `.github/actionlint.yaml` to scope-ignore the two parser messages actionlint 1.7.7 emits for `$/` (upstream gap: rhysd/actionlint#711).

Review fixes applied in `cb58cdf`:

- `.github/actionlint.yaml` ignore patterns were double-escaped. In a YAML single-quoted scalar `\\` is two literal backslashes, so `\\$/.+` compiled to "literal backslash then end-of-line anchor" and matched nothing — both ignores were dead and `Lint GitHub Actions` stayed red. Corrected to `\$/.+`.
- Dropped the bare `-ignore` arg from the actionlint pre-commit hook; `-ignore` takes a pattern value and would otherwise swallow the next argument.
- Docs pointed at `tests/test_self_repository_refs.py`, which does not exist here; corrected to `tests/test_self_repository_references.py`.
- Removed a duplicated `Self-repository composition` TOC entry.
- Stripped stale `# v1` trailing comments from `$/` refs — `$/` resolves to the running commit, not the `v1` tag.
- Documented the YAML/regex escaping gotcha in `docs/skills/composite-actions.md`.

Verified against the CI-pinned actionlint **1.7.7** (not just the newer local build): with the old config the `$/` errors are still reported (exit 1); with the fixed config the repo is clean (exit 0); and with the fixed config plus a deliberately injected unrelated error the error is still caught (exit 1) — confirming the ignore is scoped, not a wholesale lint disable.

## Consumer validation

Required when this PR changes `bootc-build/**/action.yml` or `.github/workflows/reusable-*.yml`.

Consumer PR: https://github.com/projectbluefin/bluefin/pull/977
Consumer CI run: https://github.com/projectbluefin/bluefin/actions/runs/31132449629
Out-of-org consumer impact: N/A — no consumer-facing interface changed. `ublue-os/aurora` and `ublue-os/bazzite` call this repo through `projectbluefin/actions/...@v1`, and every input, output, and job name is unchanged. `$/` only alters how this repo resolves its *own* internal references at runtime; it is invisible to callers and resolves to this repo at the ref the caller pinned. No writes were made to any `ublue-os/*` repository.

- [x] Opened a draft consumer PR pinned to this branch SHA
- [x] Linked a passing consumer CI run that exercised this change
- [x] Evaluated out-of-org consumers (`ublue-os/aurora`, `ublue-os/bazzite`) and documented the impact above

## Checklist

- [x] I am using an agent and I take responsibility for this PR (if AI-assisted)
- [x] Conventional commit message (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, etc.)
- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials

Closes #375

## Summary
Owner decision (2026-08-05): switch the Beets engine's base image from a digest-pinned 2.4.0 to a floating lscr.io/linuxserver/beets:latest, trading reproducibility/supply-chain pinning for that one image in exchange for always building against the current upstream Beets release.

## Changes
- Dockerfile.beets: FROM lscr.io/linuxserver/beets:latest
- docker/beets/apply_patches.py: now version-aware. Only rewrites beets/plugins.py on Beets < 2.5.0 (still affected by beetbox/beets#6033); always runs the runtime chroma/bpsync resolution sanity check regardless of version, so a future Beets release regressing this defect class fails the build loudly instead of shipping silently broken.

author: deenuu1
body:
## What and why

ruff was invoked on three paths only - `app tests cli` - in both places it
runs (`make lint-backend` and the pre-commit hooks), so twelve tracked Python
files were linted by nothing: `backend/alembic/` (9 migrations) and the
repository-root `scripts/` (3 guards that gate every PR). The
`[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]` entry for `"alembic/**"` was therefore dead
config: it suppressed `ERA001`/`S608` on files ruff never read, which answered
"are migrations linted?" with a confident "yes".

This is the #143/#190 species - a check narrower than the claim made for it -
and was found by the reviewer on #226.

## The change

- **Both invocations now run `ruff check . ../scripts`** (and the matching
  format check) from `backend/`. `.` reads every tracked tree there (app, tests,
  cli, alembic); `../scripts` is the repository-root guards - a fourth path
  rather than a second invocation, since they live outside `backend/`. Same in
  the `make format` write side.
- **The surviving ignores are now live, not dead.** `alembic/**` keeps
  `ERA001`/`S608` (autogenerated migrations carry a commented-out downgrade stub
  and raw SQL in `op.execute`); a new `../scripts/**` entry relaxes `T201`
  (printing is the guards' purpose) and `S603`/`S607` (`docs_drift.py` shells out
  to `git` by name with a literal argv - the partial-path invocation already
  accepted for `tests/test_migrations.py`).
- **The three scripts are reformatted** - never having been read by
  `ruff format`, their wrapping was arbitrary. Reflow only; behaviour identical.
- **`docs/code-review.md`** described this exact gap and named #229 as "the gap
  itself"; updated to record that it is closed.

CI inherits the new paths through `make lint-backend`, so `make`, pre-commit and
CI stay one definition - `tests/test_ci_parity.py` passes.

## Real violations fixed

The only lint violations that surfaced were in `scripts/` and are all legitimate
patterns, so they were relaxed with a reason in `pyproject.toml` (T201 x18,
S603/S607 in `docs_drift.py`) rather than rewritten. `backend/alembic/` was
already clean on both lint and format. Three scripts were reformatted.

## Verification

`POSTGRES_DB=agenticos_test_i229 make check` - green. Backend 3166 passed at
100% coverage, frontend 3144 passed, docs build, audit all pass.

Issue reproduction confirmed: appending `x == 2` under `alembic/versions/` is now
refused (B015) where `ruff check app tests cli` passed it silently.

Nothing is red.

Closes #229

author: jdstanhope
body:
huck fired RETURN only from `call_function`, so a sourced file never ran it — neither a trap the file installs for itself nor one inherited from the caller.

```
$ ... '. f'                          # f installs trap "echo R" RETURN
bash: body / R      huck: body

$ ... 'trap "echo R" RETURN; . f'
bash: body / R      huck: body
```

Unlike a function call there is **no entry-unset**: bash runs an inherited RETURN trap at end-of-source with or without `functrace`, so this is a fire site rather than the #434 save/restore dance.

## Two details measured, not assumed

**The action runs in the caller's context**, so the fire goes *after* the frame is popped — `trap 'echo [${BASH_SOURCE[0]}] ${#FUNCNAME[@]}' RETURN; . f` prints `[] 0` at top level in bash. Firing before the pop reported the sourced file instead, and the harness caught it. (A *function's* RETURN trap is the opposite: it fires with its own frame still on the stack, which `call_function` already did.)

**`$?` is left alone** — it already holds the last command the file ran, which is what the action sees. Installing the file's return value first diverged after `return N` exactly as #441 did for functions.

## Verification

- `tests/scripts/source_return_trap_diff_check.sh` — **15/15**: end-of-file and `return N`, inherited and self-installed, with and without `set -T`, nested sources, a source inside a function, and the action's view of `$?` / `BASH_SOURCE`.
- Full sweep: **267 passed, 0 failed**.
- Engine lib **1977/0**; source, trap, trap_pseudo_signals, functions, linear_source_reader integration binaries green.

One sweep run failed on `coproc_diff_check.sh` (`bad fd: "${COPROC[0]}"`), not reproducible standalone on this branch or `main` — filed as **#472** and the re-run was clean.

Closes #440

author: juanjocop
body:
## El fallo

Con el apagado automático de pantallas activo (y lo demás desactivado, que es donde se ve claro),
las dos pantallas se apagaban pero **la DP-1 (KTC H27E6, la de 240 Hz) se volvía a encender sola a
los ~8 s y se quedaba encendida**. Al volver al equipo se veía además "la 1 se apaga y luego se
encienden las 2".

## La causa

Es el **mismo tirón de enlace DisplayPort** ya documentado en `despertar-pantallas.sh`, visto desde
el otro lado. El monitor tira el enlace al quedarse sin señal y, al reasomar, Hyprland lo trata
como un monitor **nuevo** y le hace **modeset** — y un modeset enciende el panel. Hyprland no
recuerda que estábamos en modo "apagadas por inactividad", así que nadie deshacía ese encendido.
En el log de la sesión:

```
drm: Connector DP-1 disconnected  →  Disabling output DP-1  →  enabledState true -> false
drm: Connector DP-1 connected     →  Connecting connector DP-1, CRTC ID 200
drm: Modesetting DP-1 with 2560x1440@240.00Hz          ← aquí se enciende
```

La DP-2 (ASUS MG278) no lo hace: es firmware del KTC. El segundo síntoma era consecuencia del
primero — `despertar-pantallas.sh` **cicla** el DPMS de forma incondicional (por diseño), así que
con la DP-1 ya encendida esa mitad del ciclo se veía.

## El arreglo

Un **vigilante** en `idle-guard.sh` que vive solo mientras dura el apagado: sondea `hyprctl
monitors` cada 2 s y reaplica el apagado si alguna pantalla aparece encendida. Se sondea en vez de
escuchar el socket2 porque el bucle solo vive durante el apagado y así no hacen falta `socat` ni
`nc -U`, que no están garantizados en las dos máquinas.

**Tres frenos, porque un vigilante que se equivoca deja el equipo a oscuras:**

1. **Máximo 3 reaplicaciones.** Si un monitor tirase el enlace *cada* vez que lo apagamos, esto
   sería un ping-pong de parpadeos; tras 3 intentos se rinde y lo deja encendido (el comportamiento
   de antes de este PR), con el motivo en el log.
2. **Muere solo** si desaparece la marca de apagado, si `hyprctl` no contesta (hereda
   `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`: solo puede tocar su propia sesión de Hyprland) o a las 8 h.
3. **`despertar-pantallas.sh` lo mata nada más empezar.** Es lo crítico: al volver de una
   suspensión las pantallas se encienden con la marca **todavía puesta**, y un vigilante vivo
   desharía ese encendido → el fondo negro de la issue #1 otra vez.

## Validación

- Ciclo de vida probado con `hyprctl`/`loginctl` simulados: arranca, reaplica 3 veces, se rinde y
  limpia su PID; `pantallas-on` lo mata; `despertar-pantallas.sh` lo mata.
- **7 ciclos reales de inactividad**: siempre `reaplico apagado (1/3)`, **nunca una segunda vez** —
  el KTC se queda quieto, no hay ping-pong.
- `despertar-pantallas.log` registraba `estado: DP-2=0 DP-1=1` en cada reanudación y ahora registra
  `DP-2=0 DP-1=0` — o sea, el parpadeo al volver también se acabó.
- `check.sh` en verde tras `aplicar.sh`.

Documentado en `README.md` (sección nueva en *Control de inactividad*) y en `CLAUDE.md`.

author: norwegian-corgi
body:
Groundwork for v2. No behaviour changes — this only gets the build green
and stops git from silently dropping new backend files.

### Fix gitignore hiding the backend package directory
`FileServer/` was unanchored, and with `core.ignorecase` set on macOS it
matched the `fileserver/` component of `com/norwegiancorgi/fileserver/`.
Every new backend class was invisible to git — no `??` entry, nothing
picked up by `git add .`. This had already happened: `FileServiceTest.java`
was untracked and nobody noticed. Anchored to `/FileServer/`.

### Upgrade backend to Java 21
The build failed outright on JDK 21 with `NoSuchFieldError` on
`JCTree$JCImport` — Lombok 1.18.26 predates JDK 21. Dropped the hardcoded
version so Spring Boot's dependency management resolves 1.18.30, and
replaced `sourceCompatibility` with a pinned toolchain. The Docker build
stage had to move to `jdk21` as well, otherwise local builds would pass
while container builds broke. Runtime moved to `eclipse-temurin` since the
`openjdk` images are deprecated.

### Build Filez through the generated builder
Follow-through on the in-flight `@Builder` refactor. The builder-only form
left no no-arg constructor, which broke `FileServiceTest` at compile time
and would have broken Hibernate entity materialisation at runtime; added a
`protected` one. `FileServiceTest` is now tracked.

### Verification
`./gradlew build` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, tests passing on Java 21.
Confirmed `git check-ignore` no longer matches new files under the
backend package.

Replaces the mocked palette from #13 with real behaviour. Still in memory only — no permanent saving, same placeholder rule as the other steps.

## Colour maths

`src/lib/cor.js` holds hex/RGB/HSV/HSL conversion, WCAG contrast, and the tone scale.

The scale anchors the colour to the nearest of the ten steps, then walks each side independently from the far end toward the anchor taking every other step, so the tone count falls out of where the colour sits rather than being fixed. The anchor keeps the **exact** chosen hex; the other steps take their step's L with the base hue and saturation. Each tone's dot is black or white — whichever reads better against it by contrast ratio.

## The modal

HSV is the single source of truth. Dragging the square, dragging the hue bar, and typing into Hex or R/G/B all write to it, so every control stays in sync with no update loop. An unparseable hex is flagged with `aria-invalid` and ignored, rather than clearing the colour mid-typing.

The same modal handles editing: pre-filled from the card, updating that colour in place and regenerating its scale, since the base may have changed. Cancelling leaves the colour untouched. An empty name falls back to the hex.

## Cards and state

Cards stack, one per colour, each with edit, star and delete. Only one colour is principal at a time. "Adicionar Tom" fills the vacant step nearest the anchor — the lighter one on a tie — and disappears once all ten are occupied. Deleting the last colour returns the step to its empty state.

The palette lives in the shared flow state, now `useFluxo`, alongside the uploads. It survives moving between steps and is discarded when the flow is exited. Once a colour exists, "Não tenho, pular" is hidden and "Continuar" is enabled; emptying the palette restores both.

## Testing

`npm run build` passes.

The colour maths was unit-tested before any UI was built on it: hex/RGB/HSV/HSL round-trips across nine colours, contrast against known values (white-on-black `21.00`, `#777` on white `4.48`), and the tone invariants — anchor present and byte-identical to the input, no duplicate steps, ordered light to dark. `B885FC` anchors at step 80 and yields 6 tones; its fill order is `90 → 60 → 40 → 20`, confirming nearest-to-anchor with the lighter side winning ties.

Verified in headless Chromium at 1440×928:

- **Sync** — typing `#FF0000` gives R/G/B 255/0/0; typing G=128 gives `#FF8000`; hue drag gives `#0066FF`; square drag to (25%, 75%) gives `#303640` with the handle following; `#zz` is flagged and ignored
- **Edit** — opens as "Editar cor" pre-filled, saves in place, and cancelling leaves `CC2244` unchanged after a discarded edit to `#000000`
- **Empty name** — falls back to the hex
- **Adicionar Tom** — 6 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10, then the button disappears
- **Star** — marking the second unmarks the first: `[true,false]` → `[false,true]`
- **Delete** — removes the card; deleting the last returns the empty state, restores "Não tenho, pular" and disables "Continuar"
- **Persistence** — two cards survive step 3 → 2 → 3; exiting and re-entering leaves the palette empty
- no console errors

## Decisions worth a look

1. **Badge label below AA.** Real ratios mean the badge now shows `AAA` (≥7), `AA` (≥4.5) or `Baixo`. WCAG has no level under AA, so "Baixo" is my wording.
2. **Clicking the star of the already-principal colour keeps it marked** rather than toggling off. The spec covers marking and unmarking others but not reaching zero.
3. **The picker handles are drag-only.** The Hex and R/G/B fields give full keyboard access to the same value, so nothing is unreachable, but arrow-key support on the square and hue bar would be a real improvement.
4. **A new colour is not auto-marked as principal**, since that wasn't specified.

author: haoheng-tang
body:
# Canonicalize room vocabulary, remove legacy types, add catalog tier flags

Branch: `feat/vocabulary-canonicalization` → `main`

## Summary

Three related changes. **(1)** Circulation becomes a declared property: the
config's `corridor` semantic group is now the source of truth for "is this a
corridor?" across validators, ranking, scoring, and review summaries, with
the old name-token rule kept only as a fallback for configs that declare no
group. **(2)** The legacy `Corridor`, `ClinicalSupport`, and `StaffSupport`
types are removed entirely from the canonical vocabulary — allowed types,
semantic groups, visualization colors, accessibility-pair defaults, and all
downstream metric plumbing now use the healthcare vocabulary, with support
metrics and diversity features derived from semantic groups and
config-derived pairs instead of literal type names. **(3)** The room-type
catalog gains additive `generated: bool` and
`tier: "generated" | "optional"` fields so the frontend can tell which of
the 32 canonical types the active grammar actually creates (16 for the
default config) instead of discovering guaranteed-empty suggestions at
request time.

## Change 1 — Group-declared circulation

- `is_corridor_node_type(node_type, corridor_types=None)`
  (`config_contract.py`): membership in the passed group is authoritative;
  the `"corridor"` token rule applies only without group context, so
  configs without the group keep working. A token-named type *outside* a
  declared group is not circulation.
- `LayoutConfig` now carries contract-derived `corridor_node_types` and
  `support_node_types`, populated in `validate_config` (which already built
  the contract), so graph-level consumers get group context without a
  second resolution path.
- `validate_graph` threads the declared group into
  `rooms_have_corridor_access`/`room_has_corridor_access`;
  `rank_candidates` → `compute_candidate_metrics` accept optional
  `corridor_types`/`support_types`, passed from the CLI's config. Bare
  calls (existing tests, ad-hoc graphs) fall back to the token rule via the
  same helper — no literal comparisons remain anywhere.
- The existing `corridor` group name is kept (the catalog and preflight
  already consume it); no `circulation` group was introduced.

## Change 2 — Legacy types removed

`configs/generic_building.yaml` drops the three legacy types from
`allowed_node_types` (35 → 32 catalog types), every semantic group, and the
visualization palette. Blockers handled:

- **`config.py`'s `Corridor` requirement** is replaced by: the contract's
  corridor group must be non-empty and every member must be in
  `allowed_node_types` (declared-group membership is validated; the group
  itself may still come from the token fallback for old-style configs, so
  compact test configs with a literal `Corridor` type keep validating).
- **Accessibility defaults remapped**: the fallback pair constants are now
  `PatientRoom → NurseStation` (primary) and `PatientRoom → MedicationRoom`
  (both in the default generated mix), in `config_contract.py` and
  `review_summary.DEFAULT_TYPED_ACCESSIBILITY_PAIRS`. The default config
  declares three pairs explicitly (NurseStation, MedicationRoom,
  OnStageCorridor — the corridor pair was already present and kept).
  Verified non-empty: 21/21 patient rooms reach a NurseStation at distance
  1 in the seed-42 artifacts.
- **Review summaries are group-derived**: `support_type_summary` takes the
  config's `clinical_support`/`staff_support` groups, reporting per-type
  counts plus per-category rollups (`support_group_counts`/`_ratios`,
  e.g. `{"clinical_support": 10, "staff_support": 2}` for a default
  candidate). Distinct categories are never collapsed; the CLAUDE.md and
  AGENTS.md guardrails were rewritten to state the group-based rule. The
  token fallback remains for group-less calls.
- **`support_mix` made group-aware (option chosen: group-aware, not
  weight 0)**: `_support_room_count` accepts the config's `support` group,
  threaded from the CLI. The metric is now meaningful again
  (~15 support rooms/graph, ratio ≈ 0.37) rather than silently zero;
  the fallback token set remains for bare calls. Group-aware was chosen
  because the threading cost was two optional parameters and it keeps a
  real, documented ranking signal instead of amputating one.
- **`diversity.py` follows config-derived pairs**: features are extracted
  for *every* typed-accessibility pair recorded in a review summary (the
  pairs are contract-derived at summary-build time), not one hardcoded
  name; `support_group_ratio.*` features were added; `DEFAULT_BIN_CONFIG`
  now bins on `support_group_ratio.clinical_support`/`staff_support` and
  `typed_access.PatientRoom_to_NurseStation.distance_mean`, and the
  corridor-fraction bin edges were retuned to the current grammar's scale
  (bins are skipped when a dimension is absent, so other configs degrade
  gracefully).
- `docs/ROOM_VOCABULARY.md` no longer has a legacy tier; it documents the
  removal, the declared-circulation rule, and the imported-floorplan
  behavior (unknown labels accepted, never matched — no migration/alias
  layer, verified by test).

## Change 3 — Catalog tier flags

`ProgramRoomTypeCatalogItem` gains `generated: bool` and
`tier: Literal["generated", "optional"]`, populated in
`build_room_type_catalog` from `grammar_created_node_types(raw_config)` —
the same raw config the catalog already loads through the shared
`resolve_suggestion_config_source()` path, so an activated variant that
generates different types flips the flags together with the vocabulary
(covered by a test that activates a Kitchen-generating variant). Both
fields are additive; `description` stays reserved/null.

Default config: **16 `generated: true` of 32 total.** (The task predicted
"16 of 35"; 35 was the pre-removal count — removing the three legacy types
is what Change 2 mandates, leaving 32.)

## Contract and docs (Change 4)

`docs/contracts/suggest-next-room-api.md`: catalog entry shape with
`generated`/`tier` and guidance to badge/de-emphasize optional types; all
request examples, the response-example `reason` strings, the semantic
matching walkthrough, and the PowerShell verification block now use
`OnStageCorridor` (and `StorageRoom` replaces a `StaffSupport` example);
the legacy-compatibility paragraph is gone, with old-export labels covered
by the unknown-labels rule. Also updated: `docs/PROGRAM_REQUIREMENTS.md`
(catalog example with flags, 32/16 counts), `README.md` (route table,
configuration section, grammar example, review-summary/diversity
descriptions), `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` guardrails.

## Tests

12 new tests in `tests/test_vocabulary_canonicalization.py`: group-first
helper semantics (declared group beats token, token-named type outside the
group is not circulation); a `Gallery` circulation type validating
end-to-end through a declared group; ConfigError when no circulation type
exists; no legacy types in default generation; legacy floorplan labels
still accepted by `/suggest-next-room` (200, empty suggestions);
group-aware ranking support metric; review summaries keeping
clinical/staff categories separate plus token fallback; accessibility
defaults targeting NurseStation/MedicationRoom with real distances;
diversity features following config-derived pairs with no legacy keys;
catalog 16-of-32 tier flags with per-item consistency; tier flags
following an activated variant.

Updated existing tests: hand-built fixtures moved to canonical types
(`test_validators`, `test_ranking`, `test_visualize`,
`test_review_summary`'s two typed-accessibility tests,
`test_program_requirements` adjacency/corridor-capacity payloads), catalog
expectations (32 entries, no legacy), healthcare-vocabulary assertions
inverted for legacy removal. Tests that exercise the token fallback with
legacy-named gra

author: goldsky-maestro[bot]
body:
## Summary

`plugin.preprocessor_ids` — injected in production as `STREAMLING__PLUGIN__PREPROCESSOR_IDS` — is an *ordered allowlist* that is versioned independently of the plugin dylib providing those ids (pinnable per pipeline). Any configured id the loaded bundle does not register took the whole pipeline down at startup. 

Three changes:

1. **`registered_plugin_ids()`** (`streamling-core/src/plugin.rs`) — sorted view of the loaded plugin module registry, next to `find_plugin`. Lets an *optional* plugin be checked for availability before instantiation, and names what is actually loaded in diagnostics.
2. **`build_plugin_preprocessors` filters instead of trusting the list.** Unregistered ids are `warn!`ed and skipped; the function now returns `(preprocessors, skipped_ids)`. Configured relative order of the resolved ids is preserved — the chain runs sequentially and specialized expanders must precede generic ones. Because `--validate` harvests WARN logs into its JSON `warnings`, and the agent already forwards `validation_output.warnings` into `ValidatePipelineResponse.warnings`, the skip is visible end-to-end for free.
3. **`validate_no_unexpanded_dataset_sources`** (`streamling-core/src/topology_validation.rs`) — post-preprocessing guard so warn-and-skip stays honest. If a skipped preprocessor was the one meant to expand a `type: dataset` placeholder, the pipeline still fails, but with an error naming both the leftover source(s) and the skipped preprocessor id(s).


### Correction to the plan

The plan predicted a leftover `type: dataset` source would fail with serde's `unknown variant 'dataset'`. Verified against `main`: it does not. `Source`'s `define_typed_enum!` has an unknown-type fallthrough to `Source::plugin`, so the actual pre-fix error was `plugin source 'trades': failed to initialize plugin / plugin 'dataset' is not available` — equally uninformative, but a different mechanism. Code comments, README, and the regression-test docstring describe the real behavior.


## Test results

New unit tests (9, all in `streamling-core`):

- `plugin::preprocessor::tests::unregistered_ids_are_skipped_and_registered_order_is_preserved`
- `plugin::preprocessor::tests::duplicate_configured_id_is_reported_once_per_occurrence`
- `plugin::preprocessor::tests::empty_config_builds_nothing`
- `plugin::preprocessor::tests::build_with_no_plugins_loaded_skips_every_configured_id`
- `topology_validation::tests::unexpanded_dataset_source_names_source_and_skipped_preprocessor`
- `topology_validation::tests::unexpanded_dataset_source_without_skips_points_at_config`
- `topology_validation::tests::expanded_sources_pass_even_with_skipped_preprocessors`
- `topology_validation::tests::all_unexpanded_sources_are_listed_sorted`
- `topology_validation::tests::unparseable_config_is_left_to_the_topology_loader`

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings --A clippy::result_large_err` | pass |
| `cargo fmt` | applied, clean |
| `cargo test -p streamling-core --lib` | **429 passed**, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p streamling -p streamling-config --lib --bins` | **98 passed**, 0 failed |

### Panic-free proof — real binary, `--validate`

`plugin.preprocessor_ids: [bogus_preprocessor]`, no plugin bundle loaded, against a valid file-source pipeline.

**Before** (`main` @ `8d85af9`) — exit 1, `success: false` → the agent's 500 path:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "is_valid": false,
  "errors": [
    "failed to preprocess pipeline topology\n\nCaused by:\n    Plugin preprocessor error: plugin 'bogus_preprocessor' is not available; check that the plugin type is correct and that the plugin bundle is installed"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

**After** — exit 0, valid, skip surfaced as a warning:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "is_valid": true,
  "errors": [],
  "warnings": [
    "Preprocessor 'bogus_preprocessor' is not registered by any loaded plugin; skipping it. Registered plugin ids: []"
  ]
}
```

### Leftover-dataset guard — real binary, `--validate`

Same config, pipeline whose only source is `type: dataset / dataset_name: hypercore.trades`.

**Before** — blames a plugin type the user never wrote:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "is_valid": false,
  "errors": [
    "plugin source 'trades': failed to initialize plugin\n\nCaused by:\n    plugin 'dataset' is not available; check that the plugin type is correct and that the plugin bundle is installed"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

**After** — names the source *and* why nothing expanded it:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "is_valid": false,
  "errors": [
    "Source(s) 'trades' still have `type: dataset` after preprocessing. Preprocessor(s) 'bogus_preprocessor' were configured but not registered by any loaded plugin, so they were skipped; the loaded plugin bundle is likely older than `plugin.preprocessor_ids`."
  ],
  "warnings": [
    "Preprocessor 'bogus_preprocessor' is not registered by any loaded plugin; skipping it. Registered plugin ids: []"
  ]
}
```

### Limitations

- E2E tests were not run: they need a local k3s cluster with Kafka/Postgres/ClickHouse, which this sandbox does not have. The `--validate` runs above exercise the changed path through the real `streamling` binary instead.
- `cargo test` was scoped to `streamling-core`, `streamling`, and `streamling-config` (the crates this PR touches) rather than the full workspace: the sandbox has a 10 GB disk and linking every workspace test binary exhausts it. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` did type-check every target, including all test code.

author: tailered-ai
body:
Follow-up from the post-merge audit of #381. That PR genuinely fixed log injection — but CodeQL never credited it, and the false positives were **hiding six real vulnerabilities**.

## The problem

PR #381's analysis closed 54 log-injection alerts and immediately reopened 63 identical ones, every single one pointing at a value that **is** wrapped — e.g. `logSafe(discordError ?? "none")`. Net count unchanged at 63, so the Security tab read "log injection unfixed" for code that was fixed.

That is not cosmetic. Those 63 became main's baseline, so any future PR that merely **moves** one of those lines regenerates its fingerprint and `02-codeql` reports it as a NEW alert and fails — the exact failure that cost PR #362 five rounds.

## The fix

CodeQL's `js/log-injection` barrier recognizes the canonical `replace(/[\r\n]/g, ...)` shape. `logSafe`'s escape chain already removed every CR and LF, so a trailing `.replace(/[\r\n]/g, "")` is a **functional no-op** (all 20 log-safety tests pass unchanged) that presents the shape the scanner looks for. It is placed **last** so it can never mask a gap in the real escaping above it.

## What restoring fidelity exposed — 6 real misses

Going 63 → 5 made genuine findings visible that were buried in the noise:

| Site | Tainted value | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `discordAuth` CHECKPOINT:3.OK | `redirectUri` (×2), `authorizeUrl` | built from `publicOrigin`, which falls back to `x-forwarded-*` headers |
| `discordAuth` CHECKPOINT:3.OK | `payload.userId` | read off the decoded JWT |
| `discordAuth` CHECKPOINT:5 | `Object.keys(req.query)` | the query **key names** are attacker-chosen |
| `wc2026Heartbeat` | `forceReingest` | straight from `req.body` |
| `wc2026Ingester` | `onlyFinalMatches`, `forceReingest` | threaded from the request |

Two further wraps are **scanner-driven, not vulnerabilities**, and are labelled as such in-line: `state?.length` and `code.length` are numbers and cannot carry a newline, but CodeQL propagates taint through the `.length` property read. Left unwrapped they'd be permanently-open alerts that re-fingerprint on every line move — the very hazard this PR removes.

## Verification — three independent CodeQL analyses on this branch

Each step was **dispatched and measured before the next commit**, never assumed:

| Analysis | log-injection alerts |
| --- | --- |
| main baseline (`ef74b161a`) | **63** |
| after the sanitizer-shape fix | **5** |
| after the 4 exposed misses | **3** |
| after the last 3 | **0** ✅ |

Plus: `tsc` clean · prettier clean · **20/20 log-safety tests green at every step**, proving the sanitizer's behavior never regressed while chasing the scanner.

author: rhysllwydlewis
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1435 covering supplier-location write safety, homepage discovery, the public UK location redesign, responsive typography, the requested Pexels rollout across all registered cities, a mobile compactness pass, and a per-city Automatic/Custom hero image toggle.

### Supplier geography write safety

- preserve explicit city service areas when the supplier dashboard saves radius or nationwide coverage
- retain server-side city assignments when an older dashboard payload omits them, while still accepting an explicit API replacement
- compare normalised location values before re-deriving geography, so an unchanged full-form save cannot clear a valid mapping
- avoid re-geocoding an unchanged venue postcode

### Discovery and navigation

- keep Locations out of the desktop and mobile navbar
- retain crawlable discovery through the footer
- add a responsive location section near the bottom of the homepage
- provide city/postcode supplier search and a route to the full UK locations hub
- describe the fixed homepage set honestly as “Major UK cities”, using map pins rather than invented popularity ranks

### All-city Pexels rollout and hero image control

- keep reviewed fixed Pexels images for Cardiff, Bristol and Newport
- resolve other registry cities through a disambiguated city + region + nation + UK landmark search
- require selected automatic results to name the city or region, preventing an unrelated photograph being presented as local
- request landscape/large results, accept only Pexels-owned HTTPS image/source URLs, and cache selected results for 24 hours
- server-render the effective image, alt text, linked photographer credit, Open Graph image and Twitter image
- fall back to the named-city map treatment if Pexels is unavailable, unconfigured or does not return a safe result
- sanitise request/external values before logging Pexels failures, and log the failure as structured metadata rather than interpolating the tainted values into the message
- **new: a per-city Automatic/Custom hero source toggle in the admin editor.** Every city defaults to Automatic (curated or Pexels-resolved, refreshed on its own). Switching a city to Custom pins whatever image an editor has stored, including across edits that touch nothing else. A Custom city with no image yet — or one switched back to Automatic — falls through to the same automatic resolution and named-city placeholder every city already had. Choosing a Pexels photo or the suggested hero in the editor switches the toggle to Custom, since selecting a specific image only matters once it is actually shown.

### Mobile compactness pass

- replace the oversized mobile photo-credit pill with a 127 × 23 px rounded rectangular label; retain a larger invisible tap target
- reduce the local-coverage overlay to 121 × 36 px and shorten mobile-only wording while preserving the full desktop label
- use a 190 px hero image, smaller headline/copy/search controls and a short mobile Search label
- keep the search horizontal from 360–620 px, with a safe stacked layout below 360 px
- keep summary metrics on one adaptive row
- use two compact columns for suppliers and title-only packages where the screen allows, reverting to one column at 320 px
- reduce dead space across cards, planning content, FAQs, nearby areas, CTA and footer
- cache-bust the refreshed location stylesheet

### Visual polish

- broken hero photographs fall back to the same placeholder treatment as a city with no hero, instead of spraying alt text across the hero
- fixed the local-coverage badge escaping its pill and clipping at the screen edge on a broken hero

## Verification

Current head: `908f227`.

- Full location, supplier-geography, admin-editor and hero-image suites pass locally, including new coverage for the hero-source toggle (admin route validation, service-level resolution across all four toggle states, and the jsdom-driven editor scenarios)
- changed JavaScript/tests pass ESLint and Prettier
- browser review completed at 1440 × 1000, 390 × 844 and 320 × 800; no horizontal overflow at any reviewed size

## Runtime dependency

Automatic imagery for cities without a reviewed or editorial hero requires `PEXELS_API_KEY` in the deployed environment. If it is missing, or Pexels does not return a geographically safe result, the page shows the named-city placeholder — for both Automatic and Custom-with-nothing-stored cities.

## CI status

All GitHub check runs pass on `908f227`, including CodeQL. The only red status is **DeepSource JavaScript**, which posts no inline findings and grades the PR A across security, reliability, complexity and hygiene — it is failing a dashboard-configured metric, most likely because `.deepsource.toml` declares `module_system = "es-modules"` / `dialect = "typescript"` on a 100% CommonJS repository. Left as-is; correcting it is a repository-wide configuration decision outside this PR's scope.

author: chrismaghuhn
body:
## Summary

- add a non-normative architecture note for BattleBelief's M3 memory hierarchy
- establish the core invariant that immutable knowledge is shared while only mutable state is stored per battle
- separate Lab snapshot compilation, Runtime artifact/mapping ownership, Core semantic views, battle-local working sets, and the Search hot path
- document snapshot-local identities, battle pinning, deterministic working-set projection, and preservation of tail/OTHER mass as candidates for later normative M3 contracts
- keep Arrow IPC, read-only SQLite, packed arrays, memory mapping, numeric precision, bitsets, Rust arenas, and custom binary formats benchmark-dependent
- update the system overview and documentation index to link the new architecture note

## Scope

Documentation only:

- `docs/architecture/memory-hierarchy.md`
- `docs/architecture/overview.md`
- `docs/README.md`

This PR does not change current normative contracts, schemas, package boundaries, code, dependencies, lockfiles, registrations, M2 tasks, Runtime phase/version, or evidence artifacts.

## M2 / M3 boundary

M2 remains unchanged. Its closed-world distribution is still an evaluation-only Search artifact.

The documented hierarchy is intended for M3, where BattleBelief introduces a versioned Meta Snapshot, a storage-neutral Runtime loader, battle-local posterior state, Open-World Belief, and decision-local Search projections.

## Design boundary

Normative direction proposed for later M3 contract work:

- published snapshots are immutable and content-addressed
- internal IDs are snapshot-local
- snapshot/ruleset/schema/catalog digests travel with derived state
- a running battle remains pinned to one snapshot
- new snapshots do not affect running battles
- snapshot-to-working-set projection is deterministic
- Search performs no SQL or filesystem access
- truncated posterior mass never disappears silently

This architecture document does not itself enact those contract changes.

## Validation requested from CI

- documentation frontmatter and unique IDs
- internal link integrity
- normative-index and authority checks
- repository documentation tests
- whitespace and full PR gates

## Non-goals

- selecting Arrow or SQLite as the final Runtime format
- freezing public Python/Rust APIs
- implementing Meta Snapshot loading, Belief, Working Sets, or Search optimizations
- adding Cross-Battle learning
- changing M2
- making performance, novelty, strength, MVP, or release claims

author: derekhertz
body:
PRD §18, FRONTEND_DESIGN §4.4. `swap_tile()` has been deployed since migration
25 with no client caller, and `boards.swaps_used` and `revisions` had no reader.

A Bingo notification is a social claim. Without a budget anyone could lower a
Target from 144 to 90 in November and manufacture one, and §18.5 closes that with
scarcity plus visibility rather than by making the Board a prison. Both halves
had to be built: the budget a Member can feel, and the Feed row the Family sees
(which landed with slice 14).

- `lib/queries/swaps.ts` — the RPC, the budget, and the refusal copy. **The
  argument is `goal_text`, not `text`**: `docs/api.md` §2.1 and §8 both say
  `text` and both are wrong, and PostgREST answers a wrong argument name with
  PGRST202 — "could not find the function" — which reads exactly like a
  migration that was never deployed. `lib/rpc-signatures.test.ts` guards it now.
- `<SwapSheet>` — §4.4's five elements, and three of them are load-bearing. The
  live glyph and count, because §4.4 permits swapping a Tile at 97% and a Member
  about to do that should be looking at the 97%. The paragraph, because the
  obvious reading of "swap" is "delete" and it is wrong — the retired Goal keeps
  its Increments and they still count for the year. The three pips, because a
  budget nobody can see is not a budget anybody feels.
- The destructive-confirm treatment — `clayDeep` on `paper` inside a `hairline`
  border — used here and nowhere else, which is what §1.1 reserves it for.
  There is no red in this palette and a Member changing their mind about a goal
  in March has done nothing wrong.
- `app/board/swap.tsx` — its own route rather than a mode of `/board/goal`, and
  not duplication: Sharpening does not apply. `swap_tile()` writes only `text`
  and `target` and leaves `unit`, `unit_canonical`, `category` and `pace_hint`
  from the old Goal, so there is no server path to save a new unit and
  "Sharpen it" would offer a suggestion nothing could write.
- **Raising a Target is free, and the screen says so before the tap** (§18.3).
  Being told afterwards that it cost nothing is not the same as knowing.
- The row on the tile sheet appears only when `evaluateGoalRewrite()` says the
  Swap would be allowed. A row on the shared Centre, a completed Tile, a frozen
  Year or an exhausted budget is a row that opens a sheet whose only button the
  server refuses — and all four of those arrive as the same `PT403`, which is
  why the discrimination has to happen before the request rather than after it.

A lowered Target can finish the square on the spot: `swap_tile()` records the
Tile completion and any Lines it closes inside its own transaction, so a Swap can
produce a Bingo with no Increment involved. The mutation invalidates the
Milestones for it.

608 Vitest, tsc clean. No migration touched.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
## Overview This pull request introduces a dedicated, visually-hidden `aria-live` region to provide real-time auditory warnings to visually impaired users when low-reliability QR code patterns (e.g., Grunge, Circuit, Starburst) are selected. Previously, screen readers failed to announce these scannability warnings because the application dynamically toggled visibility classes on an existing visual DOM element instead of updating a persistent live region. This PR resolves the accessibility gap while maintaining 100% visual and layout stability. --- ## The "Why": Rationale & Key Decisions ### 1. Dedicated, Persistent Live Region vs. Reusing Existing Elements Directly converting the existing visual alert container to an `aria-live` region or dynamically modifying its roles was avoided. Toggling the visibility (`visible` / `invisible`) and layout structure of active DOM elements can cause screen readers to miss updates or prematurely interrupt user navigation. * **Decision:** We implemented a persistent, separate `div` specifically for assistive technology. This ensures the live region is always present in the DOM tree, ready to receive and announce updates reliably. ### 2. Preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) Introducing new DOM elements can inadvertently displace surrounding visual elements, triggering layout shifts. * **Decision:** The new container uses Tailwind's `.sr-only` (screen-reader-only) utility classes (width/height of 1px, clipped, absolute positioning). This guarantees that the live region remains completely invisible to sighted users and has a net-zero impact on the document flow, maintaining a Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) of 0. ### 3. Non-Intrusive & Atomic Announcements * **Decision:** The live region is configured with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`. * `polite` ensures that the warning does not rudely interrupt ongoing screen reader speech during active keyboard navigation. * `aria-atomic="true"` ensures the screen reader announces the entire warning text together rather than reading fragmented changes. ### 4. Zero Test Regression * **Decision:** The existing visual warning slot (`data-testid="pattern-warning-slot"`) has been left completely untouched. Its CSS class-toggling behavior and existing structural IDs remain unmodified to ensure zero regression in current visual layout and structural isolation test suites. --- ## Detailed Changes ### Component Updates (`src/components/style-controls/PatternControls.tsx`) - Added a visually hidden container alongside the pattern selection controls: ```tsx
{isLowReliability ? `Scannability Warning: The selected pattern ("${selectedPatternLabel}") is complex and may reduce scannability on older mobile devices or in poor lighting. Consider testing thoroughly before printing.` : ''}
``` - The warning message text dynamically updates and injects only when a low-reliability pattern is selected, and clears entirely when the user reverts to a standard, high-reliability pattern. ### Testing Updates - Added unit tests verifying that selecting Grunge, Circuit, or Starburst immediately updates the live region. - Added tests verifying that standard patterns leave the live region empty (preventing erroneous announcements). - Confirmed that all existing integration and structural isolation tests pass without modification.

author: optimal-cyber
body:
Enhances the existing globe rather than replacing it — the custom day/night shader, connection arcs, star field, and terminal palette all survive.

## What changed

**Vector country borders** — Natural Earth 110m, public domain. The single change that separates a cartographic globe from a textured ball: boundaries stay crisp at any zoom instead of coastlines baked into a JPEG that blur as you approach.

Slimmed **819KB → 149KB** (outer rings only, 2-decimal rounding ≈ 1km at the equator, duplicate points dropped). 287 rings, 10,582 points, merged into **one** `LineSegments` — one draw call, not 287. Antimeridian-crossing segments are skipped, or they draw a chord straight through the planet. A failed fetch leaves the globe intact.

**Graticule** — generated, no asset. Equator and prime meridian drawn brighter: an evenly weighted grid reads as noise, two emphasised axes read as a reference frame.

**Terrain relief, derived not downloaded** — sampling day-texture luminance either side of each fragment approximates a height gradient, perturbing the normal enough to catch light on ridges. A real normal map would be better but is another multi-MB asset on a page already shipping 2MB. Land only; perturbing ocean would fight the specular.

**Anisotropic filtering** at driver max + explicit sRGB, and sphere tessellation 64 → 128 so the limb reads as a curve.

## Two defects found by looking, not diffing

I rendered it and screenshotted before calling it done:

- The **specular highlight was a broad hot blob washing out the entire Gulf of Mexico** — exponent 55 → 190, gain 1.3 → 0.55
- The **atmospheric rim read as bloom rather than scatter** — falloff 3.0 → 3.8, gain 0.65 → 0.42

## Verified visually

Borders render accurately (US/Canada, US/Mexico, Caribbean islands), the graticule is visible, and the Rockies and Sierra Madre show genuine relief shading.

⚠️ **The specular/rim tuning is NOT visually verified** — Chrome tooling stopped responding after the change and I stopped retrying rather than loop. Worth a look before merge.

## Not done

No bloom pass (needs `@react-three/postprocessing`) and no cloud layer (needs another texture). Both are additive later if wanted.

`tsc` clean · build compiles.

author: myleshorton
body:
`h2_oneshot` sets an explicit `host` header alongside the `:authority` it derives from the URI. In HTTP/2 that's redundant — RFC 9113 §8.3.1 says clients generating h2 directly SHOULD use `:authority` rather than `Host` — and Google's frontend doesn't merely ignore it: **it answers with RST_STREAM PROTOCOL_ERROR.**

## Isolated with a 2×2 against a live GFE origin

| | no content-length | with content-length |
|---|---|---|
| **with `host`** | PROTOCOL_ERROR | PROTOCOL_ERROR |
| **without `host`** | HTTP 400 | HTTP 400 |

`content-length` makes no difference; the `host` header alone decides it. (HTTP 400 is the expected answer to the probe body — the point is that the request was *accepted at the h2 layer*.)

Akamai tolerates the header, which is why every fronted caller worked and only a **direct-origin** caller ever saw this.

## How it was found — two earlier attempts were worthless

I twice tried to test this from the outside with curl and twice got a misleading answer, because **curl normalizes**: asked to send `-H 'host: ...'` over h2 it converts that to `:authority` and sends no `host` header at all. The "control" was never sending what it appeared to.

A local h2 server capturing the actual HEADERS frame from each client settled it in one shot:

```
=== flint h2_oneshot ===          === curl ===
  :authority: df.iantem.io          :authority: 127.0.0.1:…
  host: df.iantem.io          ←     (no host header)
  (no content-length)               content-length: 2      ←
```

Exactly two differences, and the 2×2 then separated them.

## Test

Asserts the host travels in `:authority` and that no `host` header is present. I verified it **fails with the header restored**, so it isn't vacuous.

## Follow-up worth noting

`open_meek_stream` still sets `host` deliberately, and a test asserts it. That path terminates at a meek server rather than an origin, so it's unaffected today — but it would hit the same wall if ever pointed at a GFE-served host.

## Downstream

Unblocks spark's proxyless config-fetch avenue, which fails with exactly this `PROTOCOL_ERROR`. Spark needs a rev bump after merge; I'll re-run both `live_fronted_fetch` (must stay green — fronting is the caller that tolerated the header) and `live_proxyless_fetch`.

author: gabyto19
body:
A full visual refresh, plus the layout bug that was quietly constraining every page.

## Why

Each page carried its own ad-hoc CSS — hard-coded control sizes, heavy black drop shadows, `background: green` buttons — so no two pages looked alike and nothing was reusable.

## Design system

`styles.css` now holds the tokens (brand colours, spacing, radii, shadows, type) and the shared elements: card, form control, button, table, notice. Pages style only what is genuinely theirs, which is why most component stylesheets shrank to a width and a submit button.

Georgian renders through **Noto Sans Georgian** — already bundled for the PDF generator — instead of a different fallback on every platform.

## Layout bug

The shell had a real defect:

```css
main { height: 500px; width: 400px; }
```

Content was clipped on small screens and stranded in a narrow column on large ones. This is what kept the admin tables narrow regardless of their own `max-width`. It is now a centred, responsive container.

## Navigation

body:
Fixes the "twin small lines" defect described in [BIGR-773](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/BIGR-773): in the `portfolio`, `lumen`, `pulso`, and `hearth` demo builds the first viewport stacks two visually identical caption-scale lines ~100–150px apart — the header's second text row (`wp:site-tagline` or a nav row) and the hero's opening eyebrow — and in the worst case they nearly say the same thing ("documentary photography of Argentine social and political events" over "Documentary photography from Argentina").

## Root causes

1. `PlaygroundArtifact::siteOptions()` fell back to the spec's factual `topic` for the blogdescription, guaranteeing semantic collision with hero copy written from the same spec.
2. `wp:site-tagline` is a dynamic block: its rendered text is invisible to every anti-echo defense (header NO-ECHO rule, hero ownership rule, and the deterministic `dedupeAgainstHero()` pass).
3. Nothing gated the hero eyebrow on the header's shape, so a caption/uppercase/tracked eyebrow appears under two-row headers.

## Changes

**A — no more `topic`-as-tagline** (`src/PlaygroundArtifact.php`)
`blogDescription()` is the one authority: the user's stated tagline or `''`. The playground blueprint and the build steps share it.

**B — canonical header text-shape facts** (`src/AboveFoldContract.php`, `src/Steps/SectionsStep.php`, `prompts/header.md`, `prompts/hero.md`)
The contract's `header` block now carries `displays_tagline`, `tagline_text`, and `text_rows`, derived once from the archetype and the stated tagline (and reset by header degradation). `header.md` emits `wp:site-tagline` only when `displays_tagline` is true; `hero.md` gets an EYEBROW GATE — when `text_rows` is 2 the H1 must be the hero's first text line — and a ban on restating `tagline_text` verbatim **or paraphrased**.

**C — deterministic backstop** (`src/Steps/HeaderHeroStep.php`)
`dedupeAgainstHero()` now receives the text the tagline block will actually render. A blank-rendering `wp:site-tagline` is stripped; a stated tagline that paraphrases a hero eyebrow/short line is stripped via a stopword-dropping, inflection-tolerant matcher (`"argentine" ~ "argentina"`, 2+ shared content words covering ≥60% of the shorter line). Identity is the site *name*, so the tagline block is the one removed — hero copy is never touched.

## Tests

- `above_fold_contract_test.php`: text-shape facts per archetype/tagline, including degradation reset.
- `header_hero_test.php`: paraphrase strip (the audited portfolio pair), distinct-tagline survival, blank-tagline strip, idempotence.
- Full unit suite: **1497 passed, 0 failed**.

author: marbaji
body:
## Why

The 2026-07-31 amendment pulled the **frequency** lever on memory bloat — auto-memory candidates stopped being enumerated at session-end. It did not fix **placement**, so the index kept growing.

A 2026-08-05 audit across every memory silo found:

| finding | |
|---|---|
| total | **148 files across 6 live silos** |
| chalktalk silo | 97 files / **124 index lines / ~3.4k tokens loaded per session** |
| second silo | 43 files, duplicating the first **by concept with zero filename overlap** |
| examples | `user_role` vs `user_profile` · `feedback_no-em-dashes` vs `feedback_no_em_dashes` · one 95-line "where plans live" file vs **four** separate ones |
| also | several memories restated rules **already in the global `CLAUDE.md`**, paying index tokens to duplicate a file that already loads everywhere |

Root cause: nothing said *what may enter memory*, or where a lesson belongs when the answer is "not here." Project-scoped silos also cannot see each other, so a cross-project principle filed in one is invisible in the other five.

## What this adds

**Step 3a.1 — three rules governing every memory write**, including the discretionary correction-time one:

1. **Admission test.** A memory earns a slot only if it changes what I would DO on a future task in ANY project. Otherwise it routes: cross-project principles → `~/.claude/work-principles.md` (imported by `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, loads everywhere); project facts → the vault; single-repo command recipes → that project's `memory/`; already in `CLAUDE.md` → dropped rather than duplicated. The discriminator is given literally, because the line is easy to blur:
   - *"use `git rm -rf --cached` for path-based tree replacement"* → command recipe, project memory
   - *"verify a backup against live before deleting it"* → principle, `work-principles.md`
2. **Fold before you create.** Search existing memories first; if one covers the lesson, append and leave the index alone. An append costs **zero** index lines; a new file costs one forever.
3. **Rule first, incident second.** A memory that buries its rule in paragraph three reads as "do exactly what happened last time" — which is what makes memories railroady, and railroady memories get ignored or over-applied to cases that only rhyme.

**Step 7 now surfaces the index budget.** The cost of a new memory file is invisible at the moment you decide to write one, which is how an index reaches 124 lines. Past ~120 the report recommends `/dream` instead of another append, and points back at Step 3a.1 since a line that should have been an append or a principles entry is the usual cause.

## Verified before landing

`@path` imports are real, so the global principles file costs `CLAUDE.md` exactly one line. Evidence from the Claude Code 2.1.222 binary: `"This project's CLAUDE.md imports files outside the current working directory"`, `"Allow external CLAUDE.md file imports?"`, and its own recommended `@~/.claude/<name>-instructions.md` stub pattern.

Applied in the same session that wrote it: two learnings both folded into existing memories, and `MEMORY.md` stayed at 124 lines.

Source: Mo, 2026-08-05 — memories should encode workflow and generalized work principles, not project specifics, and should not be specific and railroady.

## Summary
Prompted by a user report: a site showing ERROR on "Steady Client Count 1hr Average" despite every visible number reading "(down 0.0%)" — the message gave no explanation for the color.

Root cause: `weekly_frac`/`monthly_frac`/`min_peak` are computed from thresholds config and extensively described in the docstring/comments ("below weekly_frac of the 7-day average -> ERROR"), but never actually compared against anything. `die_off_peak` was initialized to `0.0` and never reassigned — the rule could never fire, and since the "sustained die-off vs peak" explanation text only renders when `die_off_peak` is truthy, that explanation could never show either.

- Also surfaces `day_drop_pct`/`week_drop_pct`/`rate_drop_pct` in the message whenever non-trivial — these are LIVE rules (PERIOD trips at just 20% by default, well below the within-hour tier's 50%) that were computed and returned but never shown, so a PERIOD-triggered error looked identical to "no visible cause."

Companion PR in `cs` for the spoke-side twin (`central_poller.py`), which had the same gap.

author: samhren
body:
## Summary

- Adds a transaction rule action, **Swap deposit and withdrawal**, that multiplies a matched transaction's amount by `-1`. Fixes #2926.
- Motivation is provider-side sign reversal. Fidelity transactions imported over SimpleFIN currently arrive with the wrong direction, so deposits and withdrawals appear swapped. This gives users a scoped, self-service workaround while the provider fixes the upstream data.
- The action composes with existing rule conditions, so it can be narrowed to a single account, name pattern, or effective date.
- Correction state is recorded on the transaction rather than on the rule, under `extra["rules"]["invert_transaction_amount"]`. Idempotency therefore holds three ways: re-running a rule is a no-op, two overlapping inversion rules cannot cancel each other out, and a later provider sync that restores the original sign is re-corrected on the next rule run.
- Each row is corrected under a row lock so concurrent syncs cannot interleave a partial flip.
- Amount locks are respected. A user who has manually edited an amount is not overwritten unless the rule is explicitly re-applied with locks ignored.
- Transfer legs and split children are deliberately skipped, even on an explicit re-apply. Both carry a cross-record sum invariant that nothing re-checks when an entry amount is written: `Transfer` requires its two legs to have opposite signs and sum to zero, and a split requires its children to sum to the excluded parent. Flipping one side of either would leave a silently invalid row that cannot self-heal, since auto transfer matching only considers transactions not already attached to a transfer. Skipped transactions are reported as blocked in the rule run counts, the same treatment a locked amount gets.
- Affected accounts are re-synced once each from the earliest changed date so persisted balances are rematerialized.
- The correction state round-trips through family export and import, so restoring a backup does not re-apply the correction and double-flip the amount. Only this one narrowly scoped key is carried in the portable format; provider metadata under `extra` is neither exported nor overwritten.

## Verification

Run against the branch tip:

- `bin/rails test`: 6213 runs, 24715 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `bin/rails test:system test/system/rules_test.rb`: 90 runs, 0 failures
- `bin/rubocop` and `bin/brakeman`: clean, 0 warnings

Automated coverage includes idempotency on re-apply, two overlapping inversion rules not cancelling each other, amount locks, the export and re-import round trip, and the transfer-leg and split-child skips. The skip tests were confirmed to fail without the guard rather than passing vacuously.

One gap worth knowing: the account resync is stubbed in these tests, so the balance rematerialization path has no automated coverage and is worth confirming by hand.

## Test plan

- [ ] Create the rule through the UI and confirm a `-100.00` withdrawal becomes a `100.00` deposit.
- [ ] Confirm the account balance and the balance chart update to match.
- [ ] Re-sync the provider so it restores the original sign, then confirm the next rule run re-corrects it.

## Notes

- No migration and no schema change. Correction state reuses the existing `transactions.extra` jsonb column.
- `Family::DataExporter` gains one optional field. The importer guards on its presence, so older backups import unchanged.
- English locale string only, consistent with how other strings land in this repo before translation.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a rule action to swap deposit and withdrawal amounts.
  * The action skips transfers, split entries, zero amounts, and locked amounts when applicable.
  * Account balances are recalculated after eligible transactions are updated.
* **Improvements**
  * Amount-swap corrections persist through export and import.
  * Transaction metadata is preserved, and corrections are not repeated.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Invalid inversion states are rejected without overwriting unrelated metadata.
  * Malformed imported inversion data is safely ignored and logged.

body:
A public, shareable walkthrough of how this site actually works, in the same interactive
field-study form as the Data Spine and the Policy Engine.

## What it is

`/projects/engine-room` — ten sections plus a flagship instrument.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Machine** | the whole system as one hoverable map, and the numbers |
| **Conversation** | the external agent runtime, and streaming a reply that arrives in pieces |
| **Models** | four-layer model resolution, seller economics, the reasoning floor, caching |
| **Tools** | 155 tools, 21 shown; the context budget and where 4.4 seconds goes |
| **Memory** | retrieval, the knowledge graph, entity resolution, the datastore |
| **Research** | provenance, and where fabrication actually comes from |
| **Automation** | 88 node types, the fan-in collision, the nightly doctor |
| **Building** | the sandboxed builder and the nightly self-improvement engine |
| **Shipping** | gate-then-deploy, and what a machine may merge by itself |
| **Guardrails** | every rail, sorted by whether it is a boundary or merely a request |
| **Trace** | one turn across six stages and six layers, with a live clock and bill |

## Interactives, not diagrams

Pick a model seller and watch precision and latency move · drag an output budget until the
answer disappears · toggle matching signals and watch confidence cross the merge bar · try
to get generated code past the deny-list scan · wire two branches three ways and see which
one loses data · step a frame stream through two accumulators and watch the naive one
destroy a reply.

The **Ask dock** is the thing the study describes: BM25 over a corpus assembled from the
study's own typed content, streamed, citing the passages it used. Lexical rather than
vector on purpose, and the Memory section says why.

## Accuracy

Every figure was counted from source or measured, not estimated, and each stat tile carries
how it was counted. Several remembered numbers were replaced during the write-up with ones
that could actually be defended — including a widely-quoted caching multiplier that turned
out to be a single best-case turn, and a cron-timezone claim that had been fixed since.

## No secrets

No credentials, keys, addresses, hostnames, repository names, personal data or configuration
values appear anywhere in the study — not redacted, never written. Worked examples that use
real names in the source were rewritten with neutral stand-ins. The Guardrails section states
this explicitly and argues the constraint improved the writing.

## Surface change

Adding the study changed the anonymous surface by **twelve routes** (index, nine sections,
the trace instrument, and the Ask endpoint). All intended; the lockfile is updated
deliberately. This tripping the gate is itself written up in the Shipping section.

Expect **tier: high** — the change touches `.github/`, so it will not auto-merge.

## Verification

`npm run gate` green on the final state: public-routes OK, font-sizes OK, **0 type errors
across 6,600 files**, **430 test files passed**, production build clean.

author: nasytnyk
body:
## 🥊 New Boxing exhibit: boxing an empty Nullable

**Rule:** never expect a boxed **nullable** to still be nullable

### What it teaches
`Nullable<T>` does not exist inside a box. Boxing is special-cased: a *filled* `int?` boxes to a plain `int` (`GetType()` reports `Int32`), and an *empty* one boxes to a **null reference** — so `(object)(int?)null` is literally `null`. Drop an unset `int?` into an `object`-typed store and you have stored `null`; read it back with `(int)` and unboxing `null` throws `NullReferenceException` — at a cast with no visible dereference, in a component far from where it was stored, by code sure that "a value type can't be null".

### Deterministic reproduction
Store `LoadSetting("retries")` (absent → null `int?`) into a `Dictionary<string, object?>`, then read `(int)bag["retries"]`. `Good.cs` is the mirror — `(int?)bag["retries"] ?? 3`.

Verified on .NET 10 (warning-free, stable across runs):
- `dotnet run Bad.cs` → `The bag now holds null: True.` then `System.NullReferenceException` (exit 134)
- `dotnet run Good.cs` → `Retrying up to 3 times.` / `Missing setting fell back to the default.`

### Notable README content
- **😈** the roundtrip is asymmetric and aimed at the test suite: a *filled* `int?` reads back fine (even the buggy `(int)` cast works), only the *empty* case crashes — and empty is exactly the case fixtures never supply, so it ships green and dies on the first real missing config.
- **🎓** `empty.HasValue` works while `empty.GetType()` throws NRE (GetType boxes first); reverse conversions are all lenient (`(int?)(object)7` = 7), so `int?` is the safe unbox target both ways (ties to [0041-unbox-must-match-exact-type](../../boxing/0041-unbox-must-match-exact-type/)).
- **🔎** the compiler *already* warns — **CS8605 "Unboxing a possibly null value"** — and silencing it with `!` is exactly this bug; unbox to `int?` instead.

### Housekeeping
- Front page regenerated; `tools/check-links.cs` passes (43 exhibits). Memory in a separate commit (`state.md` 42→43, next id 0044; candidate removed from `backlog/boxing.md`).

author: bzreinhardt
body:
## What changed

`staging-converge.sh` now deletes old images for the staging repo before it pulls, keeping the three most recent plus whatever is serving and whatever is incoming. `STAGING_IMAGE_RETAIN` overrides the count. Documented in `deploy/STAGING.md`.

## Why

Staging deploys never cleaned up after themselves. Twenty-eight SHA-tagged images had accumulated on the staging host, filling colima's 59GB Docker volume to 93%, and every convergence then died partway through unpacking:

```
failed to extract layer ... /app/packages/twenty-shared/dist/types/SidePanelPages.d.ts:
no space left on device
```

The converger rolled back and retried every two minutes, so staging sat a commit behind `staging-target` and re-downloaded ~180MB per doomed attempt. Retrying cannot clear this, which is why the trim runs before the pull: a host that has already filled up recovers on its own next tick rather than needing someone to log in and prune by hand.

Each deploy adds ~1.3GB of layers, so at three retained images the volume settles around 5GB instead of growing without bound.

The serving image is protected because it is the rollback target, so a failed deploy still restores from a local image rather than re-pulling.

## Testing

Unit-tested the retention logic against a stubbed `docker`, under `set -euo pipefail` to match the script, 8 cases passing: default retain, an old serving image outside the retention window, an already-present incoming image, `STAGING_IMAGE_RETAIN` overrides of 1 and 0, fewer images than the budget, and an empty daemon.

An earlier draft made `retain` a budget *in addition to* the protected images, so the total kept was unbounded by the setting and the log message was wrong. The tests caught it; protected images now spend the budget while inside it.

End-to-end against the real daemon with four throwaway tags: kept three, removed three, both real images untouched, `docker rmi` on a shared-layer tag correctly untagged without disturbing the base image.

Also verified on the live host: `bash -n` clean, and a real run with two images and retain 3 removed nothing and exited 0.

## Operationally sensitive

Touches the deploy path on the host that also runs production. `production-converge.sh` is unaffected: it converges by source fast-forward and pulls no images.

The prune only ever targets tags under the staging image repo, so unrelated images on the shared daemon are left alone. Dangling/untagged images are not touched; 2.14GB of those existed during this incident and were cleared by hand, which is a possible follow-up.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The converger keeps working, it just stops reclaiming, so the volume resumes filling at ~1.3GB per deploy.

## Not addressed

The reason the volume grows so fast. `node_modules` is a 1.09GB layer that gets a fresh digest on every build even when `yarn.lock` is byte-identical: same 82,395 files with the same content hash, but `COPY` preserves mtimes that differ per CI run, so it never dedupes and is re-pulled and re-stored every deploy. Normalizing those mtimes in `packages/twenty-docker/twenty/Dockerfile` would cut per-deploy download to ~35MB and disk growth to ~190MB. Left for a separate PR.

Separately, staging deployment statuses are not reaching GitHub. Deployment `5763800339` still reads `failure` from the rollback even though staging is now healthy on `ab431455`; the success POST failed too. `~/.config/twenty-staging/github-token` does not exist, so `gh_deploy` falls back to the ambient `gh` login and the POST is rejected. Pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

## Screenshots

None, no user-visible UI change.

Updates our package publishing workflow to more heavily rely on changesets instead of manual publishing/syncing. This allows us to make targeted updates for specific packages along with still allowing all packages to be bumped when an icon is added.

Below is a mermaid chart for the new flow 👇 

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[PR adds a changeset] --> B[Merge PR into main]
    B --> C[Changesets Action runs]

    C --> D{Changesets exist?}

    D -- Yes --> E[Run changeset:version]
    E --> F[Update package.json versions]
    F --> G[Generate package changelogs]
    G --> H[Run Ruby rake version tasks]
    H --> I[Create or update Release Tracking PR]

    I --> J[Merge Release Tracking PR]
    J --> C

    D -- No --> K[Run changeset:publish]
    K --> L[Build npm packages and Ruby gems]

    L --> M[Publish Ruby gems in dependency order]
    M --> M1[octicons]
    M1 --> M2[octicons_helper]
    M1 --> M3[jekyll-octicons]

    M2 --> N[Run changeset publish]

    N --> O[Publish npm packages]
    O --> O1["@primer/octicons"]

    O --> O3["@primer/styled-octicons"]
