author: valerielinc-ops
body:
Closes #5169

## Implementato

Due difetti indipendenti, e servivano entrambi: il primo impediva al gate di
girare, il secondo gli impediva di misurare qualcosa anche quando girava.

- **Il gate non ricostruisce più `dist/`**: scarica quella che `deploy.yml` ha
  già costruito e spedito, e reidrata gli shard. Via la composite action
  `build-dist-multi-locale-merged`, via `assemble-jobs-dataset`, via
  `seo-build-data-prep`.
- **Quattro gate su sei erano inerti**: leggevano `0` come valore corrente *e*
  `0` come baseline, quindi il verdetto era `pass` qualunque cosa ci fosse in
  `dist/`. Ora leggono le chiavi che gli audit emettono davvero, e **sollevano**
  se non le trovano invece di scrivere 0.
- **`orphan-sitemap-pages` non fa più regex sullo stdout umano** ma legge il
  report JSON che l'audit scrive comunque.
- **`build-dist-multi-locale-merged` è cancellata**: con #5166 già su `main`
  (adsense audita il sito live) e questa PR, la composite action non ha più
  chiamanti. Esisteva solo per girare il build monolitico che l'OOM-killer ha
  ucciso 9 volte su 10; lasciarla in albero è un invito a ricablarla.
- **26 test** (`tests/cathedral-seo-gates-extractors.test.ts` +
  l'aggiornamento di `tests/postwalk-worker-leaf-graph.test.ts`) che ancorano i
  reader ai payload reali degli audit e ai file di baseline **committati**, più
  la forma del workflow e l'assenza della action cancellata.

### 1. Il build che veniva ucciso

Il workflow costruiva la propria dist SSG completa ed è stato ucciso
dall'**OOM-killer del kernel** in **9 delle ultime 10 run**. La run
**30795844586** è morta a **RSS ~11,3 GB dopo 72 minuti** mentre costruiva la
**prima** delle quattro locale:

```
09:26:45  [profile-mem] events-seo-pages  rss_mb=11277 heapUsed_mb=4851
09:26:51  [related-search-clusters] 349397 candidates, 7089 enriched entries
09:27:12  ##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal.
```

`heapUsed` fermo a ~4,8 GB mentre l'RSS sale a 11,3: **il grosso è fuori
dall'heap V8**, quindi né `--max-old-space-size` né la GC lo toccano — coerente
con #4943, dove `8192`, `12288` e `14336` sono falliti tutti e tre. E muore il
*processo del runner*, quindi nemmeno lo step crash-reporter di questo workflow
riesce a partire: la run risulta `cancelled`, non `failure`.

Questo **soddisfa alla lettera il revert-trigger** scritto dentro la composite
action (righe 31-37):

> *"if a scheduled run of either caller workflow still OOMs at/above the previous
> ~11.7GB ceiling after this lands, per-locale filtering is not shedding the
> memory this diagnosis assumes"*

E si capisce perché lo split per-locale di #4586 non ha retto: **la retention non
è per-locale**. I 349k candidati di `related-search-clusters` e i dataset globali
degli hub vengono caricati identici in ognuno dei quattro sub-build, quindi
dividere il lavoro non divide la memoria.

**La correzione è smettere di costruire.** `deploy.yml` costruisce esattamente
questa dist, con successo, ogni poche ore, con la sua matrice per-locale (un
runner per locale — quella sì che non OOMa). E il repo ha già la macchina per
rigiocarla (`audit-dist-from-run.yml`, documentata in `AGENTS.md → Build And
Test`). Quindi il gate ora:

1. risolve la run di deploy da auditare — la più recente riuscita su `main` che
   **abbia ancora i suoi artifact** (`retention-days: 1`, quindi si scorre
   all'indietro invece di fallire sulla prima scaduta), oppure quella che
   l'operatore passa via il nuovo input `deploy_run_id`;
2. scarica l'artifact `github-pages` e lo estrae in `dist/`;
3. reidrata **prima** gli shard di locale (hard-fail) e **poi** quelli di
   sezione (soft-fail) — stesso ordine e stesso contratto di
   `post-deploy-validate-dist.yml`, perché l'artifact è il solo **trunk**: senza
   reidratare, ogni audit che cammina `dist/` denuncia i sottoalberi assenti come
   un difetto **del sito** (è come la replay 30346794790 dichiarò ~68k URL
   cluster sotto la profondità di crawl, #4857);
4. esegue `scripts/ci/assert-dist-complete.mjs` **prima** di qualunque audit —
   precondizione, non gate: una reidratazione degradata non deve trasformarsi in
   una issue "regressed" aperta contro un baseline che sta benissimo.

Serve `permissions: actions: read` per leggere gli artifact di un'altra run.

Perché **non** si applica il rimedio di #4943 (che ha semplicemente tolto il
build e legge il sito **live**): quei gate misurano l'**HTML emesso** — lunghezza
dei `<title>`, structured data, rapporto testo/HTML, profondità BFS. Serve un
albero `dist/`. Solo: non uno costruito qui.

Effetto collaterale positivo: auditare l'artifact che il deploy ha **spedito** è
più veritiero che auditare una ricostruzione privata dello stesso.

### 2. I gate che non misuravano niente

Anche quando girava, il verdetto era finto. `extractCurrent` faceva:

```js
const offenders = p.offenders;
if (Array.isArray(offenders)) return offenders.length;
return Number(p.total ?? 0);
```

Ma tre dei sei audit emettono `offenders` come **numero**, non come array, e non
emettono affatto `total`:

| script | riga | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `audit-title-length.mjs` | 394 | `offenders: result.offendersTotal` |
| `audit-text-html-ratio.mjs` | 499 | `offenders: offenders.length` |
| `audit-title-no-disambig-hash.mjs` | 307 | `offenders: result.offendersTotal` |

`Array.isArray` → falso; `p.total` → `undefined` → **`current = 0`**. E
`extractBaseline` leggeva `b.total`, mentre **tutti** i file di baseline scrivono
`totalOffenders` (`data/title-length-baseline.json` → `totalOffenders: 4290`,
`text-html-ratio` → `6912`, `title-no-disambig-hash` → `539`; `total` non esiste
in nessuno) → **`baseline = 0`**.

Quindi `0 === 0` → status **`pass`, permanentemente**, qualunque cosa contenesse
`dist/`. L'`exitCode` dell'audit veniva registrato ma mai usato per il verdetto.
Un gate che costa 70+ minuti e non protegge niente.

Ora c'è un solo reader condiviso che accetta ogni forma realmente emessa
(`offenders` array **o** numero, `total`, `totalOffenders`) e — questo è il
punto — **solleva** se non trova nessuna delle chiavi, invece di restituire 0 in
silenzio. `evaluateGate` traduce l'eccezione in status `error`, che fa uscire il
workflow con 1. Un gate che non sa leggere il proprio input deve dirlo.

Stesso trattamento per `orphan-sitemap-pages`: cercava
`/total[^:]*orphans?\s*[:=]?\s*(\d+)/i` nello stdout, un pattern che la riga
`TOTAL` incolonnata (`audit-orphan-pages-in-sitemaps.mjs:627`) **non contiene**,
per poi ripiegare su `/(\d+)\s+orphan/i`, cioè il primo numero incidentale del
log. Ora legge `data/orphan-pages-audit.json`, che quell'audit scrive sempre
(riga 804) prima di uscire — **e ne verifica la freschezza**: quel file è
git-tracked, quindi un audit crashato prima di scriverlo lascerebbe sul disco la
copia committata e il reader valuterebbe il gate sul numero della settimana
scorsa. Esattamente la stessa classe di pass silenzioso, rientrata dalla porta di
servizio. `generatedAt` deve essere ≥ l'avvio di questo processo, altrimenti
errore.

`main()` è ora dietro una guardia di invocazione diretta, così i reader si
possono importare in un test senza far partire sei audit su `dist/`.

### Test

`tests/cathedral-seo-gates-extractors.test.ts` — 22 test:

- **nessun workflow** usa più `build-dist-multi-locale-merged`, e la cartella
  della action non esiste più (scansione di tutti i file in
  `.github/workflows/`);
- i **payload reali** dei tre audit (chiavi copiate dai loro blocchi
  `MODE_JSON`) devono produrre un `current` **> 0**, cioè esattamente ciò che
  prima dava 0;
- i **file di baseline committati** vengono letti dal disco: si asserisce che
  `raw.total` è `undefined` (la chiave che il vecchio reader cercava) e che il
  nuovo reader restituisce `totalOffenders`;
- payload/baseline senza conteggio → **throw**, non 0 (è la regressione che ha
  disarmato il gate);
- la forma vecchia con `offenders` **array** continua a funzionare;
- un payload peggiore di uno del baselin

author: edalzell
body:
## Summary

`Events::upcoming()`/`between()` fully augment every entry in the collection, then throw almost all of it away. Collections are mostly made up of events that finished long ago, so the vast majority of that work is wasted.

On a real site with **548 events**, 527 had already finished. Generating their occurrences accounted for roughly 90% of the ~1.6s an `upcoming(30)` call took — no SQL involved, it's all Stache augmentation.

## Fix

Reject already-ended events up front, in `occurrences()`, before the generator runs.

The important part is *how* the check is made: it reads **only raw values**. Augmentation is the expensive thing here — measured on one multi-day entry, augmented `$entry->days` costs ~30ms while raw `$entry->get('days')` costs 0ms — so a check that touched augmented values would just relocate the cost instead of removing it.

An event is skipped only when its **last possible date** is known to have passed, which is deliberately not the same as "started in the past":

| type | last possible date |
|---|---|
| non-recurring | `start_date` — the only occurrence |
| recurring | `end_date`; **no `end_date` means it recurs forever** |
| multi-day | the last of its `days` |

So an event that started two years ago and recurs annually is kept, and querying a past range still returns everything it used to. Dates that can't be parsed fall through rather than being excluded, and there's two days of slack because the event's own timezone isn't knowable without augmenting.

## Results

Measured on that 548-event site, `upcoming(30)`:

| | |
|---|---|
| before | ~1646ms |
| after | ~195ms |

Output is **byte-identical** — verified by diffing full dumps against unmodified `main`: 87 rows for `upcoming(30)`, and 1082 rows for a `between()` spanning three years of past events.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `tests/SkipsEndedEventsTest.php` covering the cases this could plausibly get wrong: unbounded recurring events that started years ago, annually recurring events, recurring events with a future vs passed `end_date`, multi-day events that are past/partway through, and past-range `between()` queries.
- [x] Since this is an optimization, those tests pass both before and after — so I checked they actually have teeth by temporarily implementing the naive "`start_date` is in the past" filter instead. **4 of the 8 fail** against it, including every unbounded-recurrence case and the past-range query.
- [x] Full suite green (116 passed).

References https://github.com/transformstudios/zakat.org/issues/2322

author: harshasiddartha
body:
### Description

Fixes #20206.

`FLRW.angular_diameter_distance` has the signature

```python
def angular_diameter_distance(self, z: _InputT, z2: _InputT | None = None, /) -> u.Quantity:
```

but heads its `Parameters` section `z1, z2`. The first parameter is `z`, so numpydoc pairs the entry with a name the method does not have.

The issue offered two options. This takes the first — rename the heading to `z, z2` and leave the prose alone — because the two sibling methods with exactly this signature already do that:

- `comoving_distance(self, z, z2=None, /)` heads its section `z, z2`,
- `comoving_transverse_distance(self, z, z2=None, /)` heads its section `z, z2`,

and both keep explaining the two-argument form in terms of `z1, z2` in the description underneath, as this one does. So the heading matches the signature and the wording stays consistent with its neighbours.

One line, docstring only — no signature, call site, or behaviour is touched.

### Changelog

Not added: docstring only, so per `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("in general you do not need to include a changelog entry for minor documentation or test updates") this is not user-visible. Happy to add a fragment or apply `no-changelog-entry-needed`, whichever you prefer.

author: samuelcook
body:
## Problem

`gascity/assets/workflows/do-work/prepare-worktree.md` step 4 creates each item worktree with:

    git worktree add "$WORKTREE" --detach HEAD

i.e. branched from the launcher (pool) checkout's **local** `HEAD`. In a long-running city the pool checkout's local default branch drifts behind `origin` as PRs merge — nothing fetches it between items — so agents implement on a stale base and open PRs that conflict with, or wholesale **duplicate**, work already merged to the default branch.

Observed downstream: an item re-dispatched while the pool checkout was **23 commits behind `origin/main`** rebuilt a feature already merged, producing a PR with 8 add/add conflicts against the existing files.

## Fix

Resolve the repo's default branch, fetch it, and create the worktree from the freshly-fetched `origin/<default>` tip instead of local `HEAD`. This mirrors what `gastown/assets/scripts/worktree-setup.sh` already does (fetch + `origin/HEAD` start-point) — the do-work `prepare-worktree` path just wasn't applying the same pattern.

Docs-only change to an agent-run workflow prompt; no code paths altered.

author: pher217
body:
## Goal

Two upstream bugs that make a **rebuild** of this fork fail on macOS. Neither relates to branding; both are dormant until someone re-runs `autogen.sh`, which is why the July build passed and the first rebuild did not. Split out of [#14](https://github.com/Pher217/libreoffice-fork/pull/14) since they stand alone.

## Changes

**1. harfbuzz cannot find graphite2** — `external/harfbuzz/ExternalProject_harfbuzz.mk:59`

`meson.build:113: ERROR: Dependency 'graphite2' is required but not found`. The recipe joined the graphite and icu directories into `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` with `;`, the Windows separator. On macOS and Linux pkg-config splits on `:`, so both arrived as a single nonexistent path and neither `.pc` was visible. The branch only runs when `SYSTEM_ICU` is unset, so it hits exactly the internal-ICU builds.

**2. The gallery recipe cannot clean the directory it creates** — `solenv/gbuild/Gallery.mk:19`

`rm: workdir/Gallery/backgrounds/user: is a directory` → `Error 1`. `gb_Gallery__command` opens with a non-recursive `rm -f <workdir>/<gallery>/*`, then runs `gengal` with `-env:UserInstallation=<workdir>/<gallery>/user` — creating a throwaway profile directory in the very directory the next run tries to clear. `rm -f` cannot remove a directory. A first build passes because it does not exist yet.

## Approach

Both are one-character fixes matching existing in-tree convention rather than workarounds:

- `:` is what `external/cairo/ExternalProject_cairo.mk:85-96` uses for every `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` entry, on all platforms.
- `rm -rf` lets the recipe remove the profile directory it is itself responsible for creating; the glob stays confined to that gallery's own workdir subdirectory.

Deleting the stale directories by hand was rejected — it would recur on every subsequent gallery rebuild.

## Test Summary

Verified directly, not by inference:

- **harfbuzz**: against the generated `graphite2.pc`, `pkg-config --exists graphite2` **succeeds** with `:` and **fails** with `;`. After the fix, harfbuzz configured and built, and every stage that previously failed proceeded.
- **Gallery**: with the stale `workdir/Gallery/{backgrounds,sounds}/user` directories cleared, the gallery targets rebuilt.
- **End to end**: `gmake` then produced a working `instdir/OfficeLabs.app` whose `soffice --version` reports `OfficeLabs 26.8.0.0.alpha0`.

## Files Changed

- `external/harfbuzz/ExternalProject_harfbuzz.mk` — `;` → `:`
- `solenv/gbuild/Gallery.mk` — `rm -f` → `rm -rf`

## Note

Both look like genuine upstream defects rather than fork-specific breakage, so they are candidates for upstreaming to LibreOffice.

## Still failing after this

`.dmg` packaging: `instsetoo_native/util/openoffice.lst` has no `OfficeLabs` or `OfficeLabs_SDK` product block (`ziplist.pm:153`). Separate change — the app itself builds and runs.

author: learningcircuit
body:
## What

Adds a `groups` block to the `github-actions` entry in `.github/dependabot.yml` so all `github/codeql-action` references (`init`, `analyze`, `upload-sarif`) are bumped in **one combined PR** instead of one PR per pinned ref.

```yaml
groups:
  codeql-action:
    patterns:
      - "github/codeql-action*"
```

The trailing `*` matters: SHA-pinned sub-actions are separate Dependabot dependencies named by their full path (`github/codeql-action/init`, `/analyze`, `/upload-sarif`), and group patterns without a wildcard only match exactly.

## Why

This is the root-cause prevention for the break that #5400 fixes manually.

`codeql.yml` pins `init` and `analyze` as two distinct SHA references. Without grouping, Dependabot sees two refs and opens two separate PRs (cf. the closed #5344 and #5348). Each PR alone splits the versions and the CodeQL Advanced job hard-fails:

```
##[error] Loaded a configuration file for version '4.37.4', but running version '4.36.3'
```

CodeQL's `init` step writes a version-tagged config that `analyze` must read back at the **same** version, so those refs must move in lockstep. Grouping makes Dependabot do that automatically on every future codeql-action release — no more manual replacement PRs.

## Scope

Single file, 13 added lines (config + explanatory comment). No behavior change for any other action; only `github/codeql-action` is grouped. All other GitHub-Actions dependencies continue to get individual PRs as today.

## Verification

- YAML parses cleanly (`python3 -c yaml.safe_load`): `version=2`, 11 update blocks, `groups.codeql-action.patterns = ['github/codeql-action*']` ✅
- pre-commit hooks passed ✅
- The `github/codeql-action*` pattern matches all three sub-action dependency names (`github/codeql-action/init`, `/analyze`, `/upload-sarif`): dependabot-core names SHA-pinned sub-actions by their full path (`file_parser.rb`), and its `WildcardMatcher` compiles patterns to anchored regexes with `*` → `.*` — confirmed against the titles of #5344/#5348, which are per-sub-action ✅

## Related

- #5400 — the manual bump (init + analyze → 4.37.4) that this PR makes unnecessary to repeat in the future.
- #5344, #5348 — the two broken Dependabot PRs that prompted this.

---

author: alisafari-it
body: ## The bug A student on the Dutch locale asked "algebera II" (their actual input — two words, a typo) and got the AI's answer back in Spanish, not Dutch. The only language instruction anywhere was `"Answer in the same language as the student question."` — for a short, ambiguous, or misspelled input that gives the model nothing reliable to detect a language from, so it guesses. Spanish this time; could be anything else next time. ## Fix The app already had the real signal available and just wasn't using it: the student's chosen UI locale (the `asafarim-lang` cookie, already resolved everywhere else in the app via `resolveLocaleFromCookie`). `buildSystemPrompt(localeHint?)` in `lib/server/ai-orchestrator.ts` asks the model to mirror the question's language *when that's actually identifiable from the text*, and only falls back to the student's app-locale language when it isn't. The ordering is deliberate — a student who deliberately writes in French while the app happens to be set to English should still get a French answer; the locale is a fallback for uninformative text, not an override. Both places that build this prompt now go through the shared builder with a resolved locale: - `POST /api/inquiries` — fire-and-forget orchestration on inquiry create - `GET /api/inquiries/[id]/ai` — the SSE stream that actually feeds the visible "AI Uitleg" response. This route had its own copy of the system prompt, hardcoded independently of `ai-orchestrator.ts`'s constant; it now imports the same builder instead of the two silently drifting apart over time. ## Verification - `turbo typecheck --filter=edumatch` — clean - `pnpm --filter edumatch test` — 199 passed, 5 new covering: no hint → question-only instruction; a locale hint → named-language fallback mentioning "too short or ambiguous"; the hint losing to a clearly-identifiable different language in the text; every base language maps to a real name (not `undefined`); an unrecognised locale string doesn't throw - Updated the existing inquiries-route test's assertion to the new 3-argument `orchestrateResponse` call shape **Not verified against a live model call** — this is a prompt-text change, not orchestration logic, so I didn't spend a real Anthropic/OpenAI call confirming the model actually follows the new instruction reliably. Worth trying the exact repro ("algebera II" on a Dutch-locale session) once this is live. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

the-verscienta
body:
Closes #522.

## Problem

`content_editor_live.ex` loads `@tags` once in `mount/3` and never refreshes it, but `record.tags` **is** refreshed (every autosave's `fetch!`). So a tag created and attached after mount — a collaborator, a second tab — ends up in `record.tags` but not `@tags`. `tag_sections/5` built every section (including the "Also attached" rescue) from `@tags` alone, so that tag rendered **no checkbox**.

Tags save through `manage_relationship(:tag_ids, :tags, type: :append_and_remove)`, so a checkbox that isn't rendered isn't submitted — and the next save reads its absence as "detach me", silently dropping the link.

## Fix

Render the picker from the **union** of `@tags` and `record.tags` (deduped by id, org order preserved). Both the sections and the empty-state guard key on that union now, so every attached tag always has a checked control — whatever the mount-time list happened to know.

## Test

New `editor_live_test` case: mount before any tag exists, attach a tag after mount (seeded directly into the `Tagging` join so it doesn't bump the optimistic `lock_version` and conflict the editor's autosave), then an autosave re-fetches `record.tags` while `@tags` stays empty. The latecomer now renders checked, and a title-only save keeps the link. Verified it fails without the fix; all 153 editor-live tests pass.

Full local gate green (format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict, sobelow, gettext drift, dialyzer MIX_ENV=test).

author: pablof7z-agent
body:
Closes #1301.

## What the issue asked, and what the evidence changed

#1301 asked for a `parent` spelling on **both** `create_group()` and `GroupMetadataEdit`, and flagged one caveat: that `parent` is "not in NIP-29 core; it is nostr-protocol/nips#2319, still a proposal."

Both halves of that turned out to be wrong, in opposite directions, and the correction is the whole design.

### 1. nostr-protocol/nips#2319 is MERGED

It merged on **2026-07-16** (`merged_at: 2026-07-16T00:10:48Z`), three weeks before #1301 was filed. NIP-29 now carries a `Subgroups` section defining `parent` and `child`. So `parent` is protocol, not a proposal, and not relay29 jargon — the opposite of the `public`/`open` case #1287 handled, where the row genuinely came from the reference relay's parser rather than the spec.

This also means the #1287 change-log line — *"nostr-protocol/nips#2319 is a proposed extension rather than NIP-29 proper"* — was already false when written. The change log is append-only history and is **not** edited; the correction lives in this entry and in the code.

### 2. The spec and the only implementation disagree about which KIND carries it

NIP-29's prose puts parenting on **kind:9002** and never mentions kind:9007:

> Parenting and promotion to root are triggered by a `kind:9002` (`edit-metadata`) event from an authorized admin with the desired `parent` value (or no `parent` tag to detach)

The relay both consumer applications actually use does the exact opposite. Probed live against `wss://nip29.f7z.io` on 2026-08-05:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| kind:9007 with `["parent", P]` | **honoured** — child's relay-authored kind:39000 comes back with `["parent", P]`, and P's own kind:39000 gains `["child", C]` |
| kind:9007 with a nonexistent parent | refused: `restricted: parent group 'X' doesn't exist` |
| kind:9007 where signer is not a parent admin | refused: `restricted: must be an admin of the parent group` |
| kind:9002 with `["name", …]` + `["parent", P2]` | accepted, name changed, **parent unchanged** — the row is ignored |
| kind:9002 with `["parent", P2]` alone | refused: `invalid moderation action: missing metadata tags` |
| kind:9002 with `["name", …]` and no `parent` | parent **preserved**, not detached — diverging from the spec's "Absence of the `parent` tag makes the group a root" |

That last rejection is relay29's own error string for a 9002 in which it recognised no field. `relay29/moderation_actions.go` reads `name`, `picture`, `about`, `public`/`private` and `open`/`closed`, and a `grep` for `parent`/`child`/`subgroup` across the whole reference implementation returns **nothing**.

## The decision: creation only

`parent` goes on `nmp_nip29::create_group(parent: Option<&str>)` and **not** on `GroupMetadataEdit`.

Composing it into a 9002 would emit a row that takes no effect while reading as though it had — precisely the reason #1287 excluded `banner` and `livekit`. It is worse here than there: an app would believe it had moved a group under a new parent when the relay had left it exactly where it was. On the one relay that implements subgroups a group's parent cannot be restated after creation at all, which is what makes it identity rather than mutable metadata.

The divergence is **recorded, not absorbed** — in `crates/nmp-nip29/src/operations.rs` on `create_group` (the probe, verbatim relay errors included) and on `GroupMetadataEdit` (why the field is absent), so nobody later mistakes the placement for what the spec says. If a relay ever honours `parent` on a 9002, the field is a one-line addition the day a falsifier exists for it.

Nothing is named that the protocol lacks: `parent` is NIP-29's own row name, and `Option<&str>` carries the parent's group id — NIP-29's `d` value, a relay-scoped string, never an `naddr` and never a key.

## Consumer evidence

mosaico `b4f31476`, `src/fabric/nip29/lifecycle.rs` — a module whose own doc says it exists for exactly this:

> Exactly ONE draft is left that NMP cannot express:
> * **`parent`.** Subgroups per nostr-protocol/nips#2319 …
> `parent` is filed as pablof7z/nmp#1301; when it lands, this module is deleted rather than shrunk.

```rust
pub fn group_create_subgroup(parent_h: &str) -> Result<nmp::EventBuilder> {
    Ok(nmp_nip29::create_group().tag(tag(&["parent", parent_h])?))
}
```

Its sibling `group_lock_closed_with_parent` hand-writes `["parent", …]` onto a **kind:9002**. The probe above shows that row has never done anything; the 9007 was doing all the work. So mosaico deletes both, not one — and the 9002 half was a silent no-op it believed in.

## Red, then green

Red — the door did not exist (`cargo test -p nmp-nip29`):

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 0 arguments but 1 argument was supplied
   --> crates/nmp-nip29/src/operations.rs:476:18
    |
476 |             rows(create_group(Some("darkroom"))),
    |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^ -------------------------------- unexpected argument of type `std::option::Option<&str>`
    |
note: function defined here
   --> crates/nmp-nip29/src/operations.rs:220:8
    |
220 | pub fn create_group() -> EventBuilder {
    |        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
error: could not compile `nmp-nip29` (lib test) due to 5 previous errors
```

Green:

```
test operations::tests::create_group_at_the_root_is_kind_9007_with_no_tag_at_all ... ok
test operations::tests::create_group_under_a_parent_carries_the_parent_row_on_the_create ... ok
test operations::tests::the_parent_row_carries_the_group_id_verbatim ... ok
test operations::tests::a_metadata_edit_never_composes_a_parent_row ... ok
test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

## Gates RUN on this head

`cargo test -p nmp-parity` (RUN — this changes an FFI method signature), `cargo test -p nmp-nip29 -p nmp -p nmp-ffi -p nmp-bdd` (all green), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `scripts/check-nip29-operation-catalogue.sh`, `scripts/check-nip29-ownership.sh`, `scripts/check-nip29-kind-blindness.sh`, `scripts/check-nip29-read-door.sh`, `scripts/check-sdk-parity.sh`, `scripts/check-no-compatibility-surface.sh`, `scripts/check-bdd-file-length.sh`, the behavior-traceability `check` (under the pinned `nightly-2026-07-07`), `swift build` + `swift test` (172 tests, 0 failures), and `./gradlew compileKotlin test` under JDK 17 (BUILD SUCCESSFUL).

Projection set computed on this head with `SURFACE_BASE_REF=origin/master scripts/check-surface-governance.sh --print-projections`: `ffi,kotlin,rust,swift`. `docs/surface/nmp-facade.txt` measured from the regenerated file at **28997** lines, under the 30000 cap.

## No backwards compatibility

The zero-argument `create_group()` is **DELETED** in the same change on every surface — no alias, no overload, no default-argument bridge in Rust. Every caller moves in this PR: `nmp::nip29::Group::create_group`, `FfiGroup::create_group`, `NMPGroup.createGroup`, the Kotlin equivalent, and the Rust/Swift/Kotlin tests. Swift and Kotlin take `parent` as a defaulted optional because that is those languages' ordinary spelling for an optional argument, not a compatibility shim — the Rust and FFI signatures require it explicitly.

# Summary

Test files under `packages/**` were typechecked by nothing. A `@ts-expect-error`, a type-level lock, or any other compile-time assertion written in one was **inert** — it neither failed when the guarded condition broke nor reported an unused directive. It read like a check and enforced nothing.

Found twice by negative control, independently, two weeks apart (mt#3066 → this task; mt#3569 / PR #2654 → mt#3763, now closed and subsumed here).

Planning also falsified a premise both specs carried: package **source** was NOT fully covered either. `src/` imports package subpaths (`@minsky/domain/transcripts/credential-scrubber`), never the barrels, so anything reachable only through a barrel export was in no program. `tsgo --listFiles` on the root project lists 628 of `packages/domain/src`'s 725 non-test files — **97 were uncovered**, one of them (`metadata-extraction-pipeline.ts`) carrying a real type error that root `tsgo --noEmit` reported as exit 0.

# Key Changes

**Coverage (2 lines of mechanism).** `packages/domain/package.json` and `packages/shared/package.json` each gain a `typecheck` script. That is the whole change: `validate_typecheck`'s discovery (`src/adapters/shared/commands/validate.ts`) already walks the root `package.json` `workspaces` globs and picks up every workspace that BOTH declares a `typecheck` script AND has its own `tsconfig.json` — `packages/*` was already in the globs and both package tsconfigs already existed with `include: ["src/**/*"]`. The only missing piece was the script, which is exactly what that mechanism was designed to key on ("a future workspace that adds its own typecheck is covered with no code change", mt#2256).

Considered and rejected: adding `packages` to the root `tsconfig.json` `include` (merges ~1,200 files into the root program under root options, diverging from the per-project convention every sibling tree follows), and a standalone `tsconfig.packages.json` (duplicates two tsconfigs that already exist with the right `include`). The chosen option matches the convention mt#3088 set and mt#3498 just reused one directory over.

**CI.** Root `typecheck:packages` script + a `Type check (packages)` step with `if: always()`, shaped like the existing reviewer step.

**Paydown: all 213 errors across 50 files, none suppressed.** No `@ts-nocheck`, no `@ts-ignore` added, no compiler options widened, no `include` narrowed. `packages/shared` was already clean (0).

Beyond mechanical `ConversationId` brand casts, the previously-unchecked files contained real defects:

- **5 dangling identifiers.** `notify/telegram-transport.test.ts` referenced an undefined `FetchFn` (TS2304 x5) — a type the module under test *exports*, which the test simply never imported. Same bug class as mt#3471's `SCOPE_WARNING`, which reached production behavior and motivated mt#3498.
- **Two tests that could not fail.** `tasks/multi-backend-unavailable.test.ts` and `tasks/taskService.test.ts` obtained their "error" via `.catch((e) => e as Error)`, so a call that unexpectedly **resolved** flowed through as the error object and the assertions ran against a `Task`. Replaced with `.then(expectedRejection, ...)`, whose fulfilled arm throws.
- **An assertion on a state that does not exist.** `ask/state-counts-provider.test.ts` asserted on an AskState `"resolved"`; the enum has no such member (terminal success is `"closed"`). It passed only because the bogus key rode along on an object spread.
- **An inert option.** `compile/targets/claude-md.test.ts` passed `check: true` to `target.compile(...)`; `check` is not a `MinskyTargetOptions` field and the target never reads it. Removed — `perRuleViolations` is returned unconditionally, so nothing asserted changed.
- **Fixtures drifted behind their schemas:** `FakeRow` seeds missing the mt#3278 ingest-failure columns (6 sites), `PresenceClaimRecord` missing the mt#2284 columns, `AskRecord` missing `projectId`/`severity`/`principalPagedAt`, `MinskyCompileFsDeps` missing `chmod`, `SpawnsPipelineRunResult`/`ToolCallProjectionRunResult` missing newer counters.
- **Two wrong type declarations.** `matchesProjectFilter` was annotated `: boolean` while returning a row predicate — its own caller already branched on `typeof === "function"`. And `metadata-extraction-pipeline.ts` (source) annotated a selected *branded* column as `string`, which made its own `eq(...)` reject the value it had just read.

Where an `expect(x[0].y)` became `x[0]?.y` I checked whether the comparison could then pass vacuously (two `undefined`s compare equal); where it could, a presence guard was added instead of an optional chain.

**One source type narrowed for mockability.** `createTimeoutFetch`'s `baseFetch` parameter is now `FetchLike` (fetch's call signature) rather than `typeof fetch`, which under bun-types carries `preconnect` and is unsatisfiable by any stub. Same narrowing mt#3498 applied to the reviewer's `alert-sink.ts`, and the pattern `notify/telegram-transport.ts` already documented in a comment. The RETURN type stays `typeof fetch` — callers hand it to Octokit's `request.fetch`, which demands the full global shape.

# Testing

Execution evidence:

- **Success criterion 1 — how many compile-time assertions were inert, and did any guard a broken invariant.** Audited across `packages/**`:
  ```
  $ grep -rl '@ts-expect-error' --include='*.test.ts' packages/ | wc -l     →  5 files
  $ grep -rho '@ts-expect-error' --include='*.test.ts' packages/ | wc -l    → 13 directives
  $ grep -rho '@ts-ignore'       --include='*.test.ts' packages/ | wc -l    →  0
  $ grep -rn  'AssertNotAssignable\|type Assert' --include='*.test.ts' packages/ | wc -l → 0
  ```
  Files: `transcripts/hook-preamble-matcher.test.ts`, `storage/schemas/subagent-invocations-schema.test.ts`, `ids.test.ts`, `ai/embedding-service-openai.test.ts`, `credentials/schema-derived.test.ts`. **13 directives were inert; none was guarding a broken invariant** — with coverage on, the suite typechecks clean, and an `@ts-expect-error` whose guarded condition no longer errors would itself raise `TS2578`. That inference is only load-bearing because the check can now fail, which the negative control below establishes independently.

- **Success criterion 2 / criterion 5 — coverage exists and is legible from the tool output.** `validate_typecheck`, session workspace, no `workspace` arg:
  ```
  errorCount: 0, status: "pass"
  workspaces: [".", "packages/domain", "packages/shared", "services/reviewer",
               "src/cockpit/web", "tsconfig.hooks.json", "tsconfig.scripts.json"]
  ```
  `packages/domain` and `packages/shared` are new entries. CI step: `Type check (packages)` running `bun run typecheck:packages`, alongside the existing `typecheck:hooks` / `typecheck:scripts` steps.

- **Success criterion 4 — coverage proven by negative control, not by a passing run:**
  ```
  $ printf '\n// @ts-expect-error - deliberately UNUSED directive\nconst p: string = "x";\nvoid p;\n' >> packages/domain/src/ids.test.ts
  $ bun run typecheck:packages
  packages/domain/src/ids.test.ts(62,1): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
  EXIT=2
  # validate_typecheck attributed it to the right workspace:
  #   { workspace: "packages/domain", file: "packages/domain/src/ids.test.ts",
  #     line: 62, code: "TS2578" }
  $ # probe removed:
  $ bun run typecheck:packages   ->  EXIT=0
  ```
  This is precisely the error that was invisible before this PR.

- **The mt#3763 case specifically** (its SC2, subsumed here): the same probe in `packages/domain/src/credentials/schema-derived.test.ts` -> `EXIT=2`, `TS2578` at line 198; removed -> `EXIT=0`.

- **Success criterion 3 — errors fixed, with the count recorded rather than discovered mid-PR:** 213 errors / 50 files in `packages/domain` (49 test files + 1 source file), 0 in `packages/shared`. The planning-time probe and the implementation-time count matched exactly. None deferred; full breakdown in the task spec's `## Measured cost` and `## O

body:
## Goal

Implement the smallest dependency-closed runtime-proof slice mined from **New Ideas 4-15-26(2).pdf**: schema-bound finite outcomes, fixture-driven soil-moisture evaluation, replay determinism, and explicit trust-boundary tests.

## Status

- **CONFIRMED base:** `main@739a84ffaae97f2ab61306c079c29aae3197f5a7`
- **CONFIRMED head:** `418cb82f0a7bf51010e20013ddfe9d3f84231356`
- **PROPOSED implementation:** fixture-only runtime proof; no production API route or source activation
- **Review state:** draft / human review pending

## Evidence-led adaptation

The idea packet proposes a real soil-moisture runtime layer and schema-valid `ANSWER | ABSTAIN | DENY | ERROR` envelopes. Current repository evidence narrows that proposal: the existing soil-moisture profile is explicitly `fixture_only`, `not_released`, and `promotion_eligible: false`. This PR therefore **never emits `ANSWER` for the current fixtures**. A validator-clean fixture returns `ABSTAIN` until a separate governed evidence, policy, review, and release path exists.

## Changes

- adds a deterministic, no-I/O `RuntimeResponseEnvelope` candidate builder under `packages/envelopes/`;
- exports only the reviewed builder, finite-outcome set, evidence-kind set, and safe local error type;
- validates the exact closed runtime-envelope and EvidenceRef shapes in package tests;
- adds a test-only soil-moisture mapper over the existing repository validator and fixtures;
- proves:
  - clean fixture -> `ABSTAIN` (`SOIL_MOISTURE_FIXTURE_NOT_RELEASED`),
  - missing support -> `ABSTAIN`,
  - duplicate/semantic failure -> `DENY`,
  - malformed non-object input -> `ERROR`,
  - identical inputs and injected time -> identical output,
  - no readings, station IDs, receipt internals, proof, catalog, promotion, release, or publication objects leak outward;
- adds a path-scoped, no-network runtime-proof workflow;
- emits a generated authoring receipt with byte hashes and pending-review state.

## Directory Rules basis

ADR-0029 is accepted and makes Directory Rules v2 the placement authority. The slice follows its responsibility routing:

- reusable side-effect-free candidate code -> `packages/envelopes/`;
- executable conformance/runtime-proof checks -> `tests/`;
- CI orchestration -> `.github/workflows/`;
- authoring accountability -> `data/receipts/generated/`.

No root, schema home, policy home, evidence home, release home, or publication path is created.

## Validation

Focused deterministic validation run locally against the exact authored files:

```text
python -m pytest \
  tests/packages/envelopes/test_runtime_response_candidate.py \
  tests/runtime_proof/domains/soil/soil_moisture/test_runtime_mapper.py \
  -q --strict-config --strict-markers

23 passed
```

All four finite outcomes produced by the generic builder validate against the current closed `RuntimeResponseEnvelope` and `EvidenceRef` schemas. The soil profile itself deliberately exercises only `ABSTAIN`, `DENY`, and `ERROR` under current fixture/release state.

**NEEDS VERIFICATION:** exact-head hosted workflow results after GitHub schedules them.

## Trust boundary

A green result proves only deterministic local construction and synthetic-fixture mapping. It does **not** establish live source correctness, EvidenceBundle resolution, policy allow, human review, promotion readiness, release, deployment, publication, alert authority, or public-use safety.

This PR does not add a public route, network call, source connector, model call, promotion decision, release manifest, or published artifact.

## Rollback

Before merge: close this draft PR and delete the feature branch. After an authorized merge: revert commit `418cb82f0a7bf51010e20013ddfe9d3f84231356`. The change contains no data migration, source activation, release state, or external side effect.

## Reviewer disposition

**HOLD as draft** until exact-head hosted checks complete and a reviewer confirms that the current proposed runtime-envelope profile is the intended profile for this bounded helper. Do not merge, release, deploy, promote, or publish from this PR.

author: jacobosanchez
body:
Works through [#446](https://github.com/JacoboSanchez/volley-overlay-control/issues/446), one commit per item, plus seven commits fixing review findings.

**The item worth a careful read is §5** — it replaces polling with a push protocol, so it is the only part that introduces new concurrency. Everything else is bundling, types and assets.

## What changed

| § | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Route-level code splitting + `manualChunks` | Router chunk **128 kB → 16.8 kB** raw |
| 2 | `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` | Type/import annotations only, no runtime diff |
| 3 | 14 `oid!` assertions | Gone — `handleAction` narrows once |
| 4 | Silent `catch` on customization read-back | Surfaces an error toast |
| 5 | **Audit log over the WebSocket instead of polling** | **0** `/audit` requests while scoring (was ~150–200 per match) |
| 6 | `role="button"` → native `<button>`; Material Icons subset | Font **125 kB → 5 kB** |

Also fixes the Trivy gate, which was **already failing on `main`**: the two HIGH findings are `msgpack` and `setuptools` vendored inside pip, so the runtime image no longer ships pip.

## §5 in one paragraph

Undo is tombstone-based, so a pop retroactively hides a record a client is already showing — an append-only stream would leave the cancelled chip on screen forever. Hence two messages: `audit_append` carries the new row, `audit_invalidate` means "re-read". Every mutation that changes how existing records read (pop, tombstone, restore, clear, delete) sends invalidate, and rotation downgrades an append to one. Each message carries the log's version counter, so a client applies a record only when it is exactly one ahead and re-reads on any other gap. `GET /audit` stays authoritative — a dropped frame costs one extra fetch, never a wrong history.

## Review

Codex raised **seven P2 findings across five rounds; all seven were correct** and are fixed here. Five were in the §5 protocol, two in the §1 splitting — the two items that introduced new runtime behaviour. §2 and the font work drew nothing.

Six were defects. The seventh is the one worth reading: it caught a test that asserted the *weaker* version of what its own comment claimed (the error boundary's nav was mounted but inert, and the test only checked it was mounted). Each fix ships with a test verified to fail without it.

The remaining gap is stated plainly rather than papered over: these races live in the seam between the HTTP read, the socket and the log lock, and per-case tests are a weak instrument there. A property test over "the client's view converges to the server's log" would have found all five at once — tracked separately rather than bolted on here.

## Verification

Beyond CI, §5 and §6 were driven against the real app with Playwright, because neither `tsc` nor a green suite can tell a font that loads from one that also draws, or a socket that connects from one that carries the right rows:

- Board load issues 2 `GET /audit` (mount + socket-open resync); scoring 3 points issues **0**; chips arrive as `audit_append`; undo pushes `audit_invalidate` and the chip disappears; a board loading while another client scores still shows that chip.
- Every icon on the board and in the config panel lays out as a 20–32 px glyph. An earlier subset that used the wrong OpenType feature tag loaded fine and rendered every icon as its own name at 100–544 px wide — caught only by driving the browser.

Docs: `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`, WebSocket protocol in `FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT.md`, OpenAPI contract regenerated.

Closes #446

author: cthach
body: Part of https://github.com/gravitational/core/issues/103. As of [RFD 0237 - Sub CA support](https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/blob/master/rfd/0237-sub-ca-support.md), overrides configured via [workload overrides](https://github.com/gravitational/teleport/blob/master/rfd/0194-spiffe-x509-override.md) (`workload_identity_x509_issuer_override` resources) are being deprecated in favor of the new sub-CA overrides (`cert_authority_override` resources). This change makes it so that just before an SVID is signed, the new sub-CA override resolver is checked first before falling back to the legacy workload override system. Whether both systems should interoperate and exactly how the migration will happen is still TBD. That being said, this change allows us to continue development on `master`, allowing us to activate both paths for testing, until those decisions have been made. Once they have been decided, this code will likely change, but until then, onward! 😜 --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

- Add the `moduleNameMapper` for `.js` → `.ts` rewriting to the unit Jest config in `apps/api/package.json` — a handler unit spec that injects `PrismaService` pulls the generated Prisma client into the module graph and otherwise fails to load with `Cannot find module './internal/class.js'`, even when every Prisma call is mocked.

author: alltomatos
body:
## Resumo
- Assistants passam a transcrever audio recebido via AiGateway configurado (`/audio/transcriptions`, OpenAI-compatible) e opcionalmente respondem com nota de voz sintetizada (`/audio/speech`).
- Novos settings por Assistant: `acceptsAudio` (entende audio) e `respondsWithAudio` (responde em audio); quando audio nao e aceito, o Assistant responde com mensagem fixa explicando a limitacao.
- `AiGateway` ganha `TranscriptionModel`/`SpeechModel` dedicados — nem todo gateway credencia o mesmo nome de modelo pra chat e pra audio (confirmado ao vivo: `whisper-1` cru falhou, `openrouter/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` funcionou).
- Novo pacote `internal/mediawait` correlaciona de forma sincrona o download assincrono de midia via AMQP (`media.download` -> `message.media`), permitindo que `AssistantRuntime.Execute` aguarde o audio antes de transcrever.
- Resposta em audio usa `mediaData` (base64) via AMQP direto pro engine-go — sem depender de URL publica.

## Limitacoes conhecidas

author: kirinnee
body:
Three things: the conflict that shipped into the doctrine document, the gate that would have caught it,
and the warning at the switch. Everything else that was once on this branch is on `main` already (#296,
#299) and has been dropped rather than re-applied.

## 1. `docs/grants.md` had a live conflict on `main` — resolved, not silenced

    line  59   <<<<<<< HEAD
    line  66   =======
    line 143   > > > > > > > 141154ed …      (treefmt's rewrite of `>>>>>>>`)

So both versions of the permissive-by-default section were published, and the resurrected heading
("the password is the layer") sat directly above the paragraph that refutes it ("**The primary security
layer is locality, not the password.**"). A reader could not tell which was current — the same defect as
the stacked comments this unit has been hunting, in the document that argues against them.

Resolved to the final text: the LOCALITY section is contiguous again with its two body paragraphs moved
up under its own opening, and the superseded heading and paragraph are deleted. `### pairing is the one
that produces credentials` and `## Before you add capability seven` follow it, which is where they read
correctly anyway.

**Two more artefacts of the same resolution**, found by reading the whole file rather than the markers:

- the H1 title had a "Where it lives" table row glued to its front with no newline — the doc rendered
  with **no title** and a stray table row at the top;
- that row was the intended *update* to the change-record row (`read by fy daemon config history`), which
  never reached the table it belonged to. Applied there, with the command verified to exist first
  (`packages/cli/src/lib/grants/commands.ts:58`), per this section's own rule.

`handover.md:219` carried a laundered marker from another unit. Removed.

## 2. The gate: `scripts/validate/conflict-markers.sh` (`a-conflict-markers`)

Refuses every marker shape in any tracked file:

| shape                             | why it survived until now                                            |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<<<<<<< HEAD`                    | an ordinary paragraph line to a Markdown formatter — nothing to fix   |
| `=======`                         | **already valid Markdown**: a setext H1 underline, so it renders as intended structure |
| `>>>>>>> <sha>`                   | treefmt rewrites it to `> > > > > > > <sha>`, a legal nested blockquote |

All four shapes (including the laundered one) were asserted to fail red before this landed; the script
runs on every file and scans the whole tree, because a marker reaches `main` through the file nobody was
looking at. `--fixed-strings` / `git grep -F` throughout, since `rg -r` is `--replace`.

**Do not simplify the pattern list.** Measured against the shipped file on `main` — my count, matching
temperance's independently:

| what you grep for                            | artefacts it finds                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| the shape somebody reports — raw `>>>>>>>`   | **0 of 3** — it had already been laundered    |
| all three raw markers                        | 2 of 3 — misses the laundered one             |
| this gate's list                             | 3 of 3                                        |

So the laundered patterns are not belt-and-braces on the raw ones: in a repository that formats every file
on commit they are the only thing that still matches, and a raw-marker-only gate is no cover at all for the
artefact most likely to survive review. It is also why line 143 was found by reading rather than grepping.

**The proof the gate is needed is this PR's own history:** the previous head had 22/22 checks green with
two markers still in the file. Registered in `nix/pre-commit.nix` and documented in
`docs/standards/contracts/README.md`, which also records why this is the one contract about every file
rather than a relationship between several: no type and no test can own it, because the artefact it
refuses is not code.

## 3. The warning at the switch (unchanged from the previous review)

The remote turn-off warning for `pairing` now says it also disables this device's own revoke, so revoke
the stolen device FIRST. `COARSE_SWITCH_ALSO_STOPS` is keyed per capability; `fleet` is asserted to gain
no ordering advice it cannot use; doctrine item 2 cites the constant so the doc and the control cannot
drift.

`docs/grants.md` also gains the tool-lies table this unit produced — `rg -r` rewriting output,
`--contains` answering ancestry rather than shipment, and treefmt laundering a marker — under one lesson:
**a tool answering is not a tool agreeing.**

## Verification

`task lint` green (including the new script run directly, and treefmt on the reflowed tables).
`task test:gate:unit` green with the ledger at 100% — the tier this change lives in. The int gate is
untouched by a docs-and-script diff; CI covers it.

author: larspohlmann
body:
Closes #290

## What was wrong

Subscribing to `reddit.com/r/Bitwig` stored the right feed
(`https://www.reddit.com/r/Bitwig/.rss`) and then showed nothing, with no error
anywhere.

Reddit rations that endpoint to roughly **one request per minute per address**
(measured: 200 at t=20 s and t=80 s, 429 at 0/40/60/100 s — and a Chrome UA got
a 429 seconds after our own UA got a 200, so it is the address, not the client).
Subscribing spends the budget: the page fetch plus the six probes from #283 are
seven requests in one burst. A new feed is due immediately, so the refresh that
follows draws a 429, ingests nothing, and `recordFailure()` parks a perfectly
healthy feed as `erroring` with a one-to-two-hour backoff.

## What changes

**1. The subscribe stores the document discovery already read.** Discovery has
to parse the feed to know it found one; it now carries that document
(`DiscoveredFeed`) and `FirstFetchRecorder` writes it as the feed's first fetch.
A new subscription arrives with its entries, its title and a normal schedule —
and the second request to the same URL, the one that drew the 429, never
happens. This applies to every feed, not just Reddit's: no new subscription is
empty until the first refresh any more.

Only for a feed nobody has fetched yet. A shared row somebody else already
refreshed keeps its own history and schedule.

**2. A 429 is its own answer.** `FeedThrottledException` carries `Retry-After`
(delay or date), and `FeedScheduler::recordThrottled()` sets only *when to ask
again* — clamped to [1 min, 24 h], defaulting to 15 minutes when the site named
nothing. No failure counted, no `erroring` status, no backoff growth, and
`lastFetchedAt` untouched so the manual refresh's 5-minute cooldown still
measures the last time content actually arrived. The refresh reports the run as
not having updated that feed; the feed's own health is left alone.

**3. A host that just said "slow down" is not probed** for six more paths.

## Collateral

`SubscriptionService` went past the parameter budget with the recorder
(`composer md` failed on it), so the row mechanics — cap, shared feed row,
duplicate check, tag positions — moved into `SubscriptionCreator`, leaving the
service with the decision it makes: what is there to subscribe to, and what do
we already know about it. The create response now reports the real unread count,
which used to be hardcoded 0 on the grounds that a new feed had no entries yet.

## Verified

- `reddit.com/r/Bitwig` posted to the running stack returns
  `title: "Bitwig"`, `siteUrl`, `lastFetchedAt` set — and the feed holds **25
  entries** immediately, `unreadCount: 25` in the create response itself. One
  request to reddit.com, not two. (Throwaway subscription deleted again.)
- Backend 1376 tests green on SQLite and MySQL (2 skipped on MySQL);
  `composer check` and `composer md` clean; frontend `npm run check` green.
- PhpStorm inspections were not run — the MCP server is not connected in this
  session.

## The /simplify round

Four reviewers went over the diff; the findings were worth the pass.

- **The client was handing the saved request straight back.** `onAddFeed()`
  ran a `feedId`-scoped refresh, and that scope ignores the schedule by design
  — so the second request to the same host still happened, which is the pair
  that draws the 429. It now skips the refresh when the subscription arrived
  with `lastFetchedAt` set.
- **`DiscoveredFeed` carries the ETag and Last-Modified** it was already
  holding, so a seeded feed's next poll can be a conditional GET.
- **The unread count is no longer queried.** `FirstFetchRecorder` returns what
  it ingested; the previous version ran an aggregate over every entry of every
  feed the user has, to learn a number the ingest already knew.
- **`FeedThrottledException` is a sibling, not a subclass.**
  `FeedUnreachableException` keeps its `final`, discovery catches the throttle
  directly, and 429 left `BLOCKED_STATUSES` instead of being decided twice.
- **`throttled` is its own discovery reason and its own refresh count.** The
  dialog asks the user to wait rather than declaring the site closed, and a
  rationed feed no longer hides inside `failed` — the number this bug was
  noticed by now moves when it happens.
- **`recordThrottled` writes one field**, and with no `Retry-After` it waits
  the feed's own cadence rather than polling a daily feed every 15 minutes.
- **`ResponseClassifier` takes its clock by injection**, wired to the
  pipeline's database clock (the tier that runs an hour fast is the one
  computing a `Retry-After` date), and pinned by `RefreshClockWiringTest`.
- Test scaffolding for the classifier and the scheduler became data providers.

Deliberately not done: unifying `SubscriptionCreator` with `BulkSubscriber`
(pre-existing duplication, and the batch defers every flush — a change of its
own), and carrying the scraped document the way `directFeed` now carries the
parsed one.

## Still open

The reason this was invisible: the UI renders neither `status: 'erroring'` nor
the last error message. Left for its own ticket, as noted in #290.

author: amorey
body:
## Summary

Dropping the last live `depends_on` edge to a deletion-pending target is one of the routes out of a RESTRICT-blocked collect, and the only one that signalled nothing: an edge write bumps no `resource_version` and appends no write-log entry, so no cursor can see it. The target waited for the GC sweeper's next tick — 30s by default, latency only, since the sweep always finds it.

`TODO.md` carried a deferred fix for this: a monotonic edge epoch bumped by `EdgesAdd`/`EdgesDelete`. It doesn't work. A counter is read on a driver's own schedule, so it can let a tick *skip* work but never make one arrive sooner, and it carries no identity to enqueue. Latency needs a wake. So this takes the shape the sibling routes already use — the write reports what it changed, and the caller pushes at commit.

## Key Changes

- **`EdgesDelete` returns an `EdgesDeleteResult`** (`{To GroupKind, Unblocked bool}`), beside `EdgesAddResult`. `Unblocked` is three facts in one field, because only their conjunction is ever read: an edge was really removed (`RowsAffected`, bounding the push to once per edge), the target is deletion-pending (a live one was never blocked, and `requeueNow` bypasses the re-enqueue floor), and the source is *not* (`EdgesHasIncoming` discounts an edge from a deletion-pending source, so a finalizing dependent releasing its refs lifts nothing — the common case, not an exotic one).
- **`DependenciesDelete` pushes the target** with `signalRequeueNow` when the store reports `Unblocked`, routed by `res.To` since edges are cross-kind. `AfterCommit`'s tenth user. It stays a probe — no last-referrer check — and `gcCollect` re-checks the block.
- **Two statements in the store, no transaction of their own.** The `DELETE`, then a second query only when something was removed. Wrapping them would hold the sole connection across a `BEGIN`…`COMMIT` on a path a controller walks every pass, to buy an atomicity the gap doesn't need: every way the second query can miss its rows is benign, and nothing un-deletes a row.
- **Tests**: five over the gates and cross-kind routing, four store-level, and an integration pair (with and without the push). Each cycle was verified red first; stubbing out the push fails 4 of the 7 new tests.
- **Docs**: new ADR + index entry; `CLAUDE.md` (`AfterCommit` ten users, GC bullet); `reconcile-triggers.md` (seventh push path, case 11 rewritten); `TODO.md`; `README.md`; the two sibling ADRs that asserted this route was open.

**Breaking**: `EdgesDelete`'s signature changes, and `Store` is a public alias — hence `feat(edges)!`.

**Still open, disclosed not fixed**: a *fourth* exit from the same block. Marking the last live referrer deletion-pending lifts it through that same discount, and `signalDeletionRequested` enqueues only the object it marked, so that target waits for the sweep. It has a `TODO.md` entry with the fix shape, and case 11 now names it rather than claiming every route pushes.

## Checklist

- [x] Add the correct emoji to the PR title
- [x] Related issue linked above, if any — none
- [x] Commit messages use [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org) format
- [x] Changes are minimal and focused

author: franciscomateusvg
body:
## Summary
- add the Banco Inter Pix webhook pipeline with durable archive/deduplication
- treat the unsigned callback payload only as a routing hint, then verify every charge/refund against Inter before dispatch
- mount both the registered callback path and Inter's delivery-time `/pix` suffix in the production Hono composition root
- document the complete wire contract in OpenAPI 3.1

## Runtime contract changes
- **New endpoints** — unauthenticated `POST /api/webhooks/inter/pix` and `POST /api/webhooks/inter/pix/pix`.
  - The payload is not trusted as evidence of payment state because Banco Inter does not sign this callback.
  - Every charge is re-queried through `PixCobrancaProvider.consultarCobranca`; dispatch occurs only for `concluida` with exact txid/e2e/amount binding.
  - Every refund is re-queried through `consultarDevolucao`; the B3 route archives verified refunds but does not mutate financial state until B6 provides the provider-free bookkeeping callback.
- **Limits** — streamed body cap of 256 KiB and durable PostgreSQL rate limit of 600 requests/minute per hashed trusted client IP.
- **Archive semantics** — every accepted item is durably archived and deduplicated; categorical outcomes only, with no webhook/provider PII in logs or stored processing errors.
- **Contract** — `docs/api/inter-pix-webhook.openapi.yaml` documents request/response schemas, errors, examples, auth posture, and rate-limit tier.

## Deviation from spec
The spec text named the existing generic payment/refund finalizers. Those finalizers initiate provider actions: the payment finalizer consults the currently configured generic provider (Stripe today), and the refund finalizer starts a refund. Calling either after an authoritative Inter re-query could contact the wrong provider or double-refund.

This implementation adds provider-free, verified-result finalizer seams. They accept only an already-verified transaction and enforce exact local identity, amount, status, and replay invariants. Charge dispatch uses that seam now. Refund bookkeeping remains intentionally inert until B6 supplies its provider-free callback; B3 still archives, deduplicates, and authoritatively re-queries every refund event.

## Verification
- focused pipeline/route/finalizer/PostgreSQL suite: 4 files, 35 tests passed
- independent real PostgreSQL archive integration: 12 tests passed
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir apps/eunenem-server typecheck`
- `pnpm --dir apps/eunenem-server build`
- `pnpm check:server-router-resolution` — 15/15
- full substantive `pnpm check`: lint, structure, dependency-cruiser, typechecks, codegen/barrel/router checks, examples, 174 test files / 2270 tests passed; final inherited `.husky/pre-push` absence is unchanged on canonical staging

## QA
Draft pending Izzy's independent exact-SHA verification.


## QA HOLD remediation
Head `9ced66d15eaa4449eb461046909f14094e004975` closes the concurrent failed-row retry race found by Izzy:
- added a durable, single-statement failed-to-in-flight compare-and-set (`UPDATE ... WHERE processed_at IS NULL AND processing_error IS NOT NULL RETURNING id`)
- only the successful claimant may re-query or dispatch; competing redeliveries return as duplicates
- guarded `markFailed` so a stale failure cannot produce an incoherent terminal row with both `processed_at` and `processing_error`
- added shared Memory/PostgreSQL conformance and pipeline regressions; the real PostgreSQL concurrent-redelivery test passed three consecutive isolated runs
- post-fix focused suite: 5 files, 52/52 tests; root/app typechecks, app build, and router smoke remain green

author: macbuchi
body:
## Why

While investigating #175 the documentation turned out to describe a mechanism that has not existed since **2026-07-30**: the `Push-Benachrichtigungen` workflow is `disabled_manually`, and CLAUDE.md still called it "die Zusage, die den schnellen Weg trägt".

Two separate corrections, both measured rather than assumed:

**It is off.** `gh workflow list --all` reports `disabled_manually`, last run 2026-07-30 09:44 UTC.

**It was never hourly.** The last four scheduled runs were 00:12, 03:32, 06:43 and 09:44 UTC — a bit over three hours apart on `cron: "23 14-23,0-9 * * *"`. That is exactly the #115 finding that motivated #132 in the first place: GitHub drops scheduled runs under load and does not catch up. A floor that holds every three hours is no floor under a minute-precise reminder.

## What actually carries delivery

Verified in production on 2026-08-05: the evening digest and **both** departure reminders left on the minute, six days after the job stopped.

- cadence: `pg_cron 'flush-due-push' (* * * * *)` → `flush_due_push()` → `flush-push`
- content: the client, via `pushOutboxSyncProvider`

GitHub Actions is on neither path. The departure reminder (v0.58.0, 2026-08-03) shipped four days *after* the job was switched off and therefore never had that floor.

## What is genuinely lost

Narrower than the old wording implied, and now written down: if **nobody** opens the app for a whole week, no outbox row is ever written and nothing announces itself. As long as someone opens the app, it does not show.

Whether the job comes back is left **explicitly open** — this PR does not decide it. If it returns, it returns honestly as "every few hours", not as a promise about minutes.

## Scope

Docs only — `CLAUDE.md` and the comments in `.github/workflows/notify.yml`. No version bump, no release. The "der Stundenjob" mentions elsewhere in CLAUDE.md are left standing and covered by one pointer: they describe the job's built purpose, which nobody performs while it rests. Comments in `lib/` that say the same thing are deliberately untouched — editing them would trip the Version Guard and publish a release for a documentation fix.

author: ronaldlokers
body:
Second OIDC client. First one added since the blueprint learned to declare its own credentials (#280), so this is a block of YAML rather than an archaeology exercise against a running authentik.

## Two silent failure modes, both handled

**`SOCIAL_PROVIDERS` names the allauth module to load.** Without it the provider JSON is accepted and then ignored — the app starts clean, nothing logs an error, and the login page simply has no authentik button. Verified against the `2.6.13` tag rather than the latest docs: 2.x needs *both* `SOCIAL_PROVIDERS` (module) and `SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS` (config); 1.5.x used the former alone.

**`provider_id` ties the two sides together.** allauth mounts its callback at `/accounts/oidc/<provider_id>/login/callback/`, so the string in the secret is what makes the blueprint's `redirect_uri` correct:

```
provider_id: authentik
redirect:    https://tandoor.staging.ronaldlokers.nl/accounts/oidc/authentik/login/callback/
```

A mismatch surfaces as `redirect_uri mismatch` **from authentik**, not as a 404 from Tandoor — which points the investigation at the wrong side of the connection.

Also checked and rejected: `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION` is not a Tandoor knob — `recipes/settings.py` at 2.6.13 hardcodes `SOCIALACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION = 'none'`. It would have been a plausible-looking no-op.

## Verified

Rendered output, not the source:

```
SOCIAL_PROVIDERS in rendered env: True
envFrom: ['tandoor-oidc']
ALLOWED_HOSTS kept: ['tandoor.staging.ronaldlokers.nl,localhost']
postgres/SECRET_KEY refs kept: ['POSTGRES_PASSWORD', 'POSTGRES_USER', 'SECRET_KEY']
```

Both blueprints parsed back out of the wrapped Secret before encryption, then the ciphertext checked for leaks:

```
mealie.yaml    id ok: True  secret ok: True
tandoor.yaml   id ok: True  secret ok: True
blueprint: leaks=0 encrypted_keys=2
```

Local accounts stay enabled deliberately — the existing admin account is the way back in if this is misconfigured.

⚠️ Staging cannot test the network path (#282). Nothing here depends on a NetworkPolicy; the production promotion will.

author: protz
body:
As I was trying to write a lemma that relates step1 and straightlineStep, I found myself trying to prove some basic properties, namely that directivesAt returns a prefix of directivesFrom.

I then bottomed out on the `withAddresses` function. My understanding is that `withAddresses` means: pair each instruction with its start address. I believe it is a start address because:
- directivesAtAddress returns all instructions located at that address
- furthermore, in Instruction.interp, we compute a Rco (range closed-open) that starts at pc (i.e. where the instruction was found) and ends at the "end" of the instruction (computed by adding the instruction size to the pc).

In short, it definitely looks like withAddresses really means withStartAddresses. But that's not what happens.

Here's a concrete example:

```
#eval
  let exe := Program.fakeLayout [
    .label "main",
    .instr (.mk .W64 .W64 (.lea (.low .rax .W64) (.mk .none .none (.int64 41)))),
    .instr (.mk .W64 .W64 (.inc (.reg (.low .rax .W64)))),
    .instr (.mk .W64 .W64 .ret) ]
  exe.withAddresses
```

By that logic, I would expect the `lea` to be located at the same address as the label. After all, labels have no size. But we get this:

```
 633:1-633:6: information:
[(4075551246440333312, Directive.byteArray { data := #[] }, 0), (4075551246440333312, Directive.label "main", 0),
  (4075551246440333320,
    Directive.instr
      { address_size := Width.W64, operation_size := Width.W64,
        operation := Operation.lea (Reg.low Reg64.rax Width.W64) { base := none, idx := none, disp := ↑41 } },
    8),
  (4075551246440333326,
    Directive.instr
      { address_size := Width.W64, operation_size := Width.W64,
        operation := Operation.inc ↑(Reg.low Reg64.rax Width.W64) },
    6),
  (4075551246440333333,
    Directive.instr { address_size := Width.W64, operation_size := Width.W64, operation := Operation.ret }, 7)]
```

In short, the `lea` and the label are located at different addresses. I believe this is incorrect.

This patch:
- fixes the issue by rewriting withAddresses using custom logic (perhaps this function ought to be rewritten as a tail-recursive one, let's see if this blocks us)
- rewrites directivesAt and directivesFrom to be more obvious
- leverages the rewritten definitions to state that one is a prefix of the other (likely needed for the lemma I'm trying to write)
- fixes the helper that relates layout and directivesFromStart

author: hraaaaf
ymote
body:
Fixes #1918.

Every signal the model saw after `peer_handoff` pointed at "your work is finished", and nothing pointed back:

| surface | text |
|---|---|
| description | "**Promote work OUT** of this conversation" |
| description | "You will **NOT receive the result in this turn**" |
| result | "**Do not wait for it.**" |

So the master treated a handoff as transferring ownership of its work and ended the turn, resuming only on a user nudge — serializing exactly the work delegation exists to parallelize.

**"Do not wait" answers whether to BLOCK. It never answered whether to CONTINUE.**

## Changes

**The result text** carries most of the weight — it is in context at the moment the model chooses between another tool call and ending the turn, whereas the description is read once when the tool list is built. It now ends:

> Do not wait for it — and do not stop here: if you still have work of your own, continue it now in this same turn. **Only finish if the peer took over everything that was left.**

That last sentence is load-bearing. Without it "keep working" reads as "never finish", and handing off the *primary* task is a case where stopping is right.

**The description** reframes the opening from "Promote work OUT of this conversation" to "Hand a SELF-CONTAINED piece of work … and keep working yourself", and states plainly that a handoff does not end the turn.

## What I deliberately did not change

- **The handoff-vs-spawn axis.** #1918 suggests distinguishing primary vs auxiliary tasks, but the description already splits on *does THIS turn need the result* — and the model was applying that correctly. A side question genuinely does not feed the turn's reasoning, so `peer_handoff` was the right tool. The defect was inferring "nothing to wait for" as "nothing to do". Adding a second axis would collide with the existing one.
- **`spawn`.** #1918 mentions it, but spawn returns into the turn by design; a stall there would be a functional defect, not a framing one, and wants its own issue with a transcript.
- **A structural nudge** (#1918 direction 3). It needs a notion of "pending local work" that the agent does not have — the closest is the staged-submit queue, which holds user prompts, not the model's own unfinished intent.

## Scope of the test

The new test pins the **wording**, not the behaviour. The bug is an LLM judgement and can only be confirmed live: hand a side task to a peer mid-task and watch whether the master resumes on its own. I have not verified that.

There is no central role prompt in `octos-agent` to carry this guidance, so these two surfaces are the only levers available.

2521 octos-agent lib tests pass; `cargo fmt --all --check` and `scripts/lint-tool-descriptions.py` clean (21 tools / 14 manifests).

author: gutzbenj
body:
## What

`UnitConverter.targets["power_per_area"]` was `watt_per_square_centimeter`:

```python
"power_per_area": self.units["power_per_area"][0],
```

Nothing chose W/cm² — it is simply what index `0` happened to be in the list. Every other target in that dict picks a deliberate index (`length_medium` takes `[2]`, `pressure` takes `[1]`, `conductivity` takes `[3]`); this one inherited the default and nobody noticed.

W/m² is what WMO specifies for irradiance and what **every source in this library actually publishes** (KNMI `qg`, MeteoSwiss `gre000z0`, Geosphere `cglo`, met.no, RMI — all W/m²). So the default made every affected value read 10⁴ too small.

Verified against live data — MeteoSwiss Bern, 10-minute global radiation, 1.18M non-null readings:

| | min | max | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before (W/cm²) | 0.0 | 0.1344 | 0.015 |
| after (W/m²) | 0.0 | 1344.0 | 150.2 |

0–1344 W/m² is the physically expected range for global irradiance (clear-sky peak ~1000–1200, higher under cloud enhancement). The old numbers were correct but unreadable.

## ⚠️ Breaking

Irradiance values are **10⁴ times larger**. This affects the 17 `power_per_area` declarations across **KNMI (10 minutes), MeteoSwiss, met.no Frost and RMI**.

Anyone depending on the old output can restore it per-request:

```python
Settings(ts_unit_targets={"power_per_area": "watt_per_square_centimeter"})
```

(verified working — the unit is still in the list, only the default target moved)

Irradiation (`energy_per_area`) is **untouched** and still returns J/cm², which is the conventional unit for it and what DWD publishes. The two are different quantities; only the irradiance default was wrong.

## Scope

One line of behaviour plus its test. No provider metadata changes: the sources' own declared units were already correct, and this only changes what they are converted *to*.

## Testing

- `tests/model` + `tests/test_api.py` — 239 passed
- No provider test asserts on radiation values for the four affected providers (checked)
- `lint`, `typecheck` clean
- End-to-end fetch against live MeteoSwiss, as above

## Context

Split out of #1800 deliberately. That PR renames irradiance parameters to `radiation_*_intensity`; this one fixes what unit they come back in. They are independent — the affected declarations already used `power_per_area` before #1800 — and keeping the unit change separate makes both reviewable.

It is also a prerequisite for removing Geosphere's in-parser W/m² → J/cm² conversion (`provider/geosphere/observation/api.py:119`, the only in-parser unit conversion in the tree). Removing that *before* this fix would have briefly shipped Geosphere radiation in W/cm², which is worse than either end state.
