author: vincentshipsit
body:
## Problem

The cost scan reads every `.jsonl` under `~/.claude*/projects` and `~/.codex/{sessions,archived_sessions}` and hands **every line** to `JSONSerialization.jsonObject`.

Both CLIs write pasted file contents, base64 blobs and raw tool output straight into a single line, so transcript lines get very large — the biggest on my machine is **56,660,520 B (54.04 MiB)** in a `~/.codex/archived_sessions` rollout. Parsing a line that size costs seconds of CPU and a transient allocation as large as the line, and the result is thrown away every time: a line that big is never a usage record.

## Change

- `CostScanFileSystem.maximumLineBytes` (**4 MiB**) + `isScannableLine(_:)` — one shared constant, not a literal duplicated in two files.
- `ClaudeCostScanner.parseSessionWindows` checks it before the parse.
- `CodexCostScanner.scanRollouts` checks it **before even the `token_count` byte-marker scan**, since the biggest lines there are exactly the ones guaranteed not to be usage records.

## Why 4 MiB — measured, not guessed

Scanned the full local corpus: **351,312 Claude lines / 151,089 usage-bearing** and **1,442,275 Codex lines / 372,960 usage-bearing**.

| | Claude | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| **largest usage-bearing line** | **150,055 B (146.5 KiB)** | **831 B** |
| usage-line p50 / p99 | 1,753 / 17,359 B | 722 / 807 B |
| largest line overall | 2,371,526 B (2.26 MiB) | 56,660,520 B (54.04 MiB) |
| lines skipped at 4 MiB | **0** | **108** |

4 MiB sits ~28x above the largest usage-bearing line ever observed, and no usage-bearing line in either corpus comes within an order of magnitude of it. For reference the same corpus has 1,883 lines over 1 MiB and 1,153 over 2 MiB, so a tighter cap would buy more skips at the cost of shrinking that headroom.

## Logging

One `AppLog.cost.debug` **per file that skipped anything**, not per skipped line — on this corpus that is at most ~108 entries and realistically far fewer, so a large corpus can't make the log the new cost. Only the count is `.public`; the filename stays at default redaction.

## Tests (written first)

New `MeterBarTests/OversizedScanLineTests.swift`, 8 cases covering **both** scanners:

- a line above the cap is skipped and contributes zero tokens/cost (and no session)
- a line **exactly at** the cap is still parsed and counted
- a file mixing oversized and normal lines still tallies every normal one — the giant does not abort the rest of the file
- the cap applies to **both** the period and lifetime windows

Fixtures are *valid* usage records padded to an exact byte target, so a skip can only be size-driven — a malformed giant would have been dropped by the pre-existing parse guards and proved nothing. Verified by disabling the guard: 6 of 8 fail without it (the two at-cap tests pass either way by design — they exist to catch over-rejection).

Plus a direct `isScannableLine` boundary assertion in `CostScanCollaboratorTests`.

## Verification

- `swift build` — clean
- `swift test` — **1715 tests, 0 failures** (5 skipped, pre-existing)
- `swiftlint --strict` — 0 violations

`FileLineReader.swift` is untouched, per the parallel quadratic-time fix.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved transcript scanning by safely skipping excessively large lines instead of attempting to parse them.
  * Continued processing subsequent valid records when oversized lines are encountered.
  * Applied the safeguard consistently across usage periods and supported scanning formats.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for line-size boundaries and handling of oversized records.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Populate cached device properties upon leasing proxied Android devices

Devices obtained via ProxyDeviceRunner#leaseDevice do not traverse
AndroidDeviceDelegate#setUp, which is the standard caller of
AndroidDeviceHelper#updateAndroidPropertyDimensions. Consequently,
cached system properties (such as "cached_sdk_version") remained
unpopulated for proxied Android devices, causing AndroidDevice#getSdkVersion()
to return null.

This change invokes updateAndroidPropertyDimensions immediately after
a successful lease in ProxyDeviceRunner whenever the leased target is an
instance of AndroidDevice, ensuring proxied devices carry identical cached
property dimensions as locally managed hardware.

author: copilot
body:
AudioStreaming's `AVAudioEngine`-backed `AudioPlayer` (adopted in July) makes an equalizer possible for the first time — `AVPlayer` had no supported way to insert a filter into its render chain. The Android client already ships this via platform-independent curve math; this ports that logic and wires an attach point into the new engine.

**Ported band math (no platform dependency)**
- `EqualizerPreset` — `.normal`/`.bassBoost`/`.vocal`/`.treble`, each owning its own gain curve. `.normal` uses `curve == nil` (literal 0 dB per band), not the midpoint of the device's `bandLevelRange` — on asymmetric ranges the midpoint isn't flat.
- `EqualizerCurves` — maps a curve onto a given band count and gain range. Pure function, unit-testable without any audio framework.

**Engine attach point**
- `AudioStreamingPlaybackEngine+Equalizer.swift` attaches an `AVAudioUnitEQ` via AudioStreaming's `attach(node:)`, applies `EqualizerCurves`-computed gains within a conservative ±12 dB range, and re-attaches the node after `handleMediaServicesReset()` (the engine is rebuilt from scratch on reset, so nothing survives automatically).

**Graceful degradation on non-EQ engines**
- `RadioPlaybackEngine` gains `supportsEqualizer`/`setEqualizerPreset(_:)` with a default protocol extension returning "no EQ". The watch's `AVPlayer`-backed engine and the stub engine inherit this with zero changes, so the caveat about watchOS not having a dead control is satisfied structurally rather than by convention.

**Wiring**
- `PlaybackController` exposes the capability/setter to the app layer.
- `SettingsStore` persists the chosen preset as a raw `Int`, keeping `Persistence` free of a `Playback` dependency.
- `SettingsView` shows an Equalizer picker only when the active engine reports support.

```swift
if playbackController.supportsEqualizer {
    Picker("Equalizer", selection: $settings.equalizerPresetRawValue) {
        ForEach(EqualizerPreset.allCases) { preset in
            Text(preset.displayName).tag(preset.rawValue)
        }
    }
}
```

author: vwellenberg
body:
## Problem

On half-width screens the home rows ("Recently played", …) broke into **two rows**. `maxAbumCards` derived the card count from a **measured** card width (`Math.round` over stretched 1fr cards, updated by whichever page measured last — navigation-order dependent), which can overshoot the column count the `auto-fill` grid actually builds. Concrete case: 864px of content fits exactly 4 columns (4·192 + 3·32), but `round(864/192) = 5` → the fifth card wrapped.

## Fix (root cause: two disagreeing sources of truth → one)

- **`utils/cardColumns.ts`** — the JS mirror of the CSS auto-fill formula `floor((width + gap) / (min + gap))`, incl. the `mediumPhones` 9rem minimum. Constants are documented against their SCSS sources.
- **`CardScroller`** measures its own grid (`useElementSize`) and renders exactly that many cards — a one-row scroller can no longer wrap. Placeholders follow the same count.
- **`maxAbumCards`** is now only the fetch-size heuristic / album-list group size: deterministic `floor` over the bare card minimum, no measurement feedback. `album_card_with` + `updateCardWidth` and all call sites removed.
- **Browse tiles** get a fixed CSS width (they are a free-wrapping flex row with no alignment contract to the card grid — they used to jump between ~137px and ~200px depending on which page had measured last).
- **Docs**: new section in `.claude/rules/styling.md` tying the SCSS tokens to the JS constants.

## Tests

`src/utils/__tests__/cardColumns.test.ts` — checks `cardColumns` against a reimplementation of the CSS auto-fill algorithm across every width 200–2400px (desktop) and 150–460px (phone), plus the concrete 864px wrap case and the breakpoint switch.

author: sashamit
body:
## Summary
In plain terms: when a client tells an A2A agent "send my task updates to this webhook", the agent server POSTs to **whatever URL the client supplied — no checks at all**. That means any client can make the agent server send requests to internal network addresses: cloud metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`), `localhost` admin panels, or unauthenticated internal services. This is the classic server-side request forgery (SSRF) pattern, and it fires on every task event.

Concretely, `BasePushNotificationSender._dispatch_notification` used `push_info.url` exactly as supplied:
- no scheme restriction (`ftp://`, future handler schemes),
- no destination restriction (loopback / link-local / RFC1918 / reserved),
- and configs can be registered through multiple paths (`tasks/pushNotificationConfig/create`, inline on `message/send`), so write-time validation alone wouldn't cover all of them.

## Fix
`BasePushNotificationSender` now validates each URL **at dispatch time** (one choke point covering every registration path):
- scheme must be `http`/`https`,
- host must resolve (unresolvable fails closed — the POST would fail anyway),
- every resolved address must be public unicast; loopback, link-local, private, reserved, multicast, and unspecified addresses are rejected.

Operators whose legitimate webhooks live on private networks opt out explicitly: `BasePushNotificationSender(..., allow_private_push_urls=True)`.

**Residual risk, stated honestly:** DNS rebinding between validation and the POST itself remains possible for attacker-controlled domains (validation and the actual connection resolve the name separately). Static internal targets — the realistic SSRF cases here — are fully blocked. Noted in the constructor docstring.

## Test plan
- [x] 7 new unit tests: metadata IP blocked, loopback blocked, private range blocked, non-HTTP scheme blocked, unresolvable host fails closed, public host allowed, opt-out allows private
- [x] `tests/server/tasks/` 185 pass (existing suites made DNS-hermetic)
- [x] Push-notification e2e suite passes (test app opts out — its webhooks are real local servers)
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean on touched files

Made with Cursor

author: michael-tomala
body:
Implements brief `0-2-10-to-0-2-11.md` — see:
`c4s read-brief 0-2-10-to-0-2-11.md --project 'app-spec' --workspace 'default'`

## What this is

Nine of the brief's twelve implementation items were **already in the code**. The remaining
three (items 2, 7 and 9) turned out to be one job: **the host still held static dictionaries
of entity type names.** Per the spec (`no8witqs`, `m13cel00`: *"there exists no set of
«built-in types» as a predicate, constant or filter"*), those are now gone — which types
exist, and what backs one, are answered by the registry that already knew.

`RawEntityType` and `EntityType` become `string`. `ENTITY_TABLES`, `ALL_ENTITY_TYPES`,
`isRawEntityType`, `ENTITY_TYPE_DIRS`, the release tier's three type arrays, the MCP
release-tools enums, the client's type lists and the nine `DatabaseTable*` interfaces are
deleted. Two architecture gates hold the release tier and the MCP release tools at exactly
zero entity-type literals.

## Six real bugs fell out of it

None of these were in the brief as bug reports — they are what the static lists were doing:

1. **Release snapshots covered five types.** `design-system`, `diagram` and every plugin type
   were invisible in every release diff and unrecoverable from every release, while
   `restoreSpec` restored types the snapshot had never captured. **No backfill needed** — the
   `UPDATE entity_version SET release_id` binding versions to releases was always untyped, so
   the history was captured and correctly bound all along; only the read path refused to look.
2. **Those two types reached no bundle at all** — so no export, clone or push carried them.
3. **`restoreBundleArchive` dropped rows it had just validated.** It checked each file against
   the active type set, then iterated a *different* hardcoded order.
4. **Version restore rejected every plugin type** as `type '<x>' is not restorable`.
5. **`EntityStore` wrote a plugin type's file but did not recognise it on read back**
   (`relPathFor` was widened in 2.0.0; `parseRelPath` never was).
6. **The XML-chip popovers offered three entity types**, making `ui-view`, `ac`,
   `design-system` and `diagram` unreachable from the editor.

## Breaking changes (both deliberate, both in CHANGELOG)

- **The `database_table` / `ui_view` underscore aliases no longer resolve** on the CLI and the
  `c4s-reader` MCP. A type id is always kebab-case, so those are malformed rather than
  alternative — and no other type got the courtesy.
- **`release_get` / `release_diff` `entityTypes` is no longer a closed five-value enum.** It
  rejected any other type at the MCP boundary, so the brief-authoring agent could not ask about
  the newly-covered types. Unknown types now simply match nothing.

Also user-visible: **past releases become complete retroactively** (design systems and diagrams
appear in diffs that previously showed nothing), and `snapshot.entities[]` ordering now follows
`displayOrder`.

## One deliberate deviation from the spec's answer

The spec proposed deriving bundle file names from `slugify(labelPlural)`. That breaks every
existing bundle: `ac.labelPlural` is `'Acceptance Criteria'` → `acceptance-criteria`, but every
archive ever produced contains `acs.json`, and the read path throws a hard
`BUNDLE_UNKNOWN_ENTITY_TYPE` on an unmapped name.

This uses **`basename(pathPrefix)`** instead, which reproduces all five legacy names exactly and
is indifferent to the `/api` spelling. Raised with the spec before it wrote the rule down — it
accepted, and also accepted a related correction: the spec documents `pathPrefix` as `/api/acs`
while the code declares `/acs` (the `/api` is added at mount). Filed as
`c4s file-patch --kind incorrect`.

## How it was tested

- **`npm run typecheck`** clean across server, client, types and the envelope plugin.
- **`npm test`: 1727 passing** (14 new). New: `release-bundle.test.ts` (this module had *no*
  test file, which is how it silently dropped types) with a golden assertion that the
  derivation reproduces all five legacy file names, plus a bundle round-trip;
  `release-snapshot-coverage.test.ts` as the direct regression test; two arch gates.
- **Live environment via env-runner**, built from this branch, driven in a real browser:
  created a design-system and a diagram through the real write path, cut a release, and
  confirmed the release detail renders `1 design-system · 1 diagram · 2 total captures` with
  both as proper cards. **Zero console errors, zero responses ≥ 400.** Also confirmed
  `diagram.caption` is not persisted (brief item 11).
- **Committed e2e suite: 53 passed, 3 failed.** All four failing files self-report missing seed
  data (`no plan`, `no page embeds a <diagram/>`, `no unversioned entity`) because the
  environment was ordered with `Dane: empty`. Verified against a **baseline environment built
  from `main`**, which fails the identical four files with the identical messages — this branch
  passes *more* (53 vs 48).

## Post-review corrections (commit 6/n)

A `/code-review high` pass (33 agents) found **10 issues, 7 confirmed** — all one pattern: this
branch widened the OUTBOUND side of each boundary and left the INBOUND side narrower. None was
reachable by the smoke test, which had one project, no deactivated types, no digit-bearing type
ids and no cross-version peer. All ten are fixed in `45dffa7`.

**Two of them contradicted claims made earlier in this description, now corrected:**

- I wrote that `parseRelPath`'s inbound gate was *fixed* so a plugin type's file is recognised on
  read back. It still rejected digits (`oauth2-scope` never reindexed), **and I made it stricter
  on activation** — the predicate it replaced ignored activation, and `EntityIndexer.handleUnlink`
  depends on that to drop the row of a file deleted while its type is deactivated. That was a
  regression introduced by this branch, not merely an unfixed gap. Now gates on `getAvailable`;
  `listAll()` too, since `project-context` compares its count against the DB's to choose a
  migration direction.
- I wrote "existing bundles remain readable with no compatibility shim." True in that direction
  only. The reverse was broken: new bundles carry `design-systems.json` while
  `BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION` stayed at 2, so an older peer's version guard passed and it then aborted
  on the unmappable file — blaming the archive for version skew. **Bumped to 3.**

Also fixed: the read-side basename-collision check no longer aborts every import over an unrelated
deactivated plugin (write side still refuses, where a collision would corrupt the archive); the
popovers no longer default to a hardcoded `'endpoint'` their own `<option>` list may not contain;
`snapshotToEntity` derives collection defaults from the type's `data.schema` instead of dropping
the array coercion cards rely on; `list-slugs` re-establishes the existence check
`normalizeEntityType` can no longer make; and the `tagged_list_mixed` bucket seed is restored from
AVAILABLE types, honouring the `.endpoints` → `[]` contract for a deactivated type.

Two judgment calls, both documented rather than silently changed: importing a bundle whose type is
locally deactivated stays **fatal** (skipping would drop every row of that type from the restore
without saying so), and the page-tag alias removal follows the spec's explicit ruling — but the
CHANGELOG now states that already-authored `type="database_table"` tags stop resolving and gives
the grep to find them, and a spec patch argues the ruling was decided as a question about call
arguments while it silently governs persisted user content.

New `entity-store.test.ts` pins both inbound regressions; both were verified to fail against the
pre-fix code. Suite is **1734 passing**.

**Re-verified in a rebuilt live environment on the fixed code** (the earlier smoke ran against
`1eabf7c`, so it did not cover these commits): 13/13 API+UI checks, zero console errors, zero
responses ≥ 400. Additionally exercised the two paths the fixes changed

Align the repository's public release status and package metadata with the already published CloudDoc AI Pipeline `v1.0.0` portfolio release.

author: emmettl
body:
Bumps `@driftbox/engine` and `@driftbox/app` to `0.6.0`, covering the 24 commits since `v0.5.0`.

`@driftbox/rack` deliberately stays at `0.1.0`. It has never been published, so this is its first release rather than a bump — the version it is release-ready at is the version that should go out. Its dependency on the engine moves to `^0.6.0` so the range stays satisfiable once the engine ships.

Same seven-file shape as the 0.5.0 prep: the three `package.json` files, the lockfile, and the three places that state the published version in prose.

## What is in the release

- A wavetable oscillator, the rack's second oscillator family
- A Line Mixer — six stereo channels, two aux sends and returns
- Four reverb algorithms, a wet-path EQ and a gate
- A Curve mode for Tracker lanes, matching the Matrix's third lane
- Erasable automation points
- Guided tours, better help and playable presets
- The VCV importer brought up to date with the rack it imports into
- Six groovebox songs shipped as rack++ documents
- Split view wherever there is room, a grouped and fixed rack header, and two patch-browser overlap fixes
- A large testability refactor across `RackApp`, the Groovebox and Keys faceplates, the patch browser, the stem desk and the sequencer page

## Checks

`lint`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` all run clean locally, and all three packages pack (`npm publish --dry-run`) at the right versions.

One caveat: `ChassisTitle.browser.test.ts` fails **locally only**, and it already failed on `main` before this branch. It measures real text metrics, and "Limiter" renders narrow enough in macOS Chromium to escape truncation. CI is green on `a4ddb08`, so the expected list is right for the Linux Chromium the release actually runs on — changing it would turn CI red.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## The rack's first publish (second commit)

The publish workflow could not have shipped this release as it stood. `PACKAGES` is `engine rack app`, the loop runs under `set -e`, and the rack has no trusted publisher — one cannot be configured for a name the registry has never seen. So the run would have published the engine, failed on the rack, and **aborted before the app**, half-shipping the release.

A repo `NPM_TOKEN` secret alone did not fix that: the workflow never read one. `setup-node` writes an `.npmrc` whose auth line expands `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, and nothing set it, so npm fell back to OIDC regardless.

The token is now read **for the rack only**, not for the step. npm prefers an explicit token over OIDC, so a token in scope for all three would silently take over the engine and app publishes too — and would 401 them outright if it were granted for the rack alone. The engine and the app keep OIDC and provenance untouched.

It also degrades safely: with no `NPM_TOKEN` secret present the condition is false for every package and the loop is exactly what it was before.

### After the release, undo it

1. Point `@driftbox/rack`'s npm package settings at this workflow (trusted publishing).
2. Revoke the token and delete the `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
3. Delete the `BOOTSTRAP` block from `.github/workflows/publish.yml`.

`docs/PUBLISHING.md` records all of this, including the teardown.

body:
## Summary

Four related adjustments to the 8-band EQ (user request):

- **Renamed labels**: "Low Pass" → "High Cut", "High Pass" → "Low Cut" (matches Ableton EQ8/FabFilter Pro-Q naming — says which end gets cut, not the filter-theory term). Internal `value`/DSP behavior unchanged.
- **Adjustable Q via drag**: vertical drag on a Low Cut/High Cut band's node now controls Q (resonance) instead of the DSP-inert gain — Web Audio's biquad spec gives highpass/lowpass filters no effective gain parameter at all, so dragging the point previously did nothing audible. This now matches how Ableton EQ8/FabFilter Pro-Q handle cut filters (drag up = more resonant peak at the cutoff). Node position, hit-testing, and the drag readout all updated to reflect Q for cut-type bands.
- **Fixed the curve display**: previously, once a band's real frequency response fell outside the currently visible ±dB zoom range, the curve got clamped to the range edge and drew an ugly flat plateau line across the rest of the graph. Verified via direct `getEq8Response()` measurement that this is a real, reproducible case (a shallow-slope cut filter at a small zoom range easily exceeds ±12dB) — not just a rare edge case. The curve now simply exits the visible area instead of clamping (axis gridlines/node position still clamp as before — only the curve line changed).
- **Fixed the hint text**: "Tap: select/add band" → "Tap: select · Double tap: add/remove band", matching the actual double-tap-required gesture (confirmed in the existing pointer-handling code — a single tap on empty space does nothing, you need a second tap within the double-tap window to actually create a band).

## Verification

- Added `tools/dsp-tests/eq8-cut-q-curve.mjs`: confirms Q changes produce a measurably larger resonance peak, and that the curve-exceeds-range scenario is real (not a hypothetical).
- Manually verified end-to-end that dragging a Low Cut node up through the real pointer-event path increases Q.
- Updated `eq8-basic.mjs`/`eq8-zoom-ui.mjs` for the new labels; `eq8-zoom-ui.mjs` also needed to re-locate the node's position after switching a band to a cut type, since it can now reposition to reflect Q instead of gain (expected consequence of the Q-drag feature).
- Full `dsp-check.mjs` suite passes except `damping-filter.mjs`, which is unrelated pre-existing flakiness (confirmed by diff: this PR touches nothing in the resonator/reverb code) — same test flaked in a previous, unrelated PR under similar system load.
- `layout-check.mjs` passes across all widths.

- [x] Full `dsp-check.mjs` suite passes (aside from one confirmed-unrelated flaky test)

author: jennathor
body:
What

Three places rebuilt pathway membership by splitting the Genes column on spaces — enrichmentPlot() (tree), enrichmentNetwork() (network), and the redundancy filter in server.R. FindOverlap() already has that membership as Ensembl IDs while it builds the string, so it now returns it as an I() list column, which stays aligned through the ordering and subsetting that follow. The three consumers read that. server.R's " |  |   " split is gone.

Why

A display column was analysis input, so reformatting it silently changed scientific output. Twice already: #84 (unique() collapsed unsymboled genes) and #86 (padded symbols became blank tokens). Both were fixed at the formatting end, leaving the mechanism intact — and 4f483bc's message shows the nzchar() check behind #86 came from the #84 fix. The fix for the first caused the second, days later, same function. That's a contract problem, not an attention problem.

Behavior change

Membership is now always Ensembl IDs. Since intersect() and union() de-duplicate, two paralogs sharing a symbol used to count as one element under the default and now count as two. Correct space — two paralogs are two loci — but a scientific decision:

- **Pathway overlap now counts paralogs separately when they share a gene symbol, rather than collapsing them into one gene. Previously, overlap values could change depending on the Genes column format selected in the download dialog; they no longer do.**

- **Results are unchanged for gene lists without symbol-sharing paralogs, which is the large majority, measured on the data113 db, after the deduplication ShinyGO already applies, this affects 0.29% of human protein-coding genes (60 genes across 24 symbols), 0.80% of mouse genes and 1.09% of maize genes. For lists containing gene families or tandem duplicates — defensins, KIRs, chemokines and similar — trees and networks will differ from previous releases, and pathways near the redundancy threshold may be added or removed.**

After converted() dedup on production data113: 60 of human's 20,342 protein-coding genes still share a symbol (0.29%); 0.80% of all mouse genes and 1.09% of all maize genes. Ordinary lists are unaffected — this matters for lists built around gene families or tandem duplicates.

Verification

Production data113: human (86,433 genes), mouse (78,298), maize (44,355).

- Invariance: on an adversarial query of symbol-sharing genes, tree and network overlaps are identical across all three genesColumnID settings: human GOBP 60 / GOMF 33, mouse GOBP 60 / GOMF 49, maize GOBP 60 / GOMF 60 / KEGG 33. The same maize fixture previously differed on 48.2% of GOBP pairs, up to 0.238 Jaccard, 15 crossing the 0.95 redundancy threshold.
- No regression: a realistic query (all genes of one mid-size KEGG pathway) gives byte-identical pathways, nGenes and Genes against unmodified v851pfe, human and mouse.
- Shape: membership length equals nGenes on every row, token counts unchanged, downloads still write 7 columns.

body:
Closes #1389

## What this does

Fixes an inverted precedence claim in `plugin/fabrik/skills/fabrik/SKILL.md`'s labels table.

## The bug

The `fabrik:cruise` row's parenthetical said "`fabrik:yolo` wins if both are present" — this is backwards. The actual, code-enforced behavior (per `engine/stages.go`'s end-of-Validate guards, which test the raw `fabrik:cruise` label directly and force `shouldAdvance = false` regardless of yolo) is that **`fabrik:cruise` wins**: when both labels are present, the pipeline stops at Validate with no auto-merge and no advance to Done.

This is safety-relevant because it concerns whether a PR gets auto-merged — a reader of this doc could otherwise be misled into expecting an unintended auto-merge on a both-labelled issue.

## Key changes

- `plugin/fabrik/skills/fabrik/SKILL.md`: corrected the `fabrik:cruise` row's parenthetical to state cruise wins over yolo, matching every other doc in the repo (`README.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `docs/state-machine.md`, `docs/llms-full.txt`, `plugin/fabrik-workflows/LABELS.md`, `adrs/050-convergence-budget-and-native-automerge.md`) and the existing unit tests (`TestHandleStageComplete_BothCruiseAndYolo_CruiseWins`, `TestCruiseCatchUp_BothCruiseAndYolo_CruiseWins`).

No other line in the file changed, and no code, tests, or `docs/llms-full.txt` regen are needed — this skill file is not one of the four canonical `docs/` sources that bundle regenerates from.

## How to test

`git diff` on the commit shows a single-line change (the parenthetical only); `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass clean.

body:
## What

Adds a provider extension for [OilPriceAPI](https://www.oilpriceapi.com), implementing the `CommoditySpotPrices` standard model behind `obb.commodity.price.spot`.

That command currently has **one** provider, `fred`, serving 12 hardcoded FRED series. OilPriceAPI's public catalogue (`GET /v1/commodities`) exposes **463 series** — crude benchmarks, natural gas, refined products, coal, carbon, marine fuels and drilling activity — each carrying its own source timestamp and freshness metadata.

## Behaviour

| Query | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| no `start_date`/`end_date` | `/v1/prices/latest` — latest observation |
| either date supplied | `/v1/prices/historical` — daily series |

`commodity` accepts friendly aliases (`brent`, `wti`, `dutch_ttf`, `eu_carbon`, …) **or** any raw catalogue code, forwarded unchanged.

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.commodity.price.spot(provider="oilpriceapi", commodity="brent")
obb.commodity.price.spot(provider="oilpriceapi", commodity="wti",
                         start_date="2026-01-01", end_date="2026-06-30")
```

## Design notes

- **Depends only on `openbb-core`.** Uses `amake_request` rather than adding an HTTP client.
- The API's error envelope carries `code`, `message` and `request_id` — surfaced rather than swallowed.
- `EmptyDataError` distinguishes *unknown commodity* from *valid commodity, empty window*; the first message points at `/v1/commodities`.
- Registered as an **optional** provider in `dev_install.py`, matching the `nasdaq`/`tmx` pattern.

## Verification

Run against the live API before submission, not just unit-tested:

```
latest brent          -> 1 row   2026-08-05 BRENT_CRUDE_USD 79.31 barrel USD
wti 2026-07-01..07-31 -> 29 rows 2026-07-01 WTI_USD 68.83 barrel USD
raw code passthrough  -> DUTCH_TTF_EUR 53.44 mwh EUR
unknown commodity     -> EmptyDataError naming /v1/commodities
invalid credential    -> OpenBBError UNAUTHORIZED with request_id
empty date window     -> EmptyDataError reporting records found vs window
```

## Credentials for review

Free tier is **200 requests/month, no card required** (<https://www.oilpriceapi.com/auth/signup>). There is also a **keyless** demo endpoint if you'd rather not sign up at all:

```bash
curl https://api.oilpriceapi.com/v1/demo/prices
```

Happy to provide a reviewer key — just say where to send it.

## Not included

`tests/record/` cassettes are not committed: `record_http` needs to run in your CI environment to capture them against a real key. Glad to add them however you prefer — or I can record with a throwaway key if that's the convention.

Docs: <https://docs.oilpriceapi.com> · OpenAPI: <https://api.oilpriceapi.com/.well-known/openapi.json>

body:
## Summary

Measured coverage with `coverage run --source=app -m unittest discover -s test -t .`, then added deterministic unit tests for the modules that came out lowest. No production code changed.

| module | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app/services/utils/video_effects.py` | 12% | 100% |
| `app/services/subtitle.py` | 29% | 88% |
| `app/services/task.py` | 31% | 88% |
| `app/controllers/v1/video.py` | 37% | 99% |
| `app/models/exception.py` | 41% | 100% |
| `app/controllers/manager/redis_manager.py` | 44% | 100% |
| `app/controllers/base.py` | 53% | 100% |
| `app/controllers/manager/base_manager.py` | 56% | 100% |
| `app/utils/utils.py` | 64% | 97% |
| `app/controllers/v1/llm.py` | 70% | 100% |
| `app/config/config.py` | 72% | 100% |
| **total (`app`)** | **52%** | **77%** |

New test packages (`test/config`, `test/controllers`, `test/models`, `test/utils`) plus `test/services/test_video_effects.py` and `test/services/test_task_pipeline.py`. Everything is offline: Redis is a fake client injected via `patch("redis.Redis.from_url")`, whisper is a fake `WhisperModel`, HTTP endpoints run through `TestClient(app.asgi.app)` with `sm.state` swapped for a fresh `MemoryState` and `utils.task_dir`/`song_dir`/`storage_dir` pointed at tempdirs, and every `llm`/`voice`/`video`/`material`/`upload_post` call is mocked.

Notable behaviours now pinned down, not just line coverage:
- `TaskManager` concurrency: task runs immediately below the limit, queues above it, `TaskQueueFullError` once `max_queued_tasks` is reached, queued task drains on `task_done()`, and a task raising keeps `current_tasks` from leaking a slot.
- Video API security paths: `_sanitize_upload_filename("../../etc/passwd")` → `passwd`, `stream`/`download` reject paths resolving outside the task dir (403 / 404), `_task_file_to_uri` leaves out-of-tree paths unwrapped instead of turning them into URLs, and `Range: bytes=90-` / `bytes=-10` both yield `206` with the right `Content-Range`.
- Slide transitions are asserted on actual pixels (side, half-way offset, `t=0` fully off-screen, `t=0`/duration clamping) rather than just "a clip came back".
- `task.start()` per-`stop_at` return shapes, `TASK_STATE_FAILED` on each stage failure, `video_source == "local"` skipping term generation, and the YouTube cross-post `youtube_extra` payload.

Two behaviours found while writing tests, left as-is and only documented here:
- `GET /api/v1/video_materials` globs `*.mp4`, `*.mov`, … case-sensitively, so a file uploaded as `clip.MOV` (which the upload endpoint accepts) never shows up in the listing.
- `test/services/test_voice.py::test_gemini_tts_uses_legacy_submaker_fields` fails on a fresh clone because it writes into `storage/temp`, which doesn't exist until something creates it. Pre-existing and unrelated; it is not in CI's test list.

CI now runs the new deterministic modules alongside the existing ones, and `.gitignore`'s blanket `test_*.py` exclusion is widened from `!test/services/test_*.py` to `!test/**/test_*.py` so the new packages are tracked.

author: kelseyrmonson
body:
The GABJHS callout in `00_Data_Cleaning.qmd` (added in #37) listed `deNovo_Sig` = `Serous_Sig_4` as an unresolved risk — if that SigMiner de novo signature mapped to SBS3, then a caller had reported SBS3 after all and the reassignment should be revisited.

It is not a risk. The de novo signatures are **deliberately not mapped back to COSMIC**: none was a clean one-to-one match, so they are carried under their own labels precisely so the analysis can be run both ways and the effect of forcing a mapping can be seen.

A label kept separate by design cannot then be read as SBS3 — doing so would be exactly the assumption the separation exists to avoid. So the tie-break's precondition genuinely is unmet for GABJHS, and the reassignment rests on the callers that do report COSMIC signatures.

**This strengthens #37 rather than qualifying it**, which is the opposite of what the old wording implied. Corrected and `00_` re-rendered, rather than leaving a caveat that would send the next reader chasing a mapping that was never meant to exist.

Documentation only — no data, code or results change.

author: ooples
body:
`"file no longer readable"` asserts a change of state — it *was* readable, now it is not — and the commonest way to reach that branch involves no such change. A branch that predates the file, a worktree, an uninitialised submodule, or a fresh clone all produce it.

Observed live in this repository: a finding anchored to `src/utils/search-scope.ts` reported the file gone, purely because the checked-out branch predated it.

## The file already holds itself to this standard

A few lines further down, beside the fallback text:

> **REASON-NEUTRAL.** The earlier text asserted "the anchor changed", which is only one of the ways a finding reaches this branch […] In those cases the sentence stated a cause that had not been established.

The same objection applies to this string. It was simply missed when that lesson was applied.

## The change

`anchor not readable from this checkout` — true whether the file was deleted, never existed here, or lives on another branch, and it points the reader at something they can actually check.

Wording only. The anchor is still reported stale and still carries its stored snapshot as evidence; two of the four tests assert exactly that, so this cannot quietly turn into a suppression. A genuinely changed file still reports a change.

## Correction to an earlier report

I had also described this path as dumping ~90 lines of removed content into the context. **That was wrong.** `diffLines` caps at 40 lines (20 removed, 20 added) and appends a count of the remainder — the "87 more removed" I read as content was that count. There is no unbounded output here, and nothing in this PR changes the volume.

## Gates

124 suites, 1,530 passed, 4 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` clean. eslint 0 errors. `prettier --check` clean. `sync:hooks:check` clean.

Branched off `master`, independent of #262–#265.

author: jottasystem
body:
A doc do módulo afirmava que `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` **"NÃO é requisito de scan"**.

Verdade para beacon — no Android 12+ o SDK escaneia em `BLUETOOTH_SCAN`, sem location nenhuma. **Falso para Wi-Fi**, e a diferença é invisível.

Sem ele, do Android 10 em diante, app em background recebe **lista de scan vazia** e o BSSID placeholder `02:00:00:00:00:00`. O SDK descarta o placeholder — e tem de descartar, senão todo aparelho do mundo vira o mesmo AP. Então `wifis[]` e `network.apId` chegam vazios, sem erro em lugar nenhum.

Medido em produção, com corte no instante exato:

```
fg=True    wifis=25   apId=2dc5d744…
fg=False   wifis=0    apId=None
```

Mesmo aparelho, mesma sessão, todas as permissões que ele pediu concedidas.

No iOS o equivalente é `.whenInUse` contra `.always`.

## O que muda

Só documentação. **Nenhuma mudança de comportamento.**

- **`permissions.ts`** — o cabeçalho do módulo e o doc de `requestBackgroundLocation` passam a explicar quando isso importa e o que custa
- **README** — aviso na seção de Wi-Fi, cobrindo as duas plataformas
- **AI-AGENT-SETUP** — passa a mandar **perguntar** em vez de omitir

## O que continua igual

`requestPermissions()` **não** pede background location. É permissão *dangerous*, com revisão de política da Play e vídeo de demonstração atrelados, e não é requisito de detecção. Continua opt-in explícito via `requestBackgroundLocation()`.

O que muda é o integrador **saber o que perde** ao pular — hoje a doc dizia que não perdia nada.

Espelha [bearound-android-sdk#82](https://github.com/Bearound/bearound-android-sdk/pull/82) e [bearound-ios-sdk#72](https://github.com/Bearound/bearound-ios-sdk/pull/72).

`tsc --noEmit`, lint e commitlint limpos.
